title: Impact of race, sex, and insurance status on outcomes following endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Racial, sex, and socioeconomic differences in stroke outcomes are well documented, but their associations with outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remain uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with acute ischemic stroke who underwent EVT at a comprehensive stroke center during 2016-2022. The analytic dataset contained 527 patients. Endpoint-specific available observations were used without imputation. Outcomes included expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (eTICI) grade, admission and discharge National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), discharge and 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS), treatment-time metrics, and discharge disposition. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were fitted for seven clinical and procedural endpoints.

RESULTS: Final eTICI grade was available for 493 patients. Successful reperfusion (eTICI ≥2b) occurred in 449 (91.1%), and near-complete reperfusion (eTICI ≥2c) in 309 (62.7%). No demographic or payer variable was significantly associated with either reperfusion endpoint. Poor functional outcome occurred in 344 of 448 patients (76.8%) at discharge and 247 of 376 (65.7%) at 90 days. Black race and Medicare insurance were associated with poor discharge outcome. Female sex, Black race, and Medicare insurance were associated with poor 90-day outcome. Medicare and commercial insurance were associated with non-home discharge. Among 516 patients with available door-to-puncture time, the median was 69 min (interquartile range, 54-91), without statistically significant differences by sex, race, ethnicity, or payer.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing EVT at a single comprehensive stroke center, reperfusion rates were high and were not significantly associated with observed demographic or payer variables. Differences in functional outcomes and discharge destination were observed, but residual confounding, endpoint-specific missingness, and the single-center design limit causal interpretation.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with acute ischemic stroke who underwent EVT at a comprehensive stroke center during 2016-2022. The analytic dataset contained 527 patients.

title: Combination of ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy and phlebectomy in the treatment of the anterior saphenous vein insufficiency - a single-center retrospective study with long-term follow-up.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Isolated insufficiency of the anterior saphenous vein is common and as clinically relevant as the great saphenous vein insufficiency. Data regarding its optimal management are lacking.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed data from patients with isolated anterior saphenous vein varicosities who were treated at the Department of Dermatology, University of Lübeck, between 2013 and 2021. All patients underwent combined treatment consisting of ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy of the proximal intrafascial venous segment and phlebectomy of the extrafascial tributaries. The sclerosant was polidocanol. A successful outcome was defined as a combination of successful ablation and the absence of newly developed refluxing tributaries at follow-up.

RESULTS: 70 patients (56 female, 14 male) were included, with a mean follow-up period of 6.09 years (range: 6 months-10.2 years). The overall success rate was 81.4%. At follow-up, all patients showed an improvement in their clinical class according to the Clinical, Etiological, Anatomical, and Pathophysiological (CEAP) classification (p < 0.001). A significant correlation was found between the volume of polidocanol foam injected and successful sclerotherapy (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Combined ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy and phlebectomy is an effective treatment for isolated anterior saphenous vein varicosis, providing long-term success while preserving the great saphenous vein.

Data regarding its optimal management are lacking. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed data from patients with isolated anterior saphenous vein varicosities who were treated at the Department of Dermatology, University of Lübeck, between 2013 and 2021.

title: Conversion hip arthroplasty has a higher risk of venous thromboembolism disease at 30 days than primary total hip arthroplasty and revision total hip arthroplasty.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Venous thromboembolic disease (VTED), including deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), represents a serious postoperative complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA). While revision THA is traditionally considered higher risk than primary THA, the thromboembolic risks of conversion THA are still not well defined. This study compared 30-day DVT rates across primary, conversion, and revision THA.

METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional analysis was performed using the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database. Adult patients undergoing primary, conversion, or revision THA were identified using Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes. A total of 475,002 patients met inclusion criteria (primary THA: 428,245 [90.2%], conversion THA: 10,637 [2.2%], revision THA: 36,120 [7.6%]) with a mean age of 65.6 years (range, 18 to 89); 55.0% women. The primary outcome was 30-day postoperative DVT. Multivariable logistic regressions evaluated associations between procedure type and DVT, adjusting for age, sex, BMI, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class, smoking status, chronic steroid use, and operating time.

RESULTS: Adjusted odds of DVT were significantly lower after primary THA (odds ratio (OR) 0.48, 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.28-0.88; p = 0.010) and revision THA (OR 0.44, 95% CI, 0.23-0.87; p = 0.014) compared with conversion THA. Independent predictors of higher DVT risk included older age, longer operating time, and chronic steroid use. Sex, BMI, ASA class, and smoking status were not independently associated with DVT.

CONCLUSIONS: Conversion THA is associated with higher 30-day DVT risk compared with both primary and revision THA on multivariable analyses. Recognition of conversion THA as a distinct procedural category associated with higher relative thromboembolic risk may improve perioperative risk stratification and guide more individualised thromboprophylaxis strategies.

While revision THA is traditionally considered higher risk than primary THA, the thromboembolic risks of conversion THA are still not well defined. This study compared 30-day DVT rates across primary, conversion, and revision THA.

title: Effectiveness and Safety of Prophylactic Inferior Vena Cava Filters in High-Risk Hip Fracture Patients: Clinical implications of an early retrieval strategy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of prophylactic inferior vena cava (IVC) filter in patients with hip fracture who were at high risk for pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE).

METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Single-center Level I Trauma Center.

PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients older than 50 years who sustained a low-energy hip fracture (AO/OTA 31A, B, and 32A) and underwent prophylactic IVC filter insertion before hip fracture surgery between 2005 and 2025 were included. Prophylactic IVC filter placement was selectively performed in patients with either objectively confirmed deep vein thrombosis on preoperative screening or absolute contraindications to mechanical and pharmacological venous thromboembolism prophylaxis. Those who had multiple trauma at the time of injury, a clinical follow-up duration ≤6 months after surgery, or undergone IVC filter placement following a confirmed diagnosis of PTE based on pulmonary computed tomography or lung perfusion scanning were excluded.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The primary outcome was the rate of newly developed symptomatic PTE. Secondary outcomes included IVC filter-related complications, retrieval rates, and 30-day mortality.

RESULTS: One hundred fifty-six patients were included in the prophylactic IVC filter group (39 men 25.0%], 117 women [75.0%]; mean age, 75.8 ± 11.1 years; femoral neck [AO/OTA 31B], n = 71 [45.5%]; intertrochanteric [31A], n = 75 [48.1%]; subtrochanteric [AO/OTA 32A], n = 10 [6.4%];mean indwelling time, 9.1 days; retrieval rate, 88.5%). Among these patients, no cases of newly developed symptomatic PTE were observed (0%), whereas the incidence in the overall hip fracture cohort (n=4,568) was 0.44%. Filter-related complications occurred in 3.9% of patients (minor tilting, 2.6%; vessel adhesion, 1.3%), with no major mechanical failures such as migration or perforation. Although no thrombi were detected at insertion, 4.5% of the patients had trapped thrombi at the time of removal. The 30-day all-cause mortality rate was 1.3% (2/156) in the prophylactic IVC filter group, compared with 1.5% (67/4,568) in the overall hip fracture cohort. (p=0.845). Neither death in the prophylactic IVC filter group was attributed to PTE or an IVC filter-related complication.

CONCLUSIONS: In this study's selected extreme pulmonary thromboembolism risk cohort, including patients with CT-confirmed preoperative DVT, those clinically expected to undergo prolonged perioperative immobilization, or those with contraindications to prophylactic anticoagulation, such as GI bleeding, prophylactic inferior vena cava filter served as an effective and safe temporary bridge therapy rather than a routine prophylactic strategy.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic Level III.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of prophylactic inferior vena cava (IVC) filter in patients with hip fracture who were at high risk for pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE). METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Single-center Level I Trauma Center.

title: Comparative real-world outcomes of LifeStream and Viabahn VBX balloon-expandable covered stents for iliac artery occlusive disease.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Balloon-expandable covered stents (CSs) are increasingly used for complex iliac artery occlusive disease, but direct comparative data among CS platforms remain limited. This study compared 1-year restenosis and clinical outcomes between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX CSs in patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT).

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 226 patients who underwent EVT for symptomatic iliac artery occlusive disease using either the LifeStream CS (n = 95) or Viabahn VBX CS (n = 131). Outcomes included restenosis, clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR), re-occlusion, conversion to bypass surgery, and perioperative complications (POCs). Between-group comparisons were performed using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) based on propensity scores.

RESULTS: One-year follow-up data were available for 163 of 226 patients (72.1%), and 10 restenosis events occurred during follow-up. After IPTW adjustment, the balance of measured covariates was substantially improved. The estimated 1-year freedom from restenosis was 95.8% (95% confidence interval [CI], 93.1-98.6%) in the LifeStream group and 95.8% (95% CI, 93.1-98.6%) in the Viabahn VBX group, with no statistically significant between-group difference (p = 0.99). No significant differences were detected in freedom from CD-TLR (99.2% [95% CI, 98.0-100.0%] vs. 96.7% [95% CI, 94.3-99.2%]; p = 0.13), re-occlusion (100.0% [95% CI, 100.0-100.0%] vs. 98.1% [95% CI, 96.3-99.9%]; p = 0.091), conversion to bypass surgery (100.0% [95% CI, 100.0-100.0%] vs. 98.2% [95% CI, 96.4-100.0%]; p = 0.083), or POCs.

CONCLUSION: In this IPTW-adjusted multicenter retrospective study, no statistically significant differences in 1-year restenosis or other clinical outcomes were detected between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX balloon-expandable CSs. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating because of the small number of events, incomplete follow-up, and potential residual confounding.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 226 patients who underwent EVT for symptomatic iliac artery occlusive disease using either the LifeStream CS (n = 95) or Viabahn VBX CS (n = 131).

title: Venous Thromboembolism in Necrotizing Pancreatitis A Nationwide Analysis of Incidence, Risk Factors, and Outcomes.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Necrotizing pancreatitis (NP) is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Venous thromboembolism (VTE), including portal vein thrombosis (PVT), deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and pulmonary embolism (PE), represent complications of NP. However, comprehensive characterization of individual VTE subtypes, risk factors, and outcomes in NP remains limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the 2020 National Inpatient Sample, among adult patients hospitalized with acute pancreatitis. The patients were categorized into NP and interstitial pancreatitis (IP) groups, with focus on impact of VTE in NP cohort. Outcomes included VTE incidence, risk factors, complications, mortality, length of stay, hospitalization charges, and intensive interventions. Multivariable regression analyses were performed adjusting for demographic and hospital-level covariates.

RESULTS: Of 199,190 AP hospitalizations, 5.74% had NP and 94.26% had IP. NP was associated with significantly higher incidence of PVT (6.08% vs. 0.48%, aOR 11.53), DVT (8.36% vs. 0.69%, aOR 11.19), and PE (1.44% vs. 0.24%, aOR 5.58) compared to IP (all P<0.001). All VTE subtypes significantly increased length of stay, hospitalization charges, and complication rates. Malnutrition (PVT aOR 2.79, DVT aOR 1.61, PE aOR 6.86) and coagulopathy (PVT aOR 2.41, DVT aOR 2.15) were consistent risk factors across all VTE subtypes. Among NP patients, PVT was uniquely associated with mortality (aOR 2.71, P=0.007), while DVT and PE were not.

CONCLUSIONS: NP is associated with markedly increased risks of all VTE subtypes compared to IP. VTE in patients with NP is associated with increased morbidity, with PVT uniquely associated with mortality. Malnutrition and coagulopathy represent potentially modifiable risk factors that may help identify high-risk patients. These findings support the need for prospective study of VTE screening and prophylaxis strategies in NP patients.

However, comprehensive characterization of individual VTE subtypes, risk factors, and outcomes in NP remains limited.

title: Saddle pulmonary embolism and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia in acute pancreatitis: a case report.
abstract: Acute pancreatitis causes severe inflammation, predisposing patients to thromboembolism, which can be further complicated by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and thrombosis (HITT). A 47-year-old diabetic male patient with severe acute pancreatitis developed a massive saddle pulmonary embolism. Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) treatment triggered a deep vein thrombosis, and a severe platelet drop (28 × 10 9 /l), confirming HITT. Due to a refractory response to fondaparinux, the patient was successfully switched to direct oral anticoagulation with dabigatran etexilate (150 mg twice daily). This led to rapid platelet normalization and clinical stability. When standard parenteral treatments fail in HITT, direct oral anticoagulants like dabigatran offer an effective alternative strategy.

title: Impact of Inherited Thrombophilia on Cancer-associated Thrombosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-associated thrombosis (CT) is a cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with malignancy. The contribution of inherited thrombophilia remains incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between inherited thrombophilia and other genetic determinants and CT risk in adults with malignancy.

METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies comparing genetic determinants in patients with cancer with and without venous thromboembolism (VTE). Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using Mantel-Haenszel models. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE), respectively.

RESULTS: Twenty-one studies including 4,479 patients (1,115 with VTE) were included. Factor V Leiden (FVL) was associated with increased odds of CT (OR 2.48, 95% CI: 1.75-3.51; I 2 = 32%), with consistent findings after exclusion of device- or catheter-related thrombosis. Heterozygous FVL was associated with CT (OR 1.86, 95% CI: 1.27-2.73), whereas the homozygous estimate was imprecise (OR 3.42, 95% CI: 0.75-15.59). Prothrombin G20210A was associated with CT (OR 2.67, 95% CI: 1.56-4.58; I 2 = 0%). Exploratory analyses yielded estimates for methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR; OR 1.40, 95% CI: 1.02-1.93) and blood group O (OR 0.40, 95% CI 0.23-0.70); the latter was based on only two studies. Evidence for rarer determinants was sparse. Certainty was moderate for FVL and low or very low for other determinants.

CONCLUSION: FVL and prothrombin G20210A are associated with increased odds of CT. Current evidence does not support universal genetic screening but warrants prospective evaluation of the incremental predictive value of genetic markers beyond established CT risk models.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Cancer-associated thrombosis (CT) is a cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with malignancy. The contribution of inherited thrombophilia remains incompletely defined. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between inherited thrombophilia and other genetic determinants and CT risk in adults with malignancy.

title: Vascular risk prediction in migraine: A multimodality risk score based on artificial intelligence-electrocardiogram output, echocardiogram, and detailed migraine characteristics.
abstract: AimPatients with migraine, especially those with aura, have a higher risk of stroke and other vascular events. However, the underlying mechanisms are complex, multifactorial, and may require integration of multimodal data for comprehensive characterization. We have conducted prior analyses on how artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled electrocardiogram (ECG), specifically the atrial fibrillation prediction model and age estimation model output, echocardiogram parameters, and detailed migraine characteristics separately predict vascular events. Herein, we aim to investigate the relative importance and combined effects of all three modalities for vascular risk prediction.MethodsIn this retrospective cohort study, we developed a multimodality prediction risk score to evaluate the vascular risks in patients with migraine based on the coefficients of variables extracted from our prior studies, including comprehensive AI-ECG atrial fibrillation prediction model output and computed delta age (ECG estimated age minus chronological age), echocardiogram parameters, and migraine characteristics. We then included patients with at least one 12-lead ECG, transthoracic echocardiogram, and a visit with a headache specialist at any Mayo Clinic site within three years to evaluate the risk score. The outcome is a composite endpoint of acute ischemic stroke, acute myocardial infarction, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality. We selected 20 risk parameters, including demographics, comorbidities, AI-ECG outputs, echocardiogram features, and migraine characteristics found to be predictive of vascular events. Each variable was assigned a different risk score according to the hazard ratio (HR) and beta coefficient from prior Cox regression analysis for each modality. We used Contal and Q'Quigley's method to find the optimal cut-off, and an additional multivariate Cox regression was conducted to assess the relative risk of each parameter category in the final cohort. We investigated the added value of each modality by net reclassification improvement rate.ResultsA total of 29,928 patients, 12,778 patients, and 6819 patients were included to investigate how AI-ECG outputs, echocardiogram parameters, and migraine characteristics, respectively, predicted adverse vascular outcomes, and the results were used to develop a multimodal risk score. A total of 297 patients with migraine included in previous analyses, of whom 247 (83.2%) were female and 109 (36.7%) had aura, were used for proof-of-concept evaluation of the developed risk score. The mean (standard deviation, SD) age was 39.0 (13.3) and follow-up period was 68.9 (60.9) months. Thirty-five patients (11.8%) developed the composite endpoint. Those with a risk score ≥15 had a significantly shorter vascular event-free survival (HR [95% Confidence Interval (CI)], 3.83 [1.89-7.76]; p < 0.001) compared to those with a risk score <15 in our cohort of 297 patients. Furthermore, comorbidity (HR, 1.17 [1.06-1.30]; p = 0.003) and migraine characteristics (HR, 1.33 [1.06-1.67]; p = 0.014) were significantly predictive of the composite endpoint, whereas other categories were not. Net reclassification improvement was 17.7% (95% CI, 15.9-19.9%; p < 0.001) for AI-ECG model output, 16.9% (95% CI, 14.1-19.5%; p < 0.001) for echocardiogram, and 22.1% (95% CI, 16.7-26.9%; p < 0.001) for migraine characteristics, suggesting significant contribution from each modality.ConclusionThis pilot evaluation study supports the use of combined AI-ECG output, echocardiogram, and migraine characteristics for vascular risk prediction. Although future external validation and real-world clinical assessment is necessary, our preliminary results suggest significant added value of each modality and indicate the importance of obtaining detailed migraine features for vascular risk stratification.
englishSummary: AimPatients with migraine, especially those with aura, have a higher risk of stroke and other vascular events. However, the underlying mechanisms are complex, multifactorial, and may require integration of multimodal data for comprehensive characterization. We have conducted prior analyses on how artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled electrocardiogram (ECG), specifically the atrial fibrillation prediction model and age estimation model output, echocardiogram parameters, and detailed migraine characteristics separately predict vascular events.

title: Development and Internal Validation of an Integrated Clinical, Laboratory, and Ultrasound Model for 30-Day Venous Thromboembolic Deterioration After Acute Lower-Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis.
abstract: BackgroundShort-term prognostic tools for venous thromboembolic (VTE) deterioration after acute lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) are limited. We aimed to develop and internally validate a model integrating clinical, laboratory, and duplex ultrasound characteristics.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort included 785 adults with ultrasound-confirmed acute lower-extremity DVT from January 2018 to December 2025. The primary outcome was clinically detected and objectively confirmed ipsilateral DVT progression or new-onset symptomatic pulmonary embolism (PE) within 30 days. Three nested ridge-penalized logistic models included clinical predictors (Model 1), clinical plus laboratory predictors (Model 2), and clinical, laboratory, and ultrasound predictors (Model 3). Missing data were multiply imputed, and the complete modeling procedure was internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Discrimination, calibration, Brier score, incremental performance, and decision-curve net benefit were assessed.ResultsThe primary outcome occurred in 102 patients (13.0%): 82 had DVT progression and 27 symptomatic PE, with seven having both. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.702, 0.766, and 0.808 (95% CI, 0.769-0.847) for Models 1-3, respectively. For Model 3, the optimism-corrected calibration slope was 0.94 and Brier score 0.087. Optimism-corrected ΔAUCs were 0.064 and 0.042, with corresponding ΔBrier scores of -0.009 and -0.008. Model 3 showed the highest optimism-corrected net benefit across thresholds of approximately 8%-25%. Observed outcome proportions across risk tertiles were 3.1%, 9.6%, and 26.3%.ConclusionsModel 3 provided internally validated prediction of clinically detected VTE deterioration under local treatment and imaging practices. External validation and prospective clinical-impact assessment are required before routine use.

We aimed to develop and internally validate a model integrating clinical, laboratory, and duplex ultrasound characteristics.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort included 785 adults with ultrasound-confirmed acute lower-extremity DVT from January 2018 to December 2025. The primary outcome was clinically detected and objectively confirmed ipsilateral DVT progression or new-onset symptomatic pulmonary embolism (PE) within 30 days.

title: A Two-Step Risk Stratification Model for Venous Thromboembolism Combining Caprini Score and D-Dimer in Trauma Patients Undergoing Surgery.
abstract: ObjectiveTo determine whether adding D-dimer to Caprini score-based risk assessment can further refine venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk stratification in trauma patients, particularly among those already classified as high-risk.MethodsA retrospective cohort of 206 trauma surgical patients who underwent surgical intervention was analyzed. Caprini scores and baseline plasma D-dimer levels were assessed against VTE occurrence using ROC curves. The two-step strategy consisted of initial Caprini-based stratification, followed by secondary D-dimer re-stratification using a study-derived exploratory threshold derived from the Youden index within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (Caprini score ≥9) in the same cohort. This threshold was not externally validated. All patients received mechanical VTE prophylaxis, while patients with Caprini scores ≥9 received prophylactic-dose low-molecular-weight heparin. Bilateral lower-extremity Doppler ultrasound was performed within 24 hours of admission, with subsequent surveillance according to predefined risk criteria.ResultsOverall composite VTE incidence was 31.1%. The Caprini score showed an AUC of 0.640 for VTE discrimination. D-dimer showed the highest discrimination in the full cohort (AUC = 0.669), which decreased to 0.614 within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (≥9 points, n = 118). Applying a study-derived exploratory D-dimer threshold of ≥5.5 mg/L identified a subgroup with a higher observed VTE incidence (44.8% vs. 16.1%; RR = 2.78, 95% CI: 1.21-6.37, P = 0.005). However, after adjustment for age, sex, and ISS, the association was attenuated and did not remain statistically significant (adjusted OR = 2.418, 95% CI: 0.660-8.864, P = 0.183).ConclusionsRelying solely on clinical risk scoring provides limited VTE discrimination in trauma patients. A sequential two-step strategy identified a subgroup with a higher observed VTE incidence within the Caprini high-risk category, although an independent association between the D-dimer threshold and VTE was not demonstrated after adjustment. This approach warrants prospective validation in larger cohorts.

Caprini scores and baseline plasma D-dimer levels were assessed against VTE occurrence using ROC curves. The two-step strategy consisted of initial Caprini-based stratification, followed by secondary D-dimer re-stratification using a study-derived exploratory threshold derived from the Youden index within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (Caprini score ≥9) in the same cohort.

title: The use of side-firing intravascular ultrasound for TIPS procedures: a case series.
abstract: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation is a well-established technique for managing complications of portal hypertension. Standard portal vein puncture during transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation is fluoroscopy-guided and relies on anatomical landmarks. However, the absence of direct visualization of the portal vein can lead to complications, including misdirected punctures or damage to adjacent structures. In this context, intracardiac echocardiography has emerged as a promising tool to guide portal vein puncture during transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation, as it provides good tissue penetration and high-resolution ultrasound imaging. We present our experience using intracardiac echocardiography as a guidance method for portal vein puncture during transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation. We report on 3 cases of patients undergoing transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt with an intracardiac echocardiography catheter. The fluoroscopy time was recorded in two cases (38 and 47 minutes), and the contrast volume ranged from 150 to 215ml (mean 173 ml). We describe the challenges encountered and highlight the role of intracardiac echocardiography as a valuable adjunct to conventional techniques.

title: Postpartum Retroperitoneal Haematoma Associated With Suspected Ovarian Artery Pathology Following Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery: A Case Report.
abstract: Postpartum retroperitoneal haemorrhage is rare and can be challenging to recognise because substantial blood loss may remain concealed. A 22-year-old multiparous woman presented three days after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery with syncope, severe right-sided abdominal and back pain, vomiting, and haemodynamic instability. Pelvic ultrasonography did not adequately explain the severity of her clinical presentation. Computed tomography revealed a large right-sided retroperitoneal haematoma associated with suspected ovarian artery pathology. She underwent successful endovascular coil embolization and received a blood transfusion. Her recovery was complicated by fever and a marked inflammatory response, necessitating prolonged antimicrobial treatment and close outpatient follow-up. This case highlights the importance of considering concealed extrauterine haemorrhage when postpartum symptoms are disproportionate to visible blood loss or initial ultrasonographic findings.

Pelvic ultrasonography did not adequately explain the severity of her clinical presentation.

title: Heat-Based Therapies in Hypertension Management: A Systematic Review of Physiological Mechanisms.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for several cardiovascular diseases, leading to the need for investigations of user-friendly and less costly nonpharmacological interventions, including passive heat therapies. This study synthesized information on heat-based therapies used in prehypertension and hypertension management, as well as their clinical efficacy, physiological mechanisms, and translational potential.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed 13 eligible human studies published between 2000 and 2025 per the PRISMA 2020 checklist, assessed randomized studies with RoB 2 and nonrandomized studies with ROBINS-I, and used SWiM-guided narrative synthesis because interventions, populations, comparators, and outcomes were heterogeneous. Certainty was assessed using GRADE. The review protocol was not preregistered.

RESULTS: Acute blood-pressure reductions and changes in vascular or autonomic markers were reported in some populations, but sustained comparative effects in hypertension remain uncertain. In hypertensive participants, both hot and thermoneutral immersion were associated with reductions in 24-h blood pressure (BP), limiting heat-specific attribution. A single pooled effect estimate and corresponding 95% confidence interval were not calculated. The benefits were linked to lower sympathetic activity, more nitric oxide availability, lower endothelin-1 levels, and less oxidative stress. Outcome-specific GRADE certainty was very low for SBP and DBP and the assessed mechanistic domains.

CONCLUSION: Passive heat exposure can produce short-term reductions in BP and changes in vascular function, but sustained antihypertensive efficacy, particularly when evaluated with 24-h ambulatory BP in patients with established hypertension, remains uncertain. Mechanistic findings from heart-failure and peripheral artery disease (PAD) cohorts are indirect evidence for uncomplicated hypertension. Passive heat should not replace established antihypertensive treatment. Safety evidence is limited to selected, often supervised populations, and larger trials with ambulatory BP and systematic adverse-event assessment are needed.

This study synthesized information on heat-based therapies used in prehypertension and hypertension management, as well as their clinical efficacy, physiological mechanisms, and translational potential. METHODS: We systematically reviewed 13 eligible human studies published between 2000 and 2025 per the PRISMA 2020 checklist, assessed randomized studies with RoB 2 and nonrandomized studies with ROBINS-I, and used SWiM-guided narrative synthesis because interventions, populations, comparators, and outcomes were heterogeneous.

title: Association of Betel Quid Chewing with Anthropometric Parameters and Lipid Profile in Type-2 Diabetes Mellitus Patients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Betel quid chewing is a rising concern, linked to various diseases. Several studies show an increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) among chewers. With the increasing prevalence of diabetes and metabolic disorders, the association between betel nut use and cardiovascular diseases worsens morbidity and mortality, establishing a significant socioeconomic burden. Inflammation, insulin resistance, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) metabolism may underlie the association between betel nut use and atherosclerotic adverse outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of betel quid chewing on anthropometric parameters and lipid profiles in T2DM patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: T2DM patients were screened and recruited from an endocrinology outpatient department. Patients were divided into two groups: one group with a history of betel quid chewing and another group without it. Patients with a history of ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, hypertension, chronic inflammatory diseases, or other forms of tobacco use were excluded. Comparison of anthropometric parameters and lipid profiles was performed among the two groups.

RESULTS: Significant differences were observed in hip circumference (P = 0.002), waist-to-hip ratio (P = 0.0001), and high-density lipoprotein (P = 0.0002) between the two groups of patients.

CONCLUSION: Inflammation, insulin resistance, and LDL-C metabolism may contribute to the link between betel nut usage and T2DM. Quitting the habit of chewing may have the potential to reduce the atherosclerotic vascular adversities.

title: Clinico-epidemiological Insights of Patients with Varicose Veins from Tertiary Care Teaching Hospitals - A Cross-sectional Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Varicose veins are a prevalent venous disorder causing functional limitations and cosmetic concerns. Despite its global burden, limited epidemiological data exist for the Indian population. There is a notable gap in the demographics regarding the prevalence of varicose veins among Indian populations.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study is to assess the clinico-epidemiological profile, diagnostic modalities, treatment patterns, and outcomes among patients with varicose veins admitted to tertiary care hospitals.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective, cross-sectional study was conducted in July 2024 using hospital records from 2019 to 2024 of tertiary care teaching hospitals affiliated to a medical college from Coastal South India. Data were extracted on demographics, clinical features, diagnostics, treatment, and outcomes.

RESULTS: Of the 42 patients included, 64.3% were male and most were aged 31-50 years. Hypertension (75%), diabetes (60%), and obesity (50%) were common comorbidities. Clinical features included lower limb swelling (53.7%), engorged veins (51.2%), and leg pain (48.8%). Doppler ultrasound was the primary diagnostic tool (97.1%). All patients received pharmacological treatment; 40.5% underwent nonpharmacological therapy, and 38.1% received surgical intervention. Posttreatment complications occurred in 26.8% of patients.

CONCLUSION: Varicose veins predominantly affected middle-aged males in this study, with hypertension and diabetes as common comorbidities. Doppler ultrasound remains the diagnostic standard. While conservative and surgical treatments were employed, the high rate of complications underscores the need for early diagnosis, preventive strategies, and increased awareness among high-risk occupational groups.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Varicose veins are a prevalent venous disorder causing functional limitations and cosmetic concerns. Despite its global burden, limited epidemiological data exist for the Indian population. There is a notable gap in the demographics regarding the prevalence of varicose veins among Indian populations.

title: Anterior mitral leaflet modification to prevent left ventricular outflow tract obstruction during transcatheter mitral valve replacement: the PROTECT-LVOT registry.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction remains the major limitation of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Anterior mitral leaflet (AML) modification has emerged as a key preventive strategy, yet real-world data remain limited and residual risk is still unknown.

AIMS: We sought to evaluate the outcomes of TMVR with concomitant AML modification across valve-in-mitral annular calcification (ViMAC), valve-in-ring (ViR), and valve-in-valve (ViV) substrates.

METHODS: We established a multicentre retrospective registry of consecutive patients undergoing TMVR with AML modification between 2017 and 2025. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, stroke/transient ischaemic attack, and major bleeding.

RESULTS: A total of 55 patients were included (67% females). The median age was 78 years (interquartile range [IQR] 73-81); the median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality was 6.7% (IQR 4.8-9.5). AML modification was performed in 65.5% of cases with the Laceration of the Anterior Mitral leaflet to Prevent Outflow ObstructioN technique and in 34.5% with the Balloon-Assisted Translocation of the Mitral Anterior Leaflet technique. AML modification was successful in 96.4% of cases. Despite successful AML modification, haemodynamically significant LVOT obstruction occurred in 12.7% of cases. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint occurred in 20.0% of patients, driven by cardiovascular death in 14.5% of patients. Overall in-hospital mortality was 16.4%. The ViMAC substrate was associated with the numerically highest LVOT obstruction rate (ViMAC 20.7%, ViR 0.0%, ViV 8.3%, odds ratio [OR] 4.72, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.89-47.86; p=0.070). The aortomitral angle showed a borderline association with LVOT obstruction (OR 1.22 per degree, 95% CI: 0.99-1.48; p=0.059).

CONCLUSIONS: AML modification enables TMVR in high-risk anatomies with high feasibility but does not eliminate LVOT obstruction. ViMAC represents the most challenging substrate.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction remains the major limitation of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Anterior mitral leaflet (AML) modification has emerged as a key preventive strategy, yet real-world data remain limited and residual risk is still unknown. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the outcomes of TMVR with concomitant AML modification across valve-in-mitral annular calcification (ViMAC), valve-in-ring (ViR), and valve-in-valve (ViV) substrates.

title: Bioprosthetic valve performance of transcatheter aortic valves.
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation is used increasingly in younger patients with longer life expectancy, necessitating long-term effectiveness. Randomised clinical trials have demonstrated comparable or superior haemodynamic performance of transcatheter heart valves (THVs) to surgical aortic valve replacement over midterm follow-up. Within a lifetime management framework, haemodynamic performance and durability of THVs are central considerations in patients undergoing aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis. This review provides an overview of THV design and function along with contemporary clinical evidence, with a focus on current haemodynamic assessment considerations, challenges in cross-platform interpretation of valve performance, and limitations of randomised comparative evidence, as well as future directions in the evaluation of THV performance.

title: Postpartum Ovarian Vein Thrombosis Following an Intrauterine Death Diagnosed at 31+2 Weeks.
abstract: Ovarian vein thrombosis (OVT) is an uncommon cause of postpartum abdominal pain that may be difficult to recognise when systemic features are minimal. We report the case of a 26-year-old primiparous woman who presented with severe central abdominal pain 10 days after delivery of a stillborn infant at 31+5 weeks' gestation, nine days following discharge. She was haemodynamically stable with a mild tachycardia and minimally elevated inflammatory markers. Pelvic ultrasound did not identify a clear cause for her symptoms. Subsequent contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrated a short-segment filling defect in keeping with left OVT. Therapeutic enoxaparin was commenced and subsequently changed to apixaban following haematology advice, with a planned three-month course of anticoagulation. Her pain resolved during the two-day admission, with no inpatient adverse events. Longer-term outcomes were unavailable. This case highlights the importance of considering OVT in patients with severe unexplained postpartum abdominal pain, including after stillbirth and during reported adherence to thromboprophylaxis, even when fever and substantial inflammatory abnormalities are absent.

We report the case of a 26-year-old primiparous woman who presented with severe central abdominal pain 10 days after delivery of a stillborn infant at 31+5 weeks' gestation, nine days following discharge. She was haemodynamically stable with a mild tachycardia and minimally elevated inflammatory markers.

title: Underdiagnosis, Psychosocial Burden, and Treatment Expectations in Lipedema: A Cross-Sectional Observational Study in an Italian Clinical Population.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipedema is a chronic adipose tissue disorder predominantly affecting women, characterized by symmetrical, painful accumulation of fatty tissue in the lower limbs and often the arms. It is considered widely underdiagnosed, and Italian data remain scarce. This study describes the clinical, demographic, psychological, and therapeutic characteristics of 100 patients referred to a specialist center, focusing on the proportion of patients without a previous diagnosis, the pathways through which they learned about the condition, and self-reported psychosocial difficulties.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this cross-sectional observational study, a structured, author-developed questionnaire (22 items, 19 of which collected study data) was administered to 100 consecutive female patients (mean age 35.2 ± 10.3 years; range 18-58) at the Salus Mea outpatient clinic (Milan, Italy) between September 2023 and January 2026. Overall, 85% of patients had no previous diagnosis, and 63% had discovered the condition online. Spontaneous bruising was reported by 91% of patients and pain on palpation by 76%. Avoidance of exposing the legs or arms in public was reported by 77.8%, and 59.6% reported frequent sadness, melancholy, or anger. Willingness to undergo specific treatment was declared by 89% of patients; 65% were tentatively willing to undergo surgery.

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center specialist population, most patients had not been diagnosed before referral, self-reported emotional and relational difficulties were frequent, and interest in treatment was substantial. These findings warrant confirmation in multicenter studies using validated instruments.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Lipedema is a chronic adipose tissue disorder predominantly affecting women, characterized by symmetrical, painful accumulation of fatty tissue in the lower limbs and often the arms. It is considered widely underdiagnosed, and Italian data remain scarce. This study describes the clinical, demographic, psychological, and therapeutic characteristics of 100 patients referred to a specialist center, focusing on the proportion of patients without a previous diagnosis, the pathways through which they learned about the condition, and self-reported psychosocial difficulties.

title: Risk factors for antepartum venous thromboembolism in pregnant people with sickle cell disease.
abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a thrombophilia exacerbated by pregnancy. However, there is not strong evidence for thromboprophylaxis, perhaps because most data addressing pregnancy-related thrombosis in SCD is limited by derivation from administrative datasets. We studied venous thromboembolism (VTE) in a retrospective cohort of pregnant people with SCD who delivered singleton pregnancies at two academic centres between 1990 and 2021. Among 289 pregnancies to 197 SCD subjects, 6% had VTE. We compared characteristics of the first study pregnancy in which a VTE occurred (cases) to the first study pregnancy in subjects without pregnancy-related VTE (controls). Preconception complications associated with VTE were history of VTE (cases: 33% [n = 5/15] vs. controls: 4% [n = 7/182], p < 0.001), acute chest syndrome (ACS) (80% [n = 12/15] vs. 37% [n = 68/182], p = 0.001) and acute care for vaso-occlusive crisis (VOC) in the year before pregnancy (80% [n = 12/15] vs. 43% [n = 70/182], p = 0.006). Prenatal complications associated with VTE were ACS (47% [n = 7/15] vs. 10% [n = 19/182], p < 0.001) and VOC (93% [n = 14/15] vs. 65% [n = 119/182], p = 0.026). Fetal outcomes associated with VTE included gestational age at delivery (median [IQR] 37.0 [34.0-38.1] weeks vs. 38.3 [36.9-39.3], p = 0.004). Studies are needed to establish interventions that attenuate VTE risk and define prophylactic anti-coagulation parameters for this high-risk population.

However, there is not strong evidence for thromboprophylaxis, perhaps because most data addressing pregnancy-related thrombosis in SCD is limited by derivation from administrative datasets. We studied venous thromboembolism (VTE) in a retrospective cohort of pregnant people with SCD who delivered singleton pregnancies at two academic centres between 1990 and 2021.

title: Repurposing drugs for aortic aneurysm: unlocking new therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease for which no pharmacological therapy has been proven to effectively limit disease progression. Drug repurposing (DR), which leverages existing drugs with established safety profiles, offers a promising and cost-effective strategy to accelerate therapeutic development for AA. In this review, we summarize recent advances in DR research for AA, highlighting the emerging framework that integrates computational prediction with experimental and clinical validation. We discuss key repurposed drug candidates, evaluate the current state of translational evidence, and examine the challenges that have hindered clinical success despite encouraging preclinical findings. Finally, we outline opportunities to enhance target identification, patient stratification, and clinical trial design. By bridging mechanistic discovery and translational application, DR may provide a practical pathway toward effective medical therapies for aneurysmal disease.

title: Venous thromboembolism in inflammatory bowel disease: a phase-specific framework for risk stratification and anticoagulant management.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, is a chronic inflammatory disorder associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), particularly during active disease, hospitalization or after surgery. The risk of VTE is approximately two to three times higher in patients with IBD than in the general population. The underlying mechanisms are multifactorial and include systemic inflammation, platelet activation, endothelial dysfunction, and alterations in the intestinal microbiota. Diagnosis requires a high index of clinical suspicion. D-dimer may help exclude VTE in patients with low pretest probability but is frequently elevated during active inflammation and therefore lacks specificity. Pharmacological thromboprophylaxis, preferably with low-molecular-weight heparin, is recommended for hospitalized patients with IBD, whereas the choice and duration of therapeutic anticoagulation should be individualized according to thrombotic and bleeding risk. This review summarizes current evidence on the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, prevention and management of VTE in IBD, with particular focus on recent population-based incidence data, phase-dependent thrombotic risk post-discharge prophylaxis and individualized anticoagulant selection.

title: Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative Contemporary Benchmarks: Thoracic Endovascular Aortic Repair.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe contemporary outcomes as well as temporal trends of in-hospital mortality and complication rates for patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) across indications and levels of urgency, establishing a benchmark for future analytic efforts.

METHODS: The VQI TEVAR and complex EVAR registry was queried for procedures performed between January 2014-December 2024. Primary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and major complications. Analyses were stratified by indication to include descending thoracic aortic aneurysms (DTAA), dissections, and trauma. Aneurysms involving the aortic arch (i.e. landing zone < 2) or extending to the visceral segment and distally (i.e. landing zone >5) were excluded. Linear regression and the Cochran Armitage test for trend were used to analyze yearly mortality and complication rates over time. Mortality and complication end-points were further analyzed using logistic regression with and without risk-adjustment.

RESULTS: Over the ten-year study period, 4,632 TEVARs were performed for DTAA, 6,701 for dissection, and 2,321 for trauma. For patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA, in-hospital mortality declined significantly for both elective (2014, 3.9% versus 2024, 1.0%, -0.26 percentage points per year, p=0.01) and nonelective cases (2014, 16.7% versus 2024, 8.7%, -0.63 percentage points per year, p=0.04). There was also a decline in in-hospital mortality among elective dissection patients (2014, 3.7% versus 2024, 0.5%, -0.17 percentage points per year, p=0.03). Elective TEVAR overall is associated with a mortality rate of less than two percent per year. The in-hospital complication trends declined significantly for patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA - elective patients experienced a decline in complication rates by -1.13 percentage points per year (2014, 24.8% versus 2024, 11.5% p<0.001) and non-elective patients experienced a decline in complication rates by -2.0 percentage points per year (2014, 40.5% versus 2024, 25.2%, p<0.001). Dissection patients undergoing elective repair had a decrease of -0.8 percentage points per year (2014, 16.9% versus 2024, 9.2%, p<0.001). Nonelective dissections repairs had a complication rate of 36.4% in 2014 vs 34.1% in 2024, p=0.874). Trauma patients tended toward higher complication rates over time, with a rate of 21.6% in 2014 and 32.2% in 2024, p=0.06) Trauma patients experienced an overall increase in in-hospital mortality of +0.38 percentage points per year (2014, 9.8% versus 2024, 9.4%, p=0.01).

CONCLUSION: Temporal trends within the VQI demonstrate improvements in mortality and complication rates for patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA and elective dissection repair, with contemporary yearly mortality rates of less than two percent. Patients undergoing non-elective dissection repair and those with traumatic indications represent challenging and complex pathologies requiring further research to identify opportunities to improve outcomes.

title: Final 5-year results of the Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis Feasibility Trials for Treatment of Aortic Arch Aneurysms.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report final 5-year outcomes from prospective multicenter feasibility studies of the GORE® TAG® Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis (TBE) for aneurysms involving the proximal descending thoracic aorta and aortic arch (zones 0-2).

METHODS: Forty consecutive patients (23 male; mean age, 74±10 years) were enrolled at six sites in prospective, nonrandomized feasibility trials (2014-2016). Patients underwent TEVAR with proximal TBE in zone 0/1 (n=9; NCT02264977) or zone 2 (n=31; NCT02021812). A clinical events committee adjudicated aneurysm-related and all-cause mortality, major adverse events, and cerebrovascular events. Core laboratory analysis assessed endoleaks (types I-IV), aneurysm sac enlargement, device migration, and side branch patency. Five-year cumulative risk rates (2006 days) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

RESULTS: The median follow-up time among survivors was 60.2 months (range, 25.8 to 66.0), with 17 patients completing the required 5-year clinical and imaging follow-up across both studies. Eleven late deaths occurred; KM-estimated cumulative risk of 5-year all-cause mortality was 29% (95% CI: 17%-46%). One zone 2 death was adjudicated as aortic-related (2.5%; 95% CI: 0.4%-16%) due to ascending aortic rupture, with no ruptures occurring within treated aortic segments. Reintervention risk through 5 years was low (KM-estimated cumulative risk, 5.1%; 95% CI: 1.3%-19%), with two events, both in the zone 2 cohort. Five patients experienced stroke events through 5 years, corresponding to a KM cumulative risk of 19.0% ( 95% CI: 7.2%-43%), two in zone 2 and three in zone 0/1. Two patients had target vessel instability (5.0%, 95% CI: 0.6%-16.9%). Two side-branch patency events occurred in zone 2: one complete side-branch occlusion in the LSA associated with transient mild arm claudication and one asymptomatic partial occlusion, primary patency through 5-year follow-up was 94.8% (37/39 evaluable patients). Core laboratory identified endoleaks in 12 patients (30.8%; 95% CI: 15%-45%). Three patients (7.7%) had a type I or III endoleak by 5 years, all in the zone 2 arm; these included type IA in one patient (2.6%) and type III in two patients (5.1%). Additionally indeterminate (n=8, 20.5%) and type II (n=6, 15.4%) endoleaks were observed. Cumulative risk rate of aneurysm sac enlargement through 5-years was 15.0% for all patients (95% CI: 5.6%-30.3%), with events occurring in three zone 2 patients and one zone 0/1 patient.

CONCLUSIONS: At 5 years, the early feasibility studies demonstrated excellent side branch patency, a low incidence of type IA endoleak, low aortic-related mortality, and no rupture within the treated aortic segments. Larger studies are needed to better define zone-specific cerebrovascular risk and long-term durability.

title: The Effects of Non-Psoriatic Dermatitis on Total Hip Arthroplasty Outcomes: A Propensity-Matched Analysis with Longitudinal Follow-Up.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: While psoriasis has been associated with increased complications following total hip arthroplasty (THA), the effects of non-psoriatic dermatitis (NPD) on THA outcomes remain unclear. Therefore, this study evaluated the association between NPD and postoperative outcomes following primary THA with additional stratification by dermatitis-related medication use.

METHODS: In a large national database, patients aged ≥ 18 years undergoing primary THA anytime between 2003 and 2020 were identified. Patients who had NPD were compared with a control cohort of patients who did not have NPD. Additional pairwise comparisons evaluated the effect of dermatitis-related medication use. After multiple demographics and comorbidities were propensity-matched using a 1:1 ratio, postoperative medical outcomes and surgical complications were examined with follow-up at 90 days, one year, and two years.

RESULTS: At 90 days, NPD was associated with a higher rate of emergency department admission and a lower rate of periprosthetic dislocation or instability (P ≤ 0.048). There were no other significant associations observed at one or two years. Compared to patients who do not have NPD, patients who have NPD with concurrent medication use had higher rates of inpatient readmission, emergency department admission, deep vein thrombosis, falls, and periprosthetic fracture at 90 days (P ≤ 0.027), and periprosthetic fracture remained elevated at one and two years (P ≤ 0.012). Patients who have NPD without medication use showed no significant differences for all measured outcomes across every timepoint.

CONCLUSION: Although some 90-day outcomes were significant, NPD was not independently associated with one- and two-year complications following THA. Patients receiving medications for NPD treatment may represent a high-risk subgroup with increased healthcare utilization, thromboembolic events, falls, and periprosthetic fracture. Among THA candidates who have NPD, the effects of pharmaceutical management may be considered, especially for thromboembolic risk, fall prevention, and bone health optimization.

Therefore, this study evaluated the association between NPD and postoperative outcomes following primary THA with additional stratification by dermatitis-related medication use. METHODS: In a large national database, patients aged ≥ 18 years undergoing primary THA anytime between 2003 and 2020 were identified.

title: Can Outpatient Total Hip Arthroplasty Be Done at a Complex, Academic, Quaternary Referral Center?
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary outpatient (same-day discharge) total hip arthroplasty (THA) has gained popularity, but results from academic medical centers remain limited. Same-day discharge shifts perioperative responsibilities to the surgeon. In contrast, surgeon reimbursements continue to decline. We retrospectively evaluated 90-day rates of emergency room (ER) visits, reoperations, revisions, and postoperative touches associated with outpatient THAs at our complex, academic, quaternary referral center.

METHODS: At our institution, 1,970 outpatient primary THAs were performed between 2019 and 2024 in 1,813 unique patients. The mean age was 61 years, 56% were men, the mean body mass index (BMI) was 30, the mean American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score was 2.2, and the mean Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was 1.2 (range, 1 to 10). Medical comorbidities, ER visits, reoperations, revisions, and postoperative touches within 90 days after THA were collected. Univariate logistic regression analyses were completed.

RESULTS: Rates of ER visits, reoperations, and revisions within 90 days of surgery were 8.6, 1.5, and 0.9%, respectively. Hips averaged nine postoperative touches, and total touches increased from 131 in 2019 to greater than 4,800 in 2024. The most common first-time ER visit reason was a medical issue unrelated to surgery (39%), followed by dislocation (14%) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) evaluation (12%; actual VTE incidence 0.3%). The most common reason for reoperation and revision was acute periprosthetic joint infection (PJI; incidence 0.7%). Increasing BMI was associated with risk of reoperations (odds ratio [OR] 1.1; P = 0.02), revisions (OR 1.1; P = 0.03), and PJI (OR 1.1; P = 0.03), but not with ER visits or dislocations. Increasing CCI was associated with risk of first-time ER visits (OR 1.2; P < 0.001) and dislocations (OR 1.3; P = 0.02). Increasing ASA score was associated with risk of ER visits (OR 1.8; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Outpatient THA patients had a high rate of ER visits within 90 days postoperatively, with almost 40% unattributable to surgery. Increasing BMI was associated with increased reoperation, revision, and PJI risk, while increasing CCI and ASA score increased ER visit risk, and increasing CCI increased dislocation risk. Hips averaged nine postoperative touches. As outpatient THA grows, surgeon compensation should be reevaluated given the heightened administrative burden.

Same-day discharge shifts perioperative responsibilities to the surgeon. In contrast, surgeon reimbursements continue to decline.

title: Msp1, Cdc48, and Hsp104 coordinate quality control of import-impaired mitochondrial β-barrel proteins.
abstract: Mitochondrial β-barrel proteins fulfill essential functions for cell viability, including transport of proteins, ions, and metabolites, across the outer membrane. The translocase of the outer membrane (TOM complex) and the sorting and assembly machinery (SAM complex) transport these proteins into the outer membrane. Although β-barrel proteins are essential for cell viability, the quality control mechanisms that monitor their import into the outer membrane remain unknown. We uncovered that Msp1 and Ubx2-recruited Cdc48 cooperate to remove translocation-impaired β-barrel proteins from mitochondria. Non-imported β-barrel proteins are deposited in cytosolic protein storages, termed MitoStores, to minimize accumulation of aberrant proteins in the cell. The cytosolic AAA-ATPase Hsp104 disaggregates these proteins to facilitate their proteasomal degradation. Altogether, mitochondrial and cytosolic factors cooperate to degrade translocation-arrested mitochondrial β-barrel proteins.

title: Impact of COVID-19 surgical delays on chronic venous disease: a multicenter observational study in France.
abstract: IntroductionCOVID-19 lockdowns led to widespread postponement of elective procedures, including endovenous interventions for chronic venous disease (CVD). This study aimed to evaluate the clinical impact of delayed thermal ablation in a real-world French multicenter cohort.MethodsThis prospective, multicenter observational study included 203 adults with documented great or small saphenous vein insufficiency or recurrent varicose veins whose endovenous procedures were postponed during the 2020-2021 lockdowns. Clinical severity was assessed using the Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS) and CEAP classification at the postponement assessment and at the rescheduling assessment. The primary analysis was performed on patients with a VCSS available at both time points. Paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used to assess within-patient change over time.ResultsAmong 203 enrolled patients, 86 (42.4%) had a VCSS available at both time points and were included in the primary analysis. The median delay between the postponement and rescheduling assessments was 80 days (IQR 69-101). Mean VCSS remained unchanged (5.4±3.0 vs 5.4±2.8; mean difference 0.0, 95% CI -0.4 to 0.4). CEAP classification was stable in 89.5% of patients, with no significant overall shift (p = 0.246). Adverse events occurred in 3.5% of cases, mainly superficial vein thrombosis. Physicians reported a negative impact of the delay in 60% of assessments, and a physician-perceived potential loss of therapeutic opportunity in 7.5% of the full cohort (n = 199) and 20.9% of the paired cohort at rescheduling (n = 86).ConclusionIn this real-world cohort, delayed endovenous treatment for CVD was not associated with clinically evident short-term deterioration in this sample. However, the high rate of missing paired data, the resulting risk of selection bias, and limited statistical power mean that a clinically relevant effect cannot be excluded. These findings suggest relative clinical stability in mild-to-moderate CVD during short-term delays, but further adequately powered studies are required.

title: Middle meningeal artery embolization in pediatric chronic subdural hematoma: a case-based review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) is common in the elderly but rare in the pediatric population, where it is typically associated with trauma, coagulation disorders, cerebrospinal fluid shunting, metabolic diseases, or systemic conditions. Standard management includes burr-hole drainage or, in selected cases, craniotomy. More recently, middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) has emerged as an adjunct or alternative treatment for recurrent or refractory cSDH in adults, reflecting its vascular pathophysiology; however, its use in children remains limited to isolated reports and small series.

CASE DESCRIPTION: We report a case-based review of a medically complex child affected by mucopolysaccharidosis type IIIb and an underlying coagulation disorder, who developed persistent bilateral subdural collections. Following incomplete resolution after conventional management, the patient underwent adjunctive bilateral MMAE. The procedure was well tolerated and resulted in resolution of the collections, absence of complications, and sustained neurological improvement. A focused review of the literature was performed to contextualize the role of MMAE in pediatric cSDH.

CONCLUSION: MMAE appears to be a feasible and potentially effective minimally invasive option in selected high-risk pediatric patients with cSDH. Although current evidence remains limited, this case supports its role as an adjunctive strategy, particularly in medically complex children or in cases refractory to standard surgical treatment.

More recently, middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) has emerged as an adjunct or alternative treatment for recurrent or refractory cSDH in adults, reflecting its vascular pathophysiology; however, its use in children remains limited to isolated reports and small series.

title: Exploring clinical variables and interventions to optimize utilization of multiphase CT for gastrointestinal bleeding: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Utilization of multiphase CT for gastrointestinal bleeding (CT-GIB) has experienced widespread growth in recent years, yet meaningful clinical outcomes associated with increased utilization remain uncertain. This study examines the overall positivity rate for CT-GIB, evaluates variables associated with a positive scan, and assesses the relationship between a positive CT-GIB and subsequent clinical interventions.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: IRB approved retrospective analysis of 1,040 consecutive patients undergoing CT-GIB (Jan. 2019-Mar. 2025). Demographic (age, gender), hemodynamic (heart rate, blood pressure, shock index), laboratory (hemoglobin, platelets, INR, PT/P TT, albumin, BUN, creatinine) and clinical (anticoagulant use, hypertension, malignancy, cirrhosis) parameters were extracted from the electronic medical record within the 48-h periprocedural window. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify variables independently associated with three outcomes: a positive multiphase CT-GIB scan, endovascular intervention within 48 h, and endoscopic intervention within 48 h.

RESULTS: Imaging volume increased 1,044% over the 6.25-year period. Active bleeding was detected in 143/1,040 (13.8%) of CT-GIB. Fourteen patients died within 48 h and were excluded from intervention analysis. Of the remaining positive cohort, 31/141 (22.0%), reflecting the cohort of 141 patients who survived the initial 48-h periprocedural window (i.e., after exclusion of 2 CTGIB+ patients who died within 48 h), underwent acute interventions within 48 h. Angiography was performed alone in 21/141 (14.9%), endoscopic intervention alone in 8/141 (5.7%), and both interventions were performed in 2/141 (1.4%). Variables independently associated with a positive multiphase CT-GIB: age > 65 years (OR = 2.15, 95% CI 1.41-3.30), male sex (OR = 1.54, 95% CI 1.06-2.22), and a nadir systolic BP < 105 mmHg (OR = 3.12, 95% CI 1.47-6.63). A positive multiphase CT-GIB was strongly associated with endovascular intervention (OR = 42.83, 95% CI 14.56-126.01; p < 0.001), but not with endoscopic intervention (OR = 1.53, 95% CI 0.73-3.23; p = 0.261).

CONCLUSION: Multiphase CT-GIB volumes increased exponentially while positive yields remained low. This study demonstrates associations between CT-GIB findings and subsequent treatment pathways and lays the foundation for prospective studies aimed at determining whether interventional pathway-specific imaging selection can be applied without compromising clinical safety.

title: Association between low-dose glucocorticoid administration during anesthesia induction and neurological improvement in patients with spinal dural arteriovenous fistula: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-dose glucocorticoid treatment before the diagnosis of spinal dural arteriovenous fistula (SDAVF) has been associated with acute neurological worsening, but the association of a single, comparatively low dose administered during anesthesia induction with long-term neurological recovery remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between glucocorticoid administration during anesthesia induction and neurological improvement after definitive treatment.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included patients with angiographically confirmed SDAVF treated between March 2013 and July 2021. Neurological improvement was defined as a decrease of at least 1 point in the modified Aminoff-Logue Scale score from pretreatment to the last follow-up. Patients were matched 1:1 without replacement and exactly by treatment modality using propensity scores based on age, sex, disease duration, and pretreatment neurological function. Between-group differences were evaluated using the paired risk difference, exact McNemar test, and modified Poisson regression. Glucocorticoid type and equivalent dexamethasone dose (EDD) were also evaluated among glucocorticoid-treated patients.

RESULTS: The cohort included 428 patients, of whom 172 received glucocorticoids and 256 did not. Propensity-score matching retained 167 pairs. Neurological improvement occurred in 118 of 167 patients (70.7%) in the glucocorticoid group and 119 of 167 patients (71.3%) in the nonglucocorticoid group. The paired risk difference was - 0.6 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], - 10.4 to 9.2; exact McNemar P = 1.000). Glucocorticoid administration was not associated with neurological improvement in the adjusted modified Poisson model (risk ratio [RR], 0.996; 95% CI, 0.871-1.138; P = 0.947), and sensitivity analyses yielded consistent findings. Among matched glucocorticoid-treated patients, neither glucocorticoid type (dexamethasone vs. methylprednisolone: adjusted RR, 0.979; 95% CI, 0.666-1.441; P = 0.916) nor EDD (per 5-mg increase: adjusted RR, 1.022; 95% CI, 0.931-1.121; P = 0.646) was associated with neurological improvement.

CONCLUSION: A single, comparatively low glucocorticoid dose administered during anesthesia induction was not associated with neurological improvement at the last follow-up after definitive treatment of SDAVF. No clear associations were identified for glucocorticoid type or EDD.

We evaluated the association between glucocorticoid administration during anesthesia induction and neurological improvement after definitive treatment. METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included patients with angiographically confirmed SDAVF treated between March 2013 and July 2021.

title: Initial Experience with the 6-10 mm TIPS Endoprosthesis: Technical Feasibility and Early Clinical Outcomes.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the technical feasibility, hemodynamic effects, and early clinical outcomes of the 6-10 mm GORE VIATORR TIPS Endoprosthesis with Controlled Expansion, which extends the prior 8 mm deployment floor to 6 mm.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent de novo transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) creation with the 6-10 mm device between April and July 2026. Technical success was defined as portosystemic pressure gradient (PSPG) below 12 mmHg or ≥ 50% reduction from baseline.

RESULT: Twelve patients (8 females, 4 males; mean age 57.1 ± 15.7 years; range 32-83 years) were included. Indications for TIPS creation were variceal hemorrhage (50.0%; n = 6/12), refractory ascites (33.3%; n = 4/12), and refractory hepatic hydrothorax (16.7%; n = 2/12). Final stent diameter was less than 8 mm in 91.7% (n = 11/12) of patients. Technical success was achieved in all patients, with mean PSPG decreasing from 16.7 ± 7.7 to 7.7 ± 2.9 mmHg (P < .001) and no immediate adverse events. Shunt patency was 100% at short imaging follow-up (mean, 35.6 ± 25.0 days), with no reinterventions. No recurrent variceal hemorrhage occurred, and ascites improved or resolved in 77.8% (n = 7/9) of patients at short clinical follow-up (mean, 50.5 ± 23.3 days). Four of 11 patients (36.4%) experienced symptomatic HE after TIPS creation and one patient (9.1%) died during the follow-up period.

CONCLUSION: TIPS creation using the 6-10 mm device is a technically feasible strategy with adequate short-term hemodynamic response.

title: Completion angiography and venous outflow assessment in arteriovenous graft placement: A retrospective observational study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Arteriovenous grafts are frequently used for hemodialysis access. Optimizing graft placement is important to prevent thrombosis and reinterventions. This study evaluated the association between vein diameter and clinical outcomes and evaluated the diagnostic value of completion angiography.

METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included 113 patients who underwent graft placement between 2010 and 2017. Outflow vein diameter was measured preoperatively by duplex ultrasound and intraoperatively by angiography. Angiographies were also analyzed for abnormalities. Outcomes included early graft failure (loss of primary patency within 30 days), secondary patency and access-related intervention rates. Predictive accuracy of vein diameter was assessed with ROC curves. Categorical variables were analyzed with chi square tests; Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank tests, and event rates with Poisson analysis.

RESULTS: Neither duplex nor angiography-measured vein diameters were associated with early graft failure (ROC AUC 0.63, 95% CI: 0.41-0.85, p = 0.24; and ROC AUC 0.54, 95% CI: 0.40-0.69, p = 0.57) or secondary patency (HR 1.07 per mm, 95% CI 0.84-1.38 and HR 1.06, 95% CI 0.96-1.18 respectively). Using the 4-mm cutoff recommended in clinical practice guidelines, vein diameter was not associated with access-related intervention rates. Completion angiography led to immediate revision in 15% of cases. Venous outflow abnormalities were present in 63% of final completion angiographies and were associated with higher intervention rates during follow-up (3.26 vs 2.58 per patient-year, p = 0.01), but not with early graft failure or 12-month secondary patency.

CONCLUSIONS: Vein diameter, ranging from 1.5 to 15 mm, did not predict clinical outcomes, suggesting using smaller veins than the recommended 4 mm-threshold may be reasonable in patients with limited access options. In contrast, completion angiography proved useful by prompting intra-operative revisions and by detecting outflow abnormalities that are associated with later reinterventions. Venous outflow, rather than vein diameter alone, should guide surgical decision making in arteriovenous graft placement.

This study evaluated the association between vein diameter and clinical outcomes and evaluated the diagnostic value of completion angiography.

title: Cation-Size-Controlled Structural and Magnetic Ground State Transitions in Co2+-Based Honeycomb-Derived Oxides Na0.5RE0.5Co2TeO6 (RE = La, Nd, Sm, Eu, Tb, Dy, Yb, and Y).
abstract: Honeycomb lattices containing spin-orbit-entangled Co2+ ions with effective Jeff = 1/2 moments provide promising platforms for enhancing strong quantum fluctuations and thus realizing potential quantum spin-liquid states. Here, we report a series of honeycomb-derived tellurates, "Na0.5RE0.5Co2TeO6" (NRECTO, RE = La, Nd, Sm, Eu, Tb, Dy, Yb, and Y). The increased size mismatch between Na+ and RE3+ drives an orthorhombic-to-hexagonal structural transition for NRECTO, accompanied by reconstruction in the connectivity of the [Co2TeO6]2- double-rutile chains and transformation in hexagonal channel topologies. High-resolution synchrotron X-ray diffraction and neutron powder diffraction reveal that both structures retain similar three-dimensional Co2+ topologies derived from AAA-stacked buckled honeycomb layers. Magnetic measurements revealed that orthorhombic NLaCTO exhibits a long-range antiferromagnetic order below 13 K, as confirmed by DC and AC susceptibility and a λ-type heat-capacity anomaly, whereas hexagonal NYCTO exhibits glassy magnetic freezing below 11 K, characterized by frequency-dependent AC susceptibility and slow spin dynamics. Despite comparable Co2+-O-Co2+ exchange pathways and Co-topologies are retained in both structures, their contrasting magnetic behavior demonstrates that subtle structural differences can strongly reshape the magnetic energy landscape. These results establish chemical-unit substitution as an effective strategy for controlling magnetism in Co2+-based honeycomb oxides.

title: Current documented functional status after radiocephalic straight-line onlay fistula creation: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The straight-line onlay technique (SLOT) may optimize radiocephalic fistula geometry, but available evidence remains limited. This study evaluated documented current functional status after radiocephalic SLOT creation and examined how alternative denominator constructions changed the reported proportion of functional fistulas.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 145 adult patients who underwent radiocephalic SLOT fistula creation between March 2020 and January 2024. Functional use was defined as documented access flow ⩾300 mL/min together with at least two successful two-needle hemodialysis sessions. Final status was classified as functional, failure, death-censored, transplant-censored, or unknown follow-up status. Continuous variables are reported descriptively, and proportions are presented with Wilson confidence intervals.

RESULTS: Documented functional use was confirmed in 113 of 145 patients (77.9%; 95% CI 70.5-83.9) in the full cohort. Among 124 patients with determinable current status, 113 had confirmed functional fistulas and 11 had confirmed failure, corresponding to 91.1% (95% CI 84.8-95.0). Failures comprised three early thromboses and eight nonmaturation events. Median radial artery and cephalic vein diameters were 2.4 mm and 3.3 mm.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, documented functional use was confirmed in 77.9% of the full radiocephalic SLOT cohort. The higher 91.1% estimate reflected restriction to patients with determinable final status rather than a change in the number of confirmed functional fistulas. These findings should be interpreted as descriptive current functional status, not as conventional longitudinal primary or secondary patency, and require prospective study using standardized patency definitions.

This study evaluated documented current functional status after radiocephalic SLOT creation and examined how alternative denominator constructions changed the reported proportion of functional fistulas. METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 145 adult patients who underwent radiocephalic SLOT fistula creation between March 2020 and January 2024.
