title: Clinical Significance of Cytokines in Pediatric Patients With Acquired Aplastic Anemia.
abstract: There remains limited evidence regarding serum cytokine variations in the progression of acquired aplastic anemia (aAA). Therefore, this retrospective study analyzed 12 serum cytokines in 52 pediatric patients with aAA and 56 healthy donors (HDs) to understand their role in aAA. Compared with HD, higher concentrations of interleukin-2 (IL-2), IL-5, IL-8, IL-10, and interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) were observed in aAA. Furthermore, patients with severe aplastic anemia (SAA) showed higher IL-6 than non-severe aplastic anemia (NSAA) population, and their IL-8 levels inversely correlated with neutrophil counts. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified IL-2, IL-8, and IL-10 as independent candidate biomarkers associated with aAA. A combined receiver operating characteristic curve analysis of these 3 cytokines demonstrated good discriminative performance in distinguishing aAA from HD, with an optimism-corrected area under the curve of 0.891. Our observations suggest that aberrant serum cytokine levels are associated with aAA progression through mechanisms involving immune dysregulation.

title: Peripheral Artery Disease in Acute Care Settings: Diagnosis and Management of Common Presentations and Emergencies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
abstract: People with peripheral artery disease (PAD) are often misdiagnosed or diagnosed late and, even after diagnosis, are undertreated with both pharmacologic and invasive therapies. The disease is associated with an increased risk of mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, other vascular disease, limb loss, and reduced quality of life. Although the risks and long-term management of PAD are well documented, these risks are acutely magnified when PAD exists as a comorbidity in patients hospitalized for other cardiovascular or medical conditions. Procedures requiring vascular access for the treatment of acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, or valvular heart disease, as well as procedures for the treatment of the patient's underlying PAD, require special consideration in patients with PAD. Familiarity with the use and placement of mechanical circulatory support in patients with PAD, as well as the management of recent endovascular or surgical vascular interventions, is essential for providing appropriate care in the acute care setting.

title: Endovascular robotic-assisted system for cerebral angiography (ERASE): Rationale, design, and protocol of a multicenter randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Neurointerventional therapy is a cornerstone in managing head and neck vascular disorders, with cerebral angiography serving as its fundamental diagnostic and therapeutic backbone. However, manual cerebral angiography is associated with several inherent limitations. While existing robotic-assisted systems have shown promise in mitigating some of these issues, they face challenges such as limited compatibility, lengthy setup times, and a lack of high-quality real-world evidence. The ERASE trial is a multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled trial (RCT). A total of 660 eligible patients will be enrolled from seven comprehensive stroke centers in China and randomized 1:1 to either the robotic-assisted group or the control group. Both groups use the Seldinger technique for femoral/radial artery access. Operators undergo standardized training on the robotic system. The trial adopts a prospective randomized open-label blinded endpoint (PROBE) design, with all imaging endpoints adjudicated via blinded review by an independent imaging core laboratory. All patients are followed up at baseline, end of surgery, 24 h postoperatively, and 7 days post-discharge. The primary efficacy outcome is the clinical success rate. The primary safety outcome is the incidence of perioperative/postoperative complications (e.g., vascular perforation, dissection, pseudoaneurysm), serious adverse events, and device malfunctions. Secondary outcomes include technical failure rate, overall procedural time, pre-puncture setup time, mean catheterization time per target vessel, super-selective technique success rate, DSA fluoroscopy time, participant radiation dose, primary operator radiation dose, contrast agent volume and instrument performance evaluation. A key safety endpoint is the rate of new asymptomatic cerebral infarctions detected via postoperative brain MRI-diffusion-weighted imaging. As the RCT focusing on the YDHB-NS01 Ver 2.0 system, the ERASE trial addresses critical unmet needs in neurointerventional practice and will generate high-quality evidence for robotic-assisted cerebral angiography. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07182188. TRIAL REGISTRATION DATE: 2025-09-18.

title: Adult Care in a Pediatric Hospital: Patterns and Implications of an Internal Medicine Consult Service at a Children's Hospital.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adults with childhood-onset conditions are increasingly admitted to children's hospitals, yet many pediatric systems lack the infrastructure and expertise to manage adult-related medical needs. One approach to bridge this gap is the use of an adult medicine consult service. We aim to describe the demographics, clinical complexity, and consultation patterns of patients admitted to a freestanding children's hospital and evaluated by an adult medicine consult service, which is a current gap in the literature.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective descriptive cohort study was performed of admitted patients with a Hospital Medicine Adult Care (HMAC) service consult from July 2014 through June 2023.

RESULTS: Annual adult admissions increased over the study period, from 7.4% to 10.2% of all admissions. HMAC consulted on 1666 admissions for 1008 unique patients (median age, 27 years [range, 14-71 years]). The most frequent reasons for consult were venous thromboembolism prophylaxis (33.7%), age older than 25 years (21.2%), transition of care (7.6%), and hypertension (7.6%). HMAC physicians addressed a mean of 5.5 diagnoses per encounter. Patients averaged 3.6 admissions (range, 1-22) and 4.9 comorbidities (range, 0-21) each. The most common comorbidities were technology dependence (47%), solid tumor malignancy (22.5%), genetic conditions (20.2%), epilepsy (19.7%), congenital heart disease (17.4%), and cerebral palsy (15.7%).

CONCLUSIONS: Adult consult services in children's hospitals support a medically complex population with diverse childhood-onset and adult conditions and function as longitudinal clinical partners. These findings support the role of adult medicine expertise in children's hospitals to help recognize and manage adult-specific care needs and transitions.

One approach to bridge this gap is the use of an adult medicine consult service. We aim to describe the demographics, clinical complexity, and consultation patterns of patients admitted to a freestanding children's hospital and evaluated by an adult medicine consult service, which is a current gap in the literature.

title: Influence of geometry, class imbalance and alignment on phantom reconstruction accuracy-a micro-CT phantom-based evaluation.
abstract: The accuracy of the 3D models created from medical scans depends on every stage of the pipeline- segmentation, alignment, and surface extraction. Although segmentation algorithms are well established, the effects of the type of geometry, class imbalance and voxel and point cloud alignment on accuracy remain to be sufficiently explored. This work evaluates the reconstruction accuracy and also studies the effect of voxel alignment on overlap accuracy metrics using controlled perturbation analysis. A sphere, a facemask, and an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) were printed using the stereolithography technique and scanned using a micro-CT machine. Segmentation was performed using Gaussian mixture model, Otsu thresholding and region-growing (RG) based methods. Segmented and reference models were aligned using the Kabsch-Umeyama (KU) algorithm to evaluate Dice and Jaccard scores, precision, among others. A sensitivity analysis quantified the effect of controlled translational (±5 voxels) and rotational (±5°) perturbations on post-KU-aligned voxel grids. Surface meshes, generated using the marching cubes algorithm, were registered with reference meshes using random sampling consensus and Iterative Closest Point (ICP) alignment process. Otsu thresholding yielded highest accuracy for all the geometries. The sphere, with uniform curvature and no thin-walled regions, showed the lowest sensitivity to alignment error. AAA yielded low overlap scores due to its small wall thickness and sensitivity to misalignment. AAA model was most sensitive to misalignment, with Dice and Jaccard scores decreasing by more than 90% under 5° rotation and by over 60% due to just 1°. The facemask surface was most error-prone, possibly due to misalignment during the ICP algorithm implementation. The Jaccard index yields numerically lower values and larger relative changes under perturbations than the Dice score, making alignment sensitivity more apparent for thin-walled structures. Even a sub-millimetre error in voxel alignment adversely affects accuracy. Surface-based accuracy metrics differed from the voxel-based trends, and this divergence carries diagnostic value.

Although segmentation algorithms are well established, the effects of the type of geometry, class imbalance and voxel and point cloud alignment on accuracy remain to be sufficiently explored. This work evaluates the reconstruction accuracy and also studies the effect of voxel alignment on overlap accuracy metrics using controlled perturbation analysis.

title: Pedicular Arteriovenous Fistula: Intraoperative Hemodynamic Characterization in Fasciocutaneous Free Flaps.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The pedicular arteriovenous fistula (PAVF) was introduced as a technique to manipulate free flap hemodynamics through the creation of an arteriovenous shunt within the pedicle. The goal of this study was to characterize the hemodynamic effects of PAVF creation in perforator free flaps by analyzing changes in flow and resistance.

METHODS: A retrospective review of patients who underwent free tissue transfer at a single institution was conducted. Fasciocutaneous flaps incorporating a PAVF were selected for this study. Intraoperative transit-time data were collected to measure volumetric flow and pulsatility index (PI). PI was used as a surrogate for vascular resistance. Transit-time measurements were obtained with the PAVF open and closed.

RESULTS: Twenty-one patients (23 flaps) underwent reconstruction with perforator free flaps including a PAVF. Opening the PAVF increased mean pedicle flow from 5.9 to 22.4 mL/minute (p < 0.001) and estimated flap flow from 6.2 to 10.4 mL/minute (p < 0.001). Meanwhile, pedicle PI fell from 6.0 to 2.0 (p = 0.003) with the PAVF. Larger PAVF caliber was associated with higher flow and lower PI. Only two flaps did not show flow augmentation with the PAVF, with one demonstrating possible steal.

CONCLUSION: PAVF creation was associated with significant increases in pedicle flow and estimated flap flow as well as reductions in pedicle PI. This finding is consistent with more favorable hemodynamics. Larger fistulas were associated with greater hemodynamic benefits without clear evidence of vascular steal. Our data suggest that a PAVF represents a physiologically sound and reversible method to enhance free flap hemodynamics. This technique warrants further investigation.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The pedicular arteriovenous fistula (PAVF) was introduced as a technique to manipulate free flap hemodynamics through the creation of an arteriovenous shunt within the pedicle. The goal of this study was to characterize the hemodynamic effects of PAVF creation in perforator free flaps by analyzing changes in flow and resistance. METHODS: A retrospective review of patients who underwent free tissue transfer at a single institution was conducted.

title: Decoding attempted handwritten characters based on temporal endovascular neural features.
abstract: Objective.We evaluated temporal neural features for motor decoding using a minimally-invasive endovascular brain-computer singular: interface (BCI). We hypothesised that relatively long compound movements generate distinct patterns of neural activity that are encoded by temporal features.Approach.A single participant implanted with the Stentrode endovascular BCI attempted to hand write English characters, which were then classified offline and online based on the recorded brain activity. The input to the model was a one-dimensional trajectory of high-gamma power, summed across all channels to isolate the effect of temporal information on decoding performance.Main results.A small number of classes across multiple months was reliably decoded, showing that temporal decoding could identify stable patterns of brain activity associated with each handwriting movement. Across four online sessions, where each session contained 20-30 trials/character and 80-180 rest trials, the best performing (3-class) model achieved a mean rest recall of 87% as well as character recall and precision of 65% and 59%, respectively. These results showed that attempted handwriting can be used in an online multi-class selection BCI and that temporal neural features capture the internal user context. Linear warping of trials to minimise temporal variability, where all trials were modified to have the same duration, led to significantly increased decoding performance compared to classifying raw trials.Significance.The results from our participant showed that decoding brain activity based on the differences between feature trajectories across time can be an effective strategy for discriminating different movements. Therefore, BCIs may be able to use temporal information to reduce their spatial footprint, likely making them less invasive. Overall, our study shows that further investigation of temporal decoding across multiple participants and other recording modalities is warranted. Strategies for automatic temporal alignment are likely to further improve the performance of these systems.

title: [The infected diabetic foot syndrome - diagnosis, treatment, and interdisciplinary care].
abstract: Diabetic foot syndrome (DFS) is one of the most severe long-term complications of diabetes mellitus and represents the leading cause of non-traumatic lower extremity amputations in industrialized nations. While the pathogenesis of foot ulcerations is primarily driven by a combination of diabetic polyneuropathy and peripheral arterial disease (PAD), secondary infections are frequently the main trigger for critical tissue loss. Consequently, these infections necessitate urgent inpatient admission and often result in major amputations as a last resort.The diagnosis of a diabetic foot infection is fundamentally based on clinical presentation. Key components for successful management include the early detection of underlying osteomyelitis, the identification of relevant perfusion deficits, and the immediate initiation of a structured, multimodal therapy regimen. This standard regimen comprises targeted surgical debridement, consistent pressure offloading, pathogen-specific antimicrobial therapy, and prompt vascular revascularization. Due to the highly complex underlying pathophysiology, patients with advanced disease stages benefit substantially from organized interdisciplinary care involving diabetologists, specialized podiatric surgeons, vascular surgeons, interventional radiologists, clinical infectious disease specialists, and orthopedic shoemakers. This comprehensive article provides a highly practice-oriented overview of the modern diagnosis and therapeutic management of the infected diabetic foot, strictly aligned with the current recommendations of the German Diabetes Society (DDG) and the International Working Group on the Diabetic Foot (IWGDF).

title: [Effect of sequential multi-dose tranexamic acid administration on perioperative blood loss in cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty and its safety].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of sequential multi-dose intravenous administration of tranexamic acid (TXA) on perioperative blood loss and inflammatory response in patients undergoing cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty (LMP), and to evaluate its safety.

METHODS: A prospective study was conducted in patients diagnosed with multi-level cervical spondylotic myelopathy, who underwent cervical posterior single-door LMP between January 2023 and June 2024. Using a computer-generated randomization table, patients were allocated into three groups. Placebo control group (group A): received 100 mL of normal saline intravenously at 30 minutes before incision (after anesthesia induction); the same dose was repeated every 5 hours for a total of 3 administrations. Single-dose control group (group B): received 1.0 g of TXA (dissolved in 100 mL normal saline) at 30 minutes before incision, followed by 100 mL of normal saline every 5 hours for a total of 2 additional doses. Sequential multi-dose group (group C): received 1.0 g of TXA (dissolved in 100 mL normal saline) at 30 minutes before incision, with an additional 1.0 g of TXA administered intravenously at 5 hours and 10 hours postoperatively, for a total dose of 3.0 g. A total of 120 patients met the selection criteria and were included in the study. After excluding lost-to-follow-up and withdrawn patients, 39 cases in group A, 37 in group B, and 38 in group C were included in the final analysis. There was no significant difference between groups (P>0.05) in age, gender, height, body weight, body mass index, comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes), and preoperative hematocrit (HCT), hemoglobin, D-dimer (D-D), interleukin 6 (IL-6), and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. The primary outcome was total blood loss (TBL). Secondary outcomes included intraoperative blood loss (IBL), postoperative blood loss (PBL), drain removal time (DRT), HCT, D-D, IL-6, CRP, allogeneic blood transfusion rate, and incidence of complications.

RESULTS: Blood loss assessment: TBL, PBL, DRT, postoperative decline in HCT, and the allogeneic blood transfusion rate were all the lowest in group C, followed by group B, and the highest in group A, with significant differences between groups (P<0.05). The IBL was significantly lower in groups B and C than in group A (P<0.05), while there was no significant difference between groups B and C (P>0.05). Changes in inflammatory indicators: the levels of D-D and IL-6 in 3 groups reached peak at 1 day, the level of CRP reached peak at 3 days, and both decreased at 5 days, but still remained higher than preoperative levels, with significant differences (P<0.05). At different time points, the levels of D-D, IL-6, and CRP were significant lower in group C than in groups A and B (P<0.05), and in group B than in group A (P<0.05). Safety evaluation: During the 30-day postoperative follow-up, no deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, incisional infection, incisional hematoma, or TXA-related allergic reaction occurred in 3 groups.

CONCLUSION: Sequential multi-dose TXA administration effectively reduces perioperative blood loss in cervical posterior single-door LMP, suppresses postoperative hyperfibrinolysis and inflammatory response, shortens drainage duration, and does not increase the risk of thromboembolic events. This regimen represents a safe and effective optimization strategy for perioperative blood management in LMP.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of sequential multi-dose intravenous administration of tranexamic acid (TXA) on perioperative blood loss and inflammatory response in patients undergoing cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty (LMP), and to evaluate its safety. METHODS: A prospective study was conducted in patients diagnosed with multi-level cervical spondylotic myelopathy, who underwent cervical posterior single-door LMP between January 2023 and June 2024. Using a computer-generated randomization table, patients were allocated into three groups.

title: A Novel SERPINC1 Mutation in a Teenager With Antithrombin Deficiency Leading to Pulmonary Embolism and Deep Vein Thrombosis: Implications for Diagnosis and Management.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is uncommon in adolescents, and hereditary thrombophilia should be considered in unprovoked or progressive cases. We report a 16-year-old Chinese male with pulmonary embolism and extensive deep vein thrombosis that progressed despite anticoagulation with low-molecular-weight heparin followed by unfractionated heparin. Antithrombin (AT) activity was persistently reduced (36%-49%; reference range, 80%-120%), and activated partial thromboplastin time remained subtherapeutic despite heparin dose escalation, suggesting functional heparin resistance. Switching to argatroban achieved clinical stabilization. Whole-exome sequencing identified a previously unreported heterozygous SERPINC1 variant (NM_000488.4: exon5: c.1153 G > T; p.Gly385Cys), classified as a variant of uncertain significance. The patient's mother and sister carried the same variant and had reduced AT activity. The patient was subsequently transitioned to rivaroxaban and remained asymptomatic during follow-up. AT activity remained reduced at 1 and 2 years, while follow-up imaging showed a reduction in pulmonary arterial thrombotic burden but persistent lower-extremity venous thrombi. This case highlights the importance of evaluating AT deficiency in young patients with unprovoked or progressive VTE and the need for further evidence to establish the clinical significance of novel SERPINC1 variants.

title: A Focal "Inferno Sign" With an Aberrant Innominate Artery Feeder: A Thyroid Arteriovenous Malformation Mimicking Malignancy in a Young Woman.
abstract: Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) of the thyroid gland are exceptionally rare, with only 11 cases identified in our review of the literature. They are clinically important because their hypervascularity on imaging can raise suspicion of malignancy, and biopsy or surgery may provoke life-threatening hemorrhage. We present a case of a 30-year-old female with a decade-long history of anterior neck swelling that recently became painful and enlarged. Ultrasound demonstrated a well-defined hypoechoic right-lobe nodule with marked color Doppler hypervascularity (described here as a focal "inferno sign"), a tangled vascular nidus, low-resistance arterial flow in the dominant feeding vessel, and early arterialization of the draining vein; together, these findings suggested arteriovenous shunting. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) characterized the lesion as a 1.0 cm × 0.9 cm intensely enhancing nodule supplied by an aberrant artery arising directly from the innominate artery, immediately medial to the origin of the right common carotid artery, with drainage into the right internal jugular vein. A radiological diagnosis of thyroid AVM was made without histopathological or angiographic confirmation, and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) was avoided because of the bleeding risk. The patient was referred for multidisciplinary management but was lost to follow-up. To our knowledge, this is the first reported thyroid AVM supplied by an innominate artery branch, a variant relevant to surgical and endovascular planning. Thyroid AVM should be considered in the differential diagnosis of hypervascular thyroid nodules, and CTA is valuable for mapping its vascular anatomy noninvasively.

They are clinically important because their hypervascularity on imaging can raise suspicion of malignancy, and biopsy or surgery may provoke life-threatening hemorrhage. We present a case of a 30-year-old female with a decade-long history of anterior neck swelling that recently became painful and enlarged.

title: Effect of Different Single-Session Durations of Intermittent Pneumatic Compression on the Prevention of Deep Vein Thrombosis in Postoperative ICU Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a common and potentially life-threatening complication in postoperative ICU patients. Intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) is widely used for mechanical thromboprophylaxis; however, the optimal single-session duration of IPC remains unclear. This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy of different single-session durations of IPC for preventing DVT in postoperative ICU patients. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective randomized controlled trial enrolled 138 patients who were randomized into 3 groups (n = 46 each) receiving IPC 3 times daily, with single-session durations of 40 minutes, 2 hours, or 6 hours. DVT incidence, coagulation parameters (D-dimer [mg/L] and fibrinogen [FIB; g/L]), and adverse events were compared on postoperative days 3 and 5. RESULTS Baseline characteristics were comparable among groups (P>0.05). The 6-hour group had a DVT incidence of 0% on both days, significantly lower than those in the 40-minute (15.21% and 32.61%) and 2-hour (8.70% and 34.78%) groups (P<0.05). No significant intergroup differences in D-dimer levels were observed (P>0.05); FIB levels significantly differed only on day 3 (P<0.05). Adverse events occurred in 6 patients (13.04%) in the 6-hour group, whereas none occurred in the other 2 groups. CONCLUSIONS Although 6-hour single-session IPC provides the most effective DVT prevention, it is associated with a higher risk of skin-related adverse events. Shorter, more frequent IPC (40 minutes or 2 hours per session, 3 times daily) may represent a preferable strategy for postoperative ICU patients due to its balance of efficacy, safety, and clinical feasibility.

title: Comprehensive reporting of acute aortic syndromes: a practical approach for radiologists.
abstract: Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) are a group of aortic pathologies with high morbidity and mortality. In the emergency setting, an accurate diagnosis is usually achieved by aortic computed tomography angiography (CTA). Recently, reporting and management guidelines have evolved due to modifications in surgical techniques and the expansion in utilization of endovascular techniques. This being said, radiologists require a more in-depth knowledge of key points to report to surgeons, their clinical implications, and some insights into available imaging-guided treatment options. Given the urgent nature of AAS, the need for rapid, detailed, and standardized reporting is crucial. In this review, we aim to introduce a step-by-step approach to accurate reporting of AAS, discussing recent guidelines and the role of imaging in the preprocedural evaluation of each disease entity (namely, intramural hematoma, penetrating aortic ulcer, and aortic dissection). Additionally, we will highlight the role of key imaging findings in the management of each disease entity. KEY POINTS: Question Acute aortic syndromes require rapid, sufficiently detailed, and accurate diagnosis to allow for timely patient management. Findings In this article, we propose a step-by-step approach using a structured reporting checklist. Clinical relevance Using a stepwise approach will allow timely reporting, give important details, and help guide further patient care.

title: Risk factors associated with the development of a catheter-related thrombosis in patients with critical illness: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
PURPOSE: We sought to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis with the primary objective to identify prognostic factors associated with developing a catheter-related thrombosis in the critical care setting. Our secondary objective was to report the incidence of this entity.

SOURCES: We searched, MEDLINE® and Embase® from inception through 4 May 2024 for all studies in patients with critical illness that reported catheter-related thrombosis, with an updated search performed on 23 October 2025. We included English-language studies that described prognostic factors for developing a catheter-related thrombosis or reported the incidence of this complication in the critical care setting. Two authors performed citation screening and data extraction. We pooled adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) separately for prognostic factors using a random-effects model and inverse variance weighting. Risk of bias for individual studies was evaluated using the Quality in Prognosis Studies tool. We assessed certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations approach.

PRINCIPLE FINDINGS: We included 32 studies involving 11,943 patients. Identified prognostic variables with a moderate- or high-certainty association for developing a catheter-related thrombosis include increasing age (aOR per 10-yr increase, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06 to 1.27; three studies; 1,594 patients; high certainty), trauma-related admission (aOR, 1.48; 95% CI, 0.93 to 2.34; three studies; 3,089 patients; high certainty), surgical-related admission (aOR, 2.50; 95% CI, 1.77 to 3.52; three studies; 2,208 patients; aHR, 1.35; 95% CI, 0.60 to 3.02; two studies; 297 patients; high certainty), internal jugular insertion site as compared with other insertion sites (aOR, 3.76; 95% CI, 2.82 to 5.01; four studies; 4,681 patients; high certainty), single/double-lumen as compared with more lumens (aOR, 1.61; 95% CI, 0.82 to 3.13; three studies; 1,594 patients; moderate certainty), and peripheral insertion site (aOR, 2.30; 95% CI, 0.74 to 7.08; two studies; 264 patients; moderate certainty). The median incidence of catheter-related thrombosis was 13.3% [interquartile range, 3.7%-31.3%].

CONCLUSIONS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we found that increasing age, surgical type admissions, large catheters, and factors potentially related with catheter duration were associated with developing a catheter-related thrombosis in the critical care setting. Furthermore, we identified significant variation in the reported rates of catheter-related thrombosis, with an average rate of approximately 1 in every 8 patients. When these identified risk factors are present, clinicians may consider more aggressive thromboprophylaxis regimens to better tailor prevention strategies to individual patient risk profiles.

title: Impact of True and False Lumen Origins on Target Vessel Instability in Post-Dissection F/BEVAR.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the occurrence of target artery-related adverse events in post-dissection F/BEVAR patients, based upon artery origin from the true or false lumen.

METHODS: This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI). Secondary endpoints included 5-year primary patency, freedom from secondary interventions (SIs), and type Ic and IIIc endoleaks. The analysis was performed on a per-vessel basis.

RESULTS: A total of 1052 target arteries were analyzed, primarily including the celiac, superior mesenteric, and renal arteries, with individual hepatic and splenic arteries occasionally incorporated in the repair. Of the 277 patients included, 75% were men, and 19% were black, with a mean age of 66.8 ± 10.3 years. The mean aneurysm sac diameter was 66.0 ± 11.4 mm, with extent II thoracoabdominal aneurysms being the most prevalent (72.6%) among this cohort. Technical success was obtained in 96% of the cases. As primary outcome, the incidence of target vessel instability (TVI) was significantly lower (P<0.001) among the true-lumen vessels (16.4%) compared to false-lumen (29.9%) and dual-lumen arteries (43.8%). As for the secondary outcomes, the incidence of type Ic endoleak was significantly higher (P=0.001) in false-lumen vessels (9.6%) and dual-lumen vessels (8.6%) compared to true-lumen vessels (3.3%). There was no significant difference in the incidence of type IIIc endoleak (p=0.241) or target vessel occlusion (P=0.458). Target artery stenosis was significantly more common among arteries originating from the false lumen compared to true lumen (2.6% vs 0.4%, P=0.009). Fenestrations were associated with a higher incidence (30.5%) of TVI when compared to branches (5.9% P=0.005), however, this was observed only among dual-lumen vessels. Arteries incorporated by a fenestration and that had a dual-lumen origin, were associated with a higher occurrence of secondary interventions (23.7%) compared to true-lumen vessels (8.6%, P=0.010). The same was not observed among the arteries incorporated by a branch configuration. The time-to-event analysis demonstrated a significantly higher 5-year freedom from TVI in true-lumen vessels compared to false and dual-lumen ones (True lumen: 83.6%; False=70.1 %; Dual=56.2 %; Log-rank P=0.0002). Freedom from secondary interventions at 5 years was significantly higher in true-lumen vessels compared to dual-lumen ones (Log-rank P=0.0104), but not to false-lumen arteries (Log-rank P=0.0847). The 5-year primary patency did not differ significantly among groups (True lumen: 98.3%; False = 92.6%; Dual=93.9%; Log-rank P=0.1368). On Cox proportional hazards analysis, dual-lumen (95% CI 1.24-3.28, p=0.005) and false-lumen (95% CI 1.04 - 2.60, p=0.0325) target arteries were associated with an increased hazard of TVI, when compared to true lumen arteries, having 2.02 (P=0.005) and 1.65 (P=0.0325) times more risk of presenting TVI than a true-lumen vessel CONCLUSIONS: In F/BEVAR for post-dissection aneurysms, target vessel instability and secondary intervention are significantly lower in target arteries originating from the true lumen, when compared to false-lumen or dual-lumen vessels. Device design, with use of fenestrations or branches may also play a role, with a significant difference only observed in dual-lumen target arteries.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the occurrence of target artery-related adverse events in post-dissection F/BEVAR patients, based upon artery origin from the true or false lumen. METHODS: This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI).

title: Fenestrated Endografts Provide Superior Outcomes Compared to Branched Devices in Juxtarenal Aortic Repair.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Urgent endovascular juxtarenal aortic repair with custom-made fenestrated devices is not feasible due to its long elaboration time. Off-the-shelf branched devices can be used, however, durability of the target vessels, especially renal artery branches, is of concern. Our objective is to compare mid and long-term patency of target vessels (TV), especially renal arteries (RA) in juxtarenal fenestrated or branched aortic endovascular repair.

METHODS: Single-center retrospective study identifying all patients undergoing fenestrated or branched endovascular repair (f/bEVAR) for juxtarenal aortic aneurysms (JAA) between 2011-2022. A FEVAR group with use of fenestrations to incorporate target vessels (TV) and a BEVAR group, with use of branches were created. Clinical and anatomical characteristics as well as perioperative technical success and complications were compared. The primary endpoint was the assessment of RA primary patency, freedom from endoleaks and instability (endpoint including occlusion, endoleak or need for reintervention) at follow-up. Secondary endpoints were the assessment of CT-SMA patency rates, freedom from endoleak and instability at follow-up and the evaluation of the anatomical and clinical factors associated with renal artery bridging covered stent (BCS) occlusion.

RESULTS: From 2011-2022, FEVAR was performed in 212 patients and BEVAR in 57. There were no statistical differences in demographics. The BEVAR group presented more frequently as urgencies (61% vs 11% for FEVAR p <,001). 955 TV were incorporated, including 536 RA. Technical success was 99%. BEVAR patients experienced higher perioperative death rates (14% vs 3% in FEVAR; p 0,005) and major complications (53% vs 17% in FEVAR; p <,001). Primary patency of RA in FEVAR was 99% at 3 years vs 74% for BEVAR (p < ,001). Freedom from RA BCS endoleaks were 97% at 3 years for the FEVAR group vs 87% in the BEVAR group (p <,001). Freedom from RA instability at 3 years was 95% in the FEVAR group vs 63% for the BEVAR group (p <,001). For CT-SMA only freedom from instability showed significant better outcomes at 3 years in the FEVAR group (96% vs 88% for BEVAR ; p ,006). In the multivariate analysis, the use of branches was the only factor associated with loss of patency in the RA.

CONCLUSIONS: In complex aortic repair for JAA, fenestrated devices achieved high patency rates while branched devices, mostly done for urgencies, are associated with significantly worse RA outcomes.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Urgent endovascular juxtarenal aortic repair with custom-made fenestrated devices is not feasible due to its long elaboration time. Off-the-shelf branched devices can be used, however, durability of the target vessels, especially renal artery branches, is of concern. Our objective is to compare mid and long-term patency of target vessels (TV), especially renal arteries (RA) in juxtarenal fenestrated or branched aortic endovascular repair.

title: Lesion-targeting and vascular matrix-penetrating siRNA nanotherapeutics for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract: Inefficient aneurysmal aorta enrichment and vascular matrix penetration represent major challenges against siRNA delivery for the management of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Herein, platelet membrane (PM)-reversibly camouflaged nanocomplexes (NCs) are developed to deliver Poldip2 siRNA (siPoldip2) into vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), which then restore vascular homeostasis by promoting phenotypic switching and mitigating oxidative stress. The NCs comprise a cationic nanocore assembled from siPoldip2 and a guanidinated and fluorinated bifunctional helical polypeptide (8FP), a charge-reversal intermediate layer of poly(l-lysine)-cis-aconitic acid (PC), and an outer shell of PM. After systemic administration in CaCl2-induced AAA rats, the NCs could preferentially accumulate at the aneurysmal site due to PM-mediated recognition of RGD-containing extracellular matrix proteins. The slightly acidic aneurysmal microenvironment subsequently triggers charge reversal of PC from negative to positive, which promotes the detachment of both PM and PC layers. The exposed 8FP/siPoldip2 nanocore penetrates the vascular matrix due to fluorocarbon-assisted repulsion of collagen mesh adsorption, followed by effective internalization by VSMCs. Consequently, Poldip2 expression in VSMCs is downregulated, which restores the contractile phenotype, and improves the aortic elasticity as well as structural integrity. This study provides a promising strategy for overcoming vascular delivery barriers and highlights the therapeutic promise of siRNA-based medical intervention for AAA.

title: Association between embolic protection strategy and distal embolization during Jetstream atherectomy for calcified femoropopliteal lesions.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distal embolization remains a significant complication during endovascular therapy (EVT) with atherectomy for femoropopliteal lesions. We evaluated the association between embolic protection strategies, including a novel flow-controlled anti-embolic technique (FCAT), and distal embolization.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 147 limbs in 126 patients with peripheral artery disease who underwent EVT using the Jetstream™ atherectomy system and drug-coated balloon treatment for calcified femoropopliteal lesions. Treated limbs were categorized by embolic protection strategy: no protection (n = 25), embolic protection device (EPD) alone (n = 63), EPD with proximal protection (n = 37), and FCAT (n = 22). The primary outcome was distal embolization incidence. Secondary outcomes included 6-month primary patency, target lesion revascularization (TLR), and major amputation.

RESULTS: Distal embolization occurred in 21.1% of lesions, with significant differences among groups (28.0%, 30.2%, 13.5%, and 0% for no protection, EPD alone, EPD with proximal protection, and FCAT, respectively; p = 0.012). Increasing protection intensity showed a stepwise reduction in distal embolization (p for trend = 0.008). In multivariable analysis, chronic limb-threatening ischemia was associated with increased distal embolization risk (adjusted odds ratio 2.68, 95% CI 1.10-6.54, p = 0.031), whereas embolic protection device with proximal protection including FCAT were associated with lower risk (adjusted odds ratio 0.26, 95% CI 0.07-0.96, p = 0.043). Six-month outcomes were comparable among groups, with no major amputations.

CONCLUSION: Embolic protection strategies incorporating proximal protection, including FCAT, were associated with a lower incidence of distal embolization during EVT using the Jetstream atherectomy system. Although no distal embolization was observed in the FCAT group, this FCAT-specific finding should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

We evaluated the association between embolic protection strategies, including a novel flow-controlled anti-embolic technique (FCAT), and distal embolization. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 147 limbs in 126 patients with peripheral artery disease who underwent EVT using the Jetstream™ atherectomy system and drug-coated balloon treatment for calcified femoropopliteal lesions.

title: Endovascular aortic repair for abdominal aortic aneurysm with horseshoe kidney using a physician-modified endograft to preserve an accessory renal artery.
abstract: Horseshoe kidney (HSK) associated with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is rare, and surgical repair is technically demanding because of complex anatomical variations, particularly accessory renal arteries (ARAs). The indication for ARA reconstruction remains a critical operative consideration. We report a 72-year-old man with a 43-mm AAA, a 40-mm left common iliac artery aneurysm (CIAA) and HSK. Preoperative contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated two ARAs (5 mm and 1.8 mm) supplying the renal isthmus. Endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) was performed with a physician-modified fenestrated endograft (PMEG); the dominant 5-mm ARA was reconstructed with a bridging stent. The postoperative course was uneventful and renal function was preserved (serum creatinine 0.82 → 0.76 mg/dL; eGFR 70.6 → 76.8 mL/min/1.73 m2); renal parenchymal volume was 87% of baseline. At 6-month CT, the aneurysm was stable, and at 2-year CT, both the AAA and the left CIAA had decreased by approximately 2 mm in diameter, with renal function unchanged. PMEG-based EVAR with dominant ARA reconstruction may therefore be a feasible option for AAA with HSK.

title: Portable endovascular disposable robotic assistant (PEDRA) for image-guided peripheral endovascular interventions: technical feasibility, safety, and future implications.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traditional fixed-console endovascular robots face barriers due to high capital costs and infrastructure requirements. This study evaluates the technical feasibility and safety of the LIBERTY® Endovascular Robotic System-a portable, disposable platform-across diverse Interventional Radiology procedures and vascular access sites.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A single-center retrospective review was conducted on 20 consecutive outpatient procedures performed by five operators. Cases included prostate artery embolization, uterine fibroid embolization, renal/gonadal venography, geniculate artery embolization, Y90 mapping, and Y90 radioembolization. Vascular access points included left radial and femoral approaches.

RESULTS: Procedural technical success was achieved in 100% (20/20) of cases. 100% of vessels attempted with robotic assistance were successfully selected (31/31). Complete robotic target-vessel selection-performing all procedural aspects of vessel selection robotically-was 75% (15/20). Partial robotic target-vessel selection-conversion to manual prior to completion of all vessel selections with robotic assistance-was 25% (5/20). All 5 cases of partial robotic target-vessel selection were due to hardware malfunction, rather than an inability to select target vessels with robotic assistance. Subgroup analysis of the last 10 cases after switching to utilizing updated units demonstrated 100% complete robotic target-vessel selection (10/10). No device-related serious adverse events or complications occurred.

CONCLUSION: The portable and disposable robotic platform was successfully integrated into a diverse Interventional Radiology practice, demonstrating the first documented prostate artery embolization, uterine fibroid embolization, renal/gonadal venography, geniculate artery embolization, and Y90 procedures by portable and disposable robotic-assistance, as well as the first robotic-assisted endovascular procedures via radial access. Its design may lower economic and institutional barriers, potentially expanding robotic-assisted interventions to rural or non-academic settings. The portable robotic assistant is safe and feasible for complex endovascular interventions. Further prospective studies are needed to quantify ergonomic benefits and radiation reduction.

This study evaluates the technical feasibility and safety of the LIBERTY® Endovascular Robotic System-a portable, disposable platform-across diverse Interventional Radiology procedures and vascular access sites. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A single-center retrospective review was conducted on 20 consecutive outpatient procedures performed by five operators.

title: Microsurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery and endovascular treatment of sylvian fissure arteriovenous malformations: a systematic review.
abstract: Sylvian-fissure-region arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are uncommon and anatomically heterogeneous; published labels often describe non-comparable lesions or populations. To update evidence for microsurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS), and endovascular treatment (EVT). Following PRISMA 2020, five databases were searched through May 2026 with citation chaining. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Dedicated sylvian/perisylvian cohorts were distinguished from broader cohorts and contextual technical reports. Incompatible endpoints, non-independent arms, and potentially overlapping cohorts were not pooled. Risk of bias and applicability were appraised. Nineteen reports were retained: 16 in the evidence synthesis and 3 as contextual background. Microsurgery achieved complete resection in 8/8, 40/41, and 94/94 patients. Transient deficits occurred in 4/8, 4/28, 9/94, and 18/41 patients; postoperative hematoma occurred in 2/94. Mortality windows varied. In the dedicated SRS cohort (n = 87), actuarial obliteration was 35% at 3 years, 60% at 4-5 years, and 76% at 10 years. Cumulative post-SRS hemorrhage was 5% at 1, 5, and 10 years (approximately 1% annually during latency); mortality was unreported. No dedicated curative EVT series for true sylvian AVMs was identified; available data described broader middle cerebral artery cohorts without sylvian-specific angiographic cure. Microsurgery is supported for carefully selected accessible sylvian-fissure AVMs, whereas SRS and embolization have complementary roles. Comparative superiority cannot be inferred. Future studies require explicit anatomical definitions, modality-specific denominators, angiographic endpoints, and standardized follow-up.

title: Intraoperative technology in skull base and vascular neurosurgery: a two-stage cross-sectional national survey.
abstract: Skull base and vascular neurosurgery rely on diverse intraoperative technologies, but contemporary data describing how frequently they are used at the level of individual operations are limited. On behalf of the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS) MedTech Committee, we aimed to establish a dated descriptive baseline of reported technology use across three operative paradigms. We conducted a two-stage cross-sectional survey of neurosurgeons in the UK and Ireland via the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS). Six MedTech Committee members compiled a pragmatic technology list. Respondents reported frequency of use for three exemplar procedures: transsphenoidal pituitary adenoma, retrosigmoid vestibular schwannoma, and pterional aneurysm surgery. Use was recorded on a four-point ordinal scale and analysed descriptively, with Kendall's tau-b used to explore the relationship between experience and reported use. Twenty-four responses from 20 of the 32 adult or mixed adult-paediatric UK units were analysed (11 units per index procedure). Reported use was strongly procedure specific. Neuronavigation was used always or almost always by 8/12 transsphenoidal respondents but infrequently elsewhere. Endoscopy had displaced microscopy in transsphenoidal surgery, whereas microscopy was used always or almost always by all retrosigmoid and pterional respondents. Indocyanine green and micro-Doppler were routine for aneurysms. Neurophysiological monitoring was universal for vestibular schwannoma but evenly divided for aneurysms. Exoscopes, intraoperative MRI and robotics were used infrequently or not at all; augmented reality was reported by 5/13 pterional respondents. No association was found between experience and reported use, though this was underpowered. Reported intraoperative technology use is strongly shaped by operative paradigm, with established technologies clustering around recurring procedural needs. Newer technologies were used infrequently. Because availability was not recorded, non-use cannot be distinguished from lack of access. These data provide a dated baseline against which future change can be assessed.

On behalf of the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS) MedTech Committee, we aimed to establish a dated descriptive baseline of reported technology use across three operative paradigms. We conducted a two-stage cross-sectional survey of neurosurgeons in the UK and Ireland via the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS).

title: Mitochondrial LONP1: Linking structure and function to context‑dependent roles in disease (Review).
abstract: Mitochondrial proteostasis is essential for maintaining organellar integrity, metabolic adaptation and cellular survival under physiological and stress conditions. Among mitochondrial quality control mechanisms, Lon peptidase 1 (LONP1) is an ATP‑dependent AAA+ serine protease localized predominantly in the mitochondrial matrix and plays a central role in the recognition and degradation of damaged or misfolded proteins. Recent structural, molecular and multi‑omics studies have expanded our understanding of LONP1 beyond proteolysis, implicating it in protein quality control, mitochondrial DNA maintenance, metabolic regulation and responses to oxidative and cellular stress. Increasing evidence also indicates that LONP1 functions are highly dependent on cellular and disease context, with both loss and gain of LONP1 activity associated with distinct pathological outcomes. The present review integrated recent structural and functional advances to establish a structure‑function framework for understanding how LONP1 coordinates proteolytic and chaperone‑like activities and how these functions are shaped by cellular and disease context. The present review further examined its roles in metabolic, neurodegenerative, reproductive, cardiovascular and malignant diseases, with particular emphasis on the context‑dependent consequences of LONP1 dysregulation and its emerging therapeutic potential. Finally, the present review highlighted unresolved questions concerning substrate recognition and specificity, the relative contributions of protease and chaperone‑like functions, disease‑specific directionality and the safety and feasibility of therapeutic modulation. These challenges need to be addressed to establish the functional and translational boundaries of LONP1.

title: Opinions of Brazilian nursing councils regarding peripheral intravenous puncture in the external jugular vein.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: to analyze the opinions issued by Brazilian nursing councils regarding peripheral intravenous puncture in the external jugular vein.

METHODS: this is a qualitative study conducted through virtual access to opinions available on the official websites of the Federal Nursing Council and the Regional Nursing Councils. The technical opinions were subjected to factorial analysis based on data processing using the IRAMUTEQ® software.

RESULTS: thirteen opinions published between 2009 and 2022 were analyzed, highlighting that the procedure is exclusive to nurses. Care-related, ethical, and legal aspects were identified.

FINAL CONSIDERATIONS: the opinions issued by Brazilian nursing councils regarding peripheral intravenous puncture in the external jugular vein were analyzed and indicate that nurses must demonstrate technical-scientific competence to perform the procedure. Furthermore, the importance of complying with the legal and ethical regulations governing professional nursing practice is emphasized.

METHODS: this is a qualitative study conducted through virtual access to opinions available on the official websites of the Federal Nursing Council and the Regional Nursing Councils. The technical opinions were subjected to factorial analysis based on data processing using the IRAMUTEQ® software.

title: Incidence of Venous Thromboembolism After Elective Isolated Lumbar Decompression: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the reported incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and composite venous thromboembolism (VTE) after isolated lumbar decompression.

SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Prior VTE estimates often combine decompression-only procedures with more complex spine surgery, limiting procedure-specific risk estimation.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched on March 2, 2026, with surveillance through June 17, 2026. Decompression-only cohorts without fusion or instrumentation were eligible. Clinically detected, coded, or patient-reported outcomes were analyzed separately by event type and follow-up using random-effects binomial-normal generalized linear mixed models when at least five studies contributed data. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Twenty-five studies had a combined reported sample size of 831,732 patients. At 30 days, pooled DVT incidence was 0.283% (9 studies; 235,490 patients; 95% CI, 0.203%-0.393%) and PE incidence was 0.273% (7 studies; 235,341 patients; 95% CI, 0.171%-0.437%). At 90 days, DVT incidence was 0.225% (7 studies; 163,074 patients; 95% CI, 0.056%-0.905%) and PE incidence was 0.183% (6 studies; 162,772 patients; 95% CI, 0.041%-0.825%). Composite VTE estimates were heterogeneous. The low 30-day DVT and PE estimates persisted in leave-one-out analyses, while 90-day estimates were more sensitive to study inclusion. Only three studies reported chemical prophylaxis regimens. Different cohorts contributed to the two windows, which should not be interpreted as a temporal trend.

CONCLUSION: Reported 30-day DVT and PE incidences after isolated lumbar decompression were each approximately three events per 1,000 patients. These estimates provide a procedure-specific benchmark for counseling but do not establish the risk without prophylaxis or the effectiveness and overall benefit of chemoprophylaxis.
englishSummary: STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis. OBJECTIVE: To determine the reported incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and composite venous thromboembolism (VTE) after isolated lumbar decompression. SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Prior VTE estimates often combine decompression-only procedures with more complex spine surgery, limiting procedure-specific risk estimation.

title: Preoperative GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use and Postoperative Outcomes Across Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly used for pre-operative weight loss before body-contouring procedures, yet their effects on wound healing are poorly characterised and evidence on post-operative complications is conflicting.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO ICTRP (to May 2026) for comparative studies of pre-operative GLP-1 RA use versus no use in adults undergoing plastic and reconstructive surgery. Risk ratios (RR) were pooled using random-effects models (REML; Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals [CI]); pre-specified population subgroups were compared. Analyses used R (version 4.3).

RESULTS: In total, 13 studies (n = 17,426; 8,745 GLP-1 RA users) were included. Pre-operative GLP-1 RA use was not associated with wound dehiscence (RR 1.05; 95% CI 0.73-1.52), surgical site infection (RR 0.83; 0.60-1.16), seroma (RR 1.12; 0.67-1.87), haematoma (RR 1.13; 0.67-1.90) or venous thromboembolism (RR 0.61; 0.34-1.08). Hypertrophic scarring was increased (RR 1.55; 95% CI 1.01-2.38). Tests for differences between the general-population, post-bariatric and reconstructive subgroups were non-significant for all outcomes except surgical site infection (P < .001), which showed lower rates in the reconstructive subgroup.

CONCLUSION: In adults undergoing plastic and reconstructive surgery, pre-operative GLP-1 RA use was not associated with an overall increase in post-operative complications, apart from a modest increase in hypertrophic scarring, and population subgroups did not differ except for surgical site infection. Given the very low certainty of evidence, these findings are hypothesis-generating and support individualised perioperative management rather than routine restriction of GLP-1 RAs.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III (risk/prognostic study).

Risk ratios (RR) were pooled using random-effects models (REML; Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals [CI]); pre-specified population subgroups were compared.

title: Intravascular Ultrasound-Guided Emergency Endovascular Repair of a Tracheo-Innominate Artery Fistula for Severe Motor and Intellectual Disabilities.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tracheo-innominate artery fistula (TIF) is a lethal post-tracheostomy complication. In severe motor and intellectual disabilities, skeletal deformities and low surgical tolerance render open repair prohibitive, necessitating emergency hemostasis.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 31-year-old female with cerebral palsy developed massive tracheal hemorrhage 2 months post-tracheostomy. She presented with unstable vital signs, requiring manual syringe-push transfusion. Under cuff tamponade, emergency endovascular therapy (EVT) with Gore Viabahn and Viabahn VBX was chosen over open surgery due to thoracic deformities and limited time. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) localized the angiographically occult rupture site. Hemostasis was achieved, but suspected stent graft infection developed on Day 11 despite prophylactic antibiotic therapy. Following transition to comfort care, she died 27 days post-procedure due to anemia, hypotension, and impaired ventilation.

CONCLUSION: Emergency IVUS-guided EVT under cuff tamponade is a valuable life-saving strategy and potential definitive treatment option for TIF in patients with prohibitive surgical risk, though late-onset infection remains a critical challenge.

In severe motor and intellectual disabilities, skeletal deformities and low surgical tolerance render open repair prohibitive, necessitating emergency hemostasis. CASE PRESENTATION: A 31-year-old female with cerebral palsy developed massive tracheal hemorrhage 2 months post-tracheostomy.

title: Twenty-Year Forecast of Thoracic Surgeon Demand in Chile: Simulated Scenarios Using Bayesian Methods and Publicly Available Data.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Internationally, the thoracic surgery workforce is undergoing rapid changes due to increased training availability, particularly in Chile. There is currently no method for adequately forecasting the number of training spots needed to meet demand in future years.

METHODS: A national registry of thoracic surgeons was constructed using publicly available data from the Chilean Superintendency of Health (as of October 2024). Surgeons practicing cardiac or vascular surgery, retirees, and those living abroad were excluded. A Bayesian projection model was developed that incorporates parameters such as retirement age, entry of new surgeons (including graduates and foreign-certified individuals), accidental mortality, population growth, and dynamic demand growth. Monte Carlo simulations (1000 iterations) were conducted across five scenarios (1 to 5 graduates/year, plus one certified surgeon/year). Absolute error analysis identified the optimal annual number of new graduates.

RESULTS: Of the 107 thoracic surgeons listed in Chile, only 67 were actively practicing non-cardiac thoracic surgery. The majority were concentrated in the Metropolitan Region (capital). Sex distribution was predominantly male (83.5%), with a mean age of 50.2 years. The corrected model (using 67 active surgeons as the baseline) shows that a scenario with 1 graduate per year results in a projected shortage, while scenarios with 3-5 graduates per year lead to potential oversupply. The optimal scenario, minimizing supply-demand mismatch, was training approximately two to three surgeons per year (2.6 graduates/year).

CONCLUSIONS: Strategic workforce planning is essential to avoid future imbalances in thoracic surgeon availability. Bayesian modeling provides a robust framework for anticipating demand, guiding training capacity, and ensuring equitable distribution across regions, thereby avoiding both shortages and saturation of the specialty in Chile.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Internationally, the thoracic surgery workforce is undergoing rapid changes due to increased training availability, particularly in Chile. There is currently no method for adequately forecasting the number of training spots needed to meet demand in future years. METHODS: A national registry of thoracic surgeons was constructed using publicly available data from the Chilean Superintendency of Health (as of October 2024).

title: Risk Factors for Diabetic Foot-Related Lower Extremity Amputation in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of lower limb amputation (LLA) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where evidence on adjusted risk factors remains limited. This systematic review evaluates the risk factors for LLA and amputation-related mortality in diabetic foot disease across LMICs.

METHODS: Embase, MEDLINE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (via Ovid), PubMed, and Scopus were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies of adults with diabetes in LMICs reporting LLA with adjusted effect estimates were included. Pooling of effect estimates was prespecified to require at least three comparable studies per domain. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or AXIS.

RESULTS: Sixteen studies (19,529 participants; 1604 amputation events) provided usable effect estimates; 12 reported adjusted estimates from multivariable models. No domain contained three or more comparable estimates, so quantitative synthesis was not undertaken. Osteomyelitis was independently associated with amputation in both studies assessing it (aOR 5.60, 95% CI 2.93-10.78; aOR 11.8, 95% CI 5.1-27.5). Peripheral arterial disease was associated with LLA in two of three studies using objective vascular assessment (aOR 2.80, 95% CI 1.52-5.11; aOR 3.23 per grade, 95% CI 2.68-3.89). Prior amputation was associated with LLA in two DFU cohorts reporting concordant estimates (aOR 2.86 and 3.08). Ulcer severity was associated with amputation in every study assessing it, using five different classification systems. Prolonged ulcer duration carried an adjusted odds ratio of 10.3 (95% CI 4.06-26.13), and each additional preoperative day was associated with a 9.3% increase in the odds of major amputation. Neuropathy showed no independent association of meaningful size in any adjusted analysis, and HbA1c was not associated in the largest adjusted DFU cohort analysis, although a smaller study with 10 outcome events reported a positive association.

CONCLUSION: Peripheral arterial disease, ulcer severity, osteomyelitis, prior amputation, and delayed access to care were associated with LLA in LMIC settings. Neither neuropathy nor HbA1c showed an independent association of meaningful size in adjusted analyses of established DFU cohorts. Prospective LMIC cohorts using standardized definitions are needed.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of lower limb amputation (LLA) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where evidence on adjusted risk factors remains limited. This systematic review evaluates the risk factors for LLA and amputation-related mortality in diabetic foot disease across LMICs. METHODS: Embase, MEDLINE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (via Ovid), PubMed, and Scopus were searched from inception to March 2026.

title: A Ten-Year Single-Center Evaluation of In-Hospital Versus Seven- Versus Thirty-Day Outcomes as Quality Standards After Carotid Endarterectomy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains a cornerstone for stroke prevention. The 2023 European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines recommend performing CEA only if the 30-day risk of stroke or death is < 3% for asymptomatic and < 6% for symptomatic patients. While clinical trials establish efficacy based on 30-day outcomes, reporting in-hospital complication rates offers greater feasibility in clinical routine. This study evaluates institutional compliance with ESVS thresholds and compares the reliability of in-hospital and 7-day outcomes versus the 30-day follow-up interval.

DESIGN: Retrospective single-center cohort study.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted at the Medical University of Graz, encompassing 2496 patients undergoing primary CEA between 2014 and 2023. Data were retrieved from the institutional information system and cross-referenced with national mortality registries (Statistik Austria) to ensure comprehensive follow-up. Primary endpoints included stroke and death within 7 and 30 days, stratified by symptomatic status and surgical technique-Eversion Endarterectomy (EEA) versus Conventional Endarterectomy (TEA) with patch angioplasty.

RESULTS: The final cohort comprised 2496 eligible procedures. Notably, a substantial proportion of events that occurred after hospital discharge, accounting for 17.9% (10/56) of all 30-day strokes and 60.0% (9/15) of all 30-day deaths were observed between hospital discharge and postoperative day 30. Overall, the in-hospital combined stroke and death rate was 1.5% for asymptomatic patients and 3.8% for symptomatic patients. Following discharge, additional events were recorded in 10 asymptomatic and 9 symptomatic patients, resulting in a cumulative 30-day combined stroke and death rate of 2.0% [95% CI: 1.4%-2.7%] for asymptomatic patients and 5.3% [95% CI: 3.5%-7.2%] for symptomatic patients, thereby meeting ESVS safety standards. While symptomatic status was a significant predictor of complications (p < 0.001), neither sex nor surgical technique (EEA vs. TEA-patch) exerted a significant influence on outcomes.

CONCLUSION: CEA is performed at ESVS-recommended safety levels in Graz. Contrasting a clinical tendency to favor more convenient in-hospital metrics, this study demonstrates that "in-hospital" data cannot be standardized due to highly variable discharge windows. Furthermore, while fixed 7-day complication rates provide a standardized timeline, they still significantly underestimate perioperative risks. The substantial rate of post-discharge perioperative strokes and deaths observed in our cohort underscores the clinical necessity of extending quality control to at least 30 days, which remains the superior metric for clinical audit.

The 2023 European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines recommend performing CEA only if the 30-day risk of stroke or death is < 3% for asymptomatic and < 6% for symptomatic patients. While clinical trials establish efficacy based on 30-day outcomes, reporting in-hospital complication rates offers greater feasibility in clinical routine.

title: Duplex ultrasound examination of superficial venous insufficiency of the lower limbs: A methodology proposal from the French Society of Vascular Medicine and the French Society of Phlebology.
abstract: Duplex ultrasound (DUS), in addition to clinical examination, is essential for the accurate assessment of superficial venous disease (SVD). It allows venous mapping, which is the basis of the therapeutic choice and serves as a reference for evolutionary monitoring. These guidelines, carried out at the request of the French Society of Vascular Medicine (SFMV) and the French Society of Phlebology (SFP), propose a standardized methodology for DUS examination considering the multiple clinical presentations of SVD. For each territory, the distinctive echo-anatomical data and the specific methods of the resulting examination are described. To improve and standardize practices, a unique and updated standardized template for reporting DUS findings by venous mapping is proposed.

title: Thromboembolic Complications in Cushing's syndrome: Origin, Pathophysiology, and Clinical Implications.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cushing's syndrome (CS) is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), which may persist after surgery and biochemical remission. This review synthesizes current evidence on VTE risk, underlying mechanisms, clinical assessment, and prevention and treatment strategies in patients with CS.

METHODS: This narrative review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science for relevant English-language publications from 1999 through August 2026. Eligible sources included observational studies, case series, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical guidelines, and consensus statements addressing thrombotic risk, venous thromboembolism, or mechanisms of hypercoagulability in CS. Relevant findings were synthesized qualitatively and organized thematically.

RESULTS: A systematic meta-analysis reported approximately 18-fold higher odds of spontaneous VTE in patients with endogenous CS than in the general population. The prothrombotic state involves alterations in coagulation, impaired fibrinolysis, endothelial dysfunction, platelet activation, inflammation, and venous stasis. Thrombotic risk may persist after biochemical remission, although its duration remains uncertain. The 2025 international Delphi consensus supports individualized thromboprophylaxis, with low-molecular-weight heparin preferred. Evidence supporting direct oral anticoagulants for prophylaxis remains limited. Clinical decisions should account for thrombotic and bleeding risks, including perioperative bleeding and potential drug interactions between direct oral anticoagulants and steroidogenesis inhibitors. No validated CS-specific risk prediction tool is available; a proposed framework may support individualized risk assessment. Proposed genetic, epigenetic, and non-coding RNA mechanisms remain hypothesis-generating.

CONCLUSION: VTE prevention in CS requires individualized risk assessment and careful consideration of perioperative and post-remission risk. Prospective studies are needed to establish optimal prophylaxis strategies and validate CS-specific risk prediction approaches.

This review synthesizes current evidence on VTE risk, underlying mechanisms, clinical assessment, and prevention and treatment strategies in patients with CS. METHODS: This narrative review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science for relevant English-language publications from 1999 through August 2026.

title: Single vs. Dual Antiplatelet Therapy after Fenestrated and Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after fenestrated or branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR).

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Global were searched from inception to 12 July 2026, with a supplementary targeted PubMed search on 5 September 2026.

REVIEW METHODS: Comparative studies of post-operative antiplatelet therapy were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach. Outcomes were synthesised narratively when clinical and methodological differences precluded meaningful pooling; an additional quantitative summary of study defined bleeding outcomes was also reported.

RESULTS: Six retrospective cohorts comprising 3 623 patients were included, with 3 197 patients in separately extractable single or dual antiplatelet therapy groups. Several studies reported associations favouring dual antiplatelet therapy for target vessel patency. However, differences in outcome definitions, analytical units, and treatment classification precluded a common pooled estimate, and one association was attenuated after accounting for treatment changes. Evidence regarding ischaemic events, mortality, re-intervention, and endoleak was insufficient for reliable pooled comparisons. Five cohorts reported peri-operative bleeding using heterogeneous definitions and observation periods, of which a four study summary yielded an odds ratio of 1.30 (95% confidence interval 0.87 - 1.94) for dual vs. single antiplatelet therapy. Given the differences in outcome definitions, this does not estimate a common clinical effect.

CONCLUSION: The current evidence comparing single and dual antiplatelet therapy after FBEVAR is based on heterogeneous cohort studies, focuses largely on surrogate outcomes such as target vessel patency, and shows no clear benefit for dual antiplatelet therapy. Comparative bleeding risk as well as clinical outcomes of single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after FBEVAR remain uncertain. Future prospective studies are needed to better delineate superiority of one regimen over the other.

title: Delayed Candida glabrata-associated infected thoracic aortic aneurysm after candidemia supported by identical serial MLVA profiles: a case report.
abstract: Candida-associated infected aortic aneurysms (AAs) are exceptionally rare and frequently fatal. A 76-year-old man developed Candida glabrata candidemia after surgery for ascending colon cancer; the postoperative course was complicated by an anastomotic leak and intra-abdominal infection. Echinocandin therapy was discontinued because of profound neutropenia after 12 days of treatment, following negative blood cultures. Approximately 1 year later, an enlarging descending thoracic AA was detected and treated with thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR). Despite initially negative blood cultures, a normal or only minimally elevated serum β-D-glucan concentration, and negative Candida antigen testing, the aneurysm subsequently enlarged and required repeat TEVAR. Periaortic soft-tissue changes transiently regressed, further obscuring the diagnosis. Three months after the second TEVAR, computed tomography revealed renewed aneurysm enlargement and perigraft gas. C. glabrata was recovered from one of five blood culture sets. On the fifth day of admission, the patient experienced abrupt circulatory collapse with hemoptysis and died, likely due to aneurysm rupture through an aortobronchial fistula. All available intra-abdominal and bloodstream isolates of C. glabrata obtained throughout the clinical course had identical six-locus multiple-locus variable-number tandem-repeat analysis (MLVA) profiles. A prior episode of candidemia remains clinically relevant when a new or progressive aortic lesion develops, even after prolonged culture negativity. Serial aneurysm enlargement, periaortic inflammation, and delayed perigraft gas should outweigh apparently reassuring blood cultures or fungal biomarkers and should prompt early multidisciplinary reassessment, pursuit of tissue diagnosis when feasible, source control, and prolonged antifungal therapy.

A 76-year-old man developed Candida glabrata candidemia after surgery for ascending colon cancer; the postoperative course was complicated by an anastomotic leak and intra-abdominal infection. Echinocandin therapy was discontinued because of profound neutropenia after 12 days of treatment, following negative blood cultures.

title: Trends and Impact of Early Medical Complications in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Data from the Austrian Stroke Unit Registry.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early medical complications following acute ischemic stroke (AIS) are common and might increase poststroke morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to evaluate trends in the prevalence of early medical complications over almost 2 decades and their impact on 3-month functional outcome and mortality.

METHODS: A total of 181,704 AIS patients from the Austrian Stroke Unit Registry (2006-2024) were analyzed. Early medical complications included decompensated heart failure, cardiac arrhythmia, sepsis, pneumonia, urinary tract infection (UTI), deep vein thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism. Functional outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) after 3 months, with favorable outcome defined as mRS ≤1. Associations between early medical complications and mRS were analyzed using multivariable Poisson regression models.

RESULTS: Among all patients, 16,279 (9.0%) had early medical complications. Pneumonia (4.2%), UTI (2.9%), cardiac arrhythmia (1.4%), and decompensated heart failure (1.4%) were most common, with significant declines in prevalence over time. Admission NIHSS scores decreased, and the use of intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy increased. Decompensated heart failure (RR = 1.85, 95% CI: 1.73-1.97, p < 0.001), sepsis (RR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.53-1.99, p < 0.001), pulmonary embolism (RR = 1.67, 95% CI: 1.33-2.10, p < 0.001), and pneumonia (RR = 1.64, 95% CI: 1.57-1.72, p < 0.001) were significantly associated with 3-month mortality. Furthermore, the complications least associated with a favorable outcome were pneumonia (RR = 0.36, 95% CI: 0.32-0.41, p < 0.001), decompensated heart failure (RR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.32-0.46, p < 0.001), and sepsis (RR = 0.59, 95% CI: 0.45-0.77, p < 0.001). The effect sizes did not change significantly through the observed years.

CONCLUSIONS: This study observed a significant reduction in the prevalence of early medical complications after AIS, especially decompensated heart failure, pneumonia, sepsis, and pulmonary embolism which continue to substantially affect mortality and functional outcome in AIS patients.
