This study aimed to evaluate trends in the prevalence of early medical complications over almost 2 decades and their impact on 3-month functional outcome and mortality. METHODS: A total of 181,704 AIS patients from the Austrian Stroke Unit Registry (2006-2024) were analyzed.

title: Microplastic Detection in the Ascending Aorta: An Exploratory Study Using Pyrolysis-Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry (Py-GC/MS).
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as significant environmental pollutants that have been detected in various human tissues. This pilot biomonitoring study explored polymer mass in dissected versus non-dissected ascending aortic tissue. A total of 16 ascending aortic samples (8 acute type A aortic dissection [AD] and 8 acute type B dissection with arch involvement but a non-dissected ascending aorta [ND]) were examined using pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS) to screen 11 polymers. Both groups had aortic disease. Polymer-related signals were reported in all samples, with total mass estimates ranging from 1.92 to 155.58 µg/g tissue. The predominant reported polymer was polyamide 66 (PA66; 50.7%), followed by polyvinyl chloride (PVC; 40.5%) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET; 8.8%). AD tissues showed a 3.9-fold higher estimated polymer burden than ND tissues (74.51 ± 42.81 vs. 19.25 ± 16.48 µg/g, p = 0.0077). PET estimates were also higher in AD tissues (7.36 ± 6.44 vs. 0.89 ± 1.49 µg/g, p = 0.025), but PET identification was tentative and polymer-specific tests were exploratory. Total polymer mass correlated with ascending aortic diameter (Spearman's rho = 0.865, p < 0.001). The age- and group-adjusted association (coefficient 0.079 mm per µg/g; p = 0.0098) was sensitive to omission of one observation (p = 0.140). These findings describe a difference in estimated polymer burden between two diseased-tissue groups. Incomplete analytical validation and possible perioperative contamination limit interpretation; particle identity, tissue localization, vascular toxicity and causality were not established. Further analytical and multicenter validation is needed.

title: Painless Stanford type A aortic dissection presenting with isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits: a case report.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Stanford type A aortic dissection (AAD) constitutes a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Painless AAD manifesting exclusively as isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits represents an uncommon but recognised presentation of aortic dissection that is prone to misdiagnosis. This case report adds real-world clinical data regarding atypical AAD and delivers practical diagnostic and surgical insights for front-line clinicians.

MAIN SYMPTOMS AND IMPORTANT CLINICAL FINDINGS: A 58-year-old Han Chinese female presented with acute-onset bilateral lower-limb numbness and weakness lasting one hour, in the absence of chest, back or abdominal pain. Physical examination uncovered an inter-arm systolic blood-pressure discrepancy together with bilateral lower-limb motor weakness (3/5). Emergency non-contrast chest-abdominal CT identified the aortic double-lumen sign and inward-displaced aortic wall calcified plaques, whereas bilateral distal peripheral pulses remained preserved.

MAIN DIAGNOSES, THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS, AND OUTCOMES: Painless Stanford type A aortic dissection complicated by suspected transient spinal cord malperfusion was diagnosed. Following urgent inter-hospital transfer, the patient underwent emergency Bentall procedure combined with aortic arch reconstruction and frozen elephant-trunk graft implantation, with a distal landing zone in the proximal descending thoracic aorta. Her bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits had fully resolved by postoperative day 2. A residual chronic dissection with a thrombosed false lumen persisted distally below the stent-graft and remained stable without interval enlargement. Six-month follow-up confirmed complete functional recovery without residual neurological sequelae or proximal dissection recurrence.

CONCLUSION: Undiagnosed painless Stanford type A aortic dissection presenting with isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits is associated with substantial mortality. Routine bilateral upper-arm blood-pressure measurement and recognition of calcification displacement signs on non-contrast CT facilitate early clinical suspicion. Timely confirmation by CTA and urgent comprehensive surgical reconstruction are essential to reverse end-organ malperfusion and optimize neurological as well as survival outcomes.

Painless AAD manifesting exclusively as isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits represents an uncommon but recognised presentation of aortic dissection that is prone to misdiagnosis. This case report adds real-world clinical data regarding atypical AAD and delivers practical diagnostic and surgical insights for front-line clinicians.

title: Limb Salvage and Clinical Outcomes of Percutaneous Versus Surgical Deep Venous Arterialization for No-option Chronic Limb-threatening Ischaemia: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare percutaneous with surgical deep venous arterialization for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischaemia and to examine whether percutaneous outcomes differ by device type.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: MEDLINE was searched via PubMed on 8 August 2026. Eligible cohorts reported at least 10 limbs with Rutherford class 5 or 6 chronic limb-threatening ischaemia. Hybrid procedures were classified as surgical; superficial venous arterialization was excluded. The primary endpoint was 12-month limb salvage. Proportions were pooled on the logit scale using random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals. Device type was a pre-specified secondary analysis.

RESULTS: Eleven cohorts comprising 470 limbs were included-eight percutaneous (382 limbs) and three surgical or hybrid (88 limbs). Pooled 12-month limb salvage was 71.0% (95% confidence interval [CI] 66.0-75.5%; I2 = 0.5%), with no significant difference between modalities (71.8% vs. 72.6%; p = 0.81). Technical success was 95.9% (91.7-98.0%) and did not differ between modalities (p = 0.69), but within the percutaneous arm was higher with a dedicated system than with off-the-shelf technique (97.9% vs. 94.3%; p = 0.03). Amputation-free survival was 59.5% (50.1-68.2%), and reintervention occurred in 43.5%; neither was reported by any surgical cohort. Egger test indicated small-study effects (p = 0.009).

CONCLUSION: Deep venous arterialization achieved limb salvage in approximately 71% of patients with no-option chronic limb-threatening ischaemia. Limb salvage did not differ between percutaneous and surgical approaches, whereas technical success was higher with a dedicated device. These indirect comparisons from single-arm cohorts do not establish superiority of either technique.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3 a-Systematic review of non-randomized observational studies.

title: Low-Dose Versus High-Dose Drug-Coated Balloon After Jetstream Atherectomy for Severely Calcified Femoropopliteal Lesions: The JUPITER Multicenter Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Second-generation low-dose drug-coated balloons (LD-DCBs) have shown clinical efficacy comparable to high-dose DCBs (HD-DCBs) for femoropopliteal artery (FPA) lesions. Whether paclitaxel dose density remains clinically relevant after aggressive vessel preparation with atherectomy in severely calcified FPA lesions remains uncertain. This study aimed to compare 1-year clinical outcomes of second-generation LD-DCB and HD-DCB following Jetstream atherectomy in patients with severely calcified FPA lesions.

AIMS: This study aimed to compare 1-year clinical outcomes of second-generation LD-DCB and HD-DCB following Jetstream atherectomy in patients with severely calcified FPA lesions.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 262 patients with severely calcified FPA lesions who underwent endovascular therapy with Jetstream atherectomy followed by second-generation LD-DCB (n = 175) or HD-DCB (n = 87). Propensity-score matching yielded 79 well-balanced pairs. The primary outcome was 1-year primary patency; secondary outcomes included freedom from clinically driven target-lesion revascularization (TLR), limb salvage, and overall survival.

RESULTS: In the overall cohort before matching, 1-year primary patency was similar between second-generation LD-DCB and HD-DCB (86.8% vs. 83.1%, log-rank p = 0.578), with comparable freedom from TLR, limb salvage, and overall survival. After propensity score matching, primary patency remained similar between groups (88.5% vs. 84.9%, log-rank p = 0.588), as did freedom from TLR, limb salvage, and overall survival. Findings were consistent across calcification-related subgroups. In an exploratory Cox analysis, second-generation LD-DCB was not associated with an increased risk of restenosis compared with HD-DCB.

CONCLUSIONS: After Jetstream atherectomy for severely calcified FPA lesions, second-generation LD-DCB and HD-DCB were associated with comparable 1-year clinical outcomes, suggesting that either strategy may be a reasonable treatment option.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Second-generation low-dose drug-coated balloons (LD-DCBs) have shown clinical efficacy comparable to high-dose DCBs (HD-DCBs) for femoropopliteal artery (FPA) lesions. Whether paclitaxel dose density remains clinically relevant after aggressive vessel preparation with atherectomy in severely calcified FPA lesions remains uncertain. This study aimed to compare 1-year clinical outcomes of second-generation LD-DCB and HD-DCB following Jetstream atherectomy in patients with severely calcified FPA lesions.

title: Fixed-Dose Combination Versus Add-On Therapy: Clarifying the Role of Cilostazol-Rosuvastatin in Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract: The randomized trial by Kemalasari et al. provides evidence supporting the addition of cilostazol to rosuvastatin in patients with symptomatic peripheral artery disease. However, because the study compared the fixed-dose combination (FDC) with rosuvastatin plus placebo, it does not establish whether the FDC formulation offers advantages over an equivalent free-combination regimen. Evidence from other cardiovascular settings suggests that FDC formulations may improve medication adherence and treatment persistence, although their effects on long-term clinical outcomes remain uncertain. Future randomized studies directly comparing fixed-dose and free-combination regimens, with adherence assessed over 12 months and longer-term cardiovascular and limb outcomes evaluated, are needed to clarify the clinical value of the formulation itself.

title: Influence of pathologic fractures on oncologic outcomes in extremity Ewing sarcoma: a single-institution retrospective study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathologic fractures occur in 5%-10% of patients with Ewing sarcoma and may influence the local treatment strategies. However, their prognostic impact remains unclear. This study evaluated the clinical course of patients with extremity Ewing sarcoma and pathologic fractures using a propensity score-matched analysis.

METHODS: This retrospective single-institution study reviewed 149 patients with extremity Ewing sarcoma treated between 2003 and 2020, including 12 patients (8.1%) with pathologic fractures. For comparison with patients without pathologic fractures, a 1:3 propensity score-matched control group (n = 36, adjusted group) was constructed.

RESULTS: Among the 12 patients, limb-sparing surgery was performed in 11 patients (91.7%), and limb salvage was finally achieved in 10 patients (83.3%). Three-year overall survival was 75.0% in patients with pathologic fractures, and 78.8% (unadjusted, P = .62) and 82.0% (adjusted, P = .60) in patients without pathologic fractures. Local recurrence was observed in two patients (16.7%) in the pathologic fracture group; both had a poor histologic response.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, pathologic fractures were not associated with a statistically significant difference in oncological outcomes. Limb-sparing surgery may be considered in selected patients, particularly when preoperative treatment is effective. However, the small number of the patients with the fracture limits statistical power and generalizability of the results.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Pathologic fractures occur in 5%-10% of patients with Ewing sarcoma and may influence the local treatment strategies. However, their prognostic impact remains unclear. This study evaluated the clinical course of patients with extremity Ewing sarcoma and pathologic fractures using a propensity score-matched analysis.

title: Venous thromboembolism and transfusion outcomes following intravenous tranexamic acid in primary total hip arthroplasty: A prospective two-center cohort study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used during total hip arthroplasty (THA) to reduce perioperative blood loss and transfusion requirements. Although extensive evidence supports its use, prospective real-world data from Latin America are limited. This study aimed to describe the incidence of symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE) and blood transfusion among patients receiving intravenous TXA during primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) at two institutions in Bogotá, Colombia.

METHODS: This prospective, observational, descriptive, two-center cohort study included consecutive adults who underwent elective primary THA. Patients received intravenous TXA according to institutional protocols. The primary outcome was the occurrence of symptomatic VTE, including deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism, ischemic stroke, and myocardial infarction during a 10-week follow-up period. The secondary outcomes included blood transfusion requirements, postoperative hemoglobin levels, and emergency department visits.

RESULTS: A total of 151 primary THAs were performed in 133 patients. One case of symptomatic DVT was diagnosed, corresponding to a VTE incidence of 0.75%. Five patients (3.8%) required postoperative blood transfusions, including two complex reconstructive procedures. The mean postoperative hemoglobin level was 11.8 ± 1.9 g/dL. No pulmonary embolism, ischemic stroke, or myocardial infarction was observed during the follow-up period.

CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective two-center cohort of patients receiving intravenous TXA during primary THA, including both conventional and complex cases, a low incidence of symptomatic VTE and transfusion was observed. These results provide prospective real-world evidence from a Latin American population and contribute to the regional literature on perioperative blood conservation strategies for primary THA.

Although extensive evidence supports its use, prospective real-world data from Latin America are limited. This study aimed to describe the incidence of symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE) and blood transfusion among patients receiving intravenous TXA during primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) at two institutions in Bogotá, Colombia.

title: Cost-utility analysis of surgical revascularization versus conservative management for adult moyamoya disease patients with posterior hemorrhage in Japan.
abstract:
AIMS: This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of surgical revascularization versus conservative management for adult moyamoya disease (MMD) patients with posterior hemorrhage from the perspective of the Japanese public healthcare payer.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We developed a combined decision tree and Markov model for adult posterior hemorrhagic MMD patients (mean age: 41 years; baseline modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2) over a 60-year lifetime horizon with 1-year cycles. We estimated the treatment effect using the composite endpoint hazard ratio (0.07) from the JAM Trial posterior hemorrhage subgroup as a proxy for the effect on recurrent hemorrhage. We informed health utilities with recent EQ-5D-5L data from the Fukuoka Stroke Registry, weighted by the Japan Stroke Data Bank. We estimated direct medical costs based on the national fee schedule. We discounted costs and outcomes at 2% annually. We set the willingness-to-pay threshold at JPY 7,500,000 per quality-adjusted life year (QALY).

RESULTS: In the base case, surgical revascularization yielded 21.49 QALYs for JPY 6,323,426 (USD 40,302), compared with 15.59 QALYs and JPY 5,308,637 (USD 33,835) for conservative management. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was JPY 172,220 (USD 1,098) per QALY, which falls below the reference value of JPY 7,500,000 per QALY. In scenario analyses with 5- and 10-year horizons, the ICERs were JPY 8,926,784 and JPY 2,031,693 per QALY, respectively. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis also favored surgical revascularization across the modeled parameter distributions.

LIMITATIONS: The base-case estimate of surgical efficacy was based on a composite outcome from a small subgroup, and long-term recurrence risks beyond the 5-year trial period remain uncertain.

CONCLUSION: Surgical revascularization is likely to be cost-effective for adult MMD patients with posterior hemorrhage within the Japanese healthcare system, although limited evidence leaves uncertainty about long-term rebleeding risks and the durability of surgical benefit.

title: Prediction of Stroke Outcome After Endovascular Thrombectomy From Clinical Characteristics: A Machine Learning Approach.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is challenging. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke. A total of 4353 patients who underwent EVT between 2016 and 2020 were included, with those from 2016 to 2019 assigned to the derivation cohort and those from 2020 to the validation cohort. The model was developed using 132 routinely collected clinical variables that can be rapidly obtained on patient arrival. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm, and the model was built using CatBoost. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0 to 2 at discharge.

RESULTS: Among 4353 patients treated with EVT, the derivation cohort included 2764 patients and the validation cohort, 1589 patients. In these cohorts, 973 (35.2%) and 547 (34.4%) achieved mRS 0 to 2, respectively. Boruta selected 47 predictors. CatBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.744 (95% CI, 0.710-0.776) in the derivation test set and 0.781 (95% CI, 0.755-0.803) in the validation cohort. Validation areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves were 0.792 (95% CI, 0.765-0.815) for mRS 0 to 1, 0.766 (95% CI, 0.744-0.787) for mRS 0 to 3, and 0.680 (95% CI, 0.631-0.729) for mRS 6.

CONCLUSIONS: Our machine learning model predicted outcomes following EVT using only admission clinical data. This imaging-independent machine learning approach may support early prognostication and facilitate discussions of expected clinical courses.

This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data. METHODS: We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke.

title: Predictors of Clinically Meaningful 1-Year Health Status Improvements Following Endovascular or Surgical Revascularization: Insights From the BEST-CLI Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite efforts to promote limb salvage in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the factors associated with meaningful health status improvement after revascularization remain poorly understood. We examined predictors of meaningful 1-year health status improvement following revascularization for CLTI.

METHODS: We pooled endovascular and surgical arms from the BEST-CLI (Best Endovascular Versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients With CLTI) randomized controlled trial, including patients with CLTI (150 international sites, 2014-2019). Health status was assessed at baseline and 1 year using the peripheral artery disease-specific Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire, the generic European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, and the Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary. Distribution-based minimal clinically important difference thresholds were defined as 0.5 SD of baseline health status scores. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of no meaningful 1-year improvement (same/worsened versus improved).

RESULTS: Among 1017 patients (72.0% men, mean age 66.8±9.7 years), clinically meaningful improvements were reported by 76.5% for Vascular Quality of Life, 52.8% European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, 56.7% for Short Form-12 Physical Component Summary, and 42.1% for Short Form-12 Mental Component Summary, regardless of revascularization type (surgical versus endovascular). Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status increased the odds of no meaningful improvement. Revascularization type was not associated with Vascular Quality of Life improvement (odds ratio, 1.059 [95% CI, 0.91-1.23]; P=0.445; C statistic=0.77).

CONCLUSIONS: One-year postrevascularization, over three-fourths of individuals with CLTI perceived meaningful improvements in peripheral artery disease-specific health, and over half improved overall physical health, regardless of procedure type. Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status predicted 1-year health status response. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02060630.

title: Comparison of Prosthetic Valve Deformation and Hemodynamic Performance Between Bicuspid and Tricuspid Aortic Valve Anatomy After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study compared prosthetic valve deformation and postprocedural hemodynamic performance between bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valve anatomy after transcatheter aortic valve replacement with the Venus-A prosthesis.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement between 2012 and 2022 and underwent postoperative computed tomography within 1 year. Predischarge echocardiographic assessments included the mean transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak. Computed tomography measurements included expansion ratio, ellipticity, implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening. The leaflet inflow and valve waist were collectively defined as the functional valve portion.

RESULTS: Among 212 patients (106 bicuspid and 106 tricuspid), the mean age was 74.2±7.6 years, and 43.9% were women. Patients with bicuspid anatomy had a significantly lower oversizing ratio and underwent balloon predilation and postdilation more frequently than those with tricuspid anatomy. Residual transvalvular gradients were higher with bicuspid than tricuspid anatomy (12.0 [interquartile range, 8.2-17.0] versus 10.0 [7.2-14.0] mm Hg; P=0.014), whereas moderate to severe paravalvular leak did not differ significantly. Prosthetic ellipticity was greater in bicuspid anatomy, but expansion ratios, including those within the functional valve portion, did not differ significantly. Implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening incidence also did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: Following Venus-A implantation, bicuspid anatomy was associated with greater prosthetic ellipticity and higher residual gradients, despite no significant difference in prosthetic expansion.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement between 2012 and 2022 and underwent postoperative computed tomography within 1 year. Predischarge echocardiographic assessments included the mean transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak.

title: Recurrent Multi-territory Thromboembolism As the Initial Presentation of Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma and Suspected Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis.
abstract: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE), also known as Marantic endocarditis, is an uncommon complication of malignancy that may cause systemic embolization. We report a 74-year-old woman who developed a right gastrocnemius deep vein thrombosis followed by recurrent right middle cerebral artery occlusions requiring two mechanical thrombectomies. Her subsequent course was complicated by further deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and acute limb ischemia. Repeat echocardiography demonstrated mitral valve vegetations, initially raising concern for infective endocarditis. However, repeated blood cultures and cultures of retrieved thrombotic material were negative. Imaging revealed widespread metastatic disease, and biopsy of a left supraclavicular lymph node confirmed metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The combination of recurrent arterial and venous thrombosis, advanced malignancy, and negative microbiological investigations favored a clinical diagnosis of NBTE. This case illustrates how extensive thromboembolic disease may precede the diagnosis of pancreatic cancer and highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by valvular vegetations in this setting.

We report a 74-year-old woman who developed a right gastrocnemius deep vein thrombosis followed by recurrent right middle cerebral artery occlusions requiring two mechanical thrombectomies. Her subsequent course was complicated by further deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and acute limb ischemia.

title: Severe gastric distension in a teenage boy.
abstract: A 16-year-old male presented with acute abdominal pain, nausea, and distension and was found to have severe gastric dilation on imaging. Antroduodenal manometry showed erythromycin-induced phase 3 migrating motor complex beginning in the antrum but post-prandial antral hypoactivity. Mitochondrial DNA sequencing was normal. Exome analysis revealed a rare variant of uncertain significance in the smooth muscle myosin heavy chain 11 (MYH11) gene (NM_002474.3: c.4123G>A, p.Asp1375Asn), which is necessary for smooth muscle contraction. Pathogenic MYH11 alterations cause multiple disorders, including autosomal dominant (AD) familial thoracic aortic aneurysm, AD visceral myopathy, and autosomal recessive megacystis-microcolon-intestinal-hypoperistalsis syndrome. Amino acid p.Asp1375 is within the rod region of the MYH11 protein that self-assembles to form thick filaments; thus, pathogenic variants in this region may affect filament formation and impair interactions with thin filaments. While the phenotype overlap is compelling, further research is needed to determine the clinical significance of this alteration.

title: Broadening the Indications for the SPING Block in Palliative Care: A Case Discussion.
abstract: The Spinal Phenol IN Glycerol (SPING) block is an intrathecal neurolytic technique developed to provide sustained unilateral analgesia in frail patients with nonoperative hip fractures. Its potential role in other palliative care populations remains unexplored. Two cases are described with refractory unilateral lower-limb pain: a 76-year-old male with metastatic esophageal cancer and acetabular metastasis, and an 86-year-old female with advanced dementia and critical limb ischemia. In both cases, systemic opioids failed and were associated with significant adverse effects. Both patients experienced rapid and clinically assessed sustained pain relief, reduced opioid requirements, and improved comfort until death. These two case reports suggest that SPING may provide effective palliative analgesia with opioid reduction in patients with refractory unilateral lower-limb pain caused by metastatic bone disease and critical limb ischemia. These findings support consideration of SPING as a proportionate palliative intervention beyond its current use for hip fractures when comfort is the primary goal.

title: Serglycin regulates macrophage differentiation and is associated with human atherosclerotic plaque stability.
abstract: Inflammation contributes to the destabilization of atherosclerotic plaques and increases the risk of cardiovascular events such as myocardial infarction and stroke. Extracellular matrix components modulate inflammation and immune responses within the plaque microenvironment. Serglycin (SRGN), is a proteoglycan primarily expressed by immune cells that regulates inflammation, but its role in human atherosclerotic plaques remains unclear. SRGN protein levels were quantified by ELISA in carotid endarterectomy samples from patients in the Atherosclerotic Plaque Imaging Project and compared between symptomatic and asymptomatic plaques. SRGN spatial localization was evaluated by multispectral imaging and histology. Glycosylation patterns were examined by immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting. Functional effects were investigated using CRISPR-mediated SRGN knockout in THP-1 monocytes differentiated into macrophages and exposed to oxidized low-density lipoprotein (oxLDL). SRGN levels were higher in plaques from asymptomatic patients compared with plaques from symptomatic patients and localized primarily to macrophage- and lipid-rich regions. Plaque SRGN was positively associated with histological markers of plaque stability, displayed heterogeneous molecular forms and showed an inverse association with the plaque vulnerability index. In vitro, SRGN deficiency was associated with a more pro-inflammatory macrophage profile, impaired M2-like polarization, and increased lipid retention following oxLDL exposure. These findings indicate that SRGN is associated with inflammatory cell presence, lipid accumulation, and features of plaque stability in human plaques, and suggest a role for SRGN in macrophage differentiation and lipid handling in atherosclerotic lesions.

title: Endpoint selection in clinical trials of revascularization devices for chronic limb-threatening ischemia: evolution of Japanese clinical evaluation guidance and regulatory perspectives.
abstract: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome characterized by ischemia, wounds, and infection and is associated with substantial risks of mortality, major amputation, pain, functional impairment, and diminished quality of life. These diverse clinical manifestations pose considerable challenges for selecting appropriate endpoints in clinical trials of revascularization devices. This article examines the selection and interpretation of clinical endpoints from a regulatory perspective, with particular emphasis on the evolution of Japanese clinical evaluation guidance, the regulatory review of Esprit BTK, and the characteristics of the Japanese CLTI population. The Esprit BTK case highlights a persistent evidentiary gap between demonstrating superior device performance, such as reduced restenosis, and determining whether such improvements translate into clinically meaningful benefits for patients and their limbs. To address this gap, we propose a six-step framework that is grouped into clinical conceptualization (Steps 1-2), endpoint design (Steps 3-5), and estimand and statistical strategy (Step 6). Dialysis status should be considered primarily when defining the target population, interpreting treatment effects, and evaluating the generalizability of trial findings, rather than as a determinant of endpoint selection. This framework is intended to promote greater consistency and interpretability in endpoint selection and to facilitate regulatory assessment of the benefit-risk profile of revascularization devices for CLTI.

title: Portal Vein Recanalization in Children with Extrahepatic Portal Vein Obstruction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To synthesize the technical success, safety, durability, and clinical efficacy of percutaneous portal vein recanalization in children with non-cirrhotic extrahepatic portal vein obstruction without underlying liver disease.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to May 2026 for pediatric patients with non-cirrhotic extrahepatic portal vein obstruction who underwent percutaneous portal vein recanalization. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals and prediction intervals.

RESULTS: Five retrospective single-center cohorts (73 children; variceal bleeding, hypersplenism, or both) were included. Pooled denominators were 67 for technical success, 54 for safety and mortality (Pimpalwar contributed to technical success only), and 16 for post-recanalization durability. Technical success was 55.0% (95% confidence interval 41.0-68.0; prediction interval 28.6-79.4). Procedure-related and all-cause mortality were both 0% (0/54); procedure-related hemorrhage 7% (95% confidence interval 2-23); and portal-biliary fistula 3% (95% confidence interval 0-27). Among the 16 children with successful recanalization and imaging follow-up, assisted portal vein patency was 87% (95% confidence interval 61-97); 50.8% required at least one endovascular re-intervention during surveillance, without surgical conversion; freedom from recurrent variceal or gastrointestinal bleeding among those with variceal bleeding as indication was 100% (prediction interval 73.8-100).

CONCLUSION: In children with chronic native-vessel extrahepatic portal vein obstruction, percutaneous portal vein recanalization may be feasible. No procedure-related mortality was observed, bleeding events were infrequent, and no recurrent variceal bleeding occurred after successful recanalization in patients for whom this outcome was reported.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, meta-analysis of case series and retrospective cohort studies.

TRIAL / PROTOCOL REGISTRATION: Prospectively registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO): CRD420261395918.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to May 2026 for pediatric patients with non-cirrhotic extrahepatic portal vein obstruction who underwent percutaneous portal vein recanalization. title: Stroke outcomes in patients with obesity undergoing recanalization therapy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The influence of obesity on stroke outcomes remains controversial. Some studies suggest a phenomenon known as the "obesity paradox", where patients with obesity may recover better. This study investigated the association between obesity and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients undergoing recanalization therapy.

METHODS: The ISOT Study was a prospective cohort study conducted at two comprehensive Stroke Centers in Switzerland between 01/2016 and 09/2021. The study enrolled patients treated with intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) and/or endovascular therapy (EVT) who were functionally independent prior to AIS (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2). Patients were classified into three weight groups: normal weight (BMI < 25 kg/m²), overweight (BMI 25.0-29.9 kg/m²), and obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²). Functional outcome was assessed after 3 months and 1 year. Logistic regression analyses adjusted for age and sex were performed.

RESULTS: Of the 271 patients enrolled (median age 70 years, 65% male, median NIHSS 5 [interquartile range 3-11]), 153 (56%) were treated with IVT, 56 (21%) with EVT and 62 (23%) with IVT + EVT). A total of 96 (35%) had normal weight, 113 (42%) were overweight and 62 (23%) had obesity. Obesity, when compared to normal weight, was associated with poor functional outcomes (mRS 3-6) at three months (24% vs 12%, p = 0.03; adjusted Odds Ratio [aOR] 2.82, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.16-6.88). At 1 year there was still a trend toward poorer outcomes (aOR 2.50, 95% CI 0.98-6.34). There was no difference between patients with normal weight and those who were overweight.

CONCLUSION: In this prospective cohort study, obesity was associated with worse functional outcomes at 3 months with a persistent trend at 1 year in AIS patients undergoing recanalization therapy. These findings provide exploratory, preliminary, hypothesis-generating evidence against the theory of the "obesity paradox" and warrant confirmation in larger cohorts.

This study investigated the association between obesity and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients undergoing recanalization therapy.

title: Incidence, diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes of abdominal aortic aneurysms in Ontario: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) management substantially changed in 2003 when endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) became readily available in Canada. The long-term implications to routine practice in Ontario are unknown. We therefore sought to estimate trends in stable (sAAA) and ruptured (rAAA) incidence, treatment (EVAR or open surgical repair [OSR]), and postoperative mortality.

METHODS: We constructed a population-based cohort study of patients with incident sAAA and rAAA in Ontario using administrative health data from April 2012 to March 2023. To assess patterns in incidence, autoregressive integrated moving average models were fit. Three population-level interventions were incorporated: a Canadian Society of Vascular Surgery (CSVS) position statement, sent to Ontario physicians in early 2018, about the Canadian AAA screening recommendations published in 2017; the COVID-19 pandemic onset in 2020; and publication of the CSVS screening guidelines for AAA in 2021.

RESULTS: In total, 24 619 patients were included. Patients were predominantly male (77.2%), from urban settings (87.1%), with low comorbidity (82.3%). There was a small month-over-month increase in reported sAAA identified following the CSVS position statement in 2018. Conversely, the COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a steep drop in sAAA reported, which remained thereafter. Publication of the CSVS screening guidelines in 2021 was not associated with a change in sAAA trends. Incidence of rAAA was also reduced during the pandemic but was not affected by either publication. Treatment with EVAR for rAAA increased from 10.2% to 18%, whereas treatment with OSR declined from 40.8% to 31.3%. Untreated sAAA increased from 28.2% to 42.7%. Thirty-day (54.7%) and 1-year (61.7%) postoperative mortality from rAAA was stable, whereas mortality from sAAA increased slightly (30-d: 5% to 6.5%; 1-yr: 14% to 16.5%).

CONCLUSION: Overall reporting of cases of sAAA and rAAA is decreasing in Ontario. The 2018 position statement on AAA screening guidelines led to slightly increased reported sAAA, while reporting of rAAA was not affected. As expected, the volume of patients with rAAA who received EVAR increased, while the volume of those who received OSR decreased.

The long-term implications to routine practice in Ontario are unknown. title: Truncal Marginal Veins in CLOVES and PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum: Anatomic Patterns and Potential Clinical Insights for Diagnosis and Endovascular Treatments.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe the anatomy, clinical features, and endovascular treatment outcomes of truncal marginal veins (TMVs) involving the chest or abdominal wall in patients with Congenital Lipomatous Overgrowth, Vascular Malformations, Epidermal nevi, and Skeletal abnormalities (CLOVES) and PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum (PROS).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The Vascular Anomalies Center database was retrospectively reviewed from 2008 to January 2026 to identify patients with TMVs. Imaging was reviewed for TMV diameter, origin, and insertion. Patient demographics, endovascular treatments, and follow-up data were analyzed.

RESULTS: Thirty-two patients (53% male; median age 4.2 years; CLOVES [n=26], PROS [n=6]) with 44 TMVs were included. TMVs were unilateral in 20 patients and bilateral in 12. The median TMV diameter was 9.0 mm. TMVs most commonly originated from the abdominal wall (n=21), followed by the chest wall (n=9), saphenofemoral junction (n=9), and lateral marginal vein (n=5). The most common insertion site was axillary vein (n=39) followed by the abdominal wall (n=5). Thirty embolization procedures were performed in 25 patients; a single embolic agent was used in 20 procedures and multiple agents in 10. The most commonly used agents were coils (n=26) and n-butyl cyanoacrylate glue (n=9). No treatment-related adverse events occurred. Among 26 treated TMVs with imaging follow-up (median 23 months), partial recanalization occurred in two TMVs (8%), whereas 24 (92%) remained completely occluded.

CONCLUSION: In this predominantly CLOVES cohort, TMVs most often arise from the abdominal wall and drain into the axillary vein, and endovascular treatment of TMVs appears safe, effective, and durable on imaging follow-up.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The Vascular Anomalies Center database was retrospectively reviewed from 2008 to January 2026 to identify patients with TMVs. title: Association of Cutaneous Keloids and Hypertrophic Scarring with Risk of Postoperative Arthrofibrosis After Total Knee Arthroplasty.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arthrofibrosis is a debilitating postoperative complication and a leading cause of readmission, failure, and revision surgery. The purpose of this study was to assess the association between cutaneous keloids, hypertrophic scarring, and risk of arthrofibrosis after primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA).

METHODS: Patients undergoing TKA (n = 248,094) were identified using a large national database. Exclusions included a TKA for fracture, post-traumatic osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, or congenital deformity, or a second TKA within two years. Remaining patients were assigned to a keloid cohort (prior diagnoses of hypertrophic scarring, acne keloids, or scar fibrosis; n = 6,307) and matched 1:1 to controls by demographics and comorbidities. After propensity score matching, 6,305 patients remained per cohort with no significant baseline differences. Outcomes were compared using Chi-square tests at 30 days, 60 days, one year, and two years postoperatively, with significance set at P < 0.0083 (0.05 of 6).

RESULTS: The Keloid cohort demonstrated significantly higher rates of arthrofibrosis at 60 days (odds ratio (OR) = 2.06, P < 0.001), one year (OR = 1.54, P < 0.001), and two years (OR = 1.55, P < 0.001); revision TKA at one year (OR = 1.74, P = 0.002), and two years (OR = 1.50, P = 0.006); manipulation under anesthesia at 60 days, one year, and two years (P < 0.001); and periprosthetic joint infection within 30 days (OR = 2.05, P < 0.001). There were no significant associations found for lysis of adhesions or deep vein thrombosis (DVT).

CONCLUSION: Patients who had preoperative cutaneous keloids or hypertrophic scarring demonstrate significantly higher rates of arthrofibrosis, revision TKA, manipulation under anesthesia, and periprosthetic joint infection following primary TKA. A dermatologic history of keloids and hypertrophic scarring may serve as a risk factor for identifying high-risk TKA patients.

The purpose of this study was to assess the association between cutaneous keloids, hypertrophic scarring, and risk of arthrofibrosis after primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA). METHODS: Patients undergoing TKA (n = 248,094) were identified using a large national database.

title: [Endovascular Aortic Repair (EVAR): Intravascular Ultrasound (IVUS) Procedures Compared to X-ray Procedures - a Retrospective Mono-centre Pilot Study].
abstract:
PURPOSE: Endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) is the most common procedure to treat abdominal aortic aneurysms and employs X-rays and contrast medium to visualise arteries. However, both X-rays and contrast agents bear considerable hazards, not only for patients, but for the surgical staff, too. In this monocentric pilot study, the impacts of intra-vascular ultrasound (IVUS) on quality and safety were examined, together with the dose of radiation and contrast agent.

PATIENTS, MATERIALS AND METHODS: From 2017 to 2022, a total of 59 patients were retrospectively included, using intravascular ultrasound. 52 men (88%) and 7 women (12%) were compared, with a historic group employing standard EVAR. The group of 59 patients was then divided into 2 groups: one with procedures including IVUS, radiation and contrast agents, the other one excluding contrast agents.

RESULTS: The historical group and the IVUS group did not differ with respect to patient data and results, but the dose of radiation was drastically reduced in the IVUS group. Comparing groups 1 and 2 of the IVUS group, there were no statistically significant differences with regard to gender, age, BMI, anaesthesia, diameter of the aneurysm, angulation of the neck, or symptoms, p > 0.05. Moreover, the amount of endoleaks (1a/b, 3, 4), mortality as well as complication rates did not differ, p > 0.05. However, significant differences could be demonstrated for the dosage of radiation (dose area product [DAP] group 1 53704 mGy ∙ cm2 [9036-312669] versus group 2 26653 mGy ∙ cm2 [1074-118825], p < 0.001), time of surgery (85.96 min [28-194] versus 69.60 min [27-96], p = 0.026), time of radiation (10.60 min [1-29.12] versus 7.05 min [0.48-24.37], p = 0.003), and amount of contrast medium (27.21 ml [7-65] versus 0 ml, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: EVAR employing IVUS and X-ray was shown to be as safe as standard EVAR regarding procedure quality and patient outcome. However, the dosage of radiation as well as contrast agent can be significantly reduced, decreasing health hazards for patients and surgical staff. Therefore, the use of IVUS for EVAR is strongly recommended for all centres of vascular surgery.

However, both X-rays and contrast agents bear considerable hazards, not only for patients, but for the surgical staff, too. In this monocentric pilot study, the impacts of intra-vascular ultrasound (IVUS) on quality and safety were examined, together with the dose of radiation and contrast agent.

title: Discovery and Optimization of Anticancer Dibenzothiazepinones That Target the Ribosome Biogenesis Factor NVL.
abstract: Using inducible forward genetics, we recently discovered a dibenzothiazepinone (1) with activity against cancer cells via inhibition of the ribosome biogenesis factor NVL (nuclear valosin-containing protein-like). Herein, we delineate a comprehensive structure-activity relationship (SAR) study that explores the structural space surrounding the dibenzothiazepinone scaffold. A series of 115 analogs were synthesized and evaluated for activity against the colorectal cancer cell line HCT116 and counter-screened against cells CRISPR engineered to express a compound-resistant mutation in NVL. Our initial medicinal chemistry-driven campaign focused on improving potency, metabolic stability, and in vivo exposure and clearance. A fluorescence polarization assay with recombinant human NVL established a correlation between NVL-binding and antiproliferative activity. Cryo-EM structures of human NVL with select inhibitors revealed a binding mode that is consistent with the SAR data. This study led to the in vivo analog 100 (MM927), which we reported to suppress tumor growth in vivo without detectable toxicity via targeting the NVL.

title: Aortic Dissection After Stage 1 Palliation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric aortic dissection (AD) is rare and usually associated with hypertension or aortopathies. In this case, we present a Stanford type B dissection in an asymptomatic patient with single ventricle heart disease without known genetic aortopathy following stage 1 palliation.

CASE SUMMARY: Dissection was diagnosed on routine catheterization and confirmed on computed tomography angiography. There was no progression, so no surgical intervention was pursued. He underwent stage 2 palliation at age 6 months and continues to do well.

DISCUSSION: AD is rare in pediatrics, especially infants without aortopathy. A single iatrogenic case report after hybrid palliation has been described. Our patient had at least 2 risk factors, aortic coarctation and intermittently elevated blood pressure, that could have predisposed him to dissection.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: AD is rarely seen following the Norwood operation. Stanford type B AD can be safely medically managed in pediatric patients as in the adult guidelines.

title: Hybrid and endovascular repair of aberrant subclavian artery aneurysms and Kommerell diverticulum: single-center experience and long-term outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aberrant subclavian artery (ASA) represents the most frequent congenital anomaly of the aortic arch and may occasionally develop aneurysmal dilation (aASA) at risk of dissection or rupture. Early diagnosis and tailored management are therefore crucial. We report our long-term single-center experience with endovascular and hybrid repair of aASA and Kommerell's diverticulum (KD).

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed all consecutive patients treated for aASA between January 2010 and June 2024 at our tertiary referral center. Primary endpoints were primary technical success, perioperative and late mortality, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included symptom evolution, reinterventions, and complications.

RESULTS: Ten patients (5 females, 50%; mean age 62±19 years, range 16-80) were included. Seven (70%) presented with right ASA, and two (20%) with right aortic arch and left ASA. Seven patients (70%) were symptomatic; 43% had acute type B aortic dissection, 14% type A, and 28% descending thoracic aortic aneurysm. Four patients (40%) underwent total endovascular repair, and four (40%) hybrid procedures. Primary technical success was achieved in all cases, with no intraoperative deaths. Perioperative mortality was 10% and late mortality 30%. Complications included type II endoleak, access-site hematoma or infection, and transient upper-limb ischemia. No MACE occurred during the study period.

CONCLUSIONS: Hybrid and endovascular approaches appear to represent safe and effective alternatives to open repair for complex aASA anatomy when performed in experienced referral centers. Given the limited cohort size, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

Early diagnosis and tailored management are therefore crucial. We report our long-term single-center experience with endovascular and hybrid repair of aASA and Kommerell's diverticulum (KD).

title: Longitudinal Endoleak Behaviour Following Complex Aortic Repair With Branched Devices.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine the incidence, natural history, outcomes and risk factors of endoleak following branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) for complex abdominal aortic aneurysm (cAAA) and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs).

METHODS: This retrospective, single-centre study enrolled patients with cAAA and TAAA treated with BEVAR. Patients with at least 1 target vessel incorporated using directional branches were included. End points were spontaneous resolution of endoleak detected on completion angiography, 3-year freedom from persistent type I/III endoleak and endoleak-related reintervention. Multivariable Cox regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors for type II endoleak (T2EL) and branch-related endoleak (BREL).

RESULTS: In a 6-year period, 298 patients underwent fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) of which 129 patients (mean age 72 ± 9 years; 62% male) underwent F/BEVAR for 36 cAAA (27.9%) and 93 TAAA (72.1%) with at least 1 directional branch. In all, 458 reno-mesenteric arteries were incorporated using directional branches. Completion intra-operative angiography detected endoleak in 81 patients (64.8%), of which 43.2% demonstrated spontaneous resolution on postoperative computed tomographic angiography. During a mean follow-up of 20.2 ± 19.9 months, 14 branches (3.0%) in 14 patients (10.9%) developed BREL, predominantly type Ic. Freedom from persistent type I/III endoleak and endoleak-related reintervention were 70.6% and 68.5% at 3 years, respectively. Aneurysm diameter ≥80 mm (hazard ratio [HR] 2.76, 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.54-4.95; P < .001), post-dissection aetiology (HR 1.84, 95% CI, 1.02-3.33; P = .043) and accessory renal artery (ARA) ≥3 mm in diameter that was not incorporated or pre-emptively embolised (HR 2.03, 95% CI, 1.11-3.74; P = .022) were identified as independent risk factors for T2EL.

CONCLUSION: Immediate endoleak following BEVAR was common, but a substantial proportion were self-limiting. Type Ic endoleak was the most common type of BREL and the most frequent indication for endoleak-related reintervention. Large aneurysm diameter, post-dissection aetiology and ARA increased risk for T2EL.Clinical ImpactEndoleak following branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) was commonly detected on completion angiography; however, immediate intervention was not required after ensuring adequate sealing zones and optimised bridging stent configuration, as 43% demonstrated spontaneous resolution on early postoperative imaging. Type Ic endoleak was the predominant form of branch-related endoleak, highlighting the importance of meticulous attention to target vessel landing zones. When anatomically feasible, incorporation of accessory renal artery ≥3 mm in the repair is recommended; alternatively, pre-emptive embolisation may reduce type II endoleak incidence.

title: Prognostic Impact of Post-Contrast Acute Kidney Injury in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease Undergoing Endovascular Aortic Repair.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-contrast acute kidney injury (PC-AKI) has been regarded as a serious complication after contrast administration, particularly in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, the prognostic significance of PC-AKI following endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) remains controversial due to heterogeneity in previous study populations. This study evaluated the association between PC-AKI and longitudinal changes in postoperative renal function and mortality in a well-defined CKD cohort undergoing EVAR.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective study of patients with CKD undergoing elective, primary, and non-complex infrarenal EVAR. Patients were classified according to the presence or absence of PC-AKI. Longitudinal changes in serum creatinine after EVAR, dialysis initiation, all-cause mortality, and the association between contrast volume and PC-AKI were evaluated.

RESULTS: Among 479 EVAR procedures, 164 patients with CKD were included, of whom 17 (10.4%) developed PC-AKI. The linear mixed-effects model showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P < .001). Serum creatinine remained significantly higher in the PC-AKI group than in the non-PC-AKI group at all postoperative time points. However, in the PC-AKI group, model-adjusted mean serum creatinine decreased significantly from 1.75 mg/dL in the postoperative period to 1.46 mg/dL at 12 months with an estimated change of -0.29 mg/dL (95% CI, -0.50 to -0.09; P = .003). No significant differences were observed in dialysis initiation (5.9% vs 0.7%; P = .197) or all-cause mortality (29.4% vs 23.8%; P = .565). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant difference in overall survival between the groups (log-rank P = .246). In the multivariable analysis, contrast volume was not independently associated with PC-AKI (odds ratio [OR], 1.00; 95% CI, 0.98-1.01; P = .845), whereas lower preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate remained significantly associated with PC-AKI (OR, 1.06 per 1 mL/min/1.73 m2 decrease; 95% CI, 1.01-1.12; P = .018).

CONCLUSION: In this study, PC-AKI may not necessarily be associated with adverse subsequent renal or survival outcomes. In addition, underlying renal vulnerability may be more closely associated with the development of PC-AKI than contrast volume alone. While PC-AKI should not be disregarded, judicious contrast use to ensure appropriate assessment may be reasonable even in patients with CKD.Clinical ImpactPost-contrast acute kidney injury (PC-AKI) occurred in approximately 10% of patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) undergoing elective, primary, non-complex infrarenal endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Although serum creatinine remained higher in patients with PC-AKI at all postoperative time points, it decreased significantly from the postoperative period to 12 months. No significant differences were observed in dialysis initiation or overall survival between the groups. In addition, contrast volume was not independently associated with PC-AKI, whereas lower preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate was. These findings suggest that contrast use should not be excessively restricted solely because of concerns regarding PC-AKI, and that judicious contrast use to ensure appropriate assessment may be reasonable even in patients with CKD.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Post-contrast acute kidney injury (PC-AKI) has been regarded as a serious complication after contrast administration, particularly in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, the prognostic significance of PC-AKI following endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) remains controversial due to heterogeneity in previous study populations. This study evaluated the association between PC-AKI and longitudinal changes in postoperative renal function and mortality in a well-defined CKD cohort undergoing EVAR.

title: Early neurological events after carotid revascularization and estimated whole blood viscosity.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the association between preprocedural estimated whole blood viscosity (eWBV) and the 30-day composite outcome of stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) following carotid revascularization.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 247 patients who underwent elective carotid revascularization between 2020 and 2024, comprising 105 patients who underwent carotid endarterectomy (CEA) and 142 who underwent carotid artery stenting (CAS). eWBV at high and low shear rates was estimated using the de Simone equations based on hematocrit and total plasma protein levels measured within 24 h before the procedure. The associations between eWBV and the primary outcome were assessed using separate logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, symptomatic status, stenosis severity, and procedure type.

RESULTS: Stroke or TIA occurred within 30 days after the procedure in 15 of 247 patients (6.1%), including 6 of 105 patients (5.7%) who underwent CEA and 9 of 142 patients (6.3%) who underwent CAS (p=0.839). After adjustment for the prespecified covariates, the odds ratio for the primary outcome was 25.95 (95% confidence interval [CI], 4.37-154.10) per 1-cP increase in high-shear-rate viscosity and 7.57 (95% CI, 2.52-22.75) per 10-cP increase in low-shear-rate viscosity (both p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Higher preprocedural eWBV was associated with an increased likelihood of neurological events within 30 days after carotid revascularization. However, given the small number of outcome events and the substantial uncertainty reflected in the wide CIs, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Prospective studies are needed to validate these associations before eWBV can be considered for clinical use.

title: Deep Vein Thrombosis Complicated by the Dissemination of Muscular Tuberculosis due to Acupuncture Treatment.
abstract: ObjectivesTo present a rare case of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the right upper extremity caused by muscular tuberculosis (MTB), likely disseminated via acupuncture, and to describe the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges encountered.MethodsThis case report details the clinical presentation, diagnostic workup, and management of a patient with MTB-associated DVT. The patient was treated with standard anti-tuberculosis therapy (rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol) along with anticoagulation therapy (low-molecular-weight heparin and rivaroxaban). Surgical intervention (debridement and drainage) was required due to abscess formation during treatment.ResultsInitially, the patient's DVT had an unclear etiology but was ultimately attributed to MTB. Despite complications including tuberculous abscess formation, combined medical and surgical management led to a successful outcome with resolution of infection and thrombosis.ConclusionsMuscular tuberculosis, though rare, should be considered in cases of unexplained DVT, particularly in patients with risk factors such as invasive procedures (eg, acupuncture). Early diagnosis, combined anti-TB therapy, anticoagulation, and surgical intervention, when necessary, can lead to favorable outcomes.

title: Ruff Shift Recharge: Feasibility and Acceptability of Canine-Assisted Breaks for Night-Shift Psychiatric Nurses.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of canine-assisted breaks for night-shift psychiatric nurses and the practicality of participant measures and canine welfare monitoring in inpatient staff-focused animal-assisted activity (AAA) research.

METHODS: Night-shift nurses (N = 11) were offered voluntary drop-in AAA breaks over 3 weeks at an inpatient psychiatric facility. Feasibility indicators included enrollment, attendance, survey completion, canine welfare monitoring, and adverse events. Acceptability indicators included session duration, observed engagement, and participant feedback. Mood was assessed before and after each break using the Positive and Negative Affect Schedule. Burnout and well-being were assessed 1 week before and after the intervention period. Outcomes were summarized descriptively. Therapy dog welfare was monitored through structured observation and repeated Canine Behavioral Assessment and Research Questionnaire assessments.

RESULTS: Eight nurses participated in 21 AAA breaks; durations ranged from 2 to 47 min (M = 22.3 min). Break-embedded data collection and canine welfare monitoring did not disrupt workflow, but follow-up survey attrition limited postintervention data. Feedback respondents described improved mood and energy and reduced stress. None of the 21 AAA breaks were terminated for canine stress. One site visit ended 30 min early after stress occurred without participants present.

CONCLUSIONS: Drop-in AAA breaks were deliverable and acceptable to participating nurses at this site. Findings do not establish effectiveness, comparative advantage, mechanism, sustainability, or generalizability. Future studies should retain structured canine welfare monitoring and include usual-break and active nonanimal comparison conditions.

METHODS: Night-shift nurses (N = 11) were offered voluntary drop-in AAA breaks over 3 weeks at an inpatient psychiatric facility. Feasibility indicators included enrollment, attendance, survey completion, canine welfare monitoring, and adverse events.

title: Real-world characteristics of endovascular treatment for middle cerebral artery M2 segment occlusion in Fukushima Prefecture: a prospective multicenter registry study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of endovascular treatment (EVT) in middle cerebral artery M2 segment occlusion remains inconclusive, particularly in rural areas with aging populations. We characterized EVT and medical management (MM) for M2 occlusion in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan, and explored clinical factors associated with outcomes.

METHODS: We analyzed a prospective multicenter acute ischemic stroke registry (July 2020-June 2022; 11 stroke centers). Patients with M2 occlusion were classified into EVT or MM groups; characteristics, workflow metrics, and outcomes were described and referenced against previously reported series.

RESULTS: Among 210 patients, 34 had M2 occlusion (EVT, n=10; MM, n=24). At 90 days, functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2) was 40.0% (EVT) and 45.8% (MM); symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage, 0% and 4.2%; mortality, 20.0% and 12.5%; successful reperfusion, 70.0% (EVT). Both groups were older than in previous reports (median 81 years). The EVT group also received rt-PA less often (30.0%) and had longer puncture-to-reperfusion times (81 minutes), whereas the MM group had lower pre-stroke independence (67%) and higher mortality, despite lower severity.

CONCLUSION: Advanced age, delayed reperfusion, and greater pre-stroke dependency distinguished this rural cohort from previous reports and likely account for its outcomes, underscoring the need for locally tailored patient selection for EVT in M2 occlusion.

We characterized EVT and medical management (MM) for M2 occlusion in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan, and explored clinical factors associated with outcomes. METHODS: We analyzed a prospective multicenter acute ischemic stroke registry (July 2020-June 2022; 11 stroke centers).

title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results.

METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points.

RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results.

CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion.

title: Risk of recurrence in patients with provoked venous thromboembolism: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) provoked by transient risk factors is generally considered low risk, supporting short-term anticoagulation. However, this paradigm is based on heterogeneous definitions of provoking factors. In this prospective cohort study, we evaluated recurrence risk using the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis classification of major and minor transient risk factors. Patients with symptomatic deep vein thrombosis and/or pulmonary embolism who completed ≥3 months of anticoagulation were followed after treatment discontinuation. Patients with cancer, major thrombophilia, pregnancy-associated VTE, or indication for extended anticoagulation were excluded. The primary outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE. Cumulative incidence was estimated by Kaplan-Meier analysis. The study was terminated early due to unexpectedly high recurrence risk among patients with major provoking factors. Between 2019 and 2025, 242 patients were followed for a median of 23.9 months; 72 had major and 170 had minor transient risk factors. Recurrent VTE occurred in 13 patients with major and 7 with minor risk factors. At 24 months, recurrence risk was 9.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 6.0-14.0) overall and 19.7% (11.0-30.2) after major and 5.0% (2.2-9.5) after minor risk factors. No recurrence occurred in 81 women with hormone-associated VTE; after their exclusion, the recurrence risk among patients with other minor risk factors increased to 9.1% (95% CI, 4.0-17.0). Recurrence after provoked VTE is not uniformly low and varies substantially by the type of transient risk factor. These findings challenge current treatment paradigms and support individualized decisions regarding anticoagulation duration.

However, this paradigm is based on heterogeneous definitions of provoking factors. In this prospective cohort study, we evaluated recurrence risk using the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis classification of major and minor transient risk factors.

title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist Exposure and Long-Term Outcomes in Patients with Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis: A Propensity Score-Matched Real-World Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Asymptomatic carotid stenosis is a prevalent manifestation of atherosclerotic disease and, despite contemporary guideline-directed medical therapy, remains associated with downstream cerebrovascular events and mortality. Given the vascular and cardiometabolic benefits of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1As), we evaluated whether GLP-1A exposure is associated with lower long-term event rates in patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study used the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adults (≥18 years) with carotid stenosis (January 1, 2016, to September 30, 2025) were included; patients with prior/baseline cerebrovascular events and those undergoing carotid revascularization within 6 months were excluded to operationalize an asymptomatic cohort. GLP-1A exposure was defined as any GLP-1A use within 6 months after carotid stenosis diagnosis; nonexposed patients served as comparators. Cohorts were propensity score-matched 1:1, and outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: After matching, 30,332 patients were included in each cohort. GLP-1A exposure was associated with lower hazards of ischemic stroke (hazard ratio [HR] 0.63, 0.71, and 0.73 at 1, 3, and 5 years; 5-year cumulative event probability 5.55% versus 6.85%), hemorrhagic stroke (HR 0.63, 0.69, and 0.74; 2.04% versus 2.35%), large vessel occlusion stroke (HR 0.70, 0.77, and 0.81; 2.04% versus 2.27%), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.42, 0.58, and 0.64; 17.11% versus 21.49%). The composite of ischemic stroke or mortality was also lower (HR 0.48, 0.61, and 0.66; 20.88% versus 25.85% at 5 years) in the GLP-1A-exposed cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: In a large real-world cohort with asymptomatic carotid stenosis, GLP-1A exposure was associated with lower hazards of stroke subtypes, large vessel occlusion stroke, and mortality across 1-5 years. These observational findings warrant prospective validation to clarify causality and optimal integration into contemporary medical management.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Asymptomatic carotid stenosis is a prevalent manifestation of atherosclerotic disease and, despite contemporary guideline-directed medical therapy, remains associated with downstream cerebrovascular events and mortality. Given the vascular and cardiometabolic benefits of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1As), we evaluated whether GLP-1A exposure is associated with lower long-term event rates in patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study used the TriNetX US Collaborative Network.

title: Global landscape and evolution of limb-salvage reconstruction with prostheses for primary malignant bone and soft tissue tumours: A bibliometric analysis.
abstract: PurposeTo delineate the evolution, collaborative structure, clinically relevant themes, and emerging priorities of limb-salvage prosthetic reconstruction for primary malignant bone and soft tissue tumours.MethodsEnglish-language articles and reviews published from 1 January 1995 to 31 October 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection on 31 October 2025. Co-authorship, co-citation, keyword co-occurrence and burst analyses were conducted using CiteSpace 6.4.1 and VOSviewer 1.6.20.ResultsOf 2,606 retrieved records, 2,283 underwent title and abstract screening and 997 were included. Publication output increased, peaking at 84 in 2023. The United States led publication output and cumulative citations, while China ranked second by output. Keyword analyses indicated that research attention expanded from surgical strategy selection for specific tumour types and anatomical sites to include long-term prosthetic survival, complications and functional outcomes. Recent research themes included technologies such as 3D printing, computer-assisted navigation and finite element analysis, with "3d printing" showing the strongest keyword burst (strength 9.49; 2021-2025). Research output was concentrated in a small number of centres and journals. Frequently co-cited publications provided standardised methods for assessing limb function and classifying endoprosthetic failure.ConclusionsLong-term prosthetic survival, complications, function and quality of life remain central themes in limb-salvage prosthetic reconstruction. Technologies supporting individualised reconstruction, including 3D printing, computer-assisted navigation and emerging robot-assisted techniques, are attracting increasing research interest. Future multicentre comparative studies should use standardised outcome measures and long-term follow-up to evaluate prosthesis design, fixation and selection, as well as strategies for preventing and managing reconstructive failure.

title: Cilengitide limits syndromic and sporadic thoracic aortic aneurysm by targeting specific αV integrin.
abstract: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is one of the major causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, still lacking an etiologic therapy. Aberrant activation of TGF-β and dysregulation of mechanotransduction signalling in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) play a key role in the pathology. However, a precise picture of molecular mechanisms in the disease is still unclear. Integrins containing the αV subunit are central in pro-fibrotic pathways mediated by TGF-β and mechanotransduction signalling pathways, but their role as a potential therapeutic target in syndromic and sporadic TAAs still needs investigation. We showed higher expression levels of αV integrin in both types of human TAAs and that the αV integrin inhibitor Cilengitide limits pro-fibrotic events in patient-derived VSMCs. In vivo results defined Cilengitide as the most effective and promising drug for the treatment of TAAs in humans.

title: Selective coil embolization of hepatic artery pseudoaneurysm causing hemobilia secondary to hemorrhagic hepatic hydatid cyst: A case report.
abstract: Hemobilia secondary to intrabiliary rupture of a hepatic hydatid cyst is rare, and concomitant arterial pseudoaneurysm formation further increases the risk of life-threatening hemorrhage. Case: An 80-year-old woman presented with 3 months of melena, progressing to large-volume melena and hematemesis. She was hypotensive and severely anemic (hemoglobin 6.0 g/dL). Upper endoscopy revealed a clot at the sphincter of Oddi, consistent with hemobilia. Multiphase CT showed a right-lobe hydatid cyst with active intracystic arterial extravasation and communication with the biliary ducts, with additional right-lobe hydatid cysts. Angiography identified a pseudoaneurysm arising from a segment V branch of the right hepatic artery. Given the patient's advanced age, hemodynamic instability, and high surgical risk, emergent selective endovascular embolization-rather than surgery-was chosen as first-line treatment, and superselective coil embolization achieved hemostasis. Post-procedure, hemoglobin improved to 10.6 g/dL by day 4; follow-up CT at day 4 demonstrated resolution of the pseudoaneurysm without rebleeding. Albendazole therapy was initiated after embolization. Echinococcus serology was not available, and reported follow-up was limited to 4 days; these are acknowledged as limitations. Conclusion: In elderly or hemodynamically unstable patients with hemorrhagic hydatid cyst and hemobilia, selective endovascular embolization can provide rapid, organ-preserving control of bleeding and a bridge to definitive antiparasitic management, although longer-term data are needed.

Case: An 80-year-old woman presented with 3 months of melena, progressing to large-volume melena and hematemesis. She was hypotensive and severely anemic (hemoglobin 6.0 g/dL).

title: Ruptured pheochromocytoma during preoperative doxazosin treatment.
abstract: Rupture of pheochromocytoma is rare but represents a life-threatening complication. A 43-year-old man with episodic hypertension, palpitations, and chest discomfort was incidentally found, during a computed tomography (CT) aortogram performed to rule out aortic dissection, to have a 5.2-cm right adrenal mass suspicious for pheochromocytoma. Biochemical testing confirmed catecholamine excess. He was started on oral doxazosin 1 mg daily, which was titrated to 2 mg daily after 1 week, followed by oral bisoprolol 2.5 mg daily in preparation for surgery. Five weeks later, he presented with severe right-sided abdominal pain and a blood pressure of 215/111 mmHg. Abdominal CT angiography showed interval enlargement of the adrenal mass with posterior rupture and a retroperitoneal hematoma without active bleeding. He was stabilized with conservative management and subsequently underwent robotic right adrenalectomy. Histopathology confirmed pheochromocytoma with necrosis, without angioinvasion or lymphatic invasion, and with negative margins. Pheochromocytoma rupture can occur despite appropriate α-blockade, and spontaneous hemorrhage remains the most likely proposed mechanism, although α-blockade may be a contributing factor in selected cases.
