title: Association of autoimmune diseases and transient risk factors with clinical outcomes in patients with venous thromboembolism: COMMAND VTE registry insights.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transient provoking factors are generally associated with a lower risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE). Whether this association also applies to patients with autoimmune diseases, which constitute persistent risk factors, remains uncertain.

METHODS: We analyzed 6022 patients with acute symptomatic VTE without active cancer from the retrospective, multicenter COMMAND VTE Registries, including 734 with and 5288 without autoimmune diseases. Within each subgroup, clinical outcomes were compared across major, minor, and no transient provoking factor categories, using the no transient factor category as the reference.

RESULTS: Compared with patients without autoimmune diseases, those with autoimmune diseases had higher risks of recurrent VTE [adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.73; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.31-2.28] and major bleeding (adjusted HR 1.45; 95% CI 1.14-1.83). In analyses stratified by autoimmune disease status, major transient provoking factors, compared with no transient provoking factors, were associated with a lower risk of recurrent VTE among patients without autoimmune diseases (adjusted HR 0.30; 95% CI 0.19-0.48). This association was less clear among patients with autoimmune diseases (adjusted HR 0.92; 95% CI 0.36-2.35). A similar pattern was observed in the landmark analysis after anticoagulation discontinuation.

CONCLUSIONS: The association between transient provoking factors and a lower recurrence risk was less clear in patients with autoimmune diseases. These findings suggest that transient provoking factor status alone may provide limited guidance for recurrence risk assessment in this population, although imprecise estimates preclude firm conclusions.

title: Medial Arterial Calcification in Diabetic Foot Disease: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Perfusion Assessment, and Implications for Pre-Revascularization Evaluation.
abstract: Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of ulceration, infection, lower-extremity amputation, and premature mortality. Medial arterial calcification (MAC), characterised by calcium-phosphate deposition within the arterial media, is associated with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and neuropathy. It complicates perfusion assessment and is associated with adverse limb outcomes. Its implications for interpreting perfusion tests, assessing prognosis, and evaluating patients before revascularization remain insufficiently integrated in the existing literature. This narrative review examines MAC as a distal arterial phenotype with diagnostic and prognostic relevance in diabetic foot disease. Targeted PubMed searches updated on 22 September 2026, supplemented by reference checking and topic-specific searches, informed a qualitative synthesis of clinical, imaging, and mechanistic studies. The review distinguishes medial from intimal calcification and evaluates recognition, scoring, and renal, metabolic, and neurovascular mechanisms. Observational cohorts of diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) and chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) link higher calcification burden with delayed healing, amputation, incomplete haemodynamic improvement, and selected systemic outcomes, although adjustment and endpoint definitions vary. In the MAC-prone diabetic foot, reliance on the ankle-brachial index alone may be misleading because calcified tibial and pedal arteries can produce falsely normal or elevated ankle pressures. Toe pressure, toe-brachial index (TBI), transcutaneous oxygen tension (TcPO2), skin perfusion pressure (SPP), anatomical imaging, and careful wound trajectory assessment should therefore be integrated with established limb-threat and anatomical classifications. Emerging evidence suggests that MAC scoring may complement Wound, Ischaemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) staging, Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS) assessment, and small artery disease scoring in estimating wound-healing probability and amputation risk before revascularization. MAC scoring remains an adjunctive risk marker rather than a validated determinant of revascularization modality or a proven therapeutic target. Prospective studies should determine whether adding MAC assessment to established clinical models improves management and patient outcomes.

It complicates perfusion assessment and is associated with adverse limb outcomes.

title: Ascending Aorta Dilation in the Fontan: To Intervene or Not.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ascending aorta dilation is a known finding in the congenital heart disease population and specifically in patients who have undergone single ventricle palliation.

CASE SUMMARY: We present 3 patients with single ventricle physiology who underwent single ventricle palliations and had severe ascending aorta dilation.

WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES: Guidelines for the management of these patients are lacking, and decisions are made on a case-by-case basis.

DISCUSSION: There are case reports of aortic dissection, but true risk remains unknown. Weighing the risks of surgery versus conservative management in patients with single ventricle physiology is challenging.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Surgical intervention on dilated aortas in patients with single ventricle physiology is perilous but possible in the correct circumstances.

title: Beyond Access Flow: The FLASH Multiorgan Framework for Assessing High-Flow Arteriovenous Fistulas in Hemodialysis.
abstract: High-flow arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) impose a continuous hemodynamic burden on patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis, yet access blood flow (Qa) alone does not determine their cardiovascular significance. High access blood flow, high-output physiology, and clinically relevant cardiovascular intolerance represent related but distinct states whose expression depends on the interaction among access-related hemodynamic exposure, systemic flow response, cardiovascular reserve, volume status, and downstream cardiovascular consequences. This review proposes a clinically oriented, multiorgan framework for evaluating patients in whom an AVF is suspected of contributing to cardiovascular deterioration. Assessment begins with the clinical and dialysis context and integrates five interconnected domains: FISTULA, characterizing access-related hemodynamic exposure; LOAD, evaluating the systemic circulatory response; ASSESSMENT OF EXTRAVASCULAR LUNG WATER, identifying pulmonary congestion; SYSTEMIC VENOUS CONGESTION, assessing systemic venous consequences; and HEART, evaluating cardiac adaptation and maladaptation. Integration across these domains may reveal overlapping clinical-hemodynamic patterns, including preserved tolerance despite high flow, predominantly hyperdynamic physiology, cardiac maladaptation, systemic venous- or pulmonary-predominant consequences, and multicompartmental involvement. Discordance between systemic venous and pulmonary findings may provide physiologically relevant information rather than represent conflicting evidence. Serial reassessment after ultrafiltration, clinical change, or access-flow modification further emphasizes the dynamic nature of these patterns. The framework is intended to support physiologic interpretation rather than establish AVF causality, define new diagnostic categories, or propose treatment thresholds. Ultimately, assessment should move beyond asking how much blood flows through the fistula toward determining how the individual patient responds to that flow.

title: Comparative evaluation of handheld vs. high-end ultrasound systems for TIPSS hemodynamic assessment: first impressions.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPSS) procedures require reliable post-interventional hemodynamic monitoring to detect shunt dysfunction, for which Doppler ultrasonography is the preferred modality. Owing to the rapid development of handheld ultrasound devices, their diagnostic equivalence to high-end systems warrants investigation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A pilot group of 23 patients (n = 13 males, 65%; n = 7 females; 35%; n = 3 unknown) with intrahepatic TIPSS were retrospectively analyzed. Blood flow measurements were obtained and compared using a high-end ultrasound system (Resona R9, Mindray) and modern handheld ultrasound device (Vscan Air™ CL, GE). The TIPSS was evaluated using B-mode and color Doppler sonography. Image quality was assessed using a 5-point scale and flow parameters using statistical analysis. The image quality and the difference between the two devices were analyzed using correlation coefficients and multivariable linear regression models including TIPSS flow values, skin-to-TIPSS distance, and TIPSS dwell time.

RESULTS: Both devices produced clinically interpretable images. However, the high-end device yielded superior image quality in 16 of 23 cases (p < 0.001). Significant correlations were observed between the difference in mean TIPSS flow measurements obtained by the two devices (Δ mean TIPSS flow) and corresponding average flow values measured by the two devices (Kendall's τ = 0.656; p < 0.001). Significant associations with Δ TIPSS mean flow were identified for skin-to-TIPSS distance (τ = 0.39; p = 0.014) and TIPSS dwell time (τ = -0.39; p = 0.017). In multivariable analysis, both mean TIPSS flow measured by the high-end system and skin-to-TIPSS distance remained significantly associated with Δ TIPSS mean flow. The TIPSS mean flow measured by the high-end system correlated with TIPSS dwell time (τ = 0.38; p = 0.021). Bland-Altman analysis revealed that handheld measurements tended to overestimate low flows and underestimate high flows.

CONCLUSION: Handheld ultrasound devices show promising potential for TIPSS surveillance; however, they could lead to distorted flow deviations. Contemporary handheld devices may nevertheless be useful in selected point-of-care settings but cannot yet replace high-end systems for precise hemodynamic monitoring. Larger prospective studies are required.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: No clinical trial registration was performed, as this study is a single-center retrospective observational analysis based on existing clinical data. The study did not involve prospective patient enrollment, international procedures, or assignment to treatment groups. Therefore, registration in a clinical trial registry was not applicable.

Owing to the rapid development of handheld ultrasound devices, their diagnostic equivalence to high-end systems warrants investigation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A pilot group of 23 patients (n = 13 males, 65%; n = 7 females; 35%; n = 3 unknown) with intrahepatic TIPSS were retrospectively analyzed.

title: Increased prevalence of hypertension in paediatric turner syndrome: a retrospective study.
abstract: Girls and women with Turner Syndrome (TS) are known to be at increased risk of aortic dissection, a condition for which hypertension is a modifiable risk factor. Our aim was to determine the frequency of hypertension in girls attending a tertiary paediatric TS clinic and its association with clinical characteristics. Retrospective analysis of clinical data was conducted for girls with TS attending the dedicated paediatric TS clinic at the Royal Hospital for Children Glasgow, between 1976-2023. Blood pressure (BP) was converted to centiles according to age and height. Hypertensive range BPs were defined as BPs ≥ 95th centile and pre-hypertensive range BPs were defined as BPs between the 90th-95th centiles, with measurements on 2 consecutive occasions. 184 girls with TS were included and BP data were available for a total of 172 (93%) with a median (range) age at the time of BP attainment of 12 (4, 18) years. Of these, 38 (22%) had congenital heart disease and 48 (28%) had an existing renal anomaly. The prevalence of hypertensive range BP at clinic within this cohort was 50% (n = 86), with median age of onset at 12 (4, 17) years of age. Pre-hypertensive range BPs were identified in 12 (7%). In total, 14/86 (15%) had ongoing high BP and were prescribed anti-hypertensive treatment. There is an increased prevalence of hypertension within the paediatric TS population compared to the general paediatric population. Early management of blood pressure in this group is likely to reduce cardiovascular disease burden.

Our aim was to determine the frequency of hypertension in girls attending a tertiary paediatric TS clinic and its association with clinical characteristics. title: Posterior cerebral artery dissection: clinical and angiographic spectrum, management, and outcomes in a retrospective 14-patient case series.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Posterior cerebral artery (PCA) dissection is a rare cerebrovascular disorder with heterogeneous clinical and angiographic presentations. Because evidence is largely limited to small case series and individual reports, optimal diagnostic and therapeutic strategies remain uncertain.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 14 patients with angiographically confirmed PCA dissection or dissecting PCA aneurysms identified at a single center between January 2016 and December 2025. Clinical presentation, angiographic characteristics, treatment strategy, procedural complications, and available clinical and vascular imaging follow-up were analyzed.

RESULTS: The median age was 43.5 years (IQR, 33.8-56.3; range, 20-63 years). Hemorrhagic presentation occurred in 8 patients (57.1%), including 6 with subarachnoid hemorrhage (42.9%). Two patients were managed conservatively, 3 underwent conventional stenting alone, 5 underwent flow-diverter treatment, 2 underwent coil embolization without an implanted stent, and 2 underwent conventional stenting combined with coil embolization. Most patients achieved favorable clinical and angiographic outcomes. One patient remained severely disabled (mRS 5), and one patient developed fatal post-procedural subarachnoid hemorrhage after flow-diverter treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: PCA dissection is a rare and clinically heterogeneous condition that may present with hemorrhagic or nonhemorrhagic manifestations. Management should be individualized according to rupture status, lesion morphology, vascular anatomy, collateral circulation, and the feasibility of parent-vessel preservation. Conservative management and different endovascular strategies may be appropriate in selected patients, but the small retrospective nature of available series precludes conclusions regarding superiority of any single treatment approach.

Because evidence is largely limited to small case series and individual reports, optimal diagnostic and therapeutic strategies remain uncertain. title: Elevated Lipoprotein(a) Is Associated With Heart Failure in Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] in peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains uncertain.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively studied 138 patients with intermittent claudication undergoing endovascular therapy. Patients were classified by Lp(a) level (≥30 vs. <30 mg/dL). The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a higher incidence of MACE (31.1% vs. 9.6%; P=0.002), predominantly driven by heart failure. It independently predicted MACE (HR 4.23) and heart failure (HR 5.12), but not cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke.

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) was associated with heart failure-driven MACE after endovascular therapy in patients with PAD.

title: Early prediction of surgical site complications after vascular groin incision using postoperative drainage kinetics: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Groin incisions in vascular surgery are associated with a considerable incidence of postoperative surgical site complications (SSCs), with lymphatic complications such as lymphorrhea and lymphocele representing a frequent and clinically relevant source of morbidity. Previous studies have identified postoperative drainage volume as a potential surrogate marker for impaired lymphatic healing and subsequent wound complications. Based on these observations, researchers have proposed standardized drainage management strategies to help identify high-risk patients early and guide timely intervention. This study retrospectively evaluates postoperative outcomes after implementing this strategy.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort analysis included 106 patients with 114 vertical groin incisions undergoing open vascular procedures requiring femoral exposure between June 2023 and June 2024. We defined SSCs according to a previously published classification. We defined the groin incision as the unit of analysis. The primary outcome was the incidence of clinically relevant SSCs (grades 2-4). Secondary outcomes included drainage characteristics, drain removal timing, lymphatic interventions, and risk factors for lymphatic complications.

RESULTS: Postoperative drainage volumes were significantly associated with clinically relevant surgical site complications (SSC grade 2-4). Drainage on POD 1 was not significantly associated with complications. Higher drainage volumes from POD 2 onwards were significantly associated with complications, with increasing effect sizes over time (POD 2: OR 1.048, p = 0.022; POD 3: OR 1.047, p = 0.023; POD 4: OR 1.178, p < 0.001). Cumulative drainage up to POD 4 demonstrated the highest discriminative performance (OR 1.024, p = 0.0006; c = 0.831). Overall, 43.0% of groin incisions developed clinically relevant SSC.

CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative drainage kinetics enable early identification of patients at risk for clinically relevant lymphatic complications after vascular groin surgery. While drainage of POD 1 is not predictive, drainage volumes from POD 2 onwards allow reliable risk stratification with progressively increasing predictive accuracy. POD 2 drainage output is a clinically relevant predictor of subsequent lymphatic complications. A POD2 drainage output ≥80 mL/24 h may support early identification of high-risk patients and facilitate timely interdisciplinary planning of targeted lymphatic interventions.

Previous studies have identified postoperative drainage volume as a potential surrogate marker for impaired lymphatic healing and subsequent wound complications. Based on these observations, researchers have proposed standardized drainage management strategies to help identify high-risk patients early and guide timely intervention.

title: Hybrid Revascularization of Chronic Vertebral Artery Occlusion: A Morphology-Based Classification, Novel Collateral-Channel Techniques, and Mid-Term Patency in a Single-Center Series of 26 Procedures.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic vertebral artery (VA) occlusion encompasses heterogeneous morphologies-de novo atherosclerotic occlusion, in-stent restenosis (ISR), and in-stent occlusion (ISO)-for which no classification-guided revascularization strategy exists. We report the largest single-center series of hybrid revascularization combining VA endarterectomy (VEA) with endovascular techniques, propose a morphology-based classification, and provide the first mid-term patency analysis.

METHODS: Twenty-six consecutive hybrid revascularization procedures performed in 25 patients with chronic VA occlusion between January 2018 and March 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Lesions were classified as Type I (de novo occlusion), Type II (post-stent ISR), or Type III (post-stent ISO), with a complexity modifier "C" denoting long-segment extension, tortuous/deep origin, or absence of a distal target. Technical success, periprocedural complications, and patency at last imaging follow-up were assessed.

RESULTS: Technical success was 88.5% (23/26) overall, declining across morphological types: 100% in Type I, 88.9% in Type II, and 71.4% in Type III. The C modifier strongly predicted failure (success 50.0% vs. 100% without C; P = 0.008). There was no periprocedural stroke or death; one major cardiac event (3.8%) occurred. At last follow-up (median 34 months; range, 3-96 months), 19 of 23 successfully recanalized arteries (82.6%) remained patent. Mid-term patency was 100% with adjunctive stenting versus 63.6% without (P = 0.037); both reocclusions and one of two restenoses followed stent explantation without re-scaffolding. Novel bailout techniques-VA transposition to the thyrocervical trunk and retrograde revascularization through the ascending cervical artery collateral-rescued three complex anatomies.

CONCLUSIONS: Hybrid revascularization is safe and effective for chronic VA occlusion, with outcomes that depend systematically on lesion morphology. The proposed Type I/II/III classification with the C modifier stratifies technical difficulty and guides strategy selection, while adjunctive stent scaffolding after endarterectomy appears critical for durable patency. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective validation.

We report the largest single-center series of hybrid revascularization combining VA endarterectomy (VEA) with endovascular techniques, propose a morphology-based classification, and provide the first mid-term patency analysis. METHODS: Twenty-six consecutive hybrid revascularization procedures performed in 25 patients with chronic VA occlusion between January 2018 and March 2026 were retrospectively analyzed.

title: Training Structure and Satisfaction with Learning in European Vascular Surgery Training: Results from the European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) Surveys.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study describes the availability of modifiable structural training elements across European vascular surgery programmes to identify which of these elements are independently associated with trainees' satisfaction with learning and to contextualise them with trainer reported delivery constraints.

METHODS: The study comprised two parallel cross-sectional web based European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) surveys of trainees and trainers. The main outcome variable was satisfaction with learning (10 point Likert scale). Five modifiable structural elements were identified a priori: structured curriculum; training coordinator; dedicated or protected training time; assigned mentor; and simulation access. Associations were examined using an adjusted linear mixed effects model (LMM), with secondary models for coordinator resourcing and mentorship evaluations. Trainer data were analysed descriptively.

RESULTS: Of 420 trainee responses (32 countries), 273 entered the complete case main LMM. Availability was inconsistent: structured curriculum 56.4%; dedicated or protected training time 34.3%; and simulation access 32.3%. In the adjusted LMM, learning satisfaction was higher with a structured curriculum (= 0.79, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.21 - 1.38; p = .008) and dedicated training time (= 0.62, 95% CI 0.05 - 1.19; p = .035). In secondary models, coordinators with dedicated educational time showed the largest association (= 1.76, 95% CI 1.05 - 2.46; p < .001), and mentorship with regular evaluations was associated with higher satisfaction (= 0.98, 95% CI 0.36 - 1.59; p = .002). Among 659 trainers (37 countries), mentorship importance was rated 8.26 out of 10, yet only 43.4% had dedicated mentorship time; the dominant barrier was clinical workload (84.1%). Desired improvements were dedicated mentorship time (64.4%), formalised programmes (54.3%), and regular feedback sessions (51.6%).

CONCLUSION: A structured curriculum and dedicated training time were independently associated with higher trainee learning satisfaction across European vascular surgery programmes. Organisational roles such as training coordinators and mentors were associated with higher satisfaction in exploratory secondary analyses, suggesting these roles may be most beneficial when actively resourced with dedicated time and regular evaluations. Trainer constraints converged on protected time for training and mentorship.

METHODS: The study comprised two parallel cross-sectional web based European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) surveys of trainees and trainers. The main outcome variable was satisfaction with learning (10 point Likert scale).

title: Sociodemographic predictors of postpartum anticoagulant selection in pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE) requires anticoagulation into the postpartum period that overlaps with breastfeeding initiation. Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) and vitamin K antagonists (VKA) are compatible with breastfeeding, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are currently not recommended. Postpartum anticoagulant selection may be influenced by safety, convenience and access, potentially contributing to racial and socioeconomic inequities in care. We evaluated the impact of race and sociodemographic factors on postpartum anticoagulant selection in a publicly funded healthcare system.

METHODS: This is a population-based cohort study using linked administrative health data in Ontario, Canada. We included Ontario Drug Benefit (ODB) recipients with pregnancy-associated VTE diagnosed between 2012 and 2022 who received ≥1 anticoagulant prescription within 6 months postpartum. Primary outcome was the exclusive receipt of breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulants (LMWH/VKA). Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) were determined to identify factors associated with breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulant use.

RESULTS: Of 113 ODB-eligible individuals with pregnancy-associated VTE, 62.8% received ≥6 weeks of postpartum anticoagulation. During the 6-month postpartum period, 25.7% transitioned to a DOAC. No significant association was observed between race and receipt of breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulation. However, individuals in the most materially deprived neighbourhoods were significantly less likely to receive a breastfeeding-compatible anticoagulant compared with those in less deprived areas (aOR 0.20, 95% CI 0.07-0.58).

CONCLUSIONS: In this population-based cohort, 1 in 4 individuals with pregnancy-associated VTE received a DOAC within 6 months postpartum. Postpartum anticoagulant selection was affected by socioeconomic status. These findings highlight the need to explore structural factors influencing anticoagulant selection to advance equitable postpartum care.

Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) and vitamin K antagonists (VKA) are compatible with breastfeeding, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are currently not recommended. Postpartum anticoagulant selection may be influenced by safety, convenience and access, potentially contributing to racial and socioeconomic inequities in care.

title: Feasibility, safety, and efficacy of the amber peripheral liquid embolic system: results from stage I of the first-in-human OPAL study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the early safety and technical feasibility of Amber 20 for peripheral vascular embolization in a prospective, multicenter, first-in-human stage I study.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, open-label first-in-human stage I trial conducted across 11 centers in Spain. Fifteen patients requiring peripheral embolization for various indications (including hemorrhage, aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm, endoleak, portal vein embolization, and hypervascular tumors) were enrolled. The primary endpoint was the rate of device-related serious adverse events (SAEs) within 24 h. Secondary endpoints included overall adverse events (AEs) and technical success, defined as complete vascular occlusion or devascularization on final angiography.

RESULTS: Fifteen patients (60% female; median age 56 years) underwent embolization using Amber 20. Technical success was achieved in 100% of cases (15/15). No device-related SAEs or AEs were reported within 24 h. Five patient (33%) experienced a mild adverse event (postembolization syndrome) related to the procedure. All adverse events resolved without sequelae. No device deficiencies were observed.

CONCLUSION: In this first-in-human, multicenter study, Amber 20 demonstrated a favorable safety profile and high technical success rate for peripheral vascular embolization. These preliminary findings support its potential as an effective liquid embolic agent, warranting further evaluation in larger studies with longer follow-up (stage II).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, open-label first-in-human stage I trial conducted across 11 centers in Spain. Fifteen patients requiring peripheral embolization for various indications (including hemorrhage, aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm, endoleak, portal vein embolization, and hypervascular tumors) were enrolled.

title: National incidence and predictors of in-hospital venous thromboembolism after inpatient lumbar fusion, 2016-2022.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To estimate the national incidence of in-hospital VTE recorded during the index lumbar fusion admission and identify independent comorbidity predictors.

METHODS: Adult (≥ 18 years) inpatient admissions undergoing lumbar fusion were identified in the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2022 using ICD-10-PCS procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE during the index admission. Characteristics were compared between VTE and non-VTE admissions, and multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression evaluated independent predictors. Significance was set at the P < 0.05 level.

RESULTS: Across 631,165 weighted inpatient lumbar fusion admissions, in-hospital VTE incidence was 0.6%. VTE admissions were older (age distribution, P < 0.001), more frequently male (P = 0.003), and more often involved multilevel fusion (78.5% vs. 74.2%, P = 0.007). On multivariable analysis, the largest adjusted associations were observed for other neurologic disorders (OR 3.76, 95% CI 2.93-4.83, P < 0.001), coagulopathy (OR 3.70, 95% CI 2.89-4.75, P < 0.001), weight loss (OR 3.57, 95% CI 2.35-5.42, P < 0.001), pulmonary circulation disorders (OR 2.78, 95% CI 1.82-4.23, P < 0.001), and paralysis (OR 2.78, 95% CI 2.09-3.71, P < 0.001). Additional predictors included solid tumor without metastasis (OR 1.97, P = 0.022), cerebrovascular disease (OR 1.90, P = 0.003), peripheral vascular disease (OR 1.58, P = 0.002), obesity (OR 1.75, P < 0.001), seizure disorders (OR 1.74, P = 0.016), congestive heart failure (OR 1.71, P < 0.001), and deficiency anemia (OR 1.64, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital VTE recorded during the index lumbar fusion admission was uncommon but concentrated among patients with distinct high-risk comorbidity profiles. These findings support risk-stratified inpatient surveillance and prevention strategies during hospitalization.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: To estimate the national incidence of in-hospital VTE recorded during the index lumbar fusion admission and identify independent comorbidity predictors. METHODS: Adult (≥ 18 years) inpatient admissions undergoing lumbar fusion were identified in the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2022 using ICD-10-PCS procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE during the index admission.

title: Robotic mini-thoracotomy approach to aortic valve and ascending aorta replacement.
abstract: Fully endoscopic robotic-assisted aortic valve replacement has emerged as a safe, reproducible and effective minimally invasive approach with favourable clinical outcomes. In patients undergoing aortic valve surgery, concomitant ascending aortic aneurysms should be addressed whenever indicated, as failure to do so may lead to serious long-term aortic complications. Currently these patients must undergo some form of sternotomy to address both pathologies. The use of a totally robotic minithoracotomy approach for concomitant aortic valve and ascending aortic replacement has not, to our knowledge, been previously reported. This video tutorial highlights a robotic approach for combined aortic valve and ascending aortic replacement, representing a pioneering step in the evolution of complex robotically assisted aortic surgery. Our vision is to develop a robotic aortic surgery programme that maintains the safety, efficacy and durability of conventional techniques while significantly expediting postoperative recovery for selected patients.

title: Two-year patency rates of drug-coated balloon angioplasty for radiocephalic arteriovenous fistula juxta-anastomotic stenosis: A single-center study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The study aims to assess primary and secondary patency rates and the need for reintervention after drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty performed for juxta-anastomotic AVF stenoses.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study included patients who underwent DCB angioplasty for AVF stenosis between May 2019 and December 2023. Information on reinterventions was obtained from medical records, while AVF functional patency was assessed through Duplex Ultrasound Scanning. The primary outcomes measured were patency rates at 6, 12, and 24 months.

RESULTS: The study included 69 patients. The average age was 61.4 ± 12.7 years, with 45 (65.2%) being male. Primary patency rates were 72.5% (50/69), 46.4% (32/69), and 30.4% (21/69) at 6, 12, 24 months, respectively. Secondary patency rates were 85.5% (59/69), 59.4% (41/69), and 46.4% (32/69).

DISCUSSION: DCB angioplasty shows acceptable mid-term primary patency and sustained longer-term secondary patency for treating juxta-anastomotic stenosis in primary RC AVFs. Notably, the secondary patency rates indicate that re-interventions can help preserve the access circuit.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study included patients who underwent DCB angioplasty for AVF stenosis between May 2019 and December 2023. Information on reinterventions was obtained from medical records, while AVF functional patency was assessed through Duplex Ultrasound Scanning.

title: Sirtuins in cellular senescence and cardiovascular diseases: From mechanistic basis to activator development and translational perspectives.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of mortality worldwide, and cellular senescence serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of cardiovascular degeneration and related diseases. Sirtuins act as a crucial molecular hub linking cellular senescence to CVDs, and their upregulated activity is closely associated with delayed cellular senescence and preserved normal cardiovascular function; therefore, the research and development of small-molecule Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) hold important research value and promising translational potential for CVD intervention. This review systematically elucidates the molecular mechanisms by which various Sirtuin subtypes influence senescence-related processes in CVDs through the regulation of biological events such as DNA damage repair, mitochondrial homeostasis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses. Furthermore, it comprehensively outlines their roles in major cardiovascular conditions, including hypertension, angiogenesis, atherosclerosis, aortic aneurysm and dissection, and heart failure. Finally, this paper summarizes recent advances in the development of Sirtuin activators and, in light of current challenges such as insufficient specificity and hurdles in clinical translation, provides perspectives on the future development of Sirtuin-targeted therapies for the prevention and treatment of CVDs.

title: Cardiovascular disturbances and ward hypotension after major vascular surgery: a single-centre prospective cohort study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Postoperative hypotension can be caused by vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. We sought to estimate the effects of these causes on the incidence of hypotension after major vascular surgery.

METHODS: We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study of male and female adult patients undergoing major vascular surgery. We conducted point-of-care ultrasound and sidestream darkfield microscopy imaging to detect vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. The primary outcome was hypotension (systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg or a vasopressor infusion) within 24 hr of surgery.

RESULTS: We recruited 100 patients, of whom 89 had data available for analysis. Hypotension occurred in 20 participants (23%), vasodilation in 30 (34%), and myocardial dysfunction in 11 (12%). Severe hypovolemia and obstruction were not observed. The adjusted marginal risk difference of hypotension was 33% (95% confidence interval [CI], 14% to 53%; P < 0.001) for vasodilation and 41% (95% CI, 3% to 79%; P = 0.03) for myocardial dysfunction. Vasodilation increased the risk of intensive care unit admission by 27% (95% CI, 8% to 45%; P = 0.006) and of requiring a vasopressor infusion by 22% (95% CI, 4% to 39%; P = 0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: Vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction increased the risk of postoperative hypotension, providing insight into the mechanistic development of postoperative hypotension. The absence of severe hypovolemia was surprising. Clinicians should assess for vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction as potential preludes to postoperative hypotension, potentially using point-of-care echocardiography and sidestream darkfield microscopy.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: Postoperative hypotension can be caused by vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. We sought to estimate the effects of these causes on the incidence of hypotension after major vascular surgery. METHODS: We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study of male and female adult patients undergoing major vascular surgery.

title: Severity-Based Triage for Direct Transportation to Nearest Comprehensive Stroke Center: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The efficacy of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is time dependent. Patients initially transported to a primary stroke center (PSC) may require secondary transfer, potentially delaying EVT. For severely affected patients, bypassing the PSC for direct transport to a comprehensive stroke center may expedite EVT but risks delaying IV thrombolysis. Effects of prehospital bypass strategies on functional outcomes are thus uncertain.

METHODS: For this systematic review and meta-analysis, PubMed and Web of Science were searched until December 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized studies comparing transport to the nearest stroke center with transport to a more distant comprehensive stroke center in patients with suspected stroke were included. Two investigators independently screened records, selected eligible studies, extracted summary data, and assessed risk of bias. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to quantify associations between prehospital bypass, endovascular therapy, and functional outcomes.

RESULTS: Literature search identified 1,991 distinct reports. Of 18 eligible studies, 2 were randomized controlled trials (RCTs, n = 1,540 patients), 11 before-after studies (n = 11,837), and 5 cross-sectional studies (n = 1,139), comprising a total of 14,516 patients (52% men/48% women). Risk of bias was high in nonrandomized studies. Patients undergoing prehospital bypass and control patients had similar likelihoods of receiving EVT (odds ratio [OR] 1.52, 95% CI 0.98-2.35) or thrombolysis (OR 1.12, 0.92-1.35). Prehospital bypass was associated with earlier groin puncture (median difference -63.9 minutes, 95% CI -84.1 to -43.7). Time to needle in bypass patients was longer than in control patients in RCTs (median delay 34 minutes, 23.1-44.9 minutes), but similar in nonrandomized studies. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) at 90 days was more frequent in bypass patients (OR 1.23, 1.04-1.45). In patients with intracerebral hemorrhage, bypass was associated with increased mortality (risk ratio 1.30, 1.02-1.64).

DISCUSSION: For patients with LVO stroke, benefits of expedited thrombectomy may outweigh possible risks associated with longer prehospital transport times. However, evidence is insufficient to recommend the routine implementation of prehospital bypass protocols. Further research is needed to determine circumstances under which direct access to comprehensive stroke centers should be prioritized for patients with severe stroke symptoms.

Patients initially transported to a primary stroke center (PSC) may require secondary transfer, potentially delaying EVT. For severely affected patients, bypassing the PSC for direct transport to a comprehensive stroke center may expedite EVT but risks delaying IV thrombolysis.

title: Association of Prethrombectomy Hemorrhagic Infarction on MRI With Further Transformation and Functional Outcomes: A Multicenter Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke from large vessel occlusion (LVO). Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored. We evaluated whether pretreatment MRI HI is associated with 90-day functional dependence, post-MT PH, and symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with anterior circulation LVO undergoing MT at 2 stroke centers (2015-2022). Patients required pre-MT T2*-weighted MRI. HI was graded (types I/II) per European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study III criteria in blinded fashion. The primary outcome was 90-day functional dependence (modified Rankin Scale 3-6). Secondary outcomes were post-MT ipsilateral PH and SICH. We used multivariable Bayesian and frequentist logistic regression to adjust for age, sex, NIH Stroke Scale, baseline disability, comorbidities, infarct volume, and procedural factors.

RESULTS: Among 479 patients (median age 72 years; 46% female; 50% received IV thrombolysis), pretreatment HI was identified in 25 (5.2%), with excellent inter-rater agreement (Cohen κ = 0.9). Functional dependence at 90 days occurred in 47% of the total cohort, ipsilateral PH in 9.4%, and SICH in 3.1%. In multivariable analysis, pre-MT HI was independently associated with 90-day functional dependence (Bayesian adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.66, 95% credible interval [CrI] 2.15-24.28, Pr[OR > 1] = 1.00; frequentist aOR 5.95, 95% CI 1.91-18.52, p = 0.002). Pre-MT HI also demonstrated a high posterior probability of association with post-MT ipsilateral PH (Bayesian aOR 2.76, 95% CrI 0.73-9.26, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.94; frequentist aOR 2.84, 95% CI 0.84-9.58, p = 0.091) and SICH (Bayesian aOR 5.59, 95% CrI 0.63-34.92, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.95; frequentist aOR 6.02, 95% CI 1.00-36.11, p = 0.049).

DISCUSSION: HI detected on pretreatment MRI is an independent predictor of poor long-term functional outcomes and correlates with post-MT PH/SICH. Pre-MT HI may reflect significant blood-brain barrier disruption and microvascular fragility, serving as a marker of reperfusion vulnerability. Limitations include the retrospective design and the relatively low frequency of HI, PH, and SICH, which were addressed using Bayesian modeling to quantify uncertainty. Although not a contraindication to MT, identifying HI may aid in periprocedural risk stratification and serve as a candidate marker for future neuroprotective trials.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke from large vessel occlusion (LVO). Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored.

title: Accuracy and Concordance of Agitated Saline Bubble-Enhanced Ultrasound versus Chest Radiography by Internal Jugular Insertion Site.
abstract: Non-tunneled hemodialysis catheters (HDCs) are commonly used to initiate renal replacement therapy in hospitalized patients, especially those with acute kidney injury. HDC malposition is associated with delayed therapy and inadequate dialysis. Agitated saline bubble-enhanced ultrasound (SBUS) has emerged as a method for visualizing catheter position at the time of insertion. This study aimed to analyze the accuracy and concordance of SBUS and chest radiography (CXR) for assessing HDC positioning according to the internal jugular vein (IJV) insertion site. A total of 152 hospitalized patients undergoing IJV catheter insertion were assessed from December 2019 to May 2021. Time from puncture to CXR result, procedure-related complications, blood flow during dialysis, and the accuracy and concordance of SBUS compared with CXR for determining HDC position adequacy were evaluated. The median time between catheter insertion and CXR was 191 min [interquartile range (IQR), 93-288 min], with no difference between insertion sites. The main complication after catheter insertion was arterial puncture (2% overall), with a similar incidence at both sites. Inadequate catheter blood flow was more frequent with left IJV insertion than with right IJV insertion. For right IJV catheters, concordance between SBUS and CXR was high (Gwet's AC1 = 0.95; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.915-0.992), with an accuracy of 95.6%. For left IJV catheters, concordance was low (Gwet's AC1 = 0.37; 95% CI, -0.21-0.94), with an accuracy of 64.3%. Compared with CXR, SBUS was suitable for assessing catheter placement following right IJV insertion but may be less suitable following left IJV insertion.

title: Association of an Intensive Multimodal Perioperative Management Bundle With Short-Term Recovery After Surgery for Trimalleolar Fractures: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
AIM: To examine the association between receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle and short-term functional recovery, pain, and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing surgery for trimalleolar fractures.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 84 patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for trimalleolar fractures between September 2023 and September 2025. The intensive management bundle was a pre-existing standardized routine-care pathway rather than a research intervention developed for this study. Patients were classified retrospectively according to contemporaneous medical and nursing records: 43 patients who received routine management were assigned to a routine-management group, and 41 who received the intensive bundle were assigned to an intensive-pathway group. The investigators did not prospectively enroll patients, assign pathways, deliver study-specific interventions, or collect research-specific data. Primary outcomes were the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) Ankle-Hindfoot Scale and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores; secondary outcomes included first out-of-bed mobilization, length of hospital stay, hospitalization costs, patient satisfaction, and deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Unadjusted mean differences or odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and longitudinal AOFAS and VAS data were analyzed using mixed-design repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA). Because the components were delivered together, no component-specific effect was estimated.

RESULTS: No baseline variable differed significantly between groups, although the absence of statistical significance did not establish covariate balance. In unadjusted analyses, receipt of the intensive bundle was associated with earlier first out-of-bed mobilization (mean difference [MD], -22.80 h; 95% confidence interval [CI], -26.48 to -19.12), shorter hospitalization (MD, -3.30 days; 95% CI, -4.14 to -2.46), lower hospitalization costs (MD, -13,114 CNY (1 USD = 7.1429 CNY); 95% CI, -14,979 to -11,249), and higher patient satisfaction (OR, 5.16; 95% CI, 1.04-25.56). VAS scores were lower in the intensive-pathway group at 1 week (3.9 ± 0.9 vs. 4.8 ± 1.0), 1 month (1.3 ± 0.7 vs. 3.2 ± 1.0), and 3 months (1.0 (0.0, 1.0) vs. 2.0 (1.0, 2.0)) postoperatively (all Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.001); RM-ANOVA showed significant group, time, and group-by-time interaction effects for both AOFAS and VAS scores. DVT occurred in 3/41 (7.3%) patients in the intensive-pathway group and 8/43 (18.6%) in the routine-management group, and the difference was not statistically significant (OR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.08-1.41). These findings represent associations with the integrated bundle and cannot be attributed independently to preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, analgesia, mobilization, or follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle was associated with earlier mobilization, shorter hospitalization, lower hospitalization costs, and more favorable short-term functional and pain trajectories. Because the bundle contained multiple simultaneously delivered components, the study cannot determine the independent efficacy of preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, or any other individual measure. In addition, pathway allocation was non-random and the estimates were unadjusted; therefore, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than definitive causal effects.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 84 patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for trimalleolar fractures between September 2023 and September 2025. The intensive management bundle was a pre-existing standardized routine-care pathway rather than a research intervention developed for this study.

title: Perioperative Impact of Incidental Durotomy in Elderly Patients Undergoing Elective Spine Surgery: A Multicenter European Cohort Study.
abstract:
AIM: Incidental durotomy is among the most frequent intraoperative complications in spine surgery, yet elderly patients may be especially vulnerable to its downstream consequences because of frailty, multimorbidity, delayed mobilization, and postoperative neurocognitive complications. The literature suggests that durotomy is associated with increased perioperative resource utilization, whereas long-term functional outcomes are not well reported.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study across five European academic neurosurgical centers. Consecutive patients aged 65 years or older who underwent elective spine surgery between 2019 and 2024 were reviewed. Patients with incidental durotomy during the index procedure were compared with those without durotomy. Outcomes of interest included length of stay, thromboembolic events, postoperative infection, delirium, readmission, revision surgery, postoperative intensive care use, and discharge disposition.

RESULTS: Among 723 included patients, 107 (14.8%) sustained an incidental durotomy. Operative time was longer in the durotomy cohort (median 178 vs 138 minutes; p < 0.001), as were length of stay (8 vs 5 days; p < 0.001), thromboembolic events (6.5% vs 1.8%; p = 0.010), and postoperative delirium (14.0% vs 5.2%; p = 0.001). In descriptive analyses of patients older than 75 years, median length of stay was 10 vs 6 days, delirium occurred in 17.7% vs 7.4%, and thromboembolic events occurred in 8.1% vs 2.2%. Postoperative infection, 30-day readmission, revision surgery, intensive care use, and discharge disposition were not significantly different between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In elderly patients undergoing elective spine surgery, incidental durotomy was associated mainly with increased perioperative morbidity rather than clearly worse short-term post-discharge outcomes. The signals for prolonged stay, delirium, and thromboembolic complications-especially in patients older than 75 years-support age-sensitive perioperative pathways emphasizing meticulous repair, early mobilization when clinically appropriate, delirium prevention, and close medical surveillance.

The literature suggests that durotomy is associated with increased perioperative resource utilization, whereas long-term functional outcomes are not well reported. METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study across five European academic neurosurgical centers.

title: Nursing-Related Risk Characteristics and Identification of High-Risk Patients With In-Hospital Lower-Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis After Lower-Limb Fracture Surgery: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract:
AIM: Lower-limb fractures already contribute ≥5 Caprini points for venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk, limiting the ability of the conventional >5 cutoff to discriminate individual risk within this population. We evaluated whether an admission Caprini score ≥9, preoperative immobilization ≥72 h and severe postoperative day 1 (POD1) activity dependence are associated with in-hospital lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and whether POD1 activity provides additional within-group risk stratification beyond Caprini scoring.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective, 1:3 matched case-control study of adults undergoing surgery for lower-limb fractures at Ganzhou Hospital-Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University between January 2022 and July 2024. Of 783 patients screened, 71 were excluded, leaving 712 in the source cohort (61 DVT cases and 651 ultrasound-negative, matchable controls). Cases and controls were matched 1:3 without replacement by age (±5 years), sex, and fracture site, yielding 61 matched sets (244 patients). After matching, non-matching variables were singly imputed using a random forest algorithm for the primary analysis. To assess uncertainty associated with this approach, a separate sensitivity analysis generated 20 completed datasets from the pre-imputation matched records using a stochastic chained-equation multiple-imputation procedure. Regression estimates across the 20 datasets were combined using Rubin's rules. Associations were estimated using conditional logistic regression stratified by matched set and reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Incremental within-set concordance was corrected using 2000 cluster bootstrap resamples. The primary analysis, complete-case analyses and multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis were conducted separately.

RESULTS: Matching variables were well balanced after matching, with standardized mean differences (SMD) of 0.02 for age and 0 for sex and fracture site, although several non-matching characteristics remained imbalanced. Three factors were positively associated with in-hospital DVT: admission Caprini ≥9 (OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.28-4.61), severe POD1 activity dependence (OR 3.89, 95% CI 1.38-10.94), and preoperative immobilization ≥72 h (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.14-5.67). Compared with patients without any core risk features, the OR increased to 2.81 (95% CI 1.46-5.38) among those with one feature and to 6.28 (95% CI 1.57-25.03) among those with two features. Adding severe POD1 activity dependence to Caprini ≥9 was associated with a modest increase in corrected within-set concordance from 0.589 to 0.633, corresponding to a difference of 0.044 (bootstrap SE 0.022, 95% CI 0.003-0.088). Sensitivity analyses generally preserved the direction of the main associations, although the Caprini estimate was attenuated after additional adjustment for trauma-related variables and D-dimer.

CONCLUSIONS: Admission Caprini ≥9, preoperative immobilization ≥72 h, and severe POD1 activity dependence were each associated with in-hospital lower-extremity DVT. POD1 activity assessment was associated with a modest improvement in within-set risk ranking beyond Caprini stratification. This finding should not be interpreted as evidence of established clinical utility or improved patient outcomes; however, it may help guide nursing attention toward prophylaxis delivery, activity support, and symptom surveillance. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine its clinical relevance.
englishSummary: AIM: Lower-limb fractures already contribute ≥5 Caprini points for venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk, limiting the ability of the conventional >5 cutoff to discriminate individual risk within this population. We evaluated whether an admission Caprini score ≥9, preoperative immobilization ≥72 h and severe postoperative day 1 (POD1) activity dependence are associated with in-hospital lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and whether POD1 activity provides additional within-group risk stratification beyond Caprini scoring. METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective, 1:3 matched case-control study of adults undergoing surgery for lower-limb fractures at Ganzhou Hospital-Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University between January 2022 and July 2024.

title: AI Applications in Aortic and Peripheral Artery Disease: Risk Prediction, Imaging, Procedural Support, and Longitudinal Surveillance.
abstract: Aortic disease and lower-extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD) generate substantial morbidity, mortality, and longitudinal imaging burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly studied for vascular risk prediction, image analysis, procedural support, and surveillance, but the maturity of these applications is heterogeneous. This review evaluates recent AI applications in aortic disease and PAD, emphasizing the distinction between algorithmic performance, external validation, demonstrated workflow impact, and proven patient benefit. Automated image segmentation and opportunistic abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) detection have the most mature evidence base, including retrospective external validation and, for AI-assisted AAA case finding, nonrandomized evidence of improved downstream evaluation and follow-up. Conversely, while machine-learning models for vascular risk prediction and disease progression often report high retrospective accuracy, their clinical readiness remains strictly investigational. Across most aortic and PAD applications, there is a persistent lack of independent external validation, decision-curve analysis, and prospective testing against standard care. Image-fusion guidance has clinical evidence for reducing procedural resource use, but this evidence should not be conflated with autonomous AI or robotic navigation. Cardiovascular digital twins remain largely mechanistic, computational, or early-development frameworks. AI can augment vascular imaging and risk assessment, but high retrospective accuracy is not equivalent to clinical utility. Current guideline thresholds for repair, revascularization, and surveillance should not be altered on the basis of investigational radiomics or prediction models. Translation requires multicenter external validation, prospective workflow evaluation, calibration and net-benefit assessment, transparent reporting, and trials demonstrating improved patient outcomes.

This review evaluates recent AI applications in aortic disease and PAD, emphasizing the distinction between algorithmic performance, external validation, demonstrated workflow impact, and proven patient benefit.

abstract: Massive hematemesis in children may rarely originate from vascular etiologies such as mycotic internal carotid artery pseudoaneurysm. title: NLRP3+ Macrophages: Central Inflammatory Nodes of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm and Potential Cellular Target of Omega-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a fatal inflammatory vascular disease without effective clinical treatments. Dietary patterns regulate aortic inflammation, and Mediterranean diet-derived omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (ω-3 PUFA) exert anti-inflammatory effects, yet their cellular targets in AAA remain unclear. We integrated three single-cell RNA-seq cohorts (12 AAA, 3 controls) and constructed a human aortic cell atlas with 64,258 cells. Pseudo-bulk analysis and CoVarNet multicellular network analysis revealed a core remodeling axis: protective FOLR2+ resident macrophages were depleted, while a unique AAA-enriched NLRP3+ inflammatory macrophage population (M08_Mph_NLRP3) formed the hub of pathological inflammatory networks. Three bulk transcriptomic cohorts and five complementary enrichment approaches verified this signature. An LPS/OX-LDL/IL-1β-stimulated THP-1 model recapitulated AAA macrophage pathological changes including NLRP3 inflammasome overactivation, enhanced proliferation and migration. Further functional tests demonstrated ω-3 PUFA markedly blocked inflammasome cascade, reduced IL-1β/IL-18 release and reversed all macrophage pathological phenotypes. This study identifies M08_Mph_NLRP3 as the important inflammatory mediator of AAA and provides single-cell and in vitro functional evidence supporting ω-3 PUFA as a candidate nutritional agent targeting NLRP3-driven vascular inflammation.

We integrated three single-cell RNA-seq cohorts (12 AAA, 3 controls) and constructed a human aortic cell atlas with 64,258 cells.

title: Early-onset Pulmonary Embolism After Prolonged Combined Cosmetic Breast Surgery: 2 Case Reports and a Literature Review.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) after aesthetic breast surgery is considered rare, and patients are often perceived as low risk. However, prolonged operative time and combined procedures may increase pulmonary embolism (PE) risk, and adjunctive liposuction may be a marker of procedural complexity and longer duration rather than an independent cause. We describe 2 women with intermediate Caprini scores who developed early-onset PE after prolonged combined cosmetic breast surgery (including adjunctive liposuction) and summarize relevant reports of thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast procedures. Procedures lasted 225 and 370 minutes, respectively. Dyspnea, chest discomfort, or palpitations occurred within 48 hours postoperatively. D-dimer was elevated, and computed tomography pulmonary angiography confirmed acute PE, including a saddle embolus in 1 patient. Therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin followed by rivaroxaban led to clinical improvement without observed recurrence at the short-term follow-up. A focused literature review identified additional thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast surgery, most within the first postoperative week. Early-onset PE can complicate prolonged, combined cosmetic breast surgery even in patients classified as intermediate risk. Pharmacologic venous thromboembolism prophylaxis before symptom onset could not be reliably ascertained from available records. These cases support a protocolized, Caprini-informed pathway that specifies routine mechanical measures and clear indications, agent/dose, and timing for chemoprophylaxis, with explicit documentation and vigilance for early postoperative cardiopulmonary symptoms.

We describe 2 women with intermediate Caprini scores who developed early-onset PE after prolonged combined cosmetic breast surgery (including adjunctive liposuction) and summarize relevant reports of thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast procedures.

title: CCL19 emerges as a regional signal in human abdominal aortic aneurysm through targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiling of the aneurysmal wall and neck.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: The molecular mechanisms underlying abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) progression remain incompletely understood and may vary across anatomically distinct regions of the diseased aorta. We hypothesised that the aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck exhibit distinct molecular profiles, reflecting regional heterogeneity in AAA tissue. To this end, we characterized and compared targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiles of these two anatomically distinct regions to identify molecular alterations associated with AAA pathology.

METHODS: Paired aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck tissues were obtained from 18 patients with AAA. Inflammatory proteins were quantified using the Olink Target 48 cytokine panel, with 45 proteins retained for analysis after quality-control filtering. Directional RNA sequencing was subsequently performed on matched tissue samples to characterize the expression of genes corresponding to the proteins included in the proteomic analysis and to assess concordance between transcriptomic and proteomic differences.

RESULTS: Proteomic analysis identified three differentially expressed proteins (IL6, IL15, CCL19) between aneurysmal wall and neck. Transcriptomic analysis of the corresponding genes identified three differentially expressed transcripts (CCL19, CCL11, LTA). CCL19 was consistently elevated at both the protein and transcript levels in aneurysmal wall, whereas the remaining molecular alterations were specific to either the proteomic or transcriptomic analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Aneurysm wall and neck tissues showed largely similar inflammatory molecular profiles, with only a limited number of regional differences identified either on the protein or transcript level. CCL19 being the only concordant signal in both proteomic and transcriptomic analysis.

We hypothesised that the aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck exhibit distinct molecular profiles, reflecting regional heterogeneity in AAA tissue. To this end, we characterized and compared targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiles of these two anatomically distinct regions to identify molecular alterations associated with AAA pathology.

title: Feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for nutcracker syndrome: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
abstract: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age. To evaluate the feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for NCS in terms of technical completion, conversion to open surgery, perioperative safety, postoperative recovery and symptom relief, and to explore whether heterogeneity was explained by reconstructive technique, age or sample size. Four electronic databases-PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL (Cochrane Library) and the Web of Science Core Collection-were searched from inception to 1 October 2026, and the reference lists of the retrieved articles and of earlier reviews on this topic were screened by hand. Eligible reports were original studies of robot-assisted NCS surgery from which quantitative data could be obtained, provided the series comprised at least three patients; studies of non-robotic procedures, non-NCS cohorts, asymptomatic nutcracker phenomenon, stent implantation by the endovascular route alone, narrative reviews, conference proceedings, single-patient reports and duplicate cohorts were not considered. Screening and data collection were carried out independently by two investigators, and study quality was appraised with the JBI checklist designed for case series. Stata 17.0 was used for the single-arm proportional meta-analyses: individual proportions underwent Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation before being combined under a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with the summary estimates then expressed on the original scale, while continuous variables were harmonised to mean ± SD following Wan et al. and Shi et al. Cochran's Q test and the I-squared statistic were used to quantify heterogeneity. Subgroup comparisons were restricted to outcomes with substantial heterogeneity and were interpreted as exploratory analyses of study-level variation rather than as tests of independent effects. Ten studies comprising 140 patients were included (China, 4; USA, 4; France, 2; 9 retrospective and 1 prospective). Reconstructive techniques were left renal vein (LRV) transposition (5 studies, 45 patients), extravascular renal vein stent placement (3 studies, 29 patients) and renal autotransplantation (2 studies, 66 patients). Completion and conversion status could be ascertained in 111 patients from eight studies: 110 (99.1%) completed the planned reconstruction robotically and 1 (0.9%) was converted to open surgery; status was not reported for 29 patients in two studies and these patients were not counted as zero events. The pooled symptom improvement rate was 96% (95% CI 85%-100%; I-squared = 46.66%; 6 studies, 87 patients) and the complete symptom resolution rate 69% (95% CI 34%-96%; I-squared = 77.83%; 4 studies, 35 patients). The pooled incidence of Clavien-Dindo < 3 complications was 17% (95% CI 5%-33%; I-squared = 60.86%) and that of Clavien-Dindo >= 3 complications was 5.5% (95% CI 2.3%-9.8%; I-squared = 0%; 8 studies, 6 events); lymphorrhea/chylous ascites occurred in 15% (95% CI 0%-43%; I-squared = 79.16%) and postoperative reintervention in 3% (95% CI 0%-10%; I-squared = 0%). Pooled operating time was 204.52 min (95% CI 157.47-251.57 min; I-squared = 99.1%), estimated blood loss 54.21 mL (95% CI 37.56-70.86 mL; I-squared = 96.2%) and postoperative length of stay 2.72 days (95% CI 1.60-3.85 days; I-squared = 96.2%). Exploratory technique-stratified analyses suggested lower estimated blood loss, shorter operating time and shorter length of stay after extravascular stent placement than after LRV transposition or renal autotransplantation; however, several strata contained only one or two studies and these differences are descriptive rather than evidence of comparative superiority. Robotic-assisted surgery for NCS was associated with a high rate of technical completion among patients with ascertainable status, favourable symptom improvement and a low frequency of major complications. The apparent ordering of perioperative burden across techniques is consistent with differences in procedural invasiveness but may also reflect confounding by indication, centre effects and case selection. Owing to the single-arm design, short and inconsistent follow-up, absent patency data and very low certainty, these findings should be regarded as a pooled feasibility benchmark rather than as evidence of comparative effectiveness.
englishSummary: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age.

title: Interleukin-6, soluble interleukin-6 receptor, and outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: an exploratory biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis can be treated with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Identifying clinical and laboratory factors that predict clinical outcomes after TAVI may facilitate more informed decision-making. We aimed to assess the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 12 months after TAVI and long-term survival according to baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) and soluble interleukin-6 receptor (sIL-6R) levels.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort, we evaluated clinical outcomes after TAVI according to baseline IL-6 signal and sIL-6R concentration. We included only patients with an available baseline stored plasma sample. Patients were stratified into high and low IL-6 and sIL-6R groups. Two primary end points were analyzed: (i) 12-month MACCE, and (ii) long-term overall survival. Secondary end points included the individual components of MACCE. Stored baseline plasma was available for measurements in 62 patients who underwent TAVI between December 2018 and September 2021 across three clinical sites. Patients with high IL-6 had a higher 12-month MACCE risk in age- and sex-adjusted Firth penalized Cox regression analysis (HR 3.31; 95%CI 1.02-11.04, P = 0.0458) but not in unadjusted analysis (log-rank P = 0.07). The association was not robust to alternative cutoffs and the age- and sex-adjusted continuous analysis of IL-6 also did not show a statistically significant association (hazard ratio per 1-SD increase, 1.52, 95% CI, 0.86 to 2.46, P = 0.13). No significant associations were observed in the primary models between IL-6 and long-term overall survival or between sIL-6R and either primary end point.

CONCLUSIONS: High IL-6 signal at baseline may be associated with increased 12-month MACCE risk after TAVI, although this finding was sensitive to IL-6 categorization and was not statistically significant in continuous analysis. Baseline sIL-6R concentration was not significantly associated with the analyzed clinical outcomes. These findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

Identifying clinical and laboratory factors that predict clinical outcomes after TAVI may facilitate more informed decision-making. We aimed to assess the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 12 months after TAVI and long-term survival according to baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) and soluble interleukin-6 receptor (sIL-6R) levels.

title: Outcomes with Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis versus Mechanical Thrombectomy for Patients with Intermediate/High Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Meta-Analysis of 24,090 Patients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Randomized trials comparing the outcomes with catheter-directed medical thrombolysis (CDT) versus mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for patients with intermediate/high risk pulmonary embolism (PE) are limited. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the clinical outcomes after CDT versus MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE.

METHODS: Eligible studies compared CDT and MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE underwent catheter-based therapies were retrieved from a comprehensive literature search for PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL through June 2026. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, major bleeding, and the length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay. Summary estimates were analyzed using a random effects model.

RESULTS: A total of 18 studies (24,090 intermediate/high risk patients) were eligible for the analysis. CDT was associated with longer length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay (mean difference: 1.01 days, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.87-1.15) compared with MT. While there was no statistical difference between the two groups regarding the risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio [RR] 0.88, 95% CI 0.76-1.01, p = 0.068) and major bleeding (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.74-1.55, p = 0.705). Similarly, the incidence of other clinical outcomes; all-cause readmission, PE-related readmission, blood transfusion rates, length of hospital stay, cardiac arrest, and stroke, were similar between the two groups.

CONCLUSION: Among patients with intermediate/high risk PE treated with catheter-based therapies, there was no difference regarding the clinical outcomes between CDT and MT, but CDT was associated with a longer ICU stay. Larger, well designed randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Randomized trials comparing the outcomes with catheter-directed medical thrombolysis (CDT) versus mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for patients with intermediate/high risk pulmonary embolism (PE) are limited. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the clinical outcomes after CDT versus MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE. METHODS: Eligible studies compared CDT and MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE underwent catheter-based therapies were retrieved from a comprehensive literature search for PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL through June 2026.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for people with type 2 diabetes and peripheral artery disease: reducing uncertainty in clinical practice.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) may be the most frequent first manifestation of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in type 2 diabetes (T2D). Management of PAD in T2D aims to improve symptoms and lower the high risk of major adverse cardiovascular (MACE) and limb (MALE) events. Drugs commonly used are lipid-lowering and antihypertensive medicines, antithrombotic and antihyperglycemic agents. The ADA recommends both GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) as the first-line therapy to reduce the cardio-renal risk in people with T2D, including those with PAD. Meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) show that semaglutide is better than placebo in reducing by 30% PAD events in people with T2D (with or without PAD at baseline), although no RCT was designed to investigate PAD-related hard outcomes as a primary endpoint; however, both liraglutide and semaglutide may increase walking distance by approximately 25-30 m at six months in people with T2D and PAD. Cohort studies also confirm that GLP-1RA use is better than non-use in reducing by 28% the risk of MALE in individuals with T2D and PAD, although their retrospective design might introduce residual confounding and under-ascertainment of outcomes. Dedicated RCTs will obtain more direct evidence for the promising lower limb benefits of GLP-1RAs, but the scientific outlook of specific RCTs on hard limb events is empty. In the meantime, clinicians should choose a GLP-1RA of proven efficacy in subjects with T2D and PAD to improve their cardio-nephro-metabolic outlook, as well as their walking capacity, limited at present to liraglutide and semaglutide.

Management of PAD in T2D aims to improve symptoms and lower the high risk of major adverse cardiovascular (MACE) and limb (MALE) events. Drugs commonly used are lipid-lowering and antihypertensive medicines, antithrombotic and antihyperglycemic agents.
