title: Non-invasive assessment of postoperative revascularization using slab MIP images in 3D TOF MRA in pediatric moyamoya disease.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Repeated assessment of postoperative revascularization in pediatric moyamoya disease is clinically important, but digital subtraction angiography (DSA) is invasive. We aimed to develop a novel, non-invasive scoring method (moya-ASPECTS) that applies the six cortical MCA regions of ASPECTS to slab maximum intensity projection (MIP) images from three-dimensional time-of-flight (3D TOF) magnetic resonance angiography (MRA), and to examine its correlation with DSA findings and cerebral blood flow (CBF) changes after surgery.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 45 treated hemispheres in 28 pediatric patients who underwent revascularization between 2010 and 2023. Eight hemispheres underwent indirect revascularization alone and 37 underwent combined direct and indirect revascularization. We evaluated postoperative cortical revascularization using the moya-ASPECTS score based on slab MIP images derived from 3D TOF MRA, and examined its associations with Matsushima grade, resting cerebral blood flow (CBF), cerebrovascular reserve (CVR), and regression of basal moyamoya vessels.

RESULTS: The moya-ASPECTS score showed a strong correlation with Matsushima grade (p < 0.001). Postoperative resting CBF increased by 2.27 ml/100 g/min for each point increase in moya-ASPECTS (95% CI 0.87-3.67, p = 0.003). While moya-ASPECTS was not associated with CVR change, it correlated significantly with regression of moyamoya vessels (RR 1.33, 95% CI 1.12-1.58, p < 0.001). Higher moya-ASPECTS scores were inversely associated with postoperative asymptomatic infarction, although the number of events was small.

CONCLUSION: The moya-ASPECTS score derived from slab MIP images provides a non-invasive, repeatable, and semi-quantitative method for evaluating postoperative cortical revascularization in pediatric moyamoya disease. This method correlates well with DSA-based Matsushima grade and postoperative CBF improvement, supporting its potential use as a practical non-invasive adjunct for serial outpatient follow-up.

We aimed to develop a novel, non-invasive scoring method (moya-ASPECTS) that applies the six cortical MCA regions of ASPECTS to slab maximum intensity projection (MIP) images from three-dimensional time-of-flight (3D TOF) magnetic resonance angiography (MRA), and to examine its correlation with DSA findings and cerebral blood flow (CBF) changes after surgery. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 45 treated hemispheres in 28 pediatric patients who underwent revascularization between 2010 and 2023.

title: CTA-defined calcified nodules as a predictor of adverse outcomes following carotid revascularization.
abstract: Carotid calcification can complicate carotid artery stenting (CAS), but the clinical impact may depend on calcification morphology rather than calcification burden alone. We retrospectively evaluated 92 patients who underwent carotid revascularization with either carotid endarterectomy (CEA) or CAS and classified preoperative CTA findings as no/spotty calcification (Group 1), outer calcification (Group 2), or a calcified nodule (CN) pattern directly abutting the contrast-enhanced lumen (Group 3). The primary composite endpoint comprised procedural failure, ischemic complications, or restenosis. The endpoint occurred in 4 of 83 patients (4.8%) in Groups 1/2 and in 5 of 9 patients (55.6%) in Group 3 (unadjusted OR, 24.69; 95% CI, 4.72-129.14; p < 0.001). In a parsimonious multivariable model including treatment modality and calcification pattern, Group 3 remained associated with the composite endpoint (adjusted OR, 49.05; 95% CI, 4.82-498.94; p = 0.001), whereas CEA was associated with lower risk (adjusted OR, 0.045; 95% CI, 0.003-0.664; p = 0.024). Among patients undergoing CAS, the endpoint occurred in 3 of 38 patients (7.9%) in Groups 1/2 and all 5 patients (100%) in Group 3 (p < 0.001). A CTA-defined CN pattern may identify lesions at particularly high risk for CAS-related technical failure or restenosis and may support consideration of CEA when surgically feasible.

We retrospectively evaluated 92 patients who underwent carotid revascularization with either carotid endarterectomy (CEA) or CAS and classified preoperative CTA findings as no/spotty calcification (Group 1), outer calcification (Group 2), or a calcified nodule (CN) pattern directly abutting the contrast-enhanced lumen (Group 3). The primary composite endpoint comprised procedural failure, ischemic complications, or restenosis.

title: Late Type IIIa Endoleak Despite Adequate Component Overlap after AFX2 EVAR: A Report of Two Cases.
abstract: Late type IIIa endoleak is a recognized complication of AFX2 (Endologix, Irvine, CA, USA) endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). We report 2 cases occurring 6 and 7 years after EVAR despite adequate initial overlap. In Case 1, computed tomography angiography (CTA) did not clearly demonstrate component uncoupling, whereas duplex ultrasonography showed bidirectional ("to-and-fro") flow and angiography confirmed a type IIIa endoleak. In Case 2, serial computed tomography (CT) retrospectively demonstrated progressive sideways displacement before complete uncoupling. Focal cuff relining and complete endograft relining were performed, respectively. These cases emphasize the need for lifelong surveillance for sac enlargement and changes in endograft configuration after AFX2 EVAR.

title: Native Aorta Non-Touch Total Arch Hybrid Repair for Residual Aortic Dissection after Hemiarch Replacement.
abstract: Reintervention for residual aortic arch dissection after hemiarch replacement for acute type A aortic dissection remains technically challenging. A 70-year-old man presented with progressive dissecting arch aneurysmal dilatation 6 years after hemiarch replacement. Native aorta non-touch total arch hybrid repair was performed using the previously implanted hemiarch graft as the inflow source for total supra-aortic debranching and as the site for short elephant trunk placement. Staged thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed the following day. Postoperative computed tomography showed no endoleak, and the patient remained free from aortic events at 5-year follow-up.

title: Retrograde Open Mesenteric Stenting Failure Requiring Aorto-Mesenteric Bypass in Acute-on-Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia: A Case Report.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) is a rare pathology, most commonly associated with multivessel atherosclerosis, whose diagnosis is often delayed due to nonspecific symptoms. Endovascular treatment is the first-line treatment option, although its results may be limited by restenosis or intrastent thrombosis. Open surgery remains an important option in cases where endoluminal treatment has failed. The aim of this paper is to illustrate, through a clinical case, the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges associated with severe CMI.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 69-year-old female patient, a long-term smoker being treated for peripheral arterial disease, presented with postprandial abdominal pain that had been present for 6 months, accompanied by severe malnutrition. The CT angiogram revealed occlusion of the celiac trunk and the superior mesenteric artery, with the development of extensive collateral circulation. Initial endovascular revascularization via stenting was performed in a patient presenting with gastrointestinal distress that had required segmental resection of necrotic ileojejunal loops. The course of the disease was characterized by a recurrence of symptoms and stent thrombosis, leading to surgical revascularization via an aorto-mesenteric bypass. The postoperative course was favorable, with the mesenteric angina gradually subsiding, significant weight gain, and lasting functional improvement.

CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the limitations of endovascular treatment alone in severe multivessel disease and confirms the value of a personalized treatment strategy incorporating open surgery to optimize long-term outcomes.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) is a rare pathology, most commonly associated with multivessel atherosclerosis, whose diagnosis is often delayed due to nonspecific symptoms. Endovascular treatment is the first-line treatment option, although its results may be limited by restenosis or intrastent thrombosis. Open surgery remains an important option in cases where endoluminal treatment has failed.

title: Continuation of Clopidogrel in Total Knee Arthroplasty: Perioperative Bleeding and Cardiovascular Outcomes in a Consecutive Case Series.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative clopidogrel management in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is challenging because interruption may increase thrombotic risk, whereas continuation may increase bleeding. Evidence remains limited.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 31 consecutive patients (35 knees) undergoing primary TKA while continuing clopidogrel 75 mg daily (April 2018-September 2019). A multidisciplinary team involving orthopaedic surgery, cardiology, and anesthesiology determined continuation. One senior surgeon performed all procedures using a tourniquet-free technique with intravenous and intra-articular tranexamic acid. All patients also received low-dose aspirin for at least 2 weeks postoperatively as venous thromboembolism prophylaxis. Outcomes through 90 days included bleeding, transfusion, wound complications, infection, major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events, symptomatic venous thromboembolism, and anesthesia-related complications.

RESULTS: Mean age was 69 ± 6.4 years; mean estimated blood loss was 285 ± 95 mL, and mean hemoglobin decrease was 1.8 ± 0.6 g/dL. No transfusions or major bleeding occurred. Minor wound drainage followed 3 procedures (8.6%), and superficial cellulitis occurred in 1 knee (2.9%); no deep infections occurred. Four patients (12.9%) reported mild, nonspecific headaches; none met criteria for post-dural puncture headache. No clinical signs or symptoms suggestive of spinal hematoma or persistent neurologic deficit, and no myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular death, were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Clopidogrel continuation during primary TKA may be feasible in carefully selected patients receiving multidisciplinary assessment and multimodal blood management. The small sample, retrospective design, and absence of a control group preclude conclusions about comparative safety.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Perioperative clopidogrel management in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is challenging because interruption may increase thrombotic risk, whereas continuation may increase bleeding. Evidence remains limited. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 31 consecutive patients (35 knees) undergoing primary TKA while continuing clopidogrel 75 mg daily (April 2018-September 2019).

title: Spontaneous rupture of an intrasplenic arterial aneurysm presenting as an acute abdomen: CT diagnosis and surgical management.
abstract: Aneurysms of the intrasplenic arterial branches are exceptionally rare. Rupture without trauma, and without the pancreatic disease behind most splenic arterial pseudoaneurysms, is rarer still, and it can be fatal. Cross-sectional imaging usually brings it to light. A 51-year-old multiparous woman with no relevant medical history presented with sudden left upper quadrant pain radiating to the left shoulder, and a positive Kehr sign. Her blood pressure was maintained and her hemoglobin normal. A heart rate of 101 beats/min, however, left open the possibility of early compensation for bleeding. Multiphasic contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), the arterial phase acquired as a CT angiogram, showed a ruptured saccular aneurysm of 18 × 12 mm in the mid-splenic parenchyma. There was an arterial-phase contrast blush, marking active extravasation, with a heterogeneous subcapsular hematoma and a moderate hemoperitoneum. The pancreas was normal and there had been no trauma. With no endovascular treatment on site, she underwent splenectomy. Serial counts showed no fall in hemoglobin, and she was discharged on the fifth postoperative day. Histopathology found hemorrhagic change but no malignancy, vasculitis, or fibromuscular dysplasia, and no discrete aneurysmal wall. Once rupture has occurred, CT cannot reliably tell a true aneurysm from a pseudoaneurysm, so the lesion is best called one of presumed true type. Early CT found the lesion, showed how far the bleeding had gone, and allowed treatment to start without delay. The diagnosis is worth considering in acute left upper quadrant pain, even when the blood pressure is maintained and the hemoglobin normal.

title: Association of Multimodal Collateral Profiles with Outcomes After Large Core Thrombectomy.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Cerebral collateral circulation markers in large core thrombectomy and their impact on functional outcomes have not been extensively reported. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed health system medical records of large core (Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score <6 and/or computed tomography perfusion [CTP] cerebral blood flow <30% volume ≥50 milliliters [mL]) thrombectomy patients over a 19-month period. A good collateral profile (CCC+) was defined as the combination of computed tomography angiography Tan arterial score ≥2 and CTP cerebral blood volume index (CBVI) ≥0.8. A poor profile (CCC-) was defined as Tan <2 and CBVI <0.8. All others were categorized as having a mixed profile (CCC±). Multivariable Firth's penalized logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with the primary outcome, 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-3. Results: 88 patients with median (interquartile range, IQR) age 65.5 (56.5-77.5) years and core volume 78 (55-116) mL were included. Forty-seven patients (53.4%) had poor collateral profiles, 31 (35.2%) were classified as CCC±, and 10 (11.4%) as CCC+. In the multivariable Firth's penalized logistic regression model, CCC+ patients had higher odds of achieving a 90-day mRS of 0-3 compared with CCC- patients, though the difference was not statistically significant (odds ratio [OR] 1.117, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.235-5.311, p = 0.889). No significant difference was observed between CCC± and CCC- patients (OR 0.869, 95% CI 0.293-2.577, p = 0.800). Glucose was the only factor independently associated with 90-day outcomes (OR 0.742, 95% CI 0.602-0.915, p = 0.005). Conclusions: No independent association was detected between favorable or mixed cerebral collateral circulation and 90-day mRS 0-3 after large core thrombectomy, though the study was underpowered for the CCC+ comparison. Presenting glucose may inform the likelihood of achieving independent ambulatory status at 90 days.

Methods: We retrospectively analyzed health system medical records of large core (Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score <6 and/or computed tomography perfusion [CTP] cerebral blood flow <30% volume ≥50 milliliters [mL]) thrombectomy patients over a 19-month period. A good collateral profile (CCC+) was defined as the combination of computed tomography angiography Tan arterial score ≥2 and CTP cerebral blood volume index (CBVI) ≥0.8.

title: Cross-Phenotype Genomics Reveals Heterogeneous Genetic Susceptibility Architecture Relevant to Menopause.
abstract: Background: Menopause is accompanied by substantial interindividual variation in hormonal, metabolic, cardiovascular, skeletal, and thrombotic phenotypes. Although the genetics of reproductive ageing and individual menopause-associated traits are increasingly characterised, the cross-phenotype architecture of individual menopause-relevant germline variants remains less well defined. Methods: We performed a variant-centred genomic analysis of 31 prespecified menopause-relevant germline variants. Cross-trait evidence comprised 766 variant-trait records across 52 phenotypes and was integrated with a targeted Pan-UK Biobank phenome-wide association study (PheWAS; 1462 tests across 57 endpoints), clinically relevant outcome analyses, linkage disequilibrium assessment, FinnGen R12 venous thromboembolism (VTE) associations, regional fine-mapping, and molecular annotation. Association strength, between-study heterogeneity, phenotypic breadth and sharing, and locus resolution were evaluated as distinct evidence dimensions. Results: In total, 25 of 31 variants showed at least one cross-trait association at p < 1 × 10-5 and 21 reached genome-wide significance. Phenotypic breadth varied markedly, from restricted profiles to 16 associated phenotypes, and strong associations frequently coexisted with substantial between-study heterogeneity. In Pan-UK Biobank, 222 associations involving 25 variants met false-discovery-rate correction, spanning hormonal, reproductive, cardiometabolic, skeletal, nutritional, hepatic, and neurological phenotypes. Cross-phenotype reconstruction identified recurrent connectivity through sex hormone-binding globulin, testosterone, adiposity, lipid, and skeletal traits, while linkage disequilibrium analyses distinguished phenotypic sharing from genetic redundancy. Clinically, F5 rs6025 and F2 rs1799963 showed strong VTE associations in FinnGen (OR 2.387 and 1.921, respectively), but markedly different locus resolution: rs6025 had posterior inclusion probability (PIP) 0.979 and constituted a single-variant 95% credible set, whereas rs1799963 had PIP 0.596 within a four-variant credible set. Conclusions: Menopause-relevant germline variation exhibits heterogeneous cross-phenotype architectures in which association strength, phenotypic breadth, between-study consistency, genetic independence, and locus resolution are not interchangeable. This variant-centred framework provides a basis for evaluating inherited susceptibility relevant to menopause and hormone exposure, while prospective individual-level studies remain necessary before translation into risk prediction or treatment selection.

title: Urgent Endovascular Treatment of a Pancreatitis-Related Pseudoaneurysm Identified on Follow-Up CT.
abstract: Visceral artery pseudoaneurysm (VA-PSA) is an uncommon but life-threatening complication of acute-on-chronic pancreatitis, particularly in the presence of walled-off necrosis (WON). Early radiological recognition is essential because of the high risk of rupture. We present the case of a 51-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis who developed a pseudoaneurysm arising from the proper hepatic artery within a pancreatic head necrotic collection. Follow-up contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a new arterial-phase enhancing focus within the WON. Digital subtraction angiography (DSA) confirmed the pseudoaneurysm, which was successfully excluded with a covered stent placed via a right transfemoral approach. Post-procedural recovery was uneventful, and short-term follow-up CT showed persistent exclusion of the lesion.

title: Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Sensors Placed Frontally and Parietally to Detect Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to determine whether two-channelled near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) was feasible for recognising anterior large vessel occlusion (LVO) with a device suitable for prehospital use and whether probe placement (frontal vs. parietal) made a difference.

METHODS: We analysed NIRS readings of six computed tomography angiography (CTA)-confirmed LVO-stroke patients at Tampere University Hospital during the six-month study period. We placed four sensors on patients' heads: two frontally and two parietally. We provided a detailed description and analysis of these recordings and their correlation with imaging-confirmed changes in perfusion.

RESULTS: In the frontally placed sensors, the rSO2 was 1-8 percentage points higher on the affected side before and 0-9 percentage points higher on the affected side after endovascular treatment (EVT). rSO2 values did not change significantly. One patient showed higher rSO2 on the healthy side (5 percentage points) before and after EVT. We could not recover frontal values from one patient. In parietally placed censors, all patients had 3-9 percentage points higher rSO2 on the healthy side before EVT. After EVT, 3 patients had 3-7 percentage points higher rSO2 on the healthy side. In two cases, after EVT, the difference in rSO2 changed to 1-2 percentage points higher on the affected side. We could not record parietal readings in one patient.

CONCLUSIONS: Neither NIRS sensor placement detected differences in rSO2 in LVO; therefore, NIRS appears unsuitable as a diagnostic tool for LVO. Future research should focus on other technologies.

METHODS: We analysed NIRS readings of six computed tomography angiography (CTA)-confirmed LVO-stroke patients at Tampere University Hospital during the six-month study period.

title: Cardiac Damage and Clinical Outcomes in Symptomatic Severe Aortic Stenosis Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The extent of cardiac damage in patients with aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with worse clinical outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to investigate the clinical impact of cardiac damage using the updated criteria incorporating the echocardiographic probability of pulmonary hypertension.

METHODS: This post hoc subanalysis of LANDMARK trial, which randomized 768 patients with severe AS to the Myval transcatheter heart valve (THV) series or to contemporary THVs (Sapien and Evolut series), used updated cardiac damage classification: stage 0, no cardiac damage; stage 1, left ventricular damage; stage 2, left atrial or mitral valve damage; stage 3, pulmonary artery or tricuspid valve damage; and stage 4, right ventricular damage. The impact of cumulative cardiac damage, defined as meeting all criteria for stages 1 to 4, was also assessed. The primary endpoint was 1-year all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Cardiac damage stages were assessed in 596 patients (stage 0, n = 36; stage 1, n = 88; stage 2, n = 284; stage 3, n = 84; stage 4, n = 104), with a mean age of 80.2 (5.7) years and a mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons score of 3.3% (2.4%). One-year mortality was 0%, 1.1%, 4.7%, 7.2%, and 20.4% in stages 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively (log-rank P < 0.001). The area under the curve for predicting 1-year mortality was 0.739. Patients with cumulative cardiac damage had the highest mortality (23.6%). In the multivariable analysis, stage 4 was independently associated with higher 1-year mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: The updated cardiac damage staging stratified 1-year mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement, highlighting the importance of comprehensive echocardiographic assessment in severe AS. (LANDMARK Trial: a Randomised Controlled Trial of Myval THV [LANDMARK]; NCT04275726).

title: Ruptured giant vertebrobasilar aneurysms: illustrative cases.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Giant vertebrobasilar aneurysms are rare and have a poor natural history. Compared with smaller aneurysms, giant aneurysms have a significantly higher risk of rupture, and a posterior circulation location is itself an independent predictor of rupture regardless of size. Clinical presentation and symptomatology are highly variable, often with nonspecific symptoms progressing insidiously, resulting in delays of diagnosis. There are also significant treatment challenges. The authors describe their experience in 2 cases.

OBSERVATIONS: Both patients presented with symptomatic brainstem compression. One patient presented with headache, gait difficulties, left face numbness, and facial droop. The other presented with left-sided trigeminal pain, sixth nerve palsy, blurry vision, and unsteady gait. Both patients developed catastrophic subarachnoid hemorrhage within days following presentation, before planned intervention, with rapid progression to death.

LESSONS: Consistent with prior reports, both patients presented with symptomatic brainstem compression, which may have reflected aneurysm growth or instability. These data, along with prior reports, emphasize the poor clinical outcomes associated with symptomatic brainstem compression due to giant vertebrobasilar aneurysms, as well as the urgent and timely need to treat them despite no prior hemorrhage. Higher clinical suspicion is warranted, and further advances in endovascular technologies are necessary to provide reliable, improved clinical outcomes. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26399.

title: Neurological and Medical Complications in Brain Tumor Patients. 2026 Update.
abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Patients with brain tumors have a plethora of potential complications that arise from both the tumor and its therapeutic management. These complicate clinical management and produce morbidity and occasionally mortality. In this review we discuss the most common neurological and medical complications that include tumor-related epilepsy, vasogenic edema, infection, thromboembolism, endocrine abnormalities and cognitive impairment and its management. This review is an update to the 2020 article by Schiff and Alyahya.

RECENT FINDINGS: IDH mutant gliomas cause neuronal hyperexcitability via D-2 -hydroxyglutarate production; use of IDH inhibitors may lower the rate of seizures in this patient population. Pneumocystis prophylaxis with antibiotics has been traditionally recommended with radiation and concurrent temozolomide chemotherapy but newer data suggest no difference in hospitalization or survival. Podoplanin produced by tumor cell releases into the circulation, often via extracellular vesicles, activates platelets and may contribute to venous thrombus formation. Direct oral Anticoagulants (DOACs) are the treatment of choice for venous thromboembolism, with high quality of evidence and a strong recommendation in cancer-associated thrombosis. Though brain tumor patients were underrepresented in clinical trials, retrospective studies support its safety in this population. Brain tumor patients are prone to complications arising from both the tumor and the treatment strategies. Management requires a multidisciplinary strategy with supportive medications including antiseizure medications, corticosteroids, anticoagulants for thromboembolism, and neurocognitive rehabilitation. Early recognition and timely intervention can reduce the morbidity associated with these complications leading to better patient outcomes.

These complicate clinical management and produce morbidity and occasionally mortality. In this review we discuss the most common neurological and medical complications that include tumor-related epilepsy, vasogenic edema, infection, thromboembolism, endocrine abnormalities and cognitive impairment and its management.

title: Deep vein thrombosis-primed neutrophils reshape the brain microenvironment to promote brain metastasis.
abstract: Brain metastasis (BrM) is a devastating complication of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), yet how host macroenvironmental conditions influence brain metastatic susceptibility remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the impact of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), a common complication in patients with cancer, on TNBC brain metastasis. Analysis of a large clinical cohort identified DVT as an independent risk factor for BrM in patients with metastatic breast cancer. Using two syngeneic TNBC models, we demonstrated that DVT selectively enhanced brain metastasis without significantly affecting primary tumor growth or lung metastasis. Mechanistically, DVT increased neutrophil accumulation in the brain metastatic microenvironment, and neutrophil depletion completely abrogated the metastasis-promoting effect of DVT. Single-cell RNA sequencing of CD45+ cells in peripheral blood revealed that DVT reprogrammed circulating neutrophils toward migratory and inflammatory transcriptomic profiles characterized by neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. DVT increased CXCR2 expression on circulating neutrophils and enhanced neutrophil recruitment in brain. Moreover, DVT significantly increased circulating NETs. Collectively, our findings identify DVT as a systemic driver of TNBC brain metastasis and reveal that DVT primes circulating neutrophils toward enhanced vascular recruitment and NET formation, providing a mechanistic link between cancer-associated thrombosis and brain metastatic susceptibility.

Analysis of a large clinical cohort identified DVT as an independent risk factor for BrM in patients with metastatic breast cancer.

title: Zero-Iodinated-Contrast CO2-Guided Atherectomy for Superficial Femoral Artery Chronic Total Occlusions in Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) who undergo complex femoropopliteal endovascular interventions are at heightened risk of contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI). This study assessed technical feasibility, short-term creatinine-based renal outcomes, and clinical outcomes of a zero-iodinated-contrast, carbon dioxide (CO2)-guided atherectomy approach for chronic total occlusions (CTOs) of the superficial femoral artery (SFA). Materials and Methods: In this retrospective, single-center analysis, 25 non-dialysis patients with CKD underwent CO2-only angiography-guided atherectomy for SFA CTOs. Renal function, procedural characteristics, distal embolization, limb-related outcomes, and duplex ultrasound-defined patency were evaluated. Serum creatinine was measured at baseline and within 48 h after the procedure. Results: The mean age was 65.4 ± 9.8 years, and 36% of patients presented with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). Baseline serum creatinine was 2.16 ± 0.44 mg/dL, and the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was 29.5 ± 9.1 mL/min/1.73 m2; 56% of patients had Stage 4 CKD. Technical success was achieved in all procedures. Cumulative CO2-volume data were available for 24 patients, with a mean volume of 98.8 ± 37.6 mL, and the mean procedure duration was 38.2 ± 17.2 min. Distal embolization occurred in 20% of patients (5/25), including one event requiring catheter-directed thrombolysis; all embolic events were treated endovascularly, with near-complete recanalization in the thrombolysis case. Mean serum creatinine changed by -0.016 ± 0.086 mg/dL, and no creatinine-defined AKI was observed within the available 48-h assessment. No patient required initiation of dialysis. Follow-up outcomes were available for 24 of 25 patients (96%); one patient was lost to follow-up. Over a mean follow-up period of 26 months (with incompletely reconstructed surveillance), no duplex-defined restenosis, recurrent CTO, or target lesion revascularization (TLR) was documented among patients with available follow-up imaging; this is a descriptive observation within the available follow-up and does not establish universal or long-term freedom from restenosis. Conclusions: A zero-iodinated-contrast, CO2-guided atherectomy strategy appears technically feasible for SFA CTO revascularization in patients with advanced CKD and was associated with observed short-term creatinine stability within the available 48-h assessment in this small retrospective cohort. These preliminary observations require validation in larger, prospective, controlled studies.

Materials and Methods: In this retrospective, single-center analysis, 25 non-dialysis patients with CKD underwent CO2-only angiography-guided atherectomy for SFA CTOs.

title: Quantification of vortex characteristics and rupture risk assessment in abdominal aortic aneurysms using the liutex method.
abstract: The blood flow of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) is characterized by complex vortex interactions. Previous studies have found three flow types in AAAs (Type I: multiple vortices; Type II: non-helical single vortex; Type III: helical main flow channel), and Type III has strong correlation with rupture risk. However, flow pattern classification is subjective and qualitative, hindering further improvements in risk prediction. To enhance the predictive value of vortex-based metrics, three-dimensional models of 40 infrarenal AAAs (22 ruptured and 18 unruptured) were reconstructed from preoperative CTA images for computational fluid dynamics analysis. Flow pattern types and two novel quantitative vortex parameters based on Liutex method (volume vortex fraction (vVF) and directional entropy (H)) were compared between the two groups. A multiparametric rupture risk prediction model was constructed. Receiver operating characteristic curves and the area under the curve (AUC) were employed to evaluate predictive performance. Results demonstrated that vVF in the ruptured group was significantly higher (p = 0.02). Type III AAAs exhibited a median vVF of 15.29 %, significantly surpassing those of Types I and II, and a 12.5 % threshold achieved 80 % accuracy in identifying these high-risk patterns. Ruptured cases exhibited higher entropy, facilitating more granular risk stratification. Ultimately, the integrated model combining maximum diameter, flow pattern, and directional entropy achieved an AUC of 0.86 (p < 0.001). By objectively quantifying vortex structures and establishing a multiparametric prediction model, this study significantly enhances the predictive accuracy for AAA rupture, providing a reference for risk evaluation.

Previous studies have found three flow types in AAAs (Type I: multiple vortices; Type II: non-helical single vortex; Type III: helical main flow channel), and Type III has strong correlation with rupture risk. However, flow pattern classification is subjective and qualitative, hindering further improvements in risk prediction.

title: Analysis of the Use of shRNA in Atherosclerosis Therapy: Current Status.
abstract: Atherosclerosis remains the principal pathological substrate of myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke and peripheral artery disease, and its progression is driven by an interlocking set of processes, including hepatic and vascular lipid metabolism, chronic vascular inflammation, macrophage foam cell formation and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) proliferation, none of which is fully controlled by currently approved pharmacotherapy. Short hairpin RNA (shRNA) technology, in which a DNA template encoding a stem-loop transcript is delivered to a cell and processed intracellularly into small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) that trigger sequence-specific mRNA degradation, offers a route to durable, vector-encoded gene silencing that is mechanistically distinct from transiently acting synthetic siRNA or antisense oligonucleotides and that, although non-permanent at the level of the target gene, is not readily reversible at the level of the vector, which cannot easily be withdrawn once administered. This review analyzes the current status of shRNA-based strategies for atherosclerosis therapy. We summarize the molecular mechanism and vector design principles of shRNA-mediated RNA interference (RNAi); critically examine preclinical studies in which shRNA delivered by lentiviral or adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors has been used to silence hepatic lipid-metabolism genes (PCSK9, ApoB,), the endothelial gene ANGPTL2, inflammasome and inflammatory mediators (NLRP3, TACE/ADAM17), and genes driving VSMC proliferation in restenosis models (connexin 43); we explicitly distinguish this direct shRNA evidence from complementary target-validation studies that use antisense oligonucleotides (e.g., ANGPTL4), synthetic siRNA, genetic knockout, or antimiR approaches (e.g., lncRNA AK136714, CD36, miR-33, P2X7R); and discuss the principal delivery vectors, their tissue tropism, and the toxicity arising from saturation of the endogenous microRNA-processing machinery. We further place shRNA in the context of competing and complementary RNA-based and gene-editing modalities, including clinically approved synthetic siRNA drugs (inclisiran, patisiran) and CRISPR-based gene editing of PCSK9 and ANGPTL3, both of which have now yielded human phase 1 data, to clarify why, despite two decades of robust preclinical proof-of-concept, no shRNA construct has yet reached clinical use in atherosclerosis; we further compare this with the clinical trajectory of vector-encoded shRNA in other indications, in which anti-CCR5 and anti-HCV constructs have already been administered to patients in phase 1/2 trials, in order to establish that the limiting factor is not the hairpin itself but the risk-benefit case obtainable in a chronic, largely asymptomatic disease for which withdrawable and outcome-validated therapies already exist. We conclude that shRNA remains a mechanistically attractive but clinically immature modality whose translation will depend on vector engineering that limits off-target saturation of the RNAi pathway and achieves durable, cell type-restricted expression in the liver, endothelium, macrophages or vascular wall, and, equally, on the identification of an atherosclerosis indication-most plausibly a small, high-residual-risk or locally treatable population-in which durability outweighs the vector-level irreversibility, immunogenicity and manufacturing burden of a viral vector.
englishSummary: Atherosclerosis remains the principal pathological substrate of myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke and peripheral artery disease, and its progression is driven by an interlocking set of processes, including hepatic and vascular lipid metabolism, chronic vascular inflammation, macrophage foam cell formation and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) proliferation, none of which is fully controlled by currently approved pharmacotherapy. Short hairpin RNA (shRNA) technology, in which a DNA template encoding a stem-loop transcript is delivered to a cell and processed intracellularly into small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) that trigger sequence-specific mRNA degradation, offers a route to durable, vector-encoded gene silencing that is mechanistically distinct from transiently acting synthetic siRNA or antisense oligonucleotides and that, although non-permanent at the level of the target gene, is not readily reversible at the level of the vector, which cannot easily be withdrawn once administered. This review analyzes the current status of shRNA-based strategies for atherosclerosis therapy.

title: MEX3B leads to aberrant expression of VCAN, aggravating the thoracic aortic dissection by contributing to the phenotype transformation of VSMCs.
abstract: Thoracic aortic dissection (TAD) is a lethal condition due to the risk of aortic rupture and malperfusion of arterial branches. Currently, effective treatments are unavailable due to the unclear pathogenic mechanisms; therefore, it is essential to explore the underlying mechanisms of TAD to find novel therapeutic targets. The present study aimed to explore the effects of Mex3 RNA‑binding family member B (MEX3B) on TAD pathogenesis. A murine model of TAD was established with β‑aminopropionitrile monofumarate and angiotensin II. Hematoxylin and eosin and elastic Van Gieson staining were performed to assess the TAD formation and fragmentation of elastic fibers. Echocardiography was applied to measure the diameter of thoracic aorta. RT‑qPCR, western blot, and immunohistochemistry were employed to detect the expression of phenotypic transformation markers of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). mRNA sequencing was performed to further explore the downstream factors of MEX3B. MEX3B was upregulated following TAD induction. Knockdown of MEX3B alleviated TAD formation, as evidenced by decreased diameter and hematomas of thoracic aorta, as well as the enhanced integrity of the aortic structure and decreased thrombi in the false lumens. Loss of MEX3B mitigated the TAD‑induced depletion and fragmentation of elastic fibers. In vitro, small interfering RNA pool‑mediated MEX3B downregulation triggered VSMC switching from a synthetic towards a contractile phenotype. High‑throughput transcriptomics demonstrated that the MEX3B knockdown reduced the expression of versican (VCAN). MEX3B potentiated VCAN mRNA stability by binding to its 3'untranslated region. VCAN downregulation induced a contractile phenotype of VSMCs. In conclusion, the loss of MEX3B protected against TAD, potentially via its contribution to VSMC phenotype switching, which may be associated with the downregulation of VCAN. The present study preliminarily demonstrated the function and mechanism of MEX3B in TAD. These findings provide a theoretical basis for understanding TAD pathogenesis.

Currently, effective treatments are unavailable due to the unclear pathogenic mechanisms; therefore, it is essential to explore the underlying mechanisms of TAD to find novel therapeutic targets. The present study aimed to explore the effects of Mex3 RNA‑binding family member B (MEX3B) on TAD pathogenesis.

title: Ischemic electrocardiographic changes and initial misdiagnosis of acute aortic syndromes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Ischemic electrocardiographic (ECG) changes can mimic acute myocardial infarction and obscure acute aortic dissection (AAD) or other acute aortic syndromes (AAS), but their association with initial misdiagnosis has not been synthesized. We assessed whether ischemic changes on the earliest prediagnostic ECG were associated with initial misdiagnosis.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure through July 1, 2026, for observational studies of confirmed AAD/AAS reporting 2 × 2 data for initial misdiagnosis by ischemic ECG status. Unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) were pooled with a random-effects model using restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity, prediction intervals, leave-one-out sensitivity, QUIPS risk of bias, and GRADE certainty were assessed.

RESULTS: Seven retrospective cohorts from four countries included 724 cases; 609 had analyzable ECG data, including 179 initial misdiagnoses. Ischemic ECG changes were not significantly associated with initial misdiagnosis (pooled unadjusted OR, 1.419; 95% CI, 0.608-3.312; P = 0.351; 95% prediction interval, 0.223-9.039; I2 = 62.9%). All leave-one-out 95% CIs included 1.0. Excluding the principal contributor to heterogeneity yielded an OR of 1.050 (95% CI, 0.591-1.865) with negligible residual heterogeneity. No QUIPS domain was at high risk; GRADE certainty was moderate after downgrading for serious imprecision.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence did not demonstrate a significant association, but wide confidence and prediction intervals and unadjusted retrospective data leave important effects unresolved. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized ECG timing, harmonized diagnostic criteria, and multivariable adjustment are needed.

title: Case Report: Suspected Lower Limb Congestive Injury Associated with Decreased Compliance of the External Iliac Vein After Laparoscopic Myomectomy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of lower extremity deep vein thrombosis following gynecologic laparoscopy is 4.0%, whereas postoperative well-leg compartment syndrome (WLCS) is much rarer, with a reported incidence of only 0.03%-0.20%. Both conditions can present with postoperative lower limb swelling and pain. We report a case of postoperative lower limb swelling and pain that suspected to be caused by venous congestion injury secondary to decreased compliance of the external iliac vein, a condition that has not been previously reported in the literature.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 44-year-old woman underwent an 8-hour gynecologic laparoscopic procedure in the Lloyd-Davies position. Thirty minutes after surgery, she developed acute swelling, pain, and numbness of the right lower limb. Deep vein thrombosis was initially suspected, but treatment was ineffective. Unilateral well-leg compartment syndrome (WLCS) was subsequently considered, and her symptoms were relieved following supportive treatment, including dehydration therapy and elevation of the affected limb. Repeated review of the surgical video suggested lower limb congestive injury potentially associated with decreased compliance of the external iliac vein. The patient also experienced persistent postoperative symptoms resembling venous intermittent claudication, consistent with the clinical manifestations of impaired external iliac venous outflow.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights the need for increased attention to the condition of the external iliac vascular sheath during gynecologic laparoscopic surgery. Swelling and thickening of the vascular sheath, resulting in decreased compliance of the venous wall, may lead to severe venous congestion injury of the lower limb and may require timely intraoperative intervention when necessary. This case may provide a reference for the clinical diagnosis and management of postoperative lower limb swelling and pain following gynecologic laparoscopic surgery.

Both conditions can present with postoperative lower limb swelling and pain. We report a case of postoperative lower limb swelling and pain that suspected to be caused by venous congestion injury secondary to decreased compliance of the external iliac vein, a condition that has not been previously reported in the literature.

title: Urgent Reno-Hepatic Artery Bypass for Acute on Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia Following Robotic Low Anterior Resection for Rectal Cancer in a Patient with Severe Stenosis of the Hepatosplenomesenteric Trunk.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute mesenteric ischemia, including acute exacerbation of chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI), is a life-threatening condition associated with a 50% in-hospital mortality risk and requires immediate diagnosis, revascularization, and resection of necrotic organs. In colorectal surgery, mesenteric artery stenosis can lead to anastomotic leakage which increases morbidity and mortality. Here, we describe a case of acute exacerbation of CMI caused by severe stenosis of the hepatosplenomesenteric trunk (HSMT) and ligation of the left colic and inferior mesenteric arteries in an earlier rectal surgery that was successfully treated with urgent reno-hepatic artery bypass.

CASE PRESENTATION: An 80-year-old woman was referred to our department with acute exacerbation of CMI after multiple procedures for rectal cancer. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed severe stenosis with calcification at the origin of the HSMT and hypoenhancement of the right hepatic lobe, spleen, and small intestine. Percutaneous antegrade endovascular stenting failed because the lesion was severely calcified. We opted to perform urgent open surgery, including revascularization and resection of the necrotic organs. A bypass from the right renal artery to the proper hepatic artery was selected because of the high risk of failure associated with retrograde open mesenteric stenting, the limited length of available saphenous vein, the risk of anastomotic failure secondary to infection, the patient's poor general condition, and the degree of calcification precluding aortoiliac clamping. Postoperatively, the patient developed Takotsubo cardiomyopathy and disseminated intravascular coagulation, both of which were successfully managed and resolved in the ICU. On POD 24, the patient underwent duodeno-jejunal anastomosis, ileostomy closure, and colostomy. The patient tolerated oral intake well 80 days after arterial bypass surgery and was discharged on POD 147 on single antiplatelet therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: Although hepato-renal artery bypass is typically used for renal revascularization, reno-hepatic bypass can be useful for mesenteric revascularization in patients with anatomical variations, peritonitis, or severe aortoiliac calcification.

In colorectal surgery, mesenteric artery stenosis can lead to anastomotic leakage which increases morbidity and mortality. Here, we describe a case of acute exacerbation of CMI caused by severe stenosis of the hepatosplenomesenteric trunk (HSMT) and ligation of the left colic and inferior mesenteric arteries in an earlier rectal surgery that was successfully treated with urgent reno-hepatic artery bypass.

title: Combined antegrade-retrograde technique in urgent carotid stenting for true lumen compression after total arch replacement.
abstract: Type A aortic dissection extending into the carotid arteries with true lumen compression poses a significant risk of cerebral hypoperfusion and neurological sequelae. This case report describes an elderly patient who developed an extension of the right common carotid artery dissection with associated true lumen compression immediately following total arch replacement for acute Type A aortic dissection. Urgent carotid stenting was performed using a combined antegrade-retrograde approach (trans carotid and trans radial approach) to restore blood flow. Postprocedural imaging confirmed patency without major complications. This technique highlights a viable salvage strategy for managing complex aortic dissections when traditional methods fail. A literature review discusses the combined antegrade-retrograde approach used in urgent carotid stenting, as well as the advantages of ultrasound in selecting the true lumen and its minimally invasive nature.

This case report describes an elderly patient who developed an extension of the right common carotid artery dissection with associated true lumen compression immediately following total arch replacement for acute Type A aortic dissection. Urgent carotid stenting was performed using a combined antegrade-retrograde approach (trans carotid and trans radial approach) to restore blood flow.

title: Investigating the proportion of children with pulmonary embolism who have concomitant deep vein thrombosis reveals the hazards of observational data.
abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is thought to arise from a thrombus in a distant vein. In adults, concomitant deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is only found in about half of the patients with PE. There are no studies in children addressing this question. Because PE is a low prevalent disease in children, only observational data is available. This provides an opportunity to validate concerns regarding observational studies. This analysis compared four types of observational data: a single institution retrospective review, and case reports, small series, and large database studies identified from a formal systematic review. The proportion with concomitant DVT, age, sex, PE location, DVT location, mortality, and hospital versus community acquired were compared amongst the data sources. Amongst the 268 included studies, and 22,449 children with PE, 17.6% had concomitant DVT. There was wide variability in the estimate of the proportion who had concomitant DVT. In large databases, 15.7% had DVT, 31% from the single institution study, 47.3% from small series, and 63% from case reports. In the 29 small series, the proportion with concomitant DVT ranged from 0 to 89%. This study validates concerns regarding observational data in medicine. Because of this, the overall proportion of children with concomitant DVT determined by this study is likely inaccurate. However, it is reasonable to conclude that a significant proportion, and perhaps a majority of children with PE will not have concomitant DVT.

title: Rapid Infrarenal Aortic Rupture During Persistent Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus Bacteraemia: Serial CT Evolution and Staged Endovascular Treatment-A Case Report.
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Persistent Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia can seed an atherosclerotic aorta. Early CT may show only wall thickening and periaortic inflammation, mimicking a degenerative penetrating aortic ulcer (PAU) when no ulcer crater is visible. Case Presentation: An 80-year-old woman (BMI 19.5 kg/m2) presented with hypogastric and lumbar pain. Multiphasic CT showed a calcified infrarenal aorta with periaortic inflammation but no haemorrhage. Blood cultures obtained on two occasions confirmed persistent methicillin-susceptible S. aureus bacteraemia. Interval CT angiography showed an enhancing circumferential cuff and a small anterior contrast focus without a definite ulcer crater. Eight days after the initial CT, hypotension developed; CT angiography showed focal aortic wall disruption, active extravasation, and a large retroperitoneal haematoma. Emergency aorto-bi-iliac EVAR controlled the bleeding. An inferior mesenteric artery-fed type II endoleak filled the fresh rupture cavity and was treated by coil embolisation via mesenteric collaterals. One-month CTA showed a patent graft without endoleak. At six weeks, the patient remained clinically well with healed wounds and no need for further vascular intervention. CRP fell from 148.1 mg/L on postoperative day 5 to 49.4 mg/L at six weeks and 24.2 mg/L at approximately 12 weeks; the next outpatient review was scheduled in three months, although microbiological clearance remained undocumented. Conclusions: Serial imaging and persistent MSSA bacteraemia support probable infective aortitis with focal wall disruption; an infected degenerative PAU remains possible. Persistent bacteraemia, focal pain, and a progressive periaortic cuff should prompt early vascular review and short-interval imaging.

Early CT may show only wall thickening and periaortic inflammation, mimicking a degenerative penetrating aortic ulcer (PAU) when no ulcer crater is visible. title: Clinical Outcomes of Rivaroxaban versus LMWH Thromboprophylaxis Following Gynecologic Cancer Surgery: A Retrospective Comparison Study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: We aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of rivaroxaban vs low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) for thromboprophylaxis following gynecologic cancer surgery.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective comparative study of rivaroxaban vs standard LMWH in patients undergoing gynecologic malignancy surgery. Clinical outcomes included venous thromboembolism (VTE), major bleeding, non-major bleeding, and 1-year all-cause mortality. A multivariable logistic regression model was used to adjust for potential confounding factors.

RESULTS: A total of 250 women were included, 134 received rivaroxaban and 116 received LMWH for postoperative thromboprophylaxis following gynecologic malignancy-related surgery. After adjusting for potential confounding factors using multivariable logistic regression, the 30-day VTE and bleeding events showed no significant differences between the rivaroxaban group and the LMWH groups. There were no cases of 30-day readmission related to surgery, no 30-day mortality, and no all-cause mortality during the 1-year follow-up. Notably, all distal DVT events in both groups were calf muscular vein thromboses. During the 1-year follow-up, no patients were rehospitalized or died due to VTE.

CONCLUSION: We observed no significant differences in short- and long-term outcomes between rivaroxaban and LMWH after gynecologic malignancy surgery. Given the retrospective design and limited number of events, these results should be interpreted with caution, and prospective randomized studies are warranted.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective comparative study of rivaroxaban vs standard LMWH in patients undergoing gynecologic malignancy surgery. Clinical outcomes included venous thromboembolism (VTE), major bleeding, non-major bleeding, and 1-year all-cause mortality.

title: Modelling medial degenerative features by enzymatic digestion to evaluate disease-relevant structure-function relationships in the thoracic aorta.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To clarify aortic microstructure-function relationships, we used improved, disease-motivated enzymatic digestion models of medial degeneration to evaluate individual extracellular matrix (ECM) components (i.e., elastin, collagen, and proteoglycans) and their influence on biomechanical properties of ascending aortic tissue.

METHODS: Thin, 200 µm medial porcine ascending aortic sections were progressively digested with elastase or collagenase for selective degradation of these ECM components. Full thickness human aortic tissues were treated with chondroitinase, hyaluronidase, and heparinase to completely remove proteoglycans. Low- and high-strain modulus, transition-zone behavior, strain-energy density, and energy loss were derived from planar biaxial tensile testing. Degradation of elastin was captured with two photon excitation fluorescence imaging. Degradation of collagen was captured with picrosirius red staining and polarized light microscopy. Proteoglycan content and organization was confirmed by Alcian blue staining.

RESULTS: Degradation of elastin fibers reduced low-strain modulus, strain-energy density, transition zone stress, and energy loss. Collagen degradation similarly reduced strain-energy density and decreased strain at the onset of transition, with reductions in high strain modulus and energy loss with increased degradation. Proteoglycan removal decreased energy loss and reduced strain-energy density and strain at onset of transition, and increased high strain modulus.

CONCLUSIONS: Through targeted modeling of ECM degenerative features, we have delineated the overlapping effects of major matrix constituents, underscoring the complex, multifactorial nature of structure-function relationships in aortic disease. We also identified multiple microstructural pathways to increasing energy loss and the vulnerability of aortic tissue to failure.

STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Thoracic aortic dissection results from the progressive degeneration of the aortic wall extracellular matrix, yet the contributions of individual matrix constituents to this mechanical failure remain understudied. To address this gap, we developed a disease-motivated enzymatic model that enables controlled, graded modification of key extracellular matrix constituents in aortic tissue, better replicating the partial degeneration observed in vivo than existing approaches. Using this framework, we systematically evaluated the biomechanical consequences of elastin, collagen, and proteoglycan degeneration. Here, we revealed multiple microstructural pathways to altered viscoelastic behavior, which is associated with increased susceptibility to aortic failure. These findings provide new mechanistic insight into structure-function relationships in aortic disease and help explain how matrix degeneration contributes to tissue vulnerability and dissection risk.

METHODS: Thin, 200 µm medial porcine ascending aortic sections were progressively digested with elastase or collagenase for selective degradation of these ECM components. Full thickness human aortic tissues were treated with chondroitinase, hyaluronidase, and heparinase to completely remove proteoglycans.

title: Popliteal Venous Aneurysm with Recurrent Pulmonary Embolism Treated by Ligation without Venous Reconstruction: A Case Report.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Popliteal venous aneurysm (PVA) is rare but may lead to pulmonary embolism (PE).

CASE PRESENTATION: A 73-year-old man presented with recurrent, transient loss of consciousness. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated bilateral PE and a saccular aneurysm of the right popliteal vein. Anticoagulation therapy improved his respiratory status, but surgical treatment was performed in view of the risk of recurrent embolism. The postoperative course was uneventful.

CONCLUSIONS: At the 1-year follow-up, the patient remained free of clinically apparent lower-leg edema, and venous duplex ultrasonography demonstrated no deep vein thrombosis and the development of collateral venous channels. Although ligation is not a standard procedure for PVA, it may be an effective option in patients in whom reconstruction is difficult or in those at high operative risk.

title: Genetic-multi-omics causal inference coupled with integrative in-vitro toxicology reveals immune-metabolite mediators for aortic aneurysm risk.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease characterized by immune disturbance and metabolic dysregulation. Multi-omics-driven precision toxicity prediction, integrating human genetic causal inference with functional in-vitro toxicology, remains under-explored for uncovering metabolite mediators underlying AA disease risk.This study aimed to dissect metabolite-dependent causal pathways linking immune cells to AA, and evaluate dose-response cytotoxicity of key mediating metabolites toward vascular cells.

METHODS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and two-step mediation analysis were performed using European-ancestry GWAS summary datasets covering 731 immune-cell traits, 1,091 plasma metabolites, 3,230 AA cases and 475,964 controls. Complementary in-vitro CCK-8 cytotoxicity experiments on human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs) were further conducted for candidate metabolites Adrenate (22:4n6) and BAFF-R.

RESULTS: BAFF-R on CD20- (OR = 0.859, 95%CI: 0.797-0.926, P = 7.17 × 10-5) and, to a lesser extent, Granulocyte AC (OR = 0.900, 95%CI: 0.843-0.961, P = 1.57 × 10-3) emerged as candidate protective immune-cell markers for AA. Adrenate (22:4n6) and Nisinate (24:6n3) mediated 4.47% and 9.84% of these protective effects, respectively. Adrenate triggered significant dose-dependent cytotoxicity in HASMCs.

CONCLUSION: This multi-omics genetic-toxicology study provides causal genetic evidence for immune-metabolite regulatory axes in AA pathogenesis. Notably, Adrenate presents dual biological effects: it transmits immune-protective signals but exerts direct vascular cellular toxicity. Our findings highlight the utility of MR-assisted precision toxicity prediction for disease risk evaluation and therapeutic target mining for AA.

title: More than a scratch, Capnocytophaga bacteremia induced severe sepsis with multi-organ failure with occupational dog exposure: A case report.
abstract: Capnocytophaga species are fastidious gram-negative bacilli found in the oral flora of dogs and cats. Although human infection is typically associated with localized soft tissue disease following animal exposure, invasive infection can result in severe sepsis. We present a case of Capnocytophaga bacteremia in an immunocompetent woman with occupational exposure to dogs. A 49-year-old woman with a history of Factor V Leiden mutation, prior deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, and Raynaud's syndrome presented with fever, chills, fatigue, myalgias, abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, and transient vaginal bleeding. Evaluation revealed acute kidney injury, lactic acidosis, transaminitis, severe thrombocytopenia, and a petechial rash. An extensive infectious and autoimmune workup was unrevealing. Further history revealed recurrent occupational exposure to dogs as a photographer and walker, including a recent healing scratch to her right arm without evidence of local infection. Due to persistent leukocytosis and lack of clinical improvement, antimicrobial therapy was escalated to meropenem, resulting in gradual clinical and laboratory recovery. Blood cultures eventually grew Capnocytophaga species after delayed growth on anaerobic media. The patient was transitioned to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate to complete a two-week course. Susceptibility testing could not be performed because of insufficient organism growth. This case highlights the potential for severe Capnocytophaga bacteremia in an immunocompetent host with recurrent occupational exposure to animals. The nonspecific presentation and difficulty identifying this fastidious organism contributed to diagnostic uncertainty and delayed targeted therapy. Clinicians should consider Capnocytophaga infection in patients with unexplained sepsis and a history of animal exposure, even in the absence of a significant bite wound or overt soft-tissue infection.

Although human infection is typically associated with localized soft tissue disease following animal exposure, invasive infection can result in severe sepsis. We present a case of Capnocytophaga bacteremia in an immunocompetent woman with occupational exposure to dogs.

title: Ginkgo biloba Extract for Intermittent Claudication in Patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Intermittent claudication (IC) secondary to peripheral artery disease (PAD) causes exertional leg pain and discomfort, which limits functional walking capacity. The clinical efficacy of Ginkgo biloba extract (GBE) as a therapeutic agent for IC is debatable. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of GBE compared with a placebo in patients with IC due to PAD. Methods: Databases including PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and CINAHL were searched until 24 April 2026. Eligible studies included randomized, double-blind, controlled trials (RCTs) comparing placebo. Primary outcome was absolute claudication distance (ACD) at the end of the study. Secondary outcomes were initial claudication distance (ICD), ankle-brachial index (ABI), ankle pressure, and adverse events. Walking outcomes across various treadmill protocols were standardized to estimate caloric expenditure (kcal). A random-effects model was used to pool the effect estimates across trials. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB 2). Results: A total of 14 RCTs comprising 893 participants represent the total number randomized were included. GBE was associated with a statistically significant but modest improvement in ACD compared with placebo (mean difference [MD], 3.50 kcal; 95% CI, 0.02 to 6.98; p = 0.049). This benefit was significant in trials with a 24-week duration (MD, 4.67 kcal; 95% CI, 2.26 to 7.08; p < 0.001) but not in 12-16 weeks trials (MD, 1.35 kcal; 95% CI, -2.39 to 5.09; p = 0.48). No significant changes were observed for ICD or resting ABI/ankle pressure. GBE was well tolerated, with an overall adverse event incidence comparable to placebo. Conclusions: In patients with IC due to PAD, GBE therapy improves absolute walking performance, with a significant effect observed in trials evaluating 24 weeks of treatment. Given its favorable safety and tolerability profile, GBE can represent a clinically relevant and well-tolerated therapeutic option to support functional walking capacity, particularly for patients unable to tolerate or use conventional pharmacological agents.
englishSummary: Background/Objectives: Intermittent claudication (IC) secondary to peripheral artery disease (PAD) causes exertional leg pain and discomfort, which limits functional walking capacity. The clinical efficacy of Ginkgo biloba extract (GBE) as a therapeutic agent for IC is debatable. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of GBE compared with a placebo in patients with IC due to PAD.

title: N-Butyl Cyanoacrylate Use for the Management of Type II Endoleak in Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Objective: Different endovascular techniques are available for type II endoleak management. This scoping review aimed to summarize the available evidence on the use of N-Butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA) for type II endoleak management. Methods: This review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A protocol was registered on Open Science Framework. A systematic search using the PCC (Population, Concept, Context) framework was performed in PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library. Findings were systematically presented using structured tables summarizing NBCA techniques, efficacy and safety outcomes. Results: Following full-text assessment, 65 studies were included, comprising cohort and comparative studies, case reports, technical reports and preclinical studies. Single-arm cohort studies reported technical success rates of 90-100%, complication rates of 0-40% and variable durability outcomes, with clinical success ranging from 88 to 100%, endoleak resolution from 40 to 100% and aneurysm sac increase from 13 to 50%. Comparative studies reported improved outcomes with ethanol addition to the NBCA-ethiodized oil mixture compared with NBCA-ethiodized oil alone, shorter procedure times with direct puncture versus intra-arterial approach and more durable mid-term outcomes with selective embolization of contributing branches. Individually reported complications highlighted embolization risks and technical reports focused on catheter utilization. Pre-emptive embolization showed favorable outcomes on sac diameter reduction and endoleak type II occurrence. Conclusions: NBCA demonstrated technical feasibility for type II endoleak management, with variable durability. Considerable heterogeneity existed in access techniques, mixture ratios and outcome reporting. Preventive use demonstrated promising outcomes. Given the retrospective designs, limited sample sizes and heterogenous outcomes, adequately powered prospective studies are warranted.
englishSummary: Objective: Different endovascular techniques are available for type II endoleak management. This scoping review aimed to summarize the available evidence on the use of N-Butyl cyanoacrylate (NBCA) for type II endoleak management. Methods: This review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR).

title: Secondary TEVAR After Frozen Elephant Trunk: Indications and Timing.
abstract: Frozen elephant trunk (FET) stabilizes the arch and proximal descending aorta, but complete distal remodeling is achieved in only a subset of patients with aortic dissection. Persistent false lumen perfusion, aortic growth, and distal stent graft-induced new entry lead to secondary thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), and reported distal reintervention rates range from about 13% at 5 years in pooled data to 33% in a center with routine staging. This narrative review examines the indications for and timing of secondary TEVAR after FET. PubMed was searched to September 2026, and 97 publications were included. Evidence obtained in patients treated with FET is distinguished from evidence extrapolated from primary type B dissection and from the authors' interpretation. We summarize the predictors of incomplete remodeling, including stent graft length, residual re-entry location, chronicity, aortic diameter at the distal stent level, early remodeling trajectory, and heritable aortopathy, and we contrast planned completion with surveillance-based reactive TEVAR, including technical aspects and spinal cord protection. Direct evidence on timing after FET is limited to retrospective series and one pilot randomized trial of TEVAR 1 to 3 months after type I repair; most data on the time-dependent loss of flap plasticity come from primary type B dissection. No universal timing rule is supported. We propose a phenotype-driven approach, not yet validated, in which timing is referenced to dissection onset and individualized to aortic anatomy, disease progression, and clinical condition.
englishSummary: Frozen elephant trunk (FET) stabilizes the arch and proximal descending aorta, but complete distal remodeling is achieved in only a subset of patients with aortic dissection. Persistent false lumen perfusion, aortic growth, and distal stent graft-induced new entry lead to secondary thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), and reported distal reintervention rates range from about 13% at 5 years in pooled data to 33% in a center with routine staging. This narrative review examines the indications for and timing of secondary TEVAR after FET.

title: ClpB-mediated modulation of GroEL-bound luciferase and subsequent refolding by DnaK chaperone system.
abstract: In prokaryotes, DnaK-DnaJ-GrpE (KJE), GroEL-GroES (ELS) and the AAA+ disaggregase ClpB constitute the major ATP-dependent chaperone systems involved in protein quality control machinery. Although the individual functions and interplay of KJE and ClpB systems have been extensively studied, the role of ClpB with ELS during KJE-mediated substrate refolding is still elusive. Here, we investigated the role of ClpB in KJE- and ELS-mediated refolding of chemically and heat-denatured luciferase. Simultaneous presence of KJE, ELS and ClpB significantly enhanced the refolding of chemically denatured luciferase, whereas the combination of KJE and ClpB resulted in a higher refolding yield of heat-denatured luciferase. The inhibitory effect of ELS on KJE-mediated refolding of luciferase was significantly reduced when KJE, ELS and ClpB were present simultaneously. Sequential chaperone addition experiments showed that ELS-bound heat-denatured luciferase was refolded to 24% and 36% of its native activity by KJE and ClpB respectively, whereas the KJE-ClpB chaperone system further enhanced refolding to 43%. ClpB alone did not enhanced the refolding of ELS-bound chemically denatured luciferase, while subsequent addition of KJE or KJE-ClpB restored 36% and 44% of the native activity, respectively. Turbidity assay showed that the KJE system effectively suppressed heat-induced luciferase aggregation, whereas ClpB alone exhibited no anti-aggregation activity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that ClpB cooperates with the KJE chaperone system to enhance substrate refolding and rescue ELS-stalled substrate proteins, thus providing insights into the coordinated action of ATP-dependent chaperone systems in the maintenance of cellular protein homeostasis.

Here, we investigated the role of ClpB in KJE- and ELS-mediated refolding of chemically and heat-denatured luciferase.

title: Hemodynamic changes after artificial vessel reconstruction for common iliac artery aneurysm: a case report.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Isolated iliac artery aneurysms (IIAA) frequently coexist with abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), yet their causal association remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate hemodynamic alterations following artificial vessel reconstruction for iliac aneurysm and its impact on the abdominal aorta and iliac artery.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old man with a history of thyroid adenoma presented with left lower abdominal pain. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) revealed an aneurysm involving the entire left common iliac artery (48 mm × 55 mm × 81 mm). The patient was hemodynamically stable, with unremarkable physical examination and laboratory findings. He underwent aneurysm resection and aortoiliac reconstruction with a synthetic graft. Intraoperatively, arterial tortuosity and marked dilation at the bifurcation were noted. Postoperative CTA confirmed graft patency, and the patient recovered uneventfully. Preoperative and postoperative CTA scans were used for three-dimensional vascular reconstruction, followed by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to assess hemodynamic parameters including wall shear stress (WSS), blood pressure, and flow velocity.

CONCLUSION: Prosthetic vascular reconstruction for common iliac artery aneurysm (CIAA) may produce dual hemodynamic effects on the abdominal aorta. While the causal link between CIAA and AAA is unproven, the surgery eliminates rupture risk of the target aneurysm. These exploratory results may provide hemodynamic references to optimize surgical planning for iliac artery aneurysms.

This study aimed to investigate hemodynamic alterations following artificial vessel reconstruction for iliac aneurysm and its impact on the abdominal aorta and iliac artery. CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old man with a history of thyroid adenoma presented with left lower abdominal pain.

title: Social-biological misalignment modulates the prognostic impact of infarct volume after endovascular thrombectomy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) achieves high rates of reperfusion, yet functional recovery remains heterogeneous. We investigated whether social-biological time misalignment modifies the association between final infarct volume and 90-day functional outcome.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 160 patients with large vessel occlusion treated with EVT. Misalignment was quantified using a composite score incorporating occupational shift exposure and symptom onset timing. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the interaction between misalignment and final infarct volume on favorable 90-day outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-2).

RESULTS: Misalignment was not independently associated with favorable outcome. However, a significant interaction was observed (OR = 9.70, 95% CI 1.74-54.10, LRT p = 0.008), remaining significant after FDR correction (q = 0.034), stable across profile likelihood and Firth penalized regression. The interaction improved model fit (AIC 124.35 → 119.38) and provided modest incremental net benefit. Exploratory threshold analysis suggested a potential inflection point approximating 25 mL, but this is hypothesis-generating and requires validation.

CONCLUSION: Misalignment does not exert a uniform adverse effect but acts as a state-dependent modifier, modifying the association between final infarct volume and favorable outcome. The interaction between chronobiological state and infarct burden offers a novel framework for understanding outcome heterogeneity.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) achieves high rates of reperfusion, yet functional recovery remains heterogeneous. We investigated whether social-biological time misalignment modifies the association between final infarct volume and 90-day functional outcome. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 160 patients with large vessel occlusion treated with EVT.
