title: Machine-learning-derived laboratory signatures associated with postoperative day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis after fractures around the knee.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to construct risk-discrimination models for postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) status in patients with fractures around the knee (FAK) using five machine-learning algorithms and compare model performance across five machine-learning algorithms.

METHODS: Electronic medical records of 1,071 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FAK at Suining Central Hospital from January 2023 to August 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 749) and a test set (n = 322) at a 7:3 ratio. Feature selection occurred exclusively within the training dataset. Predictive variables were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, the Boruta algorithm, and recursive feature elimination-extreme gradient boosting (RFE-XGBoost). Five predictive models were developed, including logistic regression, k-nearest neighbor (KNN), random forest (RF), light gradient-boosting machine (LightGBM), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Model performance was evaluated comprehensively via the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. Receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision-curve analysis (DCA) were utilized to identify the selected model. Finally, Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were employed to interpret the global and local prediction outputs of the selected model.

RESULTS: Seventeen overlapping features were identified via feature-selection procedures for final modelling, among which postoperative-day-1 and postoperative-day-3 laboratory biomarkers contributed most substantially to model output. XGBoost was chosen for subsequent SHAP interpretability analyses based on balanced performance observed in cross-validated out-of-fold outputs from the training set. Several non-linear models yielded comparably high discrimination, with overlapping 95% confidence intervals for AUROC.The cross-validated AUC for the XGBoost model in the training set was 0.9932, with a classification threshold of 0.57 derived from the Youden index. In the test set, the AUROC was 0.998 (95% CI: 0.993-1.000), AUPRC was 0.996 (95% CI: 0.988-1.000), accuracy was 0.991 (95% CI: 0.978-1.000), sensitivity was 0.969 (95% CI: 0.930-1.000), specificity was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), precision was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), and F1-score was 0.984 (95% CI: 0.964-1.000). The Brier score for the test set was 0.013. Calibration curves and decision-curve analysis demonstrated favourable probability calibration and higher estimated net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. SHAP-value analysis highlighted that postoperative-day-1 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FIB, postoperative-day-3 APTT, postoperative-day-3 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FDP, postoperative-day-3 PT, postoperative-day-1 UREA, and postoperative-day-1 CREA were major contributing features.

CONCLUSION: The XGBoost model demonstrated excellent discrimination and favorable calibration in the internal test set for identifying postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected DVT among patients with FAK. However, several predictors in the final model were measured on postoperative day 3, temporally proximate to the time-point of DVT ascertainment; these biomarkers may reflect biochemical changes secondary to already-formed thrombus rather than pre-thrombotic prospective risk signals. Therefore, the near-perfect discrimination observed in this retrospective cohort should be interpreted cautiously and should not be regarded as definitive evidence of prospective early-prediction performance. Temporal and multicenter external validation using a prespecified prediction time point, ideally restricted to variables available prior to DVT assessment, is required to determine the model's generalizability and prospective clinical applicability.

METHODS: Electronic medical records of 1,071 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FAK at Suining Central Hospital from January 2023 to August 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 749) and a test set (n = 322) at a 7:3 ratio.

title: Triglyceride-glucose index and the incidence of peripheral artery disease: a dose-response meta-analysis of longitudinal studies.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a simple surrogate marker of insulin resistance and has been increasingly investigated as a predictor of cardiovascular diseases. However, longitudinal evidence regarding its association with incident peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains limited and inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis to evaluate the association between the TyG index and the risk of incident PAD.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were systematically searched from inception to June 28, 2026. Longitudinal observational studies evaluating the association between the conventional TyG index and incidents PAD in adults were eligible. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) comparing the highest versus lowest TyG categories were calculated using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models. Linear and nonlinear dose-response meta-analyses were performed using restricted cubic spline models.

RESULTS: Five longitudinal studies involving 417,499 participants and 7,800 incident PAD events were included. Compared with the lowest TyG category, a high TyG index was associated with a significantly increased risk of incident PAD (RR = 1.49, 95% CI 1.06 to 2.10; p = 0.02), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 88.4%). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated robust findings. In the linear dose-response meta-analysis, each 1-unit increase in the TyG index was associated with a 22% higher risk of incident PAD (RR = 1.22, 95% CI 1.08 to 1.37; p = 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a significant overall dose-response association (p = 0.001) with no evidence of nonlinearity (p for nonlinearity = 0.367), indicating an approximately linear relationship between the TyG index and PAD risk.

CONCLUSIONS: A higher TyG index is associated with an increased risk of incident PAD in a dose-dependent and approximately linear manner.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261470450.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a simple surrogate marker of insulin resistance and has been increasingly investigated as a predictor of cardiovascular diseases. However, longitudinal evidence regarding its association with incident peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains limited and inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis to evaluate the association between the TyG index and the risk of incident PAD.

title: Efficacy and safety of flow diverters for middle cerebral artery bifurcation aneurysms: a retrospective dual-center study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of flow diverters (FDs) for the treatment of middle cerebral artery (MCA) bifurcation aneurysms.

METHODS: This retrospective, dual-center study enrolled 29 patients with unruptured MCA bifurcation aneurysms treated with flow diverters (FDs) between January 2021 and December 2024. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS), where scores of 0-2 indicated a favorable functional outcome. Aneurysm occlusion was evaluated at the 6-month follow-up using the O'Kelly-Marotta (OKM) grading scale on digital subtraction angiography (DSA). Procedure-related complications, including in-stent stenosis (ISS), were systematically recorded.

RESULTS: All 29 aneurysms were successfully treated with FD, with no technical failures, in-stent thrombosis, cerebral hemorrhage, or ischemic events observed during the perioperative period. No patients developed new neurological deficits before discharge. All patients were followed up via telephone and outpatient visits after discharge. Six-month angiographic follow-up was performed in all 29 patients by DSA. The follow-up duration ranged from 6 to 43.2 months. At the final follow-up, one patient developed vertigo and a transient episode of left limb weakness more than 2 months after treatment. The mRS score was 0 in 28 patients and 1 in one patient. The 6-month angiographic outcomes were: OKM Grade A in 1 patient (3.4%), Grade B in 5 (17.3%), Grade C in 7 (24.1%), and Grade D in 16 (55.2%). ISS was observed in 3 patients (10.3%): one moderate proximal, one moderate mid-stent, and one diffuse severe stenosis. The overall procedure-related complication rate was 3.4% (1/29), with a mortality rate of 0%. The probability of achieving complete occlusion was >88.8% for necks ≤ 3.0 mm, compared to >53.3% for necks between 3.0-5.0 mm.

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that the use of FDs is an effective and safe therapeutic option for MCA bifurcation aneurysms. A neck diameter ≤ 5.0 mm was associated with a higher likelihood of complete occlusion; this association requires external validation.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of flow diverters (FDs) for the treatment of middle cerebral artery (MCA) bifurcation aneurysms. METHODS: This retrospective, dual-center study enrolled 29 patients with unruptured MCA bifurcation aneurysms treated with flow diverters (FDs) between January 2021 and December 2024. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS), where scores of 0-2 indicated a favorable functional outcome.

title: Delayed Renal Artery Stump Pseudoaneurysm and Arteriovenous Fistula Following Nephrectomy Complicated by Pulmonary Coil Migration: Successful Laparoscopic Management.
abstract: Background: Renal arteriovenous fistula (RAVF) and renal artery pseudoaneurysm (RAP) are rare vascular complications that may occur following renal surgery, trauma, or endovascular interventions. Delayed presentation after nephrectomy is exceptionally uncommon. Case Description: We report the case of a 59-year-old woman with a pseudoaneurysm of the left renal artery stump associated with a high-flow renal arteriovenous fistula who was diagnosed three decades after left nephrectomy performed for complicated nephrolithiasis. The patient presented with episodic left flank pain without haematuria. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) and selective angiography confirmed the presence of a pseudoaneurysm and a high-flow arteriovenous fistula. Endovascular coil embolization was initially attempted; however, the coil migrated through the high-flow fistulous tract into the peripheral left pulmonary arterial circulation. Because the patient remained asymptomatic and haemodynamically stable and the coil was located peripherally, the procedural risk of retrieval was considered to outweigh the anticipated benefit. The coil was therefore left in situ under clinical and imaging surveillance. Because substantial arteriovenous shunting persisted after the unsuccessful embolization, definitive laparoscopic ligation of the left renal artery and vein stumps was successfully performed approximately one month later. During the two-year follow-up, two CTA examinations and Doppler ultrasonography confirmed complete occlusion of the fistula and pseudoaneurysm, with no recurrent abdominal symptoms or pulmonary complications related to the migrated coil. Discussion: Although post-nephrectomy arteriovenous fistulas presenting 28 and 45 years after surgery have previously been reported, the combination of a renal artery stump pseudoaneurysm, a high-flow fistula, pulmonary coil migration, persistent arteriovenous shunting, and subsequent successful laparoscopic management is particularly unusual. This case highlights the technical challenges of endovascular treatment in high-flow fistulas and the role of surgical management following unsuccessful embolization. Conclusions: Delayed renal artery stump pseudoaneurysm associated with renal arteriovenous fistula after nephrectomy is an extremely rare condition. Although endovascular embolization remains the preferred first-line treatment, surgical management may be necessary in cases complicated by technical failure or embolization-related complications.

Delayed presentation after nephrectomy is exceptionally uncommon. Case Description: We report the case of a 59-year-old woman with a pseudoaneurysm of the left renal artery stump associated with a high-flow renal arteriovenous fistula who was diagnosed three decades after left nephrectomy performed for complicated nephrolithiasis.

title: Venous Thromboembolism and Pregnancy: Prevention and Treatment.
abstract: Pregnancy-related venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality. Physiologic changes in pregnancy, along with patient-specific and pregnancy-specific risk factors, increase this VTE risk. The prevention and treatment of pregnancy-related VTE is often complex and requires the careful consideration of variation in clinical guidelines, VTE risk profile, bleeding assessment, careful delivery planning and patient preference. The mainstay of treatment for an acute VTE in pregnancy is the use of low-molecular-weight heparin. In this review, we highlight three clinical cases to review clinical approaches to the prevention and treatment of VTE in pregnancy in these scenarios. Importantly, this review goes over the current understanding of the pathophysiology and clinical practice experience for pregnant patients with VTE. We also explored the variation in professional clinical guidelines on VTE prophylaxis and treatment strategies in pregnancy, and how these guidelines may be interpreted in the context of patient care for optimal outcomes.

title: Radiomics performance to identify high-risk carotid artery plaques: a systematic review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with 15-20% of ischemic strokes caused by extracranial carotid atherosclerotic disease. Risk stratification has traditionally relied on luminal stenosis severity, which inadequately reflects plaque vulnerability. Radiomics offers an emerging solution by extracting high-dimensional quantitative data from standard medical images. This systematic review evaluated the performance of radiomics-based models for identifying high-risk carotid plaques.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across multiple databases. Studies were included if they developed or validated radiomics-based models for carotid plaque assessment and reported performance metrics, specifically the area under the curve (AUC). Data were extracted on study design, imaging modalities, segmentation methods, and modeling techniques.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies involving 6,108 patients (72.4% male) were included. Computed tomography angiography was the most commonly used imaging modality (n = 16), and manual region-of-interest segmentation was performed in 27 of 28 studies. Radiomics models showed strong predictive performance. Internal validation AUCs were as high as 0.984, whereas combined models incorporating radiomics with clinical and/or conventional radiological features achieved the best predictive accuracy, often exceeding 0.90. However, only four studies included external validation cohorts.

CONCLUSION: Radiomics is a powerful, non-invasive tool for identifying high-risk carotid plaques, offering superior discriminative power over conventional stenosis-based assessments. Despite these promising results, the field faces significant hurdles, and future research must prioritize prospective multicenter trials, the development of automated segmentation workflows, and the correlation of radiomic features with histopathological findings to ensure clinical reproducibility and transition into routine stroke prevention.

KEY POINTS: Question Standard carotid atherosclerotic disease assessments fail to capture biological plaque complexity and vulnerability, necessitating objective, reproducible, and non-invasive methods to improve stroke prevention. Findings Radiomics and combined models demonstrate superior capability in identifying high-risk carotid plaques compared to traditional assessments. With four external validations, the field remains exploratory. Relevance statement Radiomics offers a non-invasive tool for personalized stroke prevention. However, technical barriers currently prevent its transition to routine clinical use, including reliance on manual segmentation and low compliance with international standardization guidelines.

title: Role of Microcatheter Tip Position and Microguidewire Stiffness in Safe Neuroendovascular Navigation of Distal Vessels.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Advancements in neuroendovascular devices have enabled greater access to distal, tortuous vasculature. However, this expanded capability also increases the risk of serious hemorrhagic complications during device navigation. The aim of the study is to quantify how microcatheter position and microguidewire stiffness affect tip contact force at a distal MCA segment.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A moderate-tortuosity silicone model of the MCA was used to evaluate three 0.014-inch Synchro SELECT microguidewires (Soft, Standard, and Support) with a TrevoTrak microcatheter positioned proximally in the M1 or distally in the M2 segment. Tip contact forces at the distal end of the M2 segment were recorded with a digital force gauge serving as a standardized surrogate for the distal vessel wall during motorized controlled wire advancement. From the force-distance curves, tip contact force slopes (mN/mm) and maximum tip contact forces (mN) were calculated and statistically compared across wire types and catheter positions.

RESULTS: With distal microcatheter support, the average tip contact force slopes were 10.64 mN/mm (Soft), 10.85 mN/mm (Standard), and 15.28 mN/mm (Support) (P < .0001). With proximal support, the average slopes were significantly lower: 1.61 mN/mm (Soft), 3.15 mN/mm (Standard), and 3.87 mN/mm (Support) (P < .01). Distal microcatheter positioning consistently produced approximately 3- to 6-fold higher tip contact force slopes and higher maximum tip contact forces than proximal positioning.

CONCLUSIONS: Microcatheter tip position and microguidewire stiffness were the primary determinants of the tip contact force transmitted to distal vessel segments during neuroendovascular navigation in this model. Stiffer microguidewires exert significantly greater tip contact force, particularly when the microcatheter is positioned near the distal segment. Maintaining the microcatheter tip proximally attenuates these forces and offers a simple strategy to reduce mechanic loading of fragile distal branches during distal access procedures.

The aim of the study is to quantify how microcatheter position and microguidewire stiffness affect tip contact force at a distal MCA segment.

title: Histologically Validated Ex Vivo Characterization of Intraplaque Hemorrhage and Lipid Components Using Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Accurate characterization of carotid plaque components is essential for stroke risk assessment. Intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) is a well-established marker of plaque vulnerability, whereas lipid-rich necrotic cores (LRNCs) often show overlapping signal characteristics with IPH on conventional MRI. The purpose of this study was to compare quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) with conventional MRI in differentiating IPH and lipid components in carotid plaques using ex vivo histologic validation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty-four carotid plaque specimens obtained by en bloc excision during carotid endarterectomy between October 2017 and August 2021 were examined. All specimens underwent ex vivo MRI at 3T, including T1WI, T2WI, and TOF-equivalent FLASH, as well as QSM reconstructed from multiecho FLASH phase data. After MRI, specimens were serially sectioned and stained using H&E and immunohistochemical techniques. ROIs corresponding to histologically confirmed IPH and lipid components were delineated on MRI by consensus of 2 radiologists. On conventional MRI, signal intensities were measured in corresponding histologic regions, and contrast-to-noise ratios (CNRs) were calculated relative to surrounding agarose gel. On QSM, absolute magnetic susceptibility values were measured in the same regions. The difference between plaque tissue and the surrounding agarose gel was defined as the relative susceptibility value (rSV), which was used for statistical analysis. CNRs and rSVs among plaque components were compared using the Kruskal-Wallis test, followed by the Steel-Dwass test for pair-wise comparisons.

RESULTS: Seventy-nine matched cross-sectional slices were analyzed, yielding 24 IPH, 61 LRNCs, and 13 foam-cell aggregates (FAs). No significant difference in CNR was observed between IPH and LRNC on T1WI or FLASH. Histopathologic analysis demonstrated that many LRNCs exhibited erythrocyte-derived remnants consistent with prior hemorrhagic events. FAs showed lower CNRs than IPH on T1WI and FLASH (P < .05). On T2WI, IPH showed lower CNRs than LRNCs or FAs (P < .05). On QSM, IPH demonstrated higher rSVs than LRNCs or FAs (P < .01).

CONCLUSIONS: Histologic validation demonstrates that many LRNCs contain erythrocyte remnants, which may contribute to their overlapping signal characteristics with IPH on conventional MRI. QSM captures erythrocyte-derived susceptibility effects within plaques and provides complementary susceptibility-based information not available from conventional MRI.

Intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) is a well-established marker of plaque vulnerability, whereas lipid-rich necrotic cores (LRNCs) often show overlapping signal characteristics with IPH on conventional MRI. The purpose of this study was to compare quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) with conventional MRI in differentiating IPH and lipid components in carotid plaques using ex vivo histologic validation.

title: Characterization of Perfusion Scotoma in Acute Ischemic Stroke after Endovascular Treatment.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: CTP may underestimate the size of the ischemic core, a phenomenon known as perfusion scotoma. We aimed to investigate the prevalence of perfusion scotoma, characterize its baseline predictors, and explore its association with functional outcomes in a real-world population of patients with stroke treated with endovascular treatment (EVT).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data were obtained from a prospective EVT registry, selecting patients with successful recanaliztion (final modified TICI ≥2b), a good-quality baseline CTP, and an available 24-hour noncontrast CT. Ischemic core underestimated volume (ICuV) was calculated as the difference between follow-up infarct volume and CTP-estimated ischemic core. The primary outcome was the presence of perfusion scotoma, defined as ICuV ≥10 mL. Baseline characteristics with P value <.20 in univariable comparisons were entered in a backward stepwise, multivariable logistic regression analysis to identify factors independently associated with perfusion scotoma.

RESULTS: A total of 464 patients of 672 (69%) were included in the analysis. The median age was 74 years (interquartile range = 68-83), 215 (46.3%) were men, and 116 (25%) had a perfusion scotoma. Perfusion scotoma was independently associated with male sex (adjusted OR 1.62 [95% CI, 1.01-2.51]; P = .04), more distal site of occlusion (adjusted OR 1.60 [95% CI, 1.10-2.34]; P = .01; per each 1-point increase: terminal ICA to M1 to M2), lower ASPECTS at admission (adjusted OR 0.64 [95% CI, 0.54-0.76]; P < .001; per each 1-point increase), and longer onset-to-CT time (adjusted OR 1.05, [95% CI, 1.01-1.10]; P = .03; per each 1-hour increase). The optimal onset-to-CT time cutoff to distinguish between patients without and with perfusion scotoma was 420 minutes. Perfusion scotoma was associated with 90-day ordinal mRS (adjusted common OR 3.16 [95% CI, 2.12-4.76]).

CONCLUSIONS: Perfusion scotoma occurred in 1 of every 4 patients. Baseline predictors included male sex, lower ASPECTS, more distal vessel occlusion, and longer onset-to-CT time. Perfusion scotoma was associated with poorer functional outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data were obtained from a prospective EVT registry, selecting patients with successful recanaliztion (final modified TICI ≥2b), a good-quality baseline CTP, and an available 24-hour noncontrast CT.

title: Tranexamic Acid Administration is Associated With Lower Transfusion Rates and Wound Complications Following Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty for Periprosthetic Joint Infection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used in total joint arthroplasty, but data on its efficacy in periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) of the knee are scarce. We assessed TXA efficacy in revision total knee arthroplasty (TKA) for PJI.

METHODS: A national database was queried for patients ≥18 years undergoing stage-one revision TKA for PJI from 2016 to 2023. Patients with and without TXA exposure were propensity matched. Multivariable logistic regression assessed primary outcomes (postoperative transfusion, bleeding complications, and wound complications) and secondary outcomes (thromboembolic complications).

RESULTS: Overall, 13,247 TXA patients were matched 1:1 to 13,247 non-TXA patients on comorbidities, Charlson Comorbidity Index, demographics, hospital characteristics, and preoperative transfusion rates, all with standardized mean differences <0.10. Mean age was 67.4 years in both cohorts, with similar use of venous thromboembolic chemoprophylaxis. TXA was associated with decreased adjusted odds of postoperative transfusion (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 0.77, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.69-0.85, P < .001) and aggregate wound complications (aOR: 0.65, 95% CI: 0.60-0.70, P < .001), with similar odds of aggregate bleeding complications (aOR: 1.02, 95% CI: 0.95-1.09, P = .563). Odds of aggregate venous thromboembolism (aOR: 0.97, 95% CI: 0.82-1.13, P = .874), deep vein thrombosis (aOR: 1.00, 95% CI: 1.00-1.01, P = .309), and pulmonary embolism (aOR: 1.06, 95% CI: 0.83-1.34, P = .639) were similar.

CONCLUSIONS: TXA was associated with lower rates of transfusion and aggregate wound complications, without increased venous thromboembolism risk, during revision TKA for PJI.

We assessed TXA efficacy in revision total knee arthroplasty (TKA) for PJI. METHODS: A national database was queried for patients ≥18 years undergoing stage-one revision TKA for PJI from 2016 to 2023.

title: Emphysematous osteomyelitis of the lower extremity: Prevalence, imaging features, interobserver agreement and clinical outcomes in a 16-hospital cohort.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To estimate emphysematous osteomyelitis (EO) observed prevalence, compare 3-month major adverse events (death or major amputation) between EO and nonemphysematous osteomyelitis (NEO), and assess interobserver agreement for key imaging features.

METHODS: In this retrospective 16-hospital study, radiology-report text screening followed by manual report review identified CT and MRI examinations demonstrating lower-extremity osteomyelitis. EO was defined as intraosseous gas without direct bone-to-air communication. Forty-five EO cases met criteria, and 180 NEO cases were randomly sampled in a 4:1 ratio for prognostic comparison. Associations with 3-month major adverse events were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Three radiologists independently reviewed 90 cases (45 EO, 45 NEO) to assess interobserver agreement.

RESULTS: Of the 1417 imaging examinations that identified lower-extremity osteomyelitis, 45 (3.2%) met the study's EO inclusion criteria. Major adverse events occurred within 3 months in 33.3% (15/45) of EO cases and 12.8% (23/180) of nonemphysematous osteomyelitis cases. EO (adjusted OR, 3.22; 95% CI, 1.46-7.12; p = .004) and peripheral artery disease (adjusted OR, 3.11; 95% CI, 1.38-7.03; p = .006) were independently associated with higher odds of death or major amputation within 3 months. Agreement for intraosseous gas was substantial on CT (κ = 0.71) and almost perfect on MRI (κ = 0.81).

CONCLUSION: EO is uncommon but associated with worse 3-month outcomes. Our findings support consideration of EO as a potential imaging marker of short-term adverse outcomes in patients with lower-extremity osteomyelitis.

METHODS: In this retrospective 16-hospital study, radiology-report text screening followed by manual report review identified CT and MRI examinations demonstrating lower-extremity osteomyelitis. EO was defined as intraosseous gas without direct bone-to-air communication.

title: Pipeline embolization device with adjunctive coiling for ruptured blood blister-like aneurysms: a multicenter study focusing on Hunt-Hess grade I-III patients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood blister-like aneurysms (BBAs) of the internal carotid artery are rare and inherently unstable lesions that carry a high risk of rebleeding. Evidence regarding the outcomes of Pipeline embolization device (PED)-assisted coiling specifically in patients with mild-to-moderate neurological deficits (Hunt-Hess grade I-III) remains limited.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study, conducted at three comprehensive stroke centers between January 2018 and December 2023, included 28 consecutive patients with ruptured ICA BBAs. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of PED combined with adjunctive coil embolization using a deliberate loose-scaffolding strategy.

RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 100% of cases. Immediate complete angiographic occlusion (modified Raymond-Roy class I) was observed in 67.9% (19/28), increasing to 75.0% (21/28) overall at 12 months and reaching 95.5% (21/22) among those with available imaging follow-up. Notably, all seven patients with residual neck filling on immediate postoperative angiography who completed follow-up subsequently achieved complete occlusion. Favorable clinical outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) was recorded in 92.9% (26/28) at last follow-up. Perioperative complications occurred in 39.3% (11/28), predominantly neurological, including symptomatic vasospasm (21.4%, 6/28) and cerebral infarction (14.3%, 4/28); perioperative mortality was 3.6% (1/28).

CONCLUSION: PED-assisted coil embolization with a loose-scaffolding strategy is technically feasible and may yield favorable outcomes in selected patients with mild-to-moderate neurologic deficits. However, given the retrospective, single-arm design and modest sample size, these results are hypothesis-generating; prospective comparative studies are warranted.

Evidence regarding the outcomes of Pipeline embolization device (PED)-assisted coiling specifically in patients with mild-to-moderate neurological deficits (Hunt-Hess grade I-III) remains limited. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study, conducted at three comprehensive stroke centers between January 2018 and December 2023, included 28 consecutive patients with ruptured ICA BBAs.

title: "Inflammation-Thrombosis Dissociation": a retrospective study of early DVT differences after UKA between Han Chinese and Tibetan patients at high altitude.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence of early lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) after unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) between Han Chinese and Tibetan patients at high altitude, to analyze the relationships of inflammatory, hematologic, and coagulation indices with DVT, and to explore whether an "inflammation-thrombosis dissociation" phenomenon exists across ethnic groups.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 147 patients who underwent primary medial UKA at the Affiliated Hospital of Qinghai University (altitude 2,261 m) between March 2024 and June 2026, including 93 Tibetan and 54 Han Chinese patients. All patients received a standardized perioperative management protocol, including postoperative aspirin 100 mg once daily for venous thrombosis prophylaxis, and underwent bilateral lower-extremity venous color Doppler ultrasonography on postoperative days 2-3. Demographic characteristics, platelet count, hemoglobin, D-dimer, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, and aggregate index of systemic inflammation were collected. Propensity score matching was used to control differences in age, sex, and body mass index, and Firth logistic regression was used to analyze factors associated with DVT.

RESULTS: Among the 147 patients, 14 developed postoperative DVT, for an overall incidence of 9.52%. The DVT incidence was 4.30% (4/93) in Tibetan patients, lower than the 18.52% (10/54) observed in Han Chinese patients (P = 0.007). Platelet count, D-dimer, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, and aggregate index of systemic inflammation were all higher in Tibetan than in Han Chinese patients; however, these higher values did not correspond to a higher DVT incidence. After 1:1 matching for age, sex, and body mass index, 16 matched pairs were obtained; DVT incidences were 18.8% in Han Chinese patients and 0% in Tibetan patients. The difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.250), although the direction of the association was consistent with that before matching. Firth penalized-likelihood logistic regression showed that increasing age was associated with higher odds of DVT in Model 2 (OR = 1.110, 95% CI: 1.028-1.211, P = 0.007). In the primary model adjusted for age and BMI (Model 3), Tibetan ethnicity was associated with lower odds of DVT than Han Chinese ethnicity (OR = 0.206, 95% CI: 0.038-0.948, P = 0.042). However, this association was no longer statistically significant after further adjustment for sex (Model 4: OR = 0.243, 95% CI: 0.040-1.376, P = 0.109). In exploratory models separately incorporating postoperative platelet count, D-dimer, systemic immune-inflammation index, or aggregate index of systemic inflammation (Models 5-8), the association between ethnicity and DVT remained statistically significant (all P < 0.05), whereas none of these laboratory indices showed a statistically significant association with DVT (all P > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Among high-altitude UKA patients receiving a uniform aspirin prophylaxis regimen, Han Chinese patients had a higher incidence of early postoperative DVT than Tibetan patients. Although Tibetan patients had higher platelet counts and composite inflammatory indices, these measures did not increase in parallel with DVT events, suggesting a possible dissociation between inflammatory phenotype and clinical thrombotic risk among different ethnic groups at high altitude. Age and ethnicity were relatively stable DVT-associated factors in this cohort, whereas platelet count, D-dimer, and platelet-inflammation composite indices were insufficient to explain the between-ethnicity difference in risk. Given the single-center retrospective design and the limited number of outcome events and matched patients, these findings require further validation in multicenter, large-sample prospective studies.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 147 patients who underwent primary medial UKA at the Affiliated Hospital of Qinghai University (altitude 2,261 m) between March 2024 and June 2026, including 93 Tibetan and 54 Han Chinese patients. All patients received a standardized perioperative management protocol, including postoperative aspirin 100 mg once daily for venous thrombosis prophylaxis, and underwent bilateral lower-extremity venous color Doppler ultrasonography on postoperative days 2-3.

title: Modified Hybrid Repair with Open Reconstruction of Infrarenal Aortoiliac Segment for Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms Without Custom Distal Landing Zone: A Single-Center Case Series.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Inadequate distal landing zones can limit hybrid repair of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA). We evaluated a modified strategy combining prosthetic distal landing-zone reconstruction, retrograde visceral and renal revascularization, and thoracic stent-graft exclusion. Methods: This retrospective single-center case series included all nine consecutive patients with inadequate native distal landing zones who underwent single-stage modified hybrid repair in 2025. Open aneurysm excision and aortoiliac reconstruction provided the distal sealing segment and inflow for visceral and renal bypasses. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included postoperative length of hospital stay, 30-day major complication rate, 30-day paraplegia rate, 1-year reintervention rate, 30-day readmission rate, and technical success rate. Results: Five patients had Crawford extent II aneurysms and four had extent III aneurysms. Technical success was achieved in all nine patients. Median operative time, estimated blood loss, and intensive care unit stay were 724 min, 2500 mL, and 8 days, respectively. Thirty-day all-cause mortality was 0% (0/9). No spinal cord ischemia or mesenteric ischemia occurred within 30 days. Acute kidney injury occurred in six patients (66.7%), including one who received continuous renal replacement therapy. One patient required early covered stent-graft repair of a right iliac anastomotic leak. At a median follow-up of 9 months (IQR, 6-12), all reconstructed visceral and renal bypasses were patent, no new endoleak was detected, and all patients were alive. No additional reintervention was required. Conclusions: Modified hybrid repair with prosthetic distal landing-zone reconstruction was technically feasible in selected TAAA patients with inadequate distal sealing anatomy. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to evaluate durability and refine indications.

We evaluated a modified strategy combining prosthetic distal landing-zone reconstruction, retrograde visceral and renal revascularization, and thoracic stent-graft exclusion. Methods: This retrospective single-center case series included all nine consecutive patients with inadequate native distal landing zones who underwent single-stage modified hybrid repair in 2025.

title: Acute ischemic stroke in a young adult with persistently reduced protein S levels: a case report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Protein S deficiency is a rare thrombophilic disorder whose contribution to arterial ischemic stroke in young adults remains uncertain. While its association with venous thromboembolism is well established, evidence supporting a causal association with arterial ischemic stroke is limited.

PRESENTATION OF THE CASE: A 34-year-old woman with no vascular risk factors presented with acute right-sided hemiparesis and dysarthria of 6 hours' duration. Examination showed right upper motor neuron facial palsy, right-sided hemiparesis (power 3/5), and a positive Babinski sign on the right side. Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain showed an acute infarct in the left paramedian pons. Thrombophilia workup at 2 weeks showed a low free Protein S antigen level of 42% (reference range, 50-134%) by immunoturbidimetric assay. Recognized acquired causes of low Protein S were excluded. Antiplatelet therapy was discontinued, and rivaroxaban, 20 mg daily, was initiated as an individualized decision. The patient recovered fully with no recurrent thrombotic events at 3 months. Due to financial constraints, only the Protein S antigen level was reassessed at 3 months, which showed a persistently low free Protein S antigen level (40%). Without genetic testing, family screening, and total Protein S antigen measurement, the findings were considered suggestive of, but not diagnostic of, inherited Protein S deficiency.

CONCLUSION: This case report highlights persistently reduced protein S antigen levels as a possible but unconfirmed contributor to an otherwise cryptogenic arterial stroke in a young adult. It emphasizes that thrombophilia testing should be considered selectively in young stroke patients, after excluding more common etiologies, rather than performed routinely.

While its association with venous thromboembolism is well established, evidence supporting a causal association with arterial ischemic stroke is limited. PRESENTATION OF THE CASE: A 34-year-old woman with no vascular risk factors presented with acute right-sided hemiparesis and dysarthria of 6 hours' duration.

title: Age-specific associations of endovascular therapy and reperfusion delay with outcomes after large vessel occlusion: a regional registry study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The benefit of endovascular therapy (EVT) in very elderly patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) remains uncertain, and sensitivity to reperfusion delay may differ by age. We evaluated age-specific associations of treatment and reperfusion time with functional outcomes.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analysed 1,280 patients with acute LVO in an emergency medical service-based registry, divided into groups aged 85 years or older and younger than 85 years. The primary outcome was an ordinal shift towards a better 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score. Secondary outcomes were dichotomized functional measures incorporating prestroke status.

RESULTS: Among 837 patients younger than 85 years, EVT was associated with a favourable mRS shift (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.47; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07-2.01). Among 443 patients aged 85 years or older, the estimate was favourable but not statistically significant (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 0.87-1.92). No significant age-by-treatment interaction was observed for functional outcomes. Among patients treated with successful reperfusion by EVT, favourable outcomes declined more steeply with increasing onset-to-reperfusion time in those aged 85 years or older.

DISCUSSION: The association of EVT with functional outcomes was not significantly modified by age but estimates in very elderly patients were less precise. Very elderly patients appeared more vulnerable to reperfusion delay.

CONCLUSION: Treatment selection should integrate prestroke function, stroke severity, imaging findings, procedural feasibility, and the likelihood of rapid reperfusion rather than age alone.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: The benefit of endovascular therapy (EVT) in very elderly patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) remains uncertain, and sensitivity to reperfusion delay may differ by age. We evaluated age-specific associations of treatment and reperfusion time with functional outcomes. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analysed 1,280 patients with acute LVO in an emergency medical service-based registry, divided into groups aged 85 years or older and younger than 85 years.

title: Electrosurgical Septotomy Across the Full Spectrum of Aortic Dissection.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Transcatheter electrosurgical septotomy divides the dissection membrane to reconstitute a single aortic lumen. Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion.

METHODS: A retrospective intention-to-treat analysis of 21 consecutive patients scheduled for septotomy between June 2022 and May 2026. The membrane was crossed by needle re-entry and divided with an electrified through-and-through guidewire at 40-60 W under fluoroscopy, without routine intravascular ultrasound or image fusion. A perfused-lumen index (perfused lumen divided by total aortic diameter) was measured before and after the procedure.

RESULTS: Septotomy was performed in 20 of 21 patients (technical success 95% on an intention-to-treat basis). Indications were landing-zone preparation (57%), malperfusion (33%), preparation for open repair, and true-lumen collapse. Malperfusion resolved in all 7 patients treated for that indication, and the perfused-lumen index rose from a median of 0.16 to 0.98 (18 patients, P < .001). There was no stroke, spinal cord ischaemia, or retrograde type A dissection. Thirty-day, in-hospital, and overall mortality were 10%, 14%, and 19%, respectively, with 1 fatal delayed aortic rupture and no intraprocedural death. Three unplanned reinterventions occurred; median follow-up was 5.1 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Electrosurgical septotomy was feasible across the full spectrum of aortic dissection and, in selected patients, as stand-alone treatment for malperfusion, using standard electrosurgical equipment. Given the small, heterogeneous cohort and short follow-up, these findings demonstrate feasibility rather than durability.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Transcatheter electrosurgical septotomy divides the dissection membrane to reconstitute a single aortic lumen. Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion.

title: Superficial venous procedures improve clinical and hemodynamic outcomes in patients with concomitant deep venous reflux: a prospective observational study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Concurrent deep venous reflux (DVR) is frequently observed in patients with superficial venous reflux (SVR). However, the effect of SVR treatment on symptom relief and hemodynamic changes in patients with concomitant DVR remains unclear.

METHODS: This prospective observational study included patients evaluated between January 2010 and December 2019 who were found to have both DVR and SVR. Patients were categorized into the treatment group, which underwent superficial venous procedures, and the observation group, which received no intervention.

RESULTS: A total of 31 patients were enrolled, including 9 in the observation group and 22 in the treatment group. The median age was 58 years, and 25.8% were male. Baseline characteristics were not significantly different between the groups, although the treatment group tended to have a higher proportion of male patients, higher venous clinical severity score (VCSS), and higher clinical, etiological, anatomical, and pathophysiologic classifications. Among 38 limbs, 47.4% had deep axial reflux. At a median follow-up of 6.4 years, the treatment group showed significant improvement, with median VCSS and Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire improvements of 2.0 and 5.4, respectively, whereas both scores worsened in the observation group. Complete DVR resolution occurred in 9.1% of limbs in the observation group and 29.6% of limbs in the treatment group. Popliteal vein reflux duration significantly decreased from 5.1 to 3.0 seconds after treatment.

CONCLUSION: In patients with concomitant DVR and SVR, superficial venous procedures were associated with long-term symptomatic improvement and favorable hemodynamic changes in DVR. DVR should not be considered a barrier to superficial venous intervention.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: Concurrent deep venous reflux (DVR) is frequently observed in patients with superficial venous reflux (SVR). However, the effect of SVR treatment on symptom relief and hemodynamic changes in patients with concomitant DVR remains unclear. METHODS: This prospective observational study included patients evaluated between January 2010 and December 2019 who were found to have both DVR and SVR.

title: Long-term outcomes of laparoscopic aortobifemoral bypass: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Laparoscopic aortobifemoral bypass (LABF) is a minimally invasive option for extensive aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD), but data on its long-term durability are limited. We aimed to evaluate the 10-year outcomes of LABF for patients with TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) II C and D lesions.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively maintained database of 20 patients who underwent LABF for TASC II C or D AIOD at a single tertiary center between January 2004 and December 2012. Primary endpoints were primary and secondary patency rates, survival, and postoperative complications.

RESULTS: The median patient age was 65 years, and 18 (90.0%) were male. TASC II D lesions were present in 18 patients (90.0%). There was one perioperative death (5.0%). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed primary patency rates of 94.7%, 88.8%, 82.0%, and 82.0% at 1, 3, 5, and 10 years, respectively. The 10-year secondary patency rate was 88.0%. Reintervention was required in 2 patients (10.0%) during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: LABF provides excellent long-term patency rates comparable to open repair for complex AIOD. With careful patient selection, LABF represents a safe, feasible, and durable minimally invasive alternative, particularly for patients unsuitable for endovascular therapy.

We aimed to evaluate the 10-year outcomes of LABF for patients with TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) II C and D lesions. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively maintained database of 20 patients who underwent LABF for TASC II C or D AIOD at a single tertiary center between January 2004 and December 2012.

title: A 10-Year Single-Center Experience in Pediatric Thromboembolism: Management Strategies and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric thromboembolism is uncommon but clinically important, and its epidemiology varies according to age, underlying disease, catheter exposure, and referral patterns. This study evaluated the epidemiology, risk factors, management, and outcomes of pediatric thromboembolism over a 10-year period in a tertiary care center.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed children aged 0-18 years with symptomatic, radiologically confirmed thromboembolism between January 2010 and January 2020. Incidentally detected asymptomatic thromboses and cases without imaging confirmation were excluded. Venous and arterial events were analyzed separately.

RESULTS: Among 51,025 pediatric admissions, 70 patients had thromboembolism, corresponding to an admission-based rate of 13.7 per 10,000 admissions. Venous thromboembolism accounted for 51 cases (72.9%) and arterial thromboembolism for 19 cases (27.1%). Median age at diagnosis was 6 years (range, 1 day-18 years), and 49 patients (70.0%) were male. The central nervous system was the most frequent anatomical region involved. Central venous catheterization was the leading modifiable acquired risk factor. Active antithrombotic or interventional treatment was used in 68 patients (97.1%); low molecular weight heparin containing regimens were used in 46 patients (65.7%). Complete recovery was documented in 55 patients (78.6%), recurrence in 12 (17.1%), and mortality in 3 (4.3%). Recurrence was more frequent after venous than arterial events (23.5% vs 0%; p = .028).

CONCLUSION: In this 10-year cohort, venous events predominated and catheter related thrombosis remained a major preventable contributor. Recurrence was confined to venous events, supporting careful long term follow up and individualized secondary prevention for high risk children. Standardized catheter care practices and selective, appropriately timed thrombophilia testing are practical priorities.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Pediatric thromboembolism is uncommon but clinically important, and its epidemiology varies according to age, underlying disease, catheter exposure, and referral patterns. This study evaluated the epidemiology, risk factors, management, and outcomes of pediatric thromboembolism over a 10-year period in a tertiary care center. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed children aged 0-18 years with symptomatic, radiologically confirmed thromboembolism between January 2010 and January 2020.

title: Situs Inversus Totalis with Mirror-Image Dextrocardia and Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Treated by Ascending Aorta Replacement Plus Total Arch Replacement and Frozen Elephant Trunk Using an Inverted Four-Branched Graft: A Case Report.
abstract: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital condition characterized by a complete mirror-image reversal of the thoracic and abdominal viscera, usually accompanied by dextrocardia. Acute type A aortic dissection (AAD) is a highly lethal cardiovascular emergency, and its coexistence with SIT is exceedingly rare. To the best of our knowledge, apart from a recently reported pregnant patient, no case of AAD in a non-pregnant adult with SIT has been treated with ascending aorta replacement combined with total arch replacement (TAR) and frozen elephant trunk (FET) implantation. In this report, we present such a case and share our surgical experience, particularly the inverted four-branched graft technique used to resolve the mismatch between the commercially available graft and the mirrored anatomy. The postoperative course was complicated by right renal malperfusion and stage 2 acute kidney injury. Overall renal function recovered with conservative management, although the right kidney subsequently became atrophic; otherwise, recovery was satisfactory. Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) at 10 months showed the graft and all reconstructed branches patent and the FET in position without endoleak, and the patient remained in good condition at the telephone follow-up approximately 3 years after surgery.

Acute type A aortic dissection (AAD) is a highly lethal cardiovascular emergency, and its coexistence with SIT is exceedingly rare. To the best of our knowledge, apart from a recently reported pregnant patient, no case of AAD in a non-pregnant adult with SIT has been treated with ascending aorta replacement combined with total arch replacement (TAR) and frozen elephant trunk (FET) implantation.

title: Frailty as a Modifier of Revascularization-Associated Outcomes in Diabetic Foot Ulcer: A Nationwide Inpatient Study.
abstract: We examined whether frailty modifies the association between revascularization and major amputation among hospitalizations for diabetic foot ulcer. We identified adult hospitalizations in the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 through 2022 and classified frailty using the 109-code Hospital Frailty Risk Score. Survey-weighted logistic regression assessed major amputation and in-hospital mortality across four frailty strata, adjusting for demographic and clinical characteristics. Among 2 588 159 diabetic foot ulcer hospitalizations, frailty burden exceeded that of diabetes hospitalizations without foot ulcers. The association between revascularization and major amputation weakened with increasing frailty: adjusted odds ratios were 0.30 (95% confidence interval, 0.26-0.35) for low frailty, 0.68 for intermediate frailty and 0.82 for intermediate-high frailty. No statistically significant association was observed for high frailty (adjusted odds ratio, 1.05; 95% confidence interval, 0.86-1.29; interaction p < 0.001). Revascularization was associated with lower in-hospital mortality across frailty strata without significant interaction (p = 0.413). Frailty modified the observed association with major amputation, whereas mortality associations showed limited heterogeneity. Treatment selection and unmeasured clinical differences preclude causal interpretation.

title: Inferior Vena Cava Cement Migration with Pulmonary Cement Embolism: A Case Report.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Vertebral augmentation procedures, including vertebroplasty and kyphoplasty, can result in cement extravasation, which is often clinically silent. Less commonly, cement may migrate intravascularly into the inferior vena cava (IVC) and pulmonary arterial circulation, resulting in pulmonary cement embolism, a potentially life-threatening complication. Early recognition in the emergency department (ED) is essential to guide appropriate imaging, specialty consultation, and timely management.

CASE REPORT: A 76-year-old woman with recent third lumbar vertebral augmentation presented to the ED with acute worsening low back pain and burning bilateral radicular symptoms approximately one week after the procedure. Computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast demonstrated linear hyperdense material extending from the treated vertebral body into the IVC, concerning for intravascular cement migration. Additional CT of the chest demonstrated multiple bilateral subsegmental pulmonary cement emboli. Interventional radiology was consulted emergently, and the patient was transferred for endovascular retrieval of the IVC cement fragment, which was successfully removed. The pulmonary cement emboli were small, peripheral, and asymptomatic and were managed conservatively. The patient remained hemodynamically stable and was discharged after monitored hospitalization.

CONCLUSION: Inferior vena cava cement migration with pulmonary cement embolism is a potentially life-threatening complication of vertebral augmentation. Emergency physicians should maintain suspicion for this diagnosis in patients with acute pain or new cardiopulmonary symptoms following recent spinal procedures. Early imaging, multidisciplinary consultation, monitored admission, and endovascular retrieval when indicated may reduce morbidity.

Less commonly, cement may migrate intravascularly into the inferior vena cava (IVC) and pulmonary arterial circulation, resulting in pulmonary cement embolism, a potentially life-threatening complication. Early recognition in the emergency department (ED) is essential to guide appropriate imaging, specialty consultation, and timely management.

title: Atypical Presentation of Extensive Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection Initially Misattributed to Aspiration Pneumonia: A Case Report.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute aortic dissection is a life-threatening emergency that may present with nonspecific symptoms, particularly in older adults, leading clinicians to anchor on more common diagnoses.

CASE REPORT: An 85-year-old man presented with four days of cough, weakness, and constipation after a recent emergency department (ED) visit due to food impaction after he choked on a carrot. A chest radiograph obtained the day before admission showed left basal consolidation, prompting referral for suspected aspiration pneumonia. In the ED, he appeared comfortable with no complaints of chest pain. Physical examination noted mild tachycardia and wheezes bilaterally and treatment was initiated with antibiotics and bronchodilators. A low-voltage electrocardiogram led to immediate point-of-care echocardiography, which demonstrated a large circumferential pericardial effusion, a markedly dilated aortic root, and right ventricular collapse. Computed tomography angiography confirmed an extensive Stanford Type A aortic dissection.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights how deceptively calm presentations can mask catastrophic disease and why clinicians must be ready to abandon their first diagnosis when the data demands it.

title: Trends and Disparities in Peripheral Artery Disease and Dementia-Related Mortality in the United States, 1999-2024.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular risk factors are common among individuals with both peripheral artery disease (PAD) and dementia, and these co-existing conditions are a major public health problem. Our goal is to assess nationwide mortality trends and disparities associated with concomitant PAD and dementia in the United States between 1999 and 2024.

METHODS: This is a population-based analysis using the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database to assess adults aged 65 years and older. Death certificates that mentioned both PAD and dementia were included. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) and annual percent changes (APCs) were calculated to study the national trends by demographic and geographic subgroups.

RESULTS: There were 317,390 deaths among patients who had both PAD and dementia. The overall AAMR was fairly stable over the study period, rising marginally from 23.97 in 1999 to 24.22 in 2024. AAMRs were higher in non-Hispanic African Americans across racial and ethnic groups and peaked in non-metropolitan regions. The sensitivity analyses showed that mortality rates that were driven by PAD significantly declined (AAPC: -4.77) and rates driven by dementia (AAPC: 3.77) increased significantly over the 25-year period.

CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the age-standardized mortality for concomitant PAD and dementia was largely stable, but there are still important geographical and demographic differences. The mortality curves when divided by underlying cause of death show that deaths due to PAD have decreased, while deaths due to dementia have risen in the United States among older adults over the study period.

Our goal is to assess nationwide mortality trends and disparities associated with concomitant PAD and dementia in the United States between 1999 and 2024. METHODS: This is a population-based analysis using the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database to assess adults aged 65 years and older.

title: Wound blush as a predictor for limb salvage among people with non-healing diabetic foot ulcers.
abstract: Background and objectives Wound blush represents angiographic visualisation of tissue-level perfusion around a diabetic foot ulcer. While wound blush after endovascular revascularisation (EVR) predicts improved outcomes, its' prognostic value on diagnostic digital subtraction angiography (DSA) has not been studied, particularly in India. This study compared the role of wound blush after DSA and after EVR in predicting wound healing and limb salvage in non-healing diabetic foot ulcers. Methods A total of 428 individuals with diabetic foot ulcers underwent diagnostic DSA. Wound blush was assessed on DSA and, where applicable, after EVR. Participants were followed for wound healing and amputation outcomes. The wound blush positive and wound blush negative groups on DSA, among participants managed without EVR, and according to wound blush status following EVR were compared. Results On diagnostic DSA, 137(31.6%) participants were wound blush positive and 291(68.4%) were wound blush negative. Wound blush positive participants demonstrated higher rates of complete wound healing (90.5% vs. 79%; P=0.002), and lower amputation rates (7.6 vs. 22.2%; P<0.001) compared to wound blush negative participants. Among participants managed without EVR, limb salvage was significantly higher in wound blush positive than wound blush negative participants (92.4% vs.77.8%; P=0.002). Following EVR, limb salvage was achieved in 89% of participants who demonstrated wound blush compared to 77% (P=0.062) of those who remained wound blush negative. Baseline wound blush positivity predicted favourable outcomes irrespective of EVR. Interpretation and conclusions Wound blush on diagnostic angiography and after EVR is a strong predictor of wound healing and limb salvage in non-healing diabetic foot ulcers. Wound blush on initial DSA helps identifying participants in whom revascularisation may be deferred, reducing endovascular interventions without adverse limb outcomes.

This study compared the role of wound blush after DSA and after EVR in predicting wound healing and limb salvage in non-healing diabetic foot ulcers.

title: Snare-Assisted Traction Technique for Renal Artery Reconstruction in Endovascular Repair of Complex Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: Renal artery (RA) reconstruction during complex endovascular aortic repair often fails in hostile anatomy because of inadequate guidewire support. We describe snare-assisted traction (SAT), a novel endovascular bailout technique using conventional off-the-shelf devices. By combining distal snare traction with a long femoral sheath, SAT shifts target vessel reconstruction from simple wire guidance to sheath-based structural support. This provides robust stability for wire exchange and stent delivery without requiring specialized, unavailable tools or high-morbidity open conversion. Among 12 patients with severe RA angulation, ostial stenosis, or sac origin, SAT achieved 100% technical success without procedural complications. At median 6-month follow-up, all reconstructed RAs remained patent with stable renal function. SAT offers a safe, reproducible, and universally accessible solution for hostile target vessel access, significantly enhancing the feasibility and clinical safety of complex endovascular repair.

title: Venous thromboembolism after joint arthroplasty: where do we stand with aspirin?
abstract: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty remains heterogeneous, particularly regarding the role of aspirin within modern fast-track pathways. Although aspirin is widely used in North American arthroplasty practice, European guidelines remain more conservative and often provide limited or non-operational recommendations for its use after total hip and knee arthroplasty. Contemporary evidence supports aspirin as a viable prophylactic option in selected patients, with potential advantages related to its safety profile, cost, ease of administration and reduced treatment burden. The clinical role of aspirin should be interpreted within a risk-stratified framework that accounts for thromboembolic risk, bleeding risk, surgical complexity, early mobilization and duration of prophylaxis. Available evidence, including recent randomized data, supports aspirin-based prophylaxis in appropriately selected patients, both as part of sequential strategies and, increasingly, as monotherapy within contemporary fast-track pathways. This scoping review synthesizes current guideline-level evidence and contemporary clinical data to clarify practical considerations for agent selection, dosing, duration and aspirin-based prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty.

title: Reducing Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in ICUs: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators and Intervention Measures.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite established guidelines, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) remains a severe ICU complication due to cognitive and resource barriers hindering healthcare worker compliance. A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention.

AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement.

STUDY DESIGN: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was performed using PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wan fang, and CBM databases, up to August 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods research on the barriers and facilitators to CLABSI prevention implementation among ICU healthcare workers. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data synthesis and intervention development were guided by the CFIR, with targeted strategies mapped using the CFIR-ERIC (Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change) matching tool.

RESULTS: The literature search identified 1,780 records, of which 28 studies were ultimately included. The review identified 28 barriers and facilitators, which were synthesized into four major themes and mapped to 16 CFIR constructs across the catheter-care continuum. The most prominent barriers involved staff knowledge gaps, inconsistent adherence to recommended practices, limited resources, and insufficient leadership support. CFIR-ERIC mapping identified 11 Level 1 expert-endorsed implementation strategies, of which four were represented in the included literature and seven were identified as potential implementation gaps.

CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI prevention in ICUs is influenced by multilevel implementation determinants spanning individual, organizational, and practice-related factors. A structured implementation-science approach may help healthcare organizations identify context-specific barriers and prioritize targeted strategies to support more consistent implementation of evidence-based CLABSI prevention practices.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Improving CLABSI prevention may require multilevel strategies that combine targeted education and training, adequate resource allocation, leadership engagement, standardized clinical procedures, and ongoing audit and feedback. These strategies may help strengthen adherence to evidence-based practices, improve quality of care, and enhance patient safety in ICUs.

title: [From critical evaluation based on the gold standard to precision full-process management: advances in the diagnosis and treatment framework for aortic arch artery pathologies].
abstract: Supra-aortic arch artery diseases, including lesions of the carotid,subclavian,and vertebral arteries,represent major causes of cerebral and upper extremity ischemia. The diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for these conditions are undergoing a profound transformation-from conventional open surgery toward minimally invasive endovascular treatment,and further to individualized precision medicine. Recent advances in imaging assessment have substantially improved lesion characterization and risk stratification. The iterative evolution of endovascular devices has enhanced procedural safety. Meanwhile,several topics have become research hotspots,the evidence-based comparison between transcarotid artery revascularization and transfemoral carotid stenting;the renewed pathophysiological understanding of subclavian steal syndrome and vertebral artery diseases;and the construction of individualized treatment decision-making frameworks. Nevertheless,current clinical practice still faces challenges such as controversies over optimal surgical approaches,insufficient prevention and management of complications,and a lack of robust long-term outcome data. From the perspective of vascular surgery,this article systematically reviews recent advances in endovascular devices,surgical techniques,and treatment concepts,aiming to provide front-line clinicians with up-to-date,practical,and actionable insights into the management of supra-aortic arch artery diseases.

title: [A brief discussion on the progress and development directions of clinical research in vascular surgery].
abstract: Vascular surgery has experienced rapid development over the past three decades. With the application of minimally invasive and interventional techniques in the diagnosis and treatment of vascular diseases, clinical research and technological innovation in vascular surgery have expanded significantly. As populations aging accelerates globally-including in China-and the number of patients with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease within the existing healthcare system becomes increasingly evident. The future of vascular surgery will center on three core principles: minimization, precision, and intelligence. By integrating breakthroughs in basic science, engineering, and artificial intelligence, clinical translation will be accelerated. The discipline will shift from "disease treatment" to "health management", and from a "surgery-centered" single model to a "patient-centered" integrated approach model. Future developments will further incorporate artificial intelligence, big data models, precision medicine, more advanced and comprehensive minimally invasive technologies, enhancing multidisciplinary collaboration and preventive care. These advancements are expected to significantly improve diagnostic accuracy, treatment outcomes, and quality of life for patients with vascular diseases.

title: Mortality Following Recurrent Venous Thromboembolism and Major Bleeding Stratified by Active Cancer Status.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) and major bleeding are serious complications after acute VTE. However, their independent impact on subsequent mortality in the era of direct oral anticoagulants remains unclear, particularly with respect to differences between patients with and without active cancer.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the associations of recurrent VTE and major bleeding with subsequent mortality in the overall cohort and subgroups stratified by active cancer.

METHODS: We analyzed 5,197 patients with VTE from the COMMAND VTE Registry-2 using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models with recurrent VTE and major bleeding as time-updated covariates.

RESULTS: In the overall cohort, 283 patients developed recurrent VTE, 470 developed major bleeding, and 1,323 died. Recurrent VTE and major bleeding were associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 1.65, 95% CI: 1.28-2.12, P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 3.33, 95% CI: 2.83-3.91, P < 0.001, respectively). Among patients with active cancer, both recurrent VTE and major bleeding were associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 1.95, 95% CI: 1.45-2.62, P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 2.96, 95% CI: 2.42-3.61, P < 0.001, respectively). Among patients without active cancer, only major bleeding was associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 3.78, 95% CI: 2.88-4.97, P < 0.001), whereas recurrent VTE was not associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.55-1.56, P = 0.78).

CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary real-world patients with VTE in the era of direct oral anticoagulants, major bleeding was associated with increased subsequent mortality in both patients with and without active cancer, whereas recurrent VTE was associated with increased mortality in patients with active cancer, with no significant association observed in those without active cancer.

However, their independent impact on subsequent mortality in the era of direct oral anticoagulants remains unclear, particularly with respect to differences between patients with and without active cancer. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the associations of recurrent VTE and major bleeding with subsequent mortality in the overall cohort and subgroups stratified by active cancer.

title: Association of muscle strength with the incidence of venous thromboembolism and all-cause mortality among patients: a prospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Muscle strength is a well-established indicator of overall health, yet its prospective association with the incidence and prognosis of venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains inconsistent.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 481 945 participants without prior VTE from the UK Biobank for incidence analysis, and 14 908 patients with prevalent VTE at baseline for prognostic analysis. Muscle strength was assessed using grip strength relative to body weight and categorised into sex- and age-specific tertiles. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for incident VTE and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 13.72 years, 15 774 incident VTE events were documented. Each 1-standard deviation increase in muscle strength was associated with a 13% reduction in VTE risk (HR 0.87, 95% CI: 0.85-0.89). Compared with the low muscle strength group, participants in the middle and high tertiles had 12% (HR 0.88, 95% CI: 0.84-0.92) and 19% (HR 0.81, 95% CI: 0.77-0.84) lower risk of VTE. This inverse association remained consistent across all genetic risk strata. Among patients with VTE, 2884 deaths occurred during follow-up. Each 1-standard deviation increase was associated with a 14% lower mortality risk (HR 0.86, 95% CI: 0.82-0.90). High and middle muscle strength were associated with 21% (HR 0.79, 95% CI: 0.72-0.87) and 17% (HR 0.83, 95% CI: 0.76-0.91) lower all-cause mortality versus low strength.

CONCLUSION: Higher muscle strength is associated with a lower risk of incident VTE, regardless of genetic predisposition, and with lower mortality among patients with VTE.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 481 945 participants without prior VTE from the UK Biobank for incidence analysis, and 14 908 patients with prevalent VTE at baseline for prognostic analysis. Muscle strength was assessed using grip strength relative to body weight and categorised into sex- and age-specific tertiles.

title: Quantification of the flexural rigidity of endovascular surgical devices using three-point bending tests.
abstract: Endovascular surgical procedures require the navigation of catheters and wires through the vasculature to reach distal target sites. Quantitative frameworks for device selection have the potential to improve navigation success by optimizing device flexural rigidity for a given patient-specific anatomy. However, data are lacking to facilitate this technology, in part because typical endovascular devices have intricate spatial variations in mechanical properties that are challenging and tedious to quantify repeatably. We therefore developed a three-point bend test methodology using a custom rig and applied it to measure lengthwise flexural rigidity profiles of devices commonly used in neuroendovascular procedures. The methodology demonstrated high repeatability and was able to characterize transition zones in detail. We applied the methodology to generate the first comprehensive, quantitative library of device flexural rigidities, spanning guidewires, intermediate guides, and long sheaths. We observed that these three classes of device have properties that fall into distinct ranges. Additional plots examining relationships between flexural rigidity, device diameter, and length revealed application-specific trends in flexural properties. This methodology and resulting data allow for standardized characterization and comparisons to aid device selection, and have the potential to both enhance surgical planning and inform future endovascular innovation.
