title: Revascularization of Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis: Cognitive Results of the CREST-2 Randomized Trials.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Studies show that asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis is associated with diminished cognition. Whether carotid revascularization leads to cognitive improvement is unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether carotid revascularization improves cognition.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prespecified cognitive secondary outcomes of the CREST-2 randomized clinical trials of patients 35 years or older with 70% or greater asymptomatic carotid stenosis. Enrollment was December 2014 through July 2024, and follow-up ended July 2025. Five cognitive tests were administered before treatment and annually up to 4 years. Cognitive performances from 146 clinical sites were centrally assessed by telephone, blinded to treatment.

INTERVENTIONS: Two trials compared carotid stenting plus intensive medical management (CAS + IMM) with IMM alone and carotid endarterectomy plus IMM (CEA + IMM) with IMM alone.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Five cognitive tests, assessing learning, memory, executive function, attention, and processing speed, administered to all patients, were assessed for unadjusted and adjusted mean z scores using a linear mixed model. The minimal clinically important difference was 0.50 SD between treatment groups. The prespecified primary analysis was the fully adjusted composite z score at 4 years. Secondary analyses assessed the individual tests and at the test intervals.

RESULTS: Among 2366 US study patients, 2165 (91.5%) participated in cognitive assessments, 1078 in the CAS trial (529 CAS + IMM; 549 IMM alone) and 1087 in the CEA trial (543 CEA + IMM; 544 IMM alone); mean age was 70.1 years (SD, 7.7) and 37.8% were female. Following baseline, 4954 test batteries were administered for a mean of 2.24 (SD, 1.09) follow-up years. There were no treatment-related differences in the fully adjusted estimated composite z scores at 4 years for either the CAS trial (CAS + IMM, 0.22 [95% CI, 0.13 to 0.30] vs IMM alone, 0.18 [95% CI, 0.09 to 0.27]; between-group difference, 0.03 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.15]) or the CEA trial (CEA + IMM, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.33] vs IMM, 0.23 [95% CI, 0.15 to 0.32]; between-group difference, 0.02 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.14]). There were no significant differences between revascularization plus medical management vs IMM alone for any individual cognitive test.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In patients with severe asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis, revascularization with either CAS or CEA plus IMM, compared with IMM alone, did not significantly improve cognitive function at up to 4 years of follow-up.

title: Revascularization in Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Hemodynamic Impairment and Cognitive Outcomes: The CREST-H Substudy of the CREST-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients.

OBJECTIVE: To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This substudy was conducted within a multicenter phase 3 randomized clinical trial. Adults (aged 35-86 years) without dementia with eighth-grade education or higher and unilateral asymptomatic ICA stenosis greater than or equal to 70% were enrolled from January 2018 to July 2024 at 61 sites in North America (last follow-up in July 2025). Of 607 participants screened from 2485 in CREST-2, 392 were enrolled. Magnetic resonance or computed tomographic perfusion imaging tested for baseline hemodynamic impairment defined by delayed time-to-peak (TTP) arrival of intravenous contrast in the hemisphere ipsilateral minus contralateral to the stenotic artery.

INTERVENTION: Carotid revascularization (endarterectomy or stenting) plus intensive medical management (IMM) vs IMM alone.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the difference in composite cognitive z score over 1 year based on 5 cognitive tests. The primary analysis tested for an interaction between treatment group (revascularization vs IMM alone) and degree of baseline hemodynamic impairment among those with reduced baseline cognition (cognitive z score ≤-1.0 SD).

RESULTS: Of 392 participants enrolled (mean age, 71 years; 125 [32%] females), 61 were excluded for missing baseline imaging and 40 for missing cognitive examinations or other covariates, leaving 291 with complete data. Fifty-one had reduced cognition at baseline (25 in the revascularization group and 26 in the IMM alone group). TTP ranged from no interhemispheric TTP delay to a more-than-2-second delay. Mean (SD) cognitive z scores were -1.36 (0.51) at baseline and -1.17 (0.47) at 1 year in the revascularization group and -1.34 (0.83) at baseline and -1.01 (0.97) at 1 year in the IMM alone group. The primary analysis showed no difference in cognition by treatment group over 1 year, adjusting for treatment group × hemodynamic status interaction and other covariates (adjusted difference in cognitive z score, -0.15 SD [95% CI, -0.54 to 0.24]). The interaction was not significant (β estimate = 0.018 [95% CI, -0.025 to 0.061]; P = .40).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this substudy of a randomized clinical trial, there was no differential effect of revascularization vs IMM alone on cognition over 1 year by cerebral hemodynamic status among those with baseline reduced cognition, suggesting that revascularization does not improve cognitive dysfunction by restoring flow to the brain in chronic asymptomatic carotid stenosis.

title: Management strategies for right-to-left intraatrial shunt with thrombus in transit: a systematic review of 297 patients and associated mortality outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombus in transit (TIT) through a patent foramen ovale (PFO) or atrial septal defect (ASD) is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition associated with paradoxical embolism. Despite advances in imaging and interventional techniques, optimal management strategies remain poorly defined.

OBJECTIVES: To systematically characterize the clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, management strategies, and outcomes of adult patients with TIT across right-to-left intra-atrial shunts.

DESIGN: Systematic review of published cases.

DATA SOURCES AND METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception through March 2025 for case reports, case series, and letters describing adult patients with TIT visualized by transthoracic or transesophageal echocardiography. After screening 1736 records, 278 studies reporting 297 patients were included. Two independent reviewers extracted demographic, clinical, imaging, treatment, and outcome data. Descriptive statistics were summarized, and treatment groups were compared using chi-square and Mann-Whitney U tests. Kaplan-Meier survival curves with log-rank testing assessed 120-day survival, and multivariable Cox regression was used to evaluate potential predictors of mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 297 patients from 278 studies were included. The mean age was 58.5 ± 15.8 years, and 50.2% were male. Respiratory symptoms predominated (77.7%), followed by cardiac (29.7%) and neurological (23.0%) manifestations. Provoked events accounted for 70.3% of cases, most commonly in the postoperative setting. Thrombi were detected by transthoracic echocardiography in 92.1% of cases and by transesophageal echocardiography in 100%. Management strategies included surgical embolectomy (57.8%), anticoagulation (36.5%), thrombolysis (13.5%), and percutaneous aspiration (2.7%); 61.1% underwent PFO/ASD closure. Overall mortality was 8.3%. Surgical management was associated with the lowest mortality (3.0%) and the highest short-term clinical improvement (90.5%; p < 0.001). Thrombolysis and percutaneous aspiration were associated with higher mortality (16.6% and 25.0%, respectively). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated superior 120-day survival with surgical management compared with other treatment strategies (log-rank p < 0.001). In multivariable Cox models, no independent predictors of mortality were identified.

CONCLUSION: In this largest synthesis of TIT cases to date, surgical management and PFO/ASD closure were associated with favorable short-term outcomes. Surgical intervention demonstrated the lowest observed mortality, while anticoagulation provided acceptable outcomes in selected patients. Thrombolysis and percutaneous aspiration were associated with higher mortality. These findings support the role of definitive management and shunt closure in selected patients, although prospective studies are needed to establish standardized treatment strategies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered in the International Platform of Registered Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols (INPLASY) (Registration number: INPLASY202630021).

Despite advances in imaging and interventional techniques, optimal management strategies remain poorly defined. OBJECTIVES: To systematically characterize the clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, management strategies, and outcomes of adult patients with TIT across right-to-left intra-atrial shunts.

title: Spontaneous passage of an ingested full-size AAA battery through the pediatric gastrointestinal tract: a case report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cylindrical battery ingestion is far less common than button battery ingestion in children. While cylindrical batteries can cause gastrointestinal injury through pressure necrosis, corrosive leakage, or prolonged mucosal contact, most batteries that pass beyond the esophagus are managed conservatively. However, pediatric data on natural history and outcomes remain limited.

CASE PRESENTATION: A six-year-old boy presented 6 hours after accidentally swallowing a full-size AAA cylindrical battery. He remained asymptomatic throughout. Initial radiography located the battery in the stomach; subsequent imaging confirmed gradual migration through the jejunum and distal small bowel. Serial abdominal radiographs and repeated clinical assessments demonstrated continuous transit without obstruction or perforation, with subsequent spontaneous passage of the intact cylindrical battery in the stool.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates that a full-sized AAA cylindrical battery can traverse the pediatric gastrointestinal tract uneventfully after passing through the esophagus. The favorable outcome supports the existing literature advocating expectant management in carefully selected asymptomatic patients with documented radiographic progression. Nevertheless, close clinical observation and serial imaging remain essential to identify patients requiring intervention due to impaction, lack of progression, symptom development, or evidence of battery-related injury.

CONCLUSION: An intact, cylindrical AAA battery can pass spontaneously through the entire pediatric gastrointestinal tract without endoscopic or surgical intervention. Conservative management with vigilant clinical and radiological monitoring appears to be safe and effective in asymptomatic children demonstrating progressive battery transit.

While cylindrical batteries can cause gastrointestinal injury through pressure necrosis, corrosive leakage, or prolonged mucosal contact, most batteries that pass beyond the esophagus are managed conservatively. title: [Overlooked thrombophilia in a younger woman with recurrent deep vein thrombosis].
abstract: Antithrombin is the most important endogenous anticoagulant, and hereditary antithrombin deficiency increases the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). In this case, we present a young woman with recurrent VTE and factor V Leiden heterozygosity but normal antithrombin activity. SERPINC1 sequencing revealed heterozygosity for SERPINC1:p.Val30Glu (AT Dublin), which is associated with transient antithrombin deficiency and mildly increased risk of VTE. Transient antithrombin deficiency can, in some cases, affect VTE management but may be missed unless SERPINC1 is sequenced.

title: Surgery Versus Ultrasound-Guided Foam Sclerotherapy for the Treatment of Isolated Anterior Saphenous Vein Incompetence: A Single-Center Randomized Trial.
abstract: Background: Isolated anterior saphenous vein (ASV) incompetence is a clinically relevant source of symptomatic anterior thigh varicose veins, which may cause pain, heaviness, swelling and serious complication such as superficial vein thrombosis. Therefore, targeted management is often required, yet evidence guiding treatment remains limited. This single-center, randomized trial compared high ligation surgery in combination with phlebectomy and ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy (UGFS). Methods: Thirty-nine limbs of 35 patients (19 allocated to surgery, 20 to UGFS) were treated and followed up at 1 and 3 years. The primary outcome was ASV-territory recurrence defined as reflux time > 0.5 s along the ASV in the UGFS group or new anterior thigh varicosities connected to the previous saphenofemoral junction in the surgical group at 3 years. Secondary outcomes were the same duplex endpoint at 1 year, recurrence of clinically visible varicose veins, and groin neovascularization at 1 and 3 years. Results: ASV-territory recurrence was numerically higher after UGFS (63% vs. 33%) at 3 years, although the difference was not statistically significant, whereas recurrence was higher after UGFS than surgery at 1 year (65% vs. 11%; p < 0.001). Clinical recurrence rates did not differ significantly between groups at 1 and 3 years. Neovascularization was observed exclusively in the surgery group at 1 year and remained more frequent at 3 years (44% vs. 5%). Conclusions: Our findings suggest better short-term disease control with surgery than with UGFS for isolated ASV incompetence, whereas the prespecified primary endpoint of ASV-territory recurrence at 3-years did not differ significantly between groups. Both surgery and UGFS may therefore be considered for selected patients, with treatment choice guided by patient-centered factors, including vein anatomy, invasiveness, and patient preference.

Therefore, targeted management is often required, yet evidence guiding treatment remains limited. This single-center, randomized trial compared high ligation surgery in combination with phlebectomy and ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy (UGFS).

title: Cause-specific mortality after endovascular treatment for anterior vs. posterior circulation large vessel occlusion: a multicenter cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO) carries substantial mortality despite endovascular treatment (EVT). Whether causes of death differ between anterior (AVO) and posterior (PVO) circulation occlusions is poorly characterized. We compared cause-specific 90-day mortality between patients with AVO and PVO treated with EVT.

METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort, consecutive patients with AIS-LVO who underwent EVT at 111 hospitals in China (ANGEL-ACT registry [Endovascular Treatment Key Technique and Emergency Workflow Improvement of acute ischemic stroke]) were included, and adjudicated causes of death were grouped into prespecified categories. Cause-specific mortality was assessed in the complete analytic cohort using the Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model, with survivors censored at 90 days and deaths from other causes treated as competing events. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated with the Aalen-Johansen estimator.

RESULTS: Among 1,671 eligible patients (1,300 AVO, 371 PVO), 228 deaths (13.6%) occurred within 90 days. All-cause mortality was higher in PVO than AVO (19.4% vs. 12.0%). Cerebral edema-related death was significantly more frequent in PVO than AVO (90-day cumulative incidence 9.16% vs. 4.15%; adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.73, p = 0.001; Gray's test p < 0.001). Fatal hemorrhagic transformation was numerically more frequent in AVO but did not reach statistical significance in the complete cohort (3.77% vs. 1.89%; adjusted sHR 1.76, 95% CI 0.78-3.98, p = 0.17; Gray's test p = 0.076), consistent across all sensitivity analyses. Pneumonia-related (adjusted sHR 0.34, 95% CI 0.17-0.68, p = 0.003) and recurrent stroke-related (adjusted sHR 0.29, 95% CI 0.10-0.86, p = 0.026) deaths were also more frequent in PVO; the pneumonia association remained significant after Bonferroni correction, whereas the recurrent stroke association did not.

CONCLUSION: Fatal complications after EVT differ by occlusion territory. Posterior circulation occlusion is independently associated with a higher risk of death from cerebral edema, pneumonia, and recurrent stroke, although the recurrent stroke association did not survive Bonferroni correction. Hemorrhagic transformation accounted for a larger share of anterior circulation deaths, but this did not correspond to a statistically significant increase in risk in the complete cohort.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO) carries substantial mortality despite endovascular treatment (EVT). Whether causes of death differ between anterior (AVO) and posterior (PVO) circulation occlusions is poorly characterized. We compared cause-specific 90-day mortality between patients with AVO and PVO treated with EVT.

title: Arterial Blood Gas and Arterial Lines.
abstract: Arterial blood gas sampling and arterial line placement are essential bedside procedures in the care of critically ill patients. This article reviews the indications, contraindications, and preprocedural assessment for arterial access, including surface anatomy, ultrasound guidance, and site selection considerations. In particular, the article highlights differences between peripheral and central cannulation. Step-by-step procedural techniques are described for both sampling and arterial catheter insertion at radial, brachial, axillary, and femoral sites. The article also addresses equipment setup, specimen handling, postprocedure monitoring, troubleshooting, and documentation and billing considerations.

title: [Acute management of minor ischemic stroke].
abstract: This review summarizes acute-phase treatment for minor ischemic stroke, focusing on the latest evidence for reperfusion therapy and acute antithrombotic treatment. In patients with large vessel occlusion, the benefit of mechanical thrombectomy is not established and the risk of hemorrhage exists; therefore, indications should be judged carefully for each patient. Intravenous thrombolysis provides limited benefit in non-disabling cases, and dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) can be an option. For minor non-cardioembolic stroke, early DAPT is recommended, and the possible role of adding argatroban is promising, especially for suspected branch atheromatous disease. For cardioembolic stroke, early initiation of a direct oral anticoagulant is desirable in mild cases without a large infarct.

title: Patient-specific finite element modeling of image-derived shell morphoelastic growth: A general framework and application to stented aortic dissection.
abstract: Vascular pathology often manifests in complex shape evolution visualized by longitudinal computed tomography (CT) imaging. Growth and remodeling (G&R) frameworks have been integrated into finite element (FE) modeling to probe the mechanics underlying this progression, extending into patient-specific approaches. Their scalability and translatability, however, are limited by the computational burden associated with heterogeneous, anisotropic growth fields and through-thickness meshing. While existing shell growth formulations can mitigate this burden, they require nontrivial FE implementation especially in commercial softwares (e.g., Abaqus) and their efficacy in patient-specific geometries under complex loading is unclear. In this work, we present a general computational framework to implement shell morphoelastic growth computed directly from registered patient-specific CT images. This shell implementation is validated against solid 3D formulations, allows thickness tunability, and increases compatibility with CT surfaces. We demonstrate the robustness of this formulation through modeling post-operative growth in a patient-specific aortic dissection under stent-based loading. Results first show that complex stent-based loading can deform the shell dissection flap to reproduce post-operative geometry. The outer aortic wall is then given a growth field calculated from registration of 1-month and 5-year post-operative CT images, which is implemented along with stent-based loading and pressurization. Results from this model capture the trends in total and lumen morphological evolution observed at intermediate timepoints. These findings establish a general framework, validated with a patient-specific case study of aortic dissection, with the potential to expand to other complex systems, scale to larger patient populations, and apply G&R to clinical translation.

Their scalability and translatability, however, are limited by the computational burden associated with heterogeneous, anisotropic growth fields and through-thickness meshing.

title: Central Venous Access.
abstract: Central venous catheterization (CVC) is a commonly performed procedure in which an indwelling catheter is placed within a central vein to facilitate administration of vasoactive medications, chemotherapy, parenteral nutrition, and extracorporeal therapies, as well as hemodynamic monitoring. This article reviews the indications and contraindications for CVC placement, bleeding risk considerations, and factors influencing site selection. Methods for confirming catheter position, including sonographic and radiographic approaches, are discussed. Mechanical, thrombotic, and infectious complications are reviewed, along with strategies for prevention and postprocedural monitoring. Common technical and sonographic pitfalls encountered during CVC placement are also highlighted.

title: Peripheral Venous Access.
abstract: Peripheral venous access is the most common invasive procedure performed in hospitalized patients. In this review, the authors explore ultrasound-guided peripheral venous access, including peripheral intravenous catheters, midline catheters, and peripherally inserted central catheters. Indications, contraindications, and anticipated duration of therapy for each device are summarized based on current literature. Strategies to optimize cannulation success, including vessel assessment, catheter-to-vein ratio, and appropriate device selection, are reviewed. Complications such as early device failure, thrombosis, infection, and vessel injury are also discussed.

title: Computed Tomography-Derived Machine Learning for Risk Assessment in Aortic Dissection: A Narrative Review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for improving diagnosis and prognostic assessment across a wide spectrum of cardiovascular diseases.

METHODS: A literature search was conducted in PubMed and Embase to identify relevant studies focusing on ML approaches to computed tomography (CT)-based risk stratification in aortic dissection.

CONCLUSIONS: ML-based analysis of CT imaging offers significant potential to enhance prognostic assessment and risk stratification in aortic dissection. By integrating imaging, clinical, and biomarker data, these approaches may enable earlier identification of high-risk patients and support more personalized management strategies.

title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10616-026-01073-w.

title: Surgical management of splenic artery aneurysms: a case series of three patients with diverse presentations.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Splenic artery aneurysm (SAA) is the most common visceral artery aneurysm and includes true aneurysms and pseudoaneurysms, which have different etiologies and clinical behavior. Presentation ranges from incidental detection to life-threatening rupture with hemoperitoneum. Management depends on aneurysm size, symptoms, morphology, anatomical relationships, comorbidities, and rupture status.

METHODS: We retrospectively described three consecutive patients with SAA or pseudoaneurysm treated surgically at a tertiary surgical center, Loghman Hakim Hospital, Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran, between 2020 and 2025. Clinical records, imaging, operative findings, histopathology, postoperative course, and available follow-up were reviewed. The series was reported in accordance with the PROCESS 2025 reporting guideline.

CASE PRESENTATIONS: Case 1 was a 66-year-old man with chronic liver disease and thrombocytopenia in whom a giant true SAA measuring approximately 72 × 68 × 76 mm was incidentally identified during trauma imaging. The aneurysm was adjacent to the pancreatic body without rupture. Elective open splenectomy with aneurysm resection and concurrent liver wedge biopsy was performed. Case 2 was a 63-year-old woman with a 7-month history of postprandial epigastric pain and a symptomatic true SAA of undocumented size. Elective open resection with splenectomy was performed; histopathology unexpectedly demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous splenitis. Case 3 was a 38-year-old woman with sickle cell disease who developed acute abdominal pain after a generalized seizure, with severe anemia and hemoperitoneum. A ruptured splenic artery pseudoaneurysm was identified at emergency laparotomy after a ruptured ectopic pregnancy had initially been suspected.

RESULTS: All three patients underwent open splenectomy with aneurysm excision, which was elective in cases 1 and 2 and emergent in case 3. There were no intraoperative deaths or reoperations. All three patients had uneventful postoperative recoveries. 6-month follow-up was available for case 1; longer-term uniform follow-up was not available for all patients.

CONCLUSION: SAAs encompass a broad clinical spectrum, from incidentally discovered giant aneurysms to symptomatic lesions and catastrophic rupture. These cases illustrate the importance of anatomy-directed treatment selection, early recognition of rupture, and consideration of vascular causes in patients with unexplained hemoperitoneum. Endovascular therapy is preferred for anatomically suitable elective lesions, whereas open surgery remains an important option for giant, complex, or ruptured aneurysms. The proposed algorithm is an educational synthesis of published evidence, current Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines recommendations, and the clinical experience represented by this institutional series rather than a prospectively validated decision tool.

Presentation ranges from incidental detection to life-threatening rupture with hemoperitoneum. Management depends on aneurysm size, symptoms, morphology, anatomical relationships, comorbidities, and rupture status.

title: Early functional outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy in patients with large vessel occlusion and active cancer.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evaluating mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in patients with large vessel occlusion stroke (LVOS) and active cancer (AC) is challenging because cancer-related mortality substantially affects conventional functional outcomes. This study aimed to assess the association between MT and early functional outcomes while minimizing the confounding impact of cancer-related death.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with LVOS and AC between January 2016 and December 2024. Patients were categorized into MT and non-MT groups. The primary outcome was the distribution of modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores at 2 weeks, analyzed using ordinal logistic regression. A sensitivity analysis excluding patients who died from cancer progression within 2 weeks of stroke onset was also performed. LVOS was defined as ischemic stroke with occlusion of the intra- or extracranial internal carotid artery, middle cerebral artery (M1 or M2 segments), or basilar artery.

RESULTS: Among 72 patients with LVOS and AC (median age, 76 years; 36 women), 32 (44%) underwent MT (28 MT alone, and 4 MT procedures combined with intravenous thrombolysis), whereas 3 patients in the non-MT group received intravenous thrombolysis alone. At 2 weeks, MT was significantly associated with a favorable shift in mRS distribution (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.48, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22-9.97; p = 0.020). In a sensitivity analysis excluding cancer-related deaths, this association remained significant, with a larger effect size (adjusted OR, 6.21, 95% CI, 1.89-20.47; p = 0.003).

CONCLUSION: MT was associated with improved early functional outcomes in patients with LVOS and AC.

This study aimed to assess the association between MT and early functional outcomes while minimizing the confounding impact of cancer-related death. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with LVOS and AC between January 2016 and December 2024.

title: Predictive value of combined cerebral blood volume index and systemic inflammation indices for 90-day functional outcomes following endovascular treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke and proximal large vessel occlusion: machine learning model construction and population attributable fraction analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We investigated whether the cerebral blood volume (CBV) index and pretreatment systemic inflammatory indices (SIIs) provide complementary prognostic information for 90-day functional outcomes after successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion and evaluated the advantages of machine learning models in terms of prognostic outcomes and quantified adverse outcomes using the population attributable fraction (PAF).

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation. SIIs were calculated from the first venous sample obtained at presentation, before intravenous thrombolysis, and before arterial puncture for EVT. Multivariate logistic regression and eight predictive algorithms were evaluated. PAF estimates were considered exploratory.

RESULTS: Among 474 patients, 41.6% and 28.5% achieved favorable and excellent outcomes, respectively. Higher CBV indices were more frequent among patients with favorable outcomes, whereas higher inflammatory indices were associated with worse outcomes. Logistic regression showed the highest AUC for mRS 0-2 (0.868, 95% CI 0.806-0.929), while SVM had the highest AUC for mRS 0-1 (0.839, 95% CI 0.764-0.915). The external validation AUCs were 0.816 and 0.802. PAF analysis indicated that improving the CBV index increased favorable and excellent outcomes by 97.2% and 74.8%, respectively, whereas reducing inflammatory overactivation improved them by 22.4%-39.7% and 51.2%-59.5%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Baseline CBV index and pretreatment SII values provided complementary prognostic information after successful EVT. However, prospective validation in a broader population is required before clinical implementation.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation.

title: Self-Expanding Stent-Assisted Reconstruction of Distal Supra-Aortic Vessels in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A Comparative Analysis.
abstract: Background: Supra-aortic vessel reconstruction during total aortic arch replacement in acute Stanford type A aortic dissection patients with dissected distal supra-aortic vessels remains technically challenging; proximal supra-aortic vessel replacement alone carries a high risk of neurological complications secondary to intimal inversion. This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes of self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction compared with proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone. Methods and Results: We performed a single-center retrospective comparative analysis of 49 consecutive patients undergoing emergency total aortic arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection from January 2022 to December 2023. Patients were divided into two groups according to intraoperative anatomy and surgeon decision: self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction (SAVR, n = 26) and proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone (PRVA, n = 23). Neurological outcomes related to supra-aortic vessel intimal inversion, operative parameters, blood product transfusion, and short-term complications were analyzed. The mean follow-up was 18.2 ± 4.1 months (range, 12-24 months). The SAVR group exhibited significantly lower supra-aortic vessel stenosis rate (3.8% vs. 30.4%, p < 0.001) and zero cases of intimal inversion-related luminal collapse versus five cases in the PRVA group (0 vs. 5, p = 0.02). Numerically fewer cases of symptomatic stroke (0% vs. 8.7%, p = 0.09) and radiographic cerebral infarction (3.8% vs. 13.0%, p = 0.17) were observed in the SAVR group, though the differences did not achieve statistical significance. Red blood cell and fresh frozen plasma transfusion requirements, mechanical ventilation duration, and ICU stay length were significantly lower in the SAVR cohort. Cardiopulmonary bypass time and 30-day mortality were comparable between groups. Conclusions: Self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction represents a promising technical option during total arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection with distal supra-aortic dissection, associated with superior branch vessel patency and favorable numerical trends in neurological and recovery-related endpoints, with a comparable early-term safety profile. Potential benefits require further validation in larger cohorts.
englishSummary: Background: Supra-aortic vessel reconstruction during total aortic arch replacement in acute Stanford type A aortic dissection patients with dissected distal supra-aortic vessels remains technically challenging; proximal supra-aortic vessel replacement alone carries a high risk of neurological complications secondary to intimal inversion. This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes of self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction compared with proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone. Methods and Results: We performed a single-center retrospective comparative analysis of 49 consecutive patients undergoing emergency total aortic arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection from January 2022 to December 2023.

title: Development and Psychometric Validation of a Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Questionnaire on Pulmonary Embolism and Its Modifiable Risk Factors (PE-KAP-RO): Protocol for a Cross-Sectional Study in Adults from Western Romania.
abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), whose most severe manifestation is pulmonary embolism (PE), is the third most common acute cardiovascular disorder, and many of its risk factors≠-obesity, physical inactivity, smoking, and unfavorable dietary patterns-are modifiable. No validated instrument is currently available to assess knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding PE among adults in Romania, and the burden of self-reported thromboembolic risk factors in community settings has not been described with standardized measures. This protocol describes the development and psychometric validation of the PE-KAP-RO questionnaire, an integrated assessment tool comprising three scored KAP scales, three embedded validated lifestyle instruments, and an exploratory, unweighted VTE risk-factor burden index. No participants had been enrolled and no data had been collected at the time of submission; all procedures are therefore described as planned.

METHODS: The study comprises two phases. Phase 1 (development) includes qualitative concept elicitation with members of the target population, guideline- and theory-anchored item generation, expert content validation quantified by the content validity index, and pilot testing with cognitive debriefing (n ≈ 30). Phase 2 is a cross-sectional field validation in at least 450 adults (≥18 years) from Western Romania-with recruitment continuing toward 600 where feasible-through combined in-person (quota-guided) and online sampling that includes healthcare professionals, with test-retest re-administration in a subsample of at least 60 participants after 14 ± 4 days. Physical activity, diet, and nicotine dependence will be measured with the IPAQ-SF, MEDAS, and FTND. Sample size is justified separately for each analysis (precision of proportions, correlation and regression power, events per variable, split-sample factor analysis, item response theory calibration, and reliability estimation). Measurement properties will be evaluated against pre-specified acceptance criteria: item difficulty 0.20-0.80 (a screening range interpreted together with discrimination) and corrected item-total correlations ≥ 0.30; internal consistency (KR-20/Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega) 0.70-0.95; test-retest ICC ≥ 0.70 and item-level weighted kappa ≥ 0.60; structural validity by split-sample exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis (CFI/TLI ≥ 0.90, RMSEA ≤ 0.08, SRMR ≤ 0.08); item response theory calibration with formal model comparison and differential item functioning screening; construct validity requiring confirmation of ≥75% of a priori hypotheses; floor/ceiling effects < 15%; and measurement invariance across sex, age group, and administration mode.

EXPECTED RESULTS: The study will deliver a validated Romanian-language instrument, a structured characterization of PE-related knowledge, attitudes, and preventive practices, and the distribution of self-reported risk factors in the study sample.

CONCLUSIONS: PE-KAP-RO is intended as a standardized assessment tool for PE-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices; the risk-factor burden index is descriptive and does not estimate VTE probability; any future predictive tool would require a separate cohort followed for incident VTE. Reporting follows the STROBE recommendations and COSMIN-based methodology; the protocol is presented prior to participant enrollment.

No validated instrument is currently available to assess knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding PE among adults in Romania, and the burden of self-reported thromboembolic risk factors in community settings has not been described with standardized measures. This protocol describes the development and psychometric validation of the PE-KAP-RO questionnaire, an integrated assessment tool comprising three scored KAP scales, three embedded validated lifestyle instruments, and an exploratory, unweighted VTE risk-factor burden index.

title: Acute Limb Ischemia: Medicare and Medicaid Reimbursement Gaps Threaten Sustainability of Care.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute limb ischemia (ALI) is a vascular emergency associated with high morbidity and mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and substantial resource utilization. However, contemporary data evaluating the financial sustainability of ALI care across insurance types remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate hospitalization costs, reimbursement, profitability, and contribution margin (CM) for operative ALI care stratified by insurance status and revascularization strategy.

METHODS: A retrospective review of patients admitted with ALI at a quaternary medical center (2016-2024) was performed. Patients were identified using international classification of diseases-10 and currently procedural terminology codes. Exclusion criteria were outpatient encounters and nonoperative or nonprocedural management. Hospitalization cost was defined as the sum of variable and fixed costs. Profit was reimbursement minus cost. Analyses were stratified by insurance status and treatment modality. Continuous variables were compared using nonparametric tests, with statistical significance set at P < 0.05.

RESULTS: A total of 565 patients were included, of whom 60.2% were insured by Medicare, 24.2% by Medicaid, and 15.6% by commercial insurance. Median total hospitalization costs exceeded $50,000 per admission and did not differ by insurance status (Medicare $50,894 [interquartile range $33,496-$90,923], Medicaid $49,417 [$33,775-$83,379], commercial $56,603 [$35,823-$96,067]; P = 0.577) or by revascularization strategy (open versus endovascular; P > 0.05). Professional and technical cost components were similarly comparable across payer groups. Despite similar costs, reimbursement varied significantly by insurance status. Medicare and Medicaid admissions were associated with median hospital losses of -$12,673 [-$28,732 to -$1,425] and -$3,176 [-$10,035 to $3,859], respectively, while commercially insured admissions generated a median profit of $30,622 [$7,602-$50,208] (P < 0.001). These differences persisted across both open and endovascular subgroups.

CONCLUSION: Operative management of ALI is associated with substantial hospitalization costs that are consistent across revascularization strategies and payer types. While commercially insured admissions generated positive CMs, Medicare and Medicaid reimbursements were insufficient to offset costs. Given that most patients were insured through Medicare, the reimbursement disparities translated into an overall negative financial impact for ALI care. Without reimbursement reform or payment adjustment, the long-term financial sustainability of ALI care, and equitable patient access to timely revascularization, may be jeopardized.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Acute limb ischemia (ALI) is a vascular emergency associated with high morbidity and mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and substantial resource utilization. However, contemporary data evaluating the financial sustainability of ALI care across insurance types remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate hospitalization costs, reimbursement, profitability, and contribution margin (CM) for operative ALI care stratified by insurance status and revascularization strategy.

title: Sepsis Prior to Total Knee Arthroplasty Is Associated With Elevated Rates of Myocardial Infarction and Deep Vein Thrombosis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients who have sepsis often experience persistent physiological instability, which may increase vulnerability to postoperative complications. However, the impact of preoperative sepsis on outcomes following elective total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains poorly defined. Thus, the purpose of this study was to investigate the association of preoperative sepsis with 90-day and two-year postoperative complications following TKA.

METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted utilizing an insurance database. Patients who had a preoperative diagnosis of sepsis within two years prior to TKA were matched at a 1:3 ratio to controls based on demographics and comorbidities. Patients who had sepsis were stratified according to the following timeline: sepsis three months prior to surgery, three to six months prior, six to 12 months prior, 12 to 18 months prior, and 18 to 24 months prior. Medical and surgical complications were assessed at 90 days and two years following surgery. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05.

RESULTS: Patients who had sepsis within two years prior to surgery exhibited increased rates of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) (odds ratio (OR): 1.6), postoperative sepsis (OR: 2.7), acute kidney injury (OR: 1.4), urinary tract infection (OR: 1.8), blood transfusion (OR: 2.0), readmission (OR: 1.3), and wound dehiscence (OR: 1.4) within 90 days of surgery. At two years following surgery, sepsis was associated with elevated rates of revision surgery (OR: 1.3), PJI (OR: 1.6), osteomyelitis (OR: 1.9), and mortality (OR: 1.3). Sepsis within three months of operation was associated with elevated rates of myocardial infarction (OR: 2.1) and deep vein thrombosis (OR: 2.0). All findings were statistically significant at P < 0.05.

CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative sepsis is associated with increased complications following TKA, including PJI and mortality. Sepsis within three months of surgery confers a particularly elevated risk of myocardial infarction and deep vein thrombosis following TKA.

However, the impact of preoperative sepsis on outcomes following elective total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains poorly defined. Thus, the purpose of this study was to investigate the association of preoperative sepsis with 90-day and two-year postoperative complications following TKA.

title: Early Outcomes of Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis in Aortic Arch Pathologies: A Nordic Multicentre Study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the feasibility and early clinical outcomes of the Gore thoracic branch endoprosthesis (TBE) in the treatment of aortic arch pathologies.

METHODS: This multicentre retrospective study, conducted and reported in accordance with the STROBE statement, included consecutive patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair with TBE between February 2024 and July 2025. No restrictions were applied regarding the type or extent of aortic disease, use of staged procedures, or concomitant adjunctive endovascular interventions. Primary endpoints were technical success, thirty day death, and overall survival, while endoleak occurrence, primary target vessel patency, stroke, and spinal cord ischaemia (SCI) were secondary.

RESULTS: Sixty-four patients (median age 73 years [interquartile range {IQR} 59, 77]; 69% men) were included. Indications for treatment included degenerative aneurysm (n = 26; 41%), chronic dissection (n = 18; 28%), subacute dissection (n = 11; 17%), and acute dissection (n = 9; 14%). The left subclavian artery was the target vessel in 59 cases (92%), followed by the brachiocephalic trunk in three (5%) and the left common carotid artery in two (3%). Technical success was achieved in 95% of cases (n = 61), with failures attributed to two type Ia endoleaks and one type IIIa endoleak. The thirty day mortality rate was 3% (n = 2). Early unplanned re-interventions occurred in four patients (6%). No strokes or SCI were observed. Median follow up was 6 months (IQR 2, 10). There were no late deaths, and primary patency of all branches was 100%. One late unplanned re-intervention, unrelated to the TBE device, was required. During follow up, 12 patients (19%) had endoleaks, including type II (n = 4), type Ia (n = 4), type Ib (n = 2), type III (n = 1), and type V (n = 1). Estimated freedom from type Ia endoleak at 12 months was 93 ± 3%, while estimated overall survival at 12 months was 97 ± 2%.

CONCLUSION: TBE demonstrated high technical success and acceptable early outcomes across a range of aortic arch pathologies. However, the relatively high rate of endoleaks and need for early re-interventions highlight the importance of careful patient selection and close continuous post-operative surveillance.

METHODS: This multicentre retrospective study, conducted and reported in accordance with the STROBE statement, included consecutive patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair with TBE between February 2024 and July 2025. No restrictions were applied regarding the type or extent of aortic disease, use of staged procedures, or concomitant adjunctive endovascular interventions.

title: Multidisciplinary Collaboration in the Performance of Aortic Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
abstract: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.

title: Ortner's syndrome associated with a saccular aortic arch aneurysm presenting as isolated unilateral vocal cord paralysis: a case report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ortner's syndrome, or cardiovocal syndrome, is an uncommon cause of recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy due to cardiovascular pathology. Thoracic aortic aneurysm is a rare but important etiology that may present only with hoarseness.

CASE PRESENTATION: An 85-year-old man with hypertension and a history of chronic smoking presented with progressive hoarseness for 1 month. Flexible laryngoscopy showed paralysis of the left vocal cord without laryngeal pathology. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed a 22 × 17 mm saccular aneurysm arising from the distal aortic arch at the aortopulmonary window, with mural thrombus and in close proximity to the left recurrent laryngeal nerve. No cervical, mediastinal, pulmonary, or laryngeal malignancy was detected. Echocardiography showed preserved systolic function without significant valvular disease or pulmonary hypertension. Ortner's syndrome associated with the distal aortic arch aneurysm was considered the most likely diagnosis based on the clinical and radiological findings and the exclusion of other identifiable causes. Surgical repair was advised, but the patient declined and was managed conservatively. At the 11-month clinical follow-up, he remained stable with persistent hoarseness; no follow-up CT was performed.

CLINICAL DISCUSSION: Aortic arch aneurysm is a rare cause of Ortner's syndrome and may mimic more common causes of unilateral vocal cord paralysis, particularly malignancy. Imaging along the recurrent laryngeal nerve pathway, including the thorax, is essential when laryngoscopy does not reveal a local cause.

CONCLUSION: Unexplained left vocal cord paralysis should prompt an evaluation for cardiovascular causes. Early cross-sectional imaging can identify a thoracic aortic aneurysm and guide timely multidisciplinary management.

Thoracic aortic aneurysm is a rare but important etiology that may present only with hoarseness. CASE PRESENTATION: An 85-year-old man with hypertension and a history of chronic smoking presented with progressive hoarseness for 1 month.

title: Emergency Endovascular Repair of a Large Ruptured Isolated Internal Iliac Artery Aneurysm in a 98-Year-Old Patient: A Case Report.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Isolated internal iliac artery aneurysm (IIAA) is rare and carries a high mortality when ruptured. Management is particularly challenging in very elderly, anticoagulated patients in whom open repair may carry substantial perioperative risk. Herein, we report a case that illustrates device selection when a marked common iliac-external iliac size discrepancy precludes bridging with the available iliac limbs. Case Presentation: A 98-year-old man receiving apixaban presented with lower abdominal pain, nausea, and diarrhea. Computed tomography demonstrated a ruptured right IIAA measuring 79 × 72 mm in the axial plane, with retroperitoneal hematoma. A marked size discrepancy between the common iliac artery (20 mm) and external iliac artery (approximately 10 mm), together with vessel tortuosity, made common iliac-external iliac bridging with an iliac limb unsuitable with the devices available. Emergency endovascular aneurysm repair with a full aortic bifurcated endograft was combined with coil embolization of the inferior gluteal artery and gelatin sponge embolization of the sac. The contralateral internal iliac artery, which harbored a 31 mm aneurysm, was preserved. A suspected type IV endoleak had resolved on CT at day 4, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 8 without complications. At 6-month follow-up, the aneurysm sac had decreased from 79 × 72 mm to 72 × 62 mm in the axial plane with no evidence of endoleak, and he remained ambulatory without pelvic ischemic symptoms. Conclusions: A full aortic bifurcated endograft combined with coil and sac embolization may be a feasible bail-out option when a marked common iliac-external iliac size discrepancy precludes bridging with the available iliac limbs, even in a nonagenarian receiving apixaban.

title: Patient Selection and Evidence for Intervention in Deep Vein Thrombosis and Pulmonary Embolism.
abstract: Intervention for deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) should address a clinical problem that anticoagulation alone may not resolve. This narrative review separates whether to intervene, which procedure to choose, and how to maintain benefit. The review covers publications through 10 September 2026, with a later STORM-PE follow-up report identified separately. Anticoagulation remains foundational. In acute iliofemoral DVT, selected patients may gain earlier symptom relief or less severe post-thrombotic disease, but trials do not support routine thrombus removal. In established post-thrombotic obstruction, C-TRACT showed better six-month clinical severity and quality of life with stenting and enhanced antithrombotic treatment, alongside more bleeding. In selected stable PE, HI-PEITHO reduced a seven-day clinical composite from 10.3% to 4.0%, mainly through fewer episodes of decompensation; a survival benefit remains unproven. Procedure comparisons and imaging trials answer narrower questions than benefit over medical care. Limb-threatening DVT and unstable PE require urgent rescue assessment. A five-scenario table and clinical examples connect this evidence to symptoms, anatomy, recovery goals, bleeding risk, and the feasibility of continuing treatment and follow-up.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Cannulation of Arteriovenous Fistulas in Hemodialysis Units: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Arteriovenous fistulas are the preferred vascular access for hemodialysis, but difficult or unsuccessful cannulation may cause pain, complications, and access dysfunction. This review evaluated whether ultrasound-guided cannulation improves outcomes compared with standard cannulation. Methods: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for randomized controlled trials comparing ultrasound-guided and standard arteriovenous fistula cannulation in hemodialysis patients. Findings were synthesized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Results: Of 1210 records identified, five randomized trials involving 142 patients were included. Some trials reported improved cannulation success or lower pain with ultrasound guidance, but findings varied across populations and outcome measures. Three of four trials reporting procedure time found longer durations with ultrasound guidance. A consistent reduction in complications or improvement in patient satisfaction was not established. Staff findings mainly concerned confidence and acceptability. The certainty of evidence was low. Conclusions: The effects of ultrasound-guided AVF cannulation on pain varied across trials. These uncertain findings should be interpreted alongside the longer procedure times reported in several trials. Larger randomized trials with clearly defined outcomes and analyses accounting for repeated observations are needed before recommending routine use.

title: Preprocedural Serum Albumin and Early Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury After Elective Carotid Artery Stenting: Incremental Prognostic Information Beyond the PCI-Derived Mehran Score.
abstract: Background/Objectives: We assessed whether preprocedural serum albumin adds prognostic information to the PCI-derived Mehran score for early contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) after elective carotid artery stenting (CAS). Methods: This single-centre retrospective cohort included 121 consecutive elective patients (January 2020-April 2026). The primary model combined the reconstructed Mehran score with albumin < 3.5 g/dL, a conventional threshold fixed in advance. Because the score uses actual contrast volume, the combined model applies only after CAS. The outcome used KDIGO serum creatinine thresholds (≥0.3 mg/dL or ≥1.5 times baseline) from routine second-day testing. Internal validation used 1000 bootstrap resamples. Results: Early CA-AKI occurred in 32 patients (26.4%). Adjusted odds ratios were 1.35 per Mehran point (95% CI 1.13-1.60) and 11.68 for albumin < 3.5 g/dL (95% CI 4.14-32.97). AUC increased from 0.768 to 0.865 (95% CI 0.794-0.937; likelihood ratio χ2 = 24.58, p < 0.001). Corrected AUC, calibration slope, and Brier score were 0.860, 0.96, and 0.132. In exploratory decision curves (20% threshold), corrected net benefit was 0.168 for the combined model and 0.133 for Mehran alone. Conclusions: Low preprocedural albumin added prognostic information to the PCI-derived score and may help select patients for closer renal surveillance after CAS. External validation and prospective impact studies are needed before clinical use.

The primary model combined the reconstructed Mehran score with albumin < 3.5 g/dL, a conventional threshold fixed in advance.

title: From revascularization to multimodal integrated therapy for peripheral arterial disease: immunomodulation, metabolic correction, and tissue engineering.
abstract: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD), a critical manifestation of systemic atherosclerosis (AS), poses substantial therapeutic challenges. Despite pharmacological interventions and revascularization, efficacy remains constrained by high restenosis rates and suboptimal functional recovery. These limitations underscore a necessary transition from localized structural revascularization toward integrated systemic repair, with a particular focus on the underlying immunopathology. The progression of PAD is driven by a dysregulated immune response, characterized by an imbalance in macrophage polarization (M1/M2), overactivation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, and a vicious cycle of immune-metabolic coupling. Current research trajectories emphasize the synergistic orchestration of the vascular microenvironment through immunomodulation. Beyond modulating localized inflammatory responses, emerging strategies target metabolic homeostasis and advanced tissue engineering, including spatiotemporal growth factor delivery, extracellular vesicle-based therapies, and bioengineered scaffolding systems. These interdisciplinary developments point toward a multimodal integrated therapeutic strategy for PAD. Such a strategy would build on conventional revascularization and may address its limitations, including restenosis, through targeted immunomodulation and local tissue regeneration. Whether this approach can improve long-term outcomes compared with revascularization alone remains to be tested. If validated, it could shift the clinical standard beyond vessel patency toward comprehensive, long-term vascular health.

title: Role of direct intraoperative ultrasound-guided renal resistive index and its association with postoperative acute kidney injury in patients undergoing abdominal vascular surgeries: A prospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a major complication following abdominal vascular surgery, and current diagnostic markers often detect injury only after significant renal damage has occurred. Doppler-derived renal resistive index (RRI) is a promising real-time marker of renal perfusion. This study evaluated direct intraoperative ultrasound (DIOUS)-guided RRI measurement for assessing postoperative AKI in open abdominal vascular surgery.

METHODS: In this prospective study, 40 adults undergoing open abdominal vascular procedures were enroled. RRI was measured at four timepoints: preoperatively; intraoperatively, 30 minutes after aortic declamping, using DIOUS; and postoperatively at 12 and 24 hours using transabdominal Doppler ultrasonography. AKI was defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes creatinine-based criteria.

RESULTS: Postoperative AKI developed in 50% of patients. Mean DIOUS-guided RRI measured 30 minutes after declamping was higher in patients who developed AKI than in those who did not (0.74 ± 0.05 vs. 0.69 ± 0.04; P = 0.003). Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an exploratory, internally derived intraoperative RRI cut-off of 0.71, predicting postoperative AKI with 80% sensitivity and 70% specificity [area under curve 0.783; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.639-0.927]. The odds of developing AKI increased by 33% for every 0.01-unit increase in intraoperative RRI (odds ratio 1.33; 95% CI 1.03-1.71; P = 0.026).

CONCLUSION: DIOUS-guided RRI measurement is a feasible method for real-time assessment of renal haemodynamics during open abdominal vascular surgery. The association between intraoperative RRI and postoperative AKI suggests this technique may complement perioperative renal risk assessment and support early kidney-protective interventions, pending validation in larger studies.

Doppler-derived renal resistive index (RRI) is a promising real-time marker of renal perfusion. This study evaluated direct intraoperative ultrasound (DIOUS)-guided RRI measurement for assessing postoperative AKI in open abdominal vascular surgery.

title: Traditional Chinese medicine for diabetic lower extremity arterial disease: A review of recent advances.
abstract: Diabetic lower-extremity arterial disease (LEAD) is a prevalent macrovascular complication of diabetes and a critical pathological foundation for diabetic foot lesions. Its pathogenesis involves glycolipid metabolic disturbance, excessive oxidative stress, persistent vascular inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction, leading to limb ischemia, refractory foot ulcers, and increased amputation risk. Current standard treatments, including glycemic and lipid control, antiplatelet therapy, and endovascular revascularization, have improved clinical outcomes but still face challenges in fully ameliorating microcirculatory impairment and preventing long-term restenosis. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) exerts multi-component and multi-target protective effects against diabetic LEAD. This review summarizes pharmacological advances in representative TCM agents, including Salvia miltiorrhiza, Astragali Radix, and their bioactive constituents (e.g., tanshinone IIA sulfonate, salvianolic acid B, astragaloside IV, and Astragalus polysaccharide), as well as classical formulas and patent medicines such as Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu Decoction, Tongxinluo capsule, Tangbi capsule, and Danggui Sini Decoction. Their mechanisms involve protecting vascular endothelium, regulating glycolipid metabolism, suppressing vascular inflammation via NF-κB and NLRP3 pathways, and activating Nrf2-mediated antioxidant defense, HIF-1α/VEGF, PI3K-AKT, and Ang-1/Tie-2 signaling to restore microcirculation and promote angiogenesis. Clinically, TCM-assisted endovascular intervention reduces postoperative restenosis and improves lower-limb perfusion; external preparations promote diabetic foot ulcer healing; acupuncture, moxibustion, and mind-body exercises improve microcirculation and long-term management. TCM is a promising adjunctive strategy for diabetic LEAD, and further mechanistic and clinical studies are needed to advance its standardized application and improve patient prognosis.

title: Risk factors and clinical outcomes of reocclusion after endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke: an updated systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined.

METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions.

RESULTS: Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced.

CONCLUSIONS: Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.

METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE.

title: Deep Learning-Based 3D CT Body Composition Is Associated With Mortality in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent advances in artificial intelligence enable fully automated 3-dimensional computed tomography (CT)-based body composition quantification. We investigated whether automated CT-derived thoraco-abdominopelvic body composition measures are associated with mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement.

METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, consecutive patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with preprocedural CT imaging were included between 2014 and 2023. A deep learning-based pipeline performed automated 3-dimensional segmentation of thoraco-abdominopelvic noncontrast CT scans to quantify volumes (L/m2) and attenuations (Hounsfield units) of subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, muscular adipose tissue, and lean skeletal muscle, indexed to body surface area. Associations with mortality were evaluated using Cox models and Harrell C statistics, adjusting for demographics (age, sex, body mass index) and cardiometabolic risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, chronic renal failure).

RESULTS: Among 915 patients (median age, 84 years [interquartile range, 77-90]; 58% men), 160 (17.5%) died over a median follow-up of 22 months (interquartile range, 14-36). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated that lower subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation were associated with increased mortality, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation were associated with improved survival. Addition of body composition measures provided incremental discriminatory value beyond demographics and cardiometabolic risk factors (Harrell C, 0.66 versus 0.71; P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Automated 3-dimensional CT-derived body composition measures provide independent prognostic information and improve risk stratification for mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Low subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation identify patients at increased risk, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation are associated with lower mortality.

We investigated whether automated CT-derived thoraco-abdominopelvic body composition measures are associated with mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, consecutive patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with preprocedural CT imaging were included between 2014 and 2023.

title: Aspirin-Based Thromboprophylaxis Versus Anticoagulant Regimens After Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Aspirin is widely used for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA); however, uncertainty remains regarding its efficacy and safety compared with anticoagulant regimens. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated aspirin-based thromboprophylaxis versus anticoagulant regimens following THA or TKA. Materials and Methods: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched through July 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing aspirin-based prophylaxis with anticoagulant regimens. The primary outcomes were any deep vein thrombosis (DVT), symptomatic DVT, and symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE). Secondary outcomes included pulmonary embolism (PE), proximal and distal DVT, bleeding outcomes, wound complications, blood transfusion, and mortality. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Additional risk-difference sensitivity analyses incorporated CRISTAL's published cluster-adjusted estimates. Results: Sixteen trials involving 21,265 participants were included. Aspirin was associated with higher risks of symptomatic DVT (RR 1.79, 95% CI 1.35-2.38), symptomatic VTE (RR 1.70, 95% CI 1.33-2.18), PE (RR 1.89, 95% CI 1.33-2.68), and distal DVT (RR 1.47, 95% CI 1.06-2.06). Aspirin was associated with lower risks of minor bleeding (RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.31-0.71) and ecchymosis or bruising (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.39-0.93). No statistically significant differences were detected for the other assessed outcomes. Additional analyses incorporating CRISTAL's cluster-adjusted risk differences did not identify statistically significant differences for the three primary outcomes or PE. Conclusions: The main pooled analyses associated aspirin-based thromboprophylaxis with higher risks of symptomatic thromboembolic events. However, the symptomatic DVT and symptomatic VTE associations were no longer statistically significant after exclusion of CRISTAL or restriction to trials at low risk of bias. The low-risk analysis identified a significantly higher risk of any DVT with aspirin. Aspirin reduced minor bleeding and bruising without a statistically significant reduction in major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding. These findings require cautious interpretation given dependence on CRISTAL, sensitivity to trial inclusion and analytical approach, and differences in prophylactic strategies and outcome definitions.

title: Early and follow-up results of reinterventions for type 2 endoleak following endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm: The multicenter REinterventions for Type 2 Endoleak study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type II endoleak (T2EL) is frequent after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) repair and may require reintervention in selected patients. However, the optimal treatment strategy for durable resolution remains uncertain. This study aimed to retrospectively evaluate the perioperative and long-term outcomes of T2Els' reinterventions, both endovascular and open surgical, in a large patient cohort from 20 high-volume academic centers.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis of consecutive patients undergoing first reintervention for T2ELs was conducted across 20 centers over a 10-year period. Patients requiring concomitant treatment for other endoleak types were excluded. A total of 403 patients were included. Primary outcomes included technical success, 30-day AAA-related mortality and reintervention-free survival during follow-up. Secondary outcomes were perioperative complications, early reintervention, overall survival, freedom from aneurysm-related death and rupture, freedom from recurrent endoleaks, freedom from open conversion or semiconversion in patients previously treated endovascularly and sac behavior during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression analyses were performed to analyze follow-up results.

RESULTS: Patients were predominantly male (90%) with a mean age of 77 years. Reintervention was indicated for sac enlargement in 94.5% of cases; 4% presented with rupture. Median time from endovascular AAA repair to reintervention was 4.3 years. Lumbar arteries (55%) and the inferior mesenteric artery (35%) were the main sources. Endovascular treatment was performed in 86% and open conversion/semiconversion in 14%. Technical success was 96%, with 1% mortality and 4% major complications. Overall survival was 80.5% and rupture-free survival 79.2% at 5 years. Recurrent T2EL occurred in 64.2%, and reintervention-free survival was 48.3%. Endovascular group showed significantly lower freedom from reintervention rates when compared to open conversion/semiconversion group [42.4% vs 86.8%; standard error, 0.04 vs standard error, 0.05; P < .001; log-rank, 15.9]. Conversion/semiconversion after endovascular treatment occurred in 14%. No differences were recorded comparing different fabric materials of the endograft in terms of freedom for reintervention and freedom from open surgery. A sac diameter ≥7 cm at the time of reintervention predicted further reinterventions, whereas primary open treatment improved durability.

CONCLUSIONS: Reinterventions for T2ELs are safe, with satisfactory immediate technical success and low perioperative mortality. During follow-up, risks of rupture and AAA-related death remain low. However, the endoleak recurrence rate exceeds 60% at 5 years, necessitating reintervention in over 40% of patients. Early intervention for patients with a sac diameter approaching 7 cm can be suggested, whereas a primary open approach may be considered in low-risk patients.

However, the optimal treatment strategy for durable resolution remains uncertain. title: Cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling at 24 hours after stroke thrombectomy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, tissue with abnormal perfusion may have impaired oxygen extraction and metabolism. MRI model-based oxygen extraction fraction (OEFmax) and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2) were characterized in hypoperfusion and hyperemia regions 24 h post-EVT.

METHODS: Eighty-four patients were included with anterior circulation vessel occlusion, successful recanalization, and an MRI at 24 h post-EVT. Time-to-maximum (Tmax) and cerebral blood flow (CBF) were evaluated for hypoperfusion and hyperemia. CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were quantified using (i) segmentation-based and (ii) single slice region of interest (ROI) analyses. Normalized CBF, OEFmax, and CMRO2 were calculated by dividing the segmentation or ROI value by the contralateral value.

RESULTS: Sixty-seven (80%) patients had abnormal perfusion; hypoperfusion in 22 (26%), hyperemia in 36 (43%), and both in 9 (11%). Compared to control, hypoperfused regions demonstrated a 62% CBF decrease, 52% CMRO2 decrease, and 68% OEFmax increase (p < 0.01). Hyperemic regions demonstrated a 58% CBF increase, 26% CMRO2 increase, and 25% OEFmax decrease (p < 0.01). Hyperemia had no significant correlation between normalized CBF and CMRO2 (p = 0.14).

CONCLUSION: Hyperemia regions demonstrated cerebral blood flow-oxygen metabolism uncoupling, suggesting the underlying mechanism as loss of cerebrovascular autoregulation rather than hypermetabolic demand.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Following successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, tissue with abnormal perfusion may have impaired oxygen extraction and metabolism. MRI model-based oxygen extraction fraction (OEFmax) and cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO2) were characterized in hypoperfusion and hyperemia regions 24 h post-EVT. METHODS: Eighty-four patients were included with anterior circulation vessel occlusion, successful recanalization, and an MRI at 24 h post-EVT.
