title: Optimizing pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis in medical inpatients using sequential IMPROVE risk assessment models: Clinical, economic and environmental implications.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major preventable cause of morbidity and mortality in hospitalized medical patients. Current recommendations support broad pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, while individualized risk assessment may help refine prescribing. The IMPROVE VTE and IMPROVE Bleeding scores provide standardized risk assessment tools but should complement, rather than replace, clinical judgment.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the discrepancy between real-world thromboprophylaxis prescribing and a prespecified sequential IMPROVE-based strategy and assess its economic and environmental implications.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study in internal medicine over one month. Adults hospitalized for>48h were included, excluding those receiving therapeutic anticoagulation. IMPROVE VTE and Bleeding scores were calculated retrospectively. Pharmacologic prophylaxis was supported by the strategy for patients with an IMPROVE Bleeding score<7 and IMPROVE VTE score≥2. Observed prescriptions were compared with the prespecified strategy using contingency analysis and Fisher's exact test.

RESULTS: Among 99 patients, 79.8% received pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, whereas 46.5% met the strategy criteria. Among treated patients, 46.8% did not meet these criteria. Strict application of the strategy would theoretically result in 292 fewer doses over one month, corresponding to €233.60 in estimated savings and approximately 405kg CO2eq.

CONCLUSION: Real-world prescribing differed substantially from the prespecified strategy. Strict application would theoretically reduce anticoagulant use, costs, and carbon emissions. However, clinical outcomes were not assessed, and RAMs should complement rather than replace clinical judgment. Prospective studies incorporating VTE and bleeding outcomes are required to assess the safety of this approach.

Current recommendations support broad pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis, while individualized risk assessment may help refine prescribing. The IMPROVE VTE and IMPROVE Bleeding scores provide standardized risk assessment tools but should complement, rather than replace, clinical judgment.

title: Transseptal Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Mitral Annular Calcification: ENCIRCLE MAC Registry 1-Year Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with symptomatic mitral valve dysfunction (MVD) and mitral annular calcification (MAC) represent one of the most challenging populations in structural heart disease. Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate 1-year clinical, echocardiographic, and patient-centered outcomes after transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system in patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD.

METHODS: The ENCIRCLE (SAPIEN M3 System Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement Via Transseptal Access) trial MAC Registry is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study that enrolled symptomatic patients with MAC-related MVD, including ≥ moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (MR), severe mitral stenosis, or combined moderate MR with at least moderate mitral stenosis, who were considered unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair. The primary endpoint was a nonhierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year.

RESULTS: Among 364 screened patients, TVMR was attempted in 100, and the valve was implanted in 93. Mean age was 76.1 ± 9.2 years, 51.0% were male, 73.0% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 8.4% ± 4.9%. At 1 year, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 33.6% (95% CI: 25.0%-44.1%), with 21.1% all-cause mortality and 19.4% HFH. Disabling stroke occurred in 5.1%, clinically significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in 4.8%, valve thrombosis in 2.3%, hemolysis requiring transfusion or mitral valve reintervention in 9.2%, and mitral valve re-intervention in 11.4%. Among implanted patients, MR ≤1+ was achieved in 98.5% at 1 year. Improvements in NYHA functional class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score, and 6-minute walk distance were sustained through 1 year.

CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair, transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system was associated with sustained MR reduction and meaningful improvements in symptoms and quality of life through 1 year. These findings support consideration of transseptal TMVR as a treatment pathway for selected patients with MAC-related MVD.

Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain.

title: Real-life venous thromboembolism risk scores in multiple myeloma receiving daratumumab, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment with daratumumab and lenalidomide has improved survival in patients with multiple myeloma (MM), however the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) is high. Data on the accuracy of VTE risk scores in MM receiving daratumumab are limited.

OBJECTIVES: To assess (i) the prognostic accuracy of available VTE risk scores (IMPEDE-VTE, SAVED, PRISM, and EHR-CAT scores) in non-transplant-eligible MM (NTE-MM) and relapsed/refractory MM (RRMM) consecutively treated with daratumumab, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Dara-Rd); and (ii) the feasibility and safety of guideline-recommended thromboprophylaxis with low molecular weight heparin for 6 months followed by aspirin (LMWH-ASA).

DESIGN: Single-center, retrospective, cohort study.

METHODS: All consecutive MM patients treated with Dara-Rd and concomitant LMWH-ASA thromboprophylaxis between July, 2018 and September, 2023 were evaluated through chart review. Kaplan-Meier method and Concordance-Index (C-index) were used to estimate risk scores' prognostic accuracy.

RESULTS: 95 patients (median age 74 years) were included (n= 47 NTE-MM, and n= 48 RRMM). At 12 months from Dara-Rd initiation, 10 (10.4%) patients developed VTE; 4 (4.2%) had bleeding complications, and 2 (2.1%) patients died. Six VTE events (6.2%) occurred within first 6 months from Dara-Rd initiation while on LMWH prophylaxis, whereas 2 VTE (2%) developed in two patients receiving aspirin. The accuracy of IMPEDE-VTE, SAVED, PRISM and EHR-CAT scores was generally poor, with C-Index values ranging from 0.43 (95% confidence intervals [95%CI] 0.30 to 0.56) to 0.53 (95%CI: 0.38 to 0.68). LMWH-ASA prophylaxis was completed by 89.5% of the cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-life cohort of MM patients treated with Dara-Rd and guideline-recommended antithrombotic prophylaxis, currently available VTE risk scores demonstrated moderate to poor prognostic accuracy. LMWH-ASA prophylaxis was feasible but associated with residual VTE risk.

Data on the accuracy of VTE risk scores in MM receiving daratumumab are limited. OBJECTIVES: To assess (i) the prognostic accuracy of available VTE risk scores (IMPEDE-VTE, SAVED, PRISM, and EHR-CAT scores) in non-transplant-eligible MM (NTE-MM) and relapsed/refractory MM (RRMM) consecutively treated with daratumumab, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Dara-Rd); and (ii) the feasibility and safety of guideline-recommended thromboprophylaxis with low molecular weight heparin for 6 months followed by aspirin (LMWH-ASA).

title: Direct oral anticoagulants versus vitamin K antagonists for the treatment of venous thromboembolism in adults with sickle cell disease: a Bayesian meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly used as alternatives to vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) for the treatment of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients with sickle cell disease (SCD). However, comparative evidence is limited to small observational studies, and prior frequentist meta-analyses may be unreliable due to sparse data and zero-event outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of DOACs versus VKAs for VTE treatment in adults with SCD.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis of studies comparing DOACs with VKAs in patients with SCD and VTE. PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to March 2026. Primary outcomes were recurrent VTE and major bleeding (MB). Bayesian random-effects models with weakly informative priors were used to estimate pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). Posterior probabilities were derived using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling.

RESULTS: Four retrospective studies including 271 patients (155 DOACs and 116 VKAs) were included. Recurrent VTE did not differ between groups (OR, 0.82; 95% CrI, 0.38-1.75), with a 67.1% posterior probability favoring DOACs, indicating equipoise. DOACs were associated with a significantly lower risk of MB (OR, 0.25; 95% CrI, 0.07-0.80), with a 99.2% probability of superiority. Between-study heterogeneity was low (τ = 0.15 for recurrent VTE; τ = 0.30 for MB).

CONCLUSION: DOACs demonstrate comparable efficacy to VKAs for preventing recurrent VTE in SCD, with a clinically meaningful reduction in MB. Given their safety profile and convenience, DOACs may be preferred; randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

However, comparative evidence is limited to small observational studies, and prior frequentist meta-analyses may be unreliable due to sparse data and zero-event outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of DOACs versus VKAs for VTE treatment in adults with SCD.

title: Morganella morganii Detected During Transfemoral Amputation in a Diabetic Foot With Soft Tissue Necrosis.
abstract: This case report describes a 63-year-old man with diabetes mellitus and peripheral arterial disease who was referred to our clinic with circulatory insufficiency and a foul-smelling necrotizing wound of the right lower extremity. The patient had previously undergone bilateral balloon angioplasty, which restored distal pulses; however, progressive soft tissue deterioration led to extensive purulent ulcers along the anteromedial and posterior aspects of the lower leg. Imaging demonstrated subcutaneous gas in the posterior soft tissues, and transfemoral amputation was performed. During surgical dissection, purulent discharge was observed along the anteromedial aspect of the femur, and intraoperative samples were obtained for microbiological analysis. Cultures yielded Enterobacter species and Morganella morganii, the latter being an opportunistic Gram-negative bacillus that is rarely implicated in musculoskeletal infections. This case is notable for the uncommon identification of Morganella morganii in a deep musculoskeletal infection and emphasizes the importance of broad microbiological consideration in necrotizing soft tissue infections, particularly in patients with diabetes or other predisposing conditions. Timely surgical intervention, adequate source control, and culture-directed antimicrobial therapy remain essential in such complex clinical scenarios.

Imaging demonstrated subcutaneous gas in the posterior soft tissues, and transfemoral amputation was performed.

title: The prediagnostic period of Behçet's disease: a nationwide population-based study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The diagnosis of Behçet's disease (BD) is often delayed because its characteristic manifestations may emerge sequentially over time. Whether BD is preceded by a clinically active prediagnostic phase remains unclear. We aimed to characterize the clinical and laboratory features during the five-year period preceding the formal diagnosis of BD.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective matched case-control study using the electronic health records of Leumit Health Services. Patients with BD fulfilling the International Criteria for Behçet's Disease or International Study Group classification criteria were identified by manual chart review and matched 1:5 with controls by sex, age, socioeconomic category and year of first observation. Clinical diagnoses, diagnostic investigations and laboratory measurements and medication dispensing recorded during the five years preceding diagnosis were compared between groups. Early and late laboratory measurements within the prediagnostic period were analyzed to assess temporal trends. Manifestations documented over the entire available record were analyzed separately.

RESULTS: The study included 218 patients who subsequently developed BD and 1,090 matched controls. During the five years preceding diagnosis, future patients with BD more frequently exhibited oral aphthosis (36.2% vs 3.0%; OR 18.2), panuveitis (4.6% vs 0.1%; OR 52.4), inflammatory polyarthritis (7.3% vs 0.6%; OR 14.3), and venous thromboembolism (4.6% vs 0.2%; OR 26.2) (all P<0.001). Over the entire available record, oral aphthosis was documented in 61.0% of patients with BD and 11.8% of controls. Autoimmune serology was frequently requested but remained largely negative. Laboratory analyses demonstrated a biphasic trajectory. Absolute monocyte count and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio were lower than in controls at the early assessment (0.40 vs 0.44 ×109/L, P = 0.009, and 1.45 vs 1.49, P = 0.023) but significantly higher near diagnosis (0.64 vs 0.58 ×109/L, P = 0.025, and 2.44 vs 2.09, P = 0.003). This transition was accompanied by rising CRP, ESR, platelet count and globulin levels, persistently lower mean corpuscular volume and consistently higher IgA at both assessments (247 vs 189 mg/dL, P = 0.009, and 256 vs 189 mg/dL, P = 0.012), whereas IgG and IgM remained comparable between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: BD seems to be preceded by a clinically and biologically active prediagnostic phase characterized by a distinct inflammatory multisystem footprint.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: The diagnosis of Behçet's disease (BD) is often delayed because its characteristic manifestations may emerge sequentially over time. Whether BD is preceded by a clinically active prediagnostic phase remains unclear. We aimed to characterize the clinical and laboratory features during the five-year period preceding the formal diagnosis of BD.

title: Clinical significance of the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index in glycemic control and ischemic limb damage in type 2 diabetes with chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical relevance of the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) complicated by chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) .

METHODS: A total of 520 patients with CLTI were collected and divided into two groups based on the history of T2DM: the combined T2DM group and the non-T2DM group. The CTI of the patients was calculated, and its relationship with blood glucose control levels, risk factors, and the degree of ischemia in CLTI patients was analyzed.

RESULTS: The CTI in the combined T2DM group was significantly greater than that in the non-T2DM group (P < 0.001). The CTI in the poorly controlled blood glucose group was significantly greater than that in the well controlled blood glucose group (P < 0.001). Regardless of whether CLTI patients had T2DM, the CTI in the overweight group was greater than that in the non-overweight group (P < 0.05). The area under the curve (AUC) for the CTI discriminating the high wound, ischemia, and foot infection (WIfI) classification was 0.813 (P < 0.001). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses showed that an increased CTI was an independently associated factor for the high WIfI classification in CLTI patients (OR = 6.409, P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that patients with CLTI and high CTI levels had significantly lower 1-year amputation-free survival compared to those with low CTI levels.

CONCLUSIONS: The CTI was closely related to the presence of T2DM, blood glucose control level, and overweight status in CLTI patients. The CTI has certain clinical value in discriminating the degree of ischemia in CLTI, and high CTI levels had significantly lower 1-year amputation-free survival compared to those with low CTI levels.

The CTI of the patients was calculated, and its relationship with blood glucose control levels, risk factors, and the degree of ischemia in CLTI patients was analyzed.

title: Postoperative Complications Following Carotid Endarterectomy are Differentially Impacted by Sex and Plaque Instability.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to provide novel evidence on the role of sex and plaque instability in postcarotid endarterectomy (CEA) outcomes. Current clinical guidelines regarding recommendation for CEA rely solely on grade of stenosis and cerebrovascular symptomatology, despite emerging evidence emphasizing the role of sex and plaque instability in determining postoperative outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of an ongoing cohort study of males and females undergoing CEA for clinical indications. We performed multivariable binary logistic regression to examine the relationship of biological sex and plaque instability with postoperative outcomes.

RESULTS: Data of 394 participants (31% female) were analyzed. Plaque instability was independently associated with decreased odds of hemorrhagic complications at 1 month and 1 year postsurgery, as well as with decreased respiratory complications at 1 year postsurgery. Plaque features accounting for these associations were lipid core, cap infiltration, and plaque inflammation. Female sex was independently associated with increased odds of restenosis at 1 month and 1 year postsurgery. In addition, females with unstable plaques had more cerebrovascular complications at 1 month than males with unstable plaques, and females with stable plaques had double the odds of any complication at 1 month compared with males with unstable plaques.

CONCLUSION: Our findings show that sex and plaque instability differentially impact postendarterectomy outcomes, with males with unstable plaques experiencing the least postoperative complications. Sex and plaque instability may therefore be important factors that play a role in postoperative complications, highlighting their importance in the context of surgical decision-making.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to provide novel evidence on the role of sex and plaque instability in postcarotid endarterectomy (CEA) outcomes. Current clinical guidelines regarding recommendation for CEA rely solely on grade of stenosis and cerebrovascular symptomatology, despite emerging evidence emphasizing the role of sex and plaque instability in determining postoperative outcomes. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of an ongoing cohort study of males and females undergoing CEA for clinical indications.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Amputation and Related Outcomes in Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects over 236 million individuals globally and carries substantial risks of amputation, major adverse limb events, and mortality. Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction. We aimed to conduct the first quantitative meta-analysis evaluation the discriminative performance, methodological rigor, and certainty of evidence of ML-based prognostic models for adverse limb outcomes in PAD.

METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)/Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses literature search extension (PRISMA-S) guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 15, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction) and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) analysis were performed; certainty was rated with Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE).

RESULTS: Ten studies were included. The pooled area under the curve (AUC) for amputation-related outcomes was 0.88 (95% confidence interval, 0.83-0.94; prediction interval, 0.79-0.98) with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 95.4%). HSROC yielded pooled sensitivity 0.85 and specificity 0.84. Registry-based studies showed higher pooled AUC than nonregistry studies (0.92 vs 0.80; P = 0.004). All models had a high or unclear risk of bias in the analysis domain; none underwent independent external validation. GRADE certainty was very low.

CONCLUSION: ML models demonstrate high discriminative performance for predicting amputation-related outcomes in PAD, but very low certainty of evidence, absence of external validation, and high risk of bias currently limit clinical implementation. Prospective multicenter validation and adherence to artificial intelligence reporting guidelines are essential before clinical translation.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects over 236 million individuals globally and carries substantial risks of amputation, major adverse limb events, and mortality. Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction.

title: Prevalence of Guideline-Recommended Genetic Testing in Patients at Risk for Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease.
abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts. We conducted a retrospective study using the TriNetX Research Network (2005-2025). Three guideline-based cohorts were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes: (1) thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, (2) family history of thoracic aortic disease, and (3) nonthoracic arterial aneurysms. Genetic testing was defined by ICD-10-CM codes for genetic screening or susceptibility. Testing prevalence was stratified by age, sex, race, and ethnicity, and annual testing incidence (2005-2024) was evaluated. Among 57,935 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, 1,205 (2.09%) underwent genetic testing. Among 2,811,862 patients with a family history of thoracic aortic disease, 66,699 (2.38%) received testing. Among 347,000 patients with nonthoracic arterial aneurysms, 4,913 (1.42%) underwent testing. Testing was consistently higher in females than males and varied across age groups. Annual testing incidence increased over time but remained <0.6% by 2024. In conclusion, genetic testing for HTAD remains markedly underutilized, with <2.5% of at-risk patients tested despite guideline recommendations, highlighting persistent implementation gaps and the need to improve equitable access to genetic evaluation.
englishSummary: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts.

title: One-year outcomes of hepatic artery stenosis after pediatric liver transplantation: Results from the international, multicenter HEPATIC registry.
abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to describe one-year graft and patient survival after hepatic artery stenosis (HAS) following pediatric liver transplantation (pLT), and to explore outcomes by timing of HAS diagnosis and treatment strategy within the HAS cohort.

METHODS: Patients who developed HAS after pLT were included as per definition from the HEPATIC registry. The registry contains data from 32 centers across 21 countries over a 20-year period, during which 10,564 primary pLTs were performed. Donor-, recipient-, and transplant-related characteristics were analyzed. The primary outcome was one-year graft and patient survival.

RESULTS: HAS was diagnosed in 1.2% of patients (n = 130; 51% female; median age 4.4 years [IQR 1.4-11.6]), of whom 5% (n = 7) progressed to thrombosis (HAT). One-year graft and patient survival were 93% and 96%, respectively. Management consisted mainly of antithrombotic therapy alone (41.5%) or endovascular therapy (EVT; 41.5%), with no significant difference in one-year graft or patient survival between these approaches. Early HAS (≤21 days post-pLT) was associated with significantly higher one-year graft loss than late HAS (16%vs. 1%; p < 0.001). All deaths occurred in the early HAS group.

CONCLUSIONS: One-year graft and patient survival after HAS were high. Antithrombotic therapy alone and EVT were the most common management strategies. Early HAS was associated with lower one-year survival. Prospective studies with standardized diagnostic and treatment criteria are needed for validation.
englishSummary: AIM: This study aimed to describe one-year graft and patient survival after hepatic artery stenosis (HAS) following pediatric liver transplantation (pLT), and to explore outcomes by timing of HAS diagnosis and treatment strategy within the HAS cohort. METHODS: Patients who developed HAS after pLT were included as per definition from the HEPATIC registry. The registry contains data from 32 centers across 21 countries over a 20-year period, during which 10,564 primary pLTs were performed.

title: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion With Signs of Ocular Hypoperfusion After Parent Artery Occlusion for a Traumatic Carotid-Cavernous Fistula: A Case Report.
abstract: A carotid-cavernous fistula (CCF) can cause a wide range of ocular complications, including venous stasis retinopathy, secondary glaucoma, and central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO). Retinal complications have been reported after endovascular closure of the shunt, but there are few reports describing the ophthalmic course of an eye in which the shunt persisted and in which parent artery occlusion of the internal carotid artery was required. A 63-year-old man was diagnosed with a traumatic right internal carotid artery CCF after a road traffic injury and underwent endovascular treatment on the second and third days after the injury. Because both the transvenous and the transarterial approaches were unsuccessful, parent artery occlusion of the right internal carotid artery was performed. According to the report from the referring institution, occlusion of the shunt was incomplete, and shunt flow into the right superior ophthalmic vein persisted. Angiography approximately six months after the injury confirmed the residual shunt, and no further endovascular treatment was considered feasible. Two months later, the patient noticed decreased vision in the right eye, presented to a local ophthalmologist, and was referred to our department. At presentation, best-corrected visual acuity was 0.2 (logMAR 0.70) in the right eye, and the intraocular pressure (IOP) was 14 mmHg. The right eye showed dilated episcleral vessels, dilated retinal veins, attenuated retinal arteries, retinal hemorrhages extending from the posterior pole to the periphery, and marked macular edema, but venous tortuosity was not prominent. The pupillary light reflex was reduced, and pharmacologic mydriasis was poor, without posterior synechiae or iris atrophy. Spontaneous pulsation of the central retinal artery was present in the affected eye and was augmented by gentle digital pressure, whereas no pulsation was seen in the fellow eye. On widefield fluorescein angiography, dye first entered the central retinal artery 20.1 seconds after the start of injection and complete arterial filling was reached at 25 seconds; numerous microaneurysms were seen from the posterior pole to the mid-periphery, with widespread vascular leakage and reduced perfusion of the retinal capillary network. The fellow eye showed only a few microaneurysms and scattered hard exudates, consistent with mild nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy. The patient had type 2 diabetes mellitus, untreated for approximately 10 years and restarted after the current injury, and hypertension. An intravitreal injection of an aflibercept biosimilar 2 mg was given on the day of presentation, followed by panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) delivered in four sessions for a total of 1,580 burns. Twenty-five days after the injection, the macular edema had clearly decreased but had not completely resolved, and it had recurred by day 67. Throughout the course, the IOP remained consistently lower in the affected eye than in the fellow eye. No iris or angle neovascularization was observed. In this eye, findings of CRVO coexisted with findings suggesting reduced ocular perfusion pressure. Even in a patient with systemic risk factors, local factors should be considered when the findings are confined to, or markedly more severe in, one eye. When no further treatment of the causative lesion is possible, management of the ocular complications is limited to ophthalmic measures, and their effects and limitations must be evaluated separately.

Retinal complications have been reported after endovascular closure of the shunt, but there are few reports describing the ophthalmic course of an eye in which the shunt persisted and in which parent artery occlusion of the internal carotid artery was required. A 63-year-old man was diagnosed with a traumatic right internal carotid artery CCF after a road traffic injury and underwent endovascular treatment on the second and third days after the injury.

title: Clinical outcomes, anticoagulation practice patterns, and quality of life after cancer-associated pulmonary embolism: secondary outcomes of the Hydra randomized clinical trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite its high prevalence, practice-based data on management and outcomes after cancer-associated pulmonary embolism (PE) are scarce, and no studies have investigated quality of life.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes, anticoagulation practice patterns, and quality of life after cancer-associated PE.

METHODS: The Hydra randomized clinical trial assessed the safety of the YEARS algorithm versus computed tomography pulmonary angiography only to exclude acute PE in patients with cancer. Patients with PE at baseline or during 90-day follow-up were included in this study. Outcomes were recurrent venous thromboembolism, major bleeding, all-cause mortality, anticoagulation practice patterns, and quality of life as assessed by the Pulmonary Embolism Quality of Life (PEmb-QoL) questionnaire. PEmb-QoL scores were compared with those for the general PE population reported in the FOCUS study. Lower scores indicate better QoL.

RESULTS: A total of 125 patients were included, of which 103 (82%) had PE at baseline, and 22 (18%) developed PE during follow-up. The 90-day cumulative incidence of recurrent venous thromboembolism and major bleeding was 2.5% (95% CI 0.67%-6.6%) and 2.5% (95% CI 0.68%-6.7%), respectively. All-cause mortality at 90 days was 32% (95% CI 23%-40%). Two-thirds of patients continued anticoagulation until less than 24 hours before death, and the median time between stopping anticoagulation and death was 10 days (IQR, 4-14). The median 90-day PEmb-QoL score was 33% (IQR, 13-51) versus 20% (IQR, 10-40) reported in the FOCUS study.

CONCLUSION: Patients with cancer-associated PE suffer from high mortality, high morbidity, and impaired quality of life. Anticoagulation therapy is frequently continued until the last days of life.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes, anticoagulation practice patterns, and quality of life after cancer-associated PE. METHODS: The Hydra randomized clinical trial assessed the safety of the YEARS algorithm versus computed tomography pulmonary angiography only to exclude acute PE in patients with cancer.

title: Adherence to the British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) Guidelines for the Management of Neck of Femur Fractures.
abstract: Introduction Over 72,000 hip fractures occur annually in the United Kingdom, costing over £2 billion, with 10% mortality at 30 days and 30% annually. Therefore, the study aimed to compare hip fracture care at North Manchester General Hospital with the British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) guidelines. Methodology A retrospective review of electronic patient records at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust was conducted from September to November 2025. Patients aged >60 years with native intracapsular or extracapsular femoral neck fractures, or those aged >60 years with pathological femoral neck fractures, were included. Descriptive analysis was performed to ascertain compliance with BOAST guidelines. Results The management of 51 patients was audited against 13 BOAST parameters. 100% compliance was achieved in seven parameters: certainty of diagnosis, a multidisciplinary team (MDT) approach to patient care, preoperative optimisation by an orthogeriatric team within 72 hours, documented weight-bearing status, falls risk assessment, bone health assessment, and data entry into the National Hip Fracture Database (NHFD). Parameters with less than 100% compliance were post-operative physiotherapy (50, 98%), venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis (50, 98%), analgesia (46, 91%), VTE assessment (45, 88%), post-operative delirium assessment (43, 84%), and surgery within 36 hours (32, 62.8%). Reasons for non-compliance included transfer to the intensive care unit (ICU) for post-operative physiotherapy; workload-related delays in VTE prophylaxis; unfamiliarity with local analgesia protocols among newly appointed National Health Service (NHS) doctors; inconsistent documentation of VTE assessment; and inconsistent completion of post-operative delirium assessments, with unclear responsibilities between doctors and coordinators. Limited theatre capacity and the need for medical optimisation accounted for non-compliance with the 36-hour surgery target. Conclusions BOAST compliance was good overall, but gaps in documentation, timing, and role clarity remain. Improvements include enforcing admission checklists, recording arousal, attention, and acute change using the abbreviated mental test-4 (4AT), pharmacist incident reporting, trauma coordinator oversight, and neck of femur training.

Methodology A retrospective review of electronic patient records at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust was conducted from September to November 2025.

title: Preoperative White Matter Lesions and Functional Recovery after Revascularization for Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Restoring ambulation is an important goal of revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), but predictors of functional recovery remain limited. We investigated whether preoperative white matter lesion (WML) burden was associated with ambulatory recovery after revascularization.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 196 patients with CLTI, tissue loss, Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection ischemia grade 2 or 3, and brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) within 3 months before revascularization. Preoperative brain MRI was routinely obtained in patients considered for open surgical revascularization for cerebrovascular risk assessment. Periventricular and deep subcortical white matter hyperintensities were graded using the Fazekas scale; a total score of 3 or greater defined a high-grade WML burden. The primary outcome was the achievement of a Functional Ambulation Category score of 3 or greater within 180 days. Associations were evaluated using multivariable Cox models.

RESULTS: High-grade WML burden was present in 120 patients. Six-month ambulatory recovery was lower in the high-grade group than in the low-grade group (63.1% vs 82.4%; P = 0.019). High-grade WML burden was independently associated with slower ambulatory recovery (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 0.65; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43-0.96; P = 0.032) and delayed final discharge (adjusted HR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.43-0.92; P = 0.017), but not with wound healing or wound-free functional limb achievement.

CONCLUSION: High-grade WML burden was associated with impaired ambulatory recovery and delayed discharge after CLTI revascularization. When preoperative brain MRI is available, WML assessment may complement limb staging and help anticipate rehabilitation and discharge needs.

title: Carotid stenosis reporting in Doppler ultrasound: why specifying NASCET or ECST criteria matters-an outpatient study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Carotid artery stenosis represents a major risk factor for ischemic stroke, and Doppler ultrasound is widely used as the first-line imaging modality for its assessment. The degree of stenosis is commonly expressed as a percentage and can be calculated according to different methods, most notably the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) and the European Carotid Surgery Trial (ECST) criteria. However, in routine clinical practice, the classification system used to determine the percentage of stenosis is not always specified in the ultrasound report. These methods consider different reference diameters, making values non-comparable and potentially misleading for clinical decisions.

METHODS: In this study, we reviewed 1,400 patients evaluated in the Doppler ultrasound outpatient clinic of Internal Medicine at Poma Hospital, Mantova, Italy. All examinations were performed during routine clinical activity over four years by a physician tutor of the Italian Society of Medical and Biological Ultrasonology (SIUMB). The patient population included individuals aged between 18 and 97 years.

RESULTS: During follow-up evaluations, it was frequently observed that previous ultrasound reports indicated a percentage of carotid stenosis without specifying whether NASCET or ECST criteria had been used.

CONCLUSIONS: Our experience highlights the importance of clearly stating the classification system used for stenosis grading in carotid Doppler reports. Standardized reporting may improve longitudinal comparison of examinations, facilitate clinical decision-making, and enhance communication among healthcare professionals involved in the management of carotid artery disease.

The degree of stenosis is commonly expressed as a percentage and can be calculated according to different methods, most notably the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) and the European Carotid Surgery Trial (ECST) criteria. title: Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage during bridging anticoagulation in primary antiphospholipid syndrome: a case-based review.
abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a major cause of acquired thrombophilia and is frequently associated with recurrent venous thromboembolism requiring long-term anticoagulation. We report a 42-year-old man with primary APS and recurrent pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis who developed acute right upper-quadrant abdominal pain during peri-procedural bridging anticoagulation with enoxaparin. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute-to-subacute unilateral right adrenal haemorrhage without evidence of abdominal trauma, malignancy or infection. The patient remained haemodynamically stable and did not develop adrenal insufficiency. This case highlights the complexity of anticoagulation management in high-risk APS patients and emphasises the importance of considering adrenal haemorrhage in APS patients presenting with abdominal pain during anticoagulation modification. A review of previously reported unilateral APS-associated adrenal haemorrhage cases is also presented. Key Points • Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage is a rare manifestation of primary antiphospholipid syndrome. • Bridging anticoagulation may represent a vulnerable period for adrenal haemorrhage in high-risk APS. • Early CT/MRI imaging and assessment of adrenal function are essential. • Conservative management with careful reintroduction of anticoagulation may lead to favourable outcomes.

title: Updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing Myval versus Sapien 3 transcatheter heart valves in severe aortic stenosis: focus on early and one-year mortality.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a guideline-recommended treatment for severe aortic stenosis (AS). While the balloon-expandable Edwards Sapien 3 valve has long been the benchmark, the newer Myval valve has emerged as a potential alternative. Comparative data on mid-term survival, specifically one-year all-cause mortality, are lacking but crucial for clinical evaluation.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised direct comparative evidence on the Myval versus Sapien 3 valves in patients undergoing TAVI, searching PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central up to November 2025. The primary outcomes included all-cause mortality within 30 days and 1 year. Secondary outcomes were 30-day safety events and hemodynamic parameters.

RESULTS: Five studies (n = 2771) were included. The pooled analysis indicated no statistical difference in 30-day mortality (RR: 1.05, 95% CI: 0.53-2.07; p = 0.89; I2=0%) or in one-year all-cause mortality (RR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.64-1.35; p = 0.70; I2=0%). Rates of stroke, major bleeding, pacemaker implantation, and other 30-day complications were also comparable (all p > 0.05). Hemodynamically, the Myval valve was superior at 30 days, with a lower mean gradient (MD: -2.37, 95% CI: -3.45 to -1.30; p < 0.0001) and larger effective orifice area (MD: 0.26, 95% CI: 0.17-0.35; p < 0.00001). Available one-year data from two randomised trials indicated this hemodynamic benefit was sustained.

CONCLUSION: This updated meta-analysis demonstrates that the newer Myval valve offers comparable early safety and one-year survival to the established Sapien 3 valve, with superior and sustained hemodynamic performance. These findings support its role as a safe and effective alternative in the TAVI landscape.

title: Characteristics of pediatric central venous catheter malfunction and subsequent catheter-related deep vein thrombosis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central venous catheters (CVCs) are increasingly placed in children; however, malfunction and deep vein thrombosis (DVT) are reasons for frequent removal.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to evaluate variables associated with CVC malfunction and, subsequently, the development of CVC-related DVT (CR-DVT).

METHODS: This subanalysis of the multicenter, prospective Clot Incidence Rates in Central Lines study enrolled children aged 6 months to <18 years with newly placed peripherally inserted central catheters or tunneled lines from 2013 to 2018. Time from CVC placement to first malfunction was analyzed in the full cohort using univariable and multivariable Weibull regression. Among CVCs that malfunctioned, time from first malfunction to CR-DVT was analyzed to assess tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) use and subsequent thrombosis.

RESULTS: Malfunction occurred in 380/1951 CVCs (19.5%). In multivariable analysis, prior CVC use (hazard ratio [HR], 1.51; 95% CI, 1.19-1.90; P = .001), multilumen catheters (HR, 2.89; 95% CI, 2.30-3.65; P < .001), and >2 insertion attempts (HR, 2.21; 95% CI, 1.42-3.45; P < .001) were associated with a higher risk of malfunction, whereas catheter size >4 French and interventional radiology placement were associated with a lower risk. Among malfunctioning CVCs, 22/380 (5.8%) developed CR-DVT, with a median time to CR-DVT of 6 days after malfunction. Increasing t-PA use showed a nonsignificant trend toward higher subsequent CR-DVT.

CONCLUSION: CVC malfunction is common and associated with several modifiable catheter-related factors. Six percent of malfunctioning CVCs develop CR-DVT, and repeated t-PA use and persistent CVC dysfunction may warrant further evaluation for underlying thrombosis.

METHODS: This subanalysis of the multicenter, prospective Clot Incidence Rates in Central Lines study enrolled children aged 6 months to <18 years with newly placed peripherally inserted central catheters or tunneled lines from 2013 to 2018.

title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation.
abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

title: Automated Detection of Endoleaks in CT Angiography Using a Single Deep Learning Model.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop and evaluate a single deep learning object detection model for automated detection of endoleaks on post-endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) computed tomography (CT) angiography, including in the presence of artifacts caused by ethylene vinyl alcohol copolymer embolization.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective data set comprising 249 CT scans was used, divided into training (129 scans) and test (120 scans) data sets. Ground truth annotations were obtained through 3-dimensional manual segmentation, and a preprocessing pipeline was applied. The model was trained on slices extracted from the training data set and validated using standard metrics, including sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve (AUC).

RESULTS: The model achieved high performance at both the per-slice and per-series levels. Per-slice detection yielded a receiver operating characteristic AUC of 0.96, with a sensitivity of 91%, specificity of 93%, positive predictive value of 55%, and negative predictive value of 99%. At the per-series level, sensitivity and specificity were 93% and 95%, respectively. Notably, the present study's method introduces a per-slice detection metric, which was not reported in previous studies, and uses a single model, making it computationally efficient and easy to train.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the feasibility of using deep learning for endoleak detection, offering a robust and efficient tool for clinical practice. Future work could focus on expanding the data set and integrating additional predictive capabilities, such as endoleak classification and localization.

title: In Vitro Development and Evaluation of an Endovascular Islet Cell Stent for Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe the in vitro development and benchtop evaluation of the IsletStent, an endovascular biological stent graft incorporating expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) semipermeable membranes, designed for portal venous delivery of pancreatic islets as a treatment for Type 1 diabetes mellitus.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prototypes with a 0.22-μm pore ePTFE membrane were seeded with murine (approximately 5,000-6,000 islet equivalents [IEQs]) or human (approximately 10,000 IEQs) islets. A benchtop normothermic perfusion circuit simulated intravascular deployment. Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion was assessed in a repeated-measures design (n = 4 devices per experiment); murine islet-seeded devices were perfused under zero (0 mM), low (2.8 mM), and high (28 mM) glucose, and human islet-seeded devices were perfused under low and high glucose only, with insulin quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Computational fluid dynamics modeling under idealized, nonphysiologic single-fluid conditions evaluated candidate device geometries.

RESULTS: Murine islet-seeded devices demonstrated glucose-responsive insulin secretion: 3-hour insulin concentrations were 83 μIU/mL (SD ± 8) versus 145 μIU/mL (SD ± 20) under low versus high glucose (P = .02), and secretion rates were 5,344 μIU/h (SD ± 144) versus 6,795 μIU/h (SD ± 503) (P = .008). Human islet-seeded devices responded concordantly, with 3-hour insulin concentrations of 229 μIU/mL (SD ± 13) versus 300 μIU/mL (SD ± 17) (P = .014).

CONCLUSIONS: In this benchtop perfusion model, islets housed within an ePTFE-based endovascular stent graft retained glucose-responsive insulin secretion. In vivo evaluation of islet viability, direct immunoisolation, hemodynamic impact, and long-term function is required before clinical translation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Prototypes with a 0.22-μm pore ePTFE membrane were seeded with murine (approximately 5,000-6,000 islet equivalents [IEQs]) or human (approximately 10,000 IEQs) islets. title: Cerebral Air Embolism After Navigational Bronchoscopy Treated With Aspiration Thrombectomy: A Case Report.
abstract: Systemic arterial air embolism is a rare but potentially devastating complication of bronchoscopic lung biopsy. A 68-year-old man with severe emphysema developed abrupt bradycardia, hypotension, and failure to regain consciousness after navigational bronchoscopy under general anaesthesia. Computed tomography demonstrated air within the left middle cerebral artery, and angiography confirmed proximal large-vessel occlusion. Urgent aspiration thrombectomy achieved complete reperfusion after one pass, with retrieved material compatible with thrombus. Despite technically successful reperfusion, major neurological deficits persisted. This case highlights haemodynamic collapse and delayed emergence as warning signs and supports rapid neuroimaging with selective endovascular treatment when an accessible large-vessel occlusion is present.

title: Recognizing Pelvic Venous Disease in Chronic Pelvic Pain: A Primary Care Case Report.
abstract: Chronic pelvic pain is a common and challenging condition with a broad differential diagnosis and a substantial impact on quality of life. Pelvic congestion syndrome (PCS) is a clinical manifestation of pelvic venous disease that may involve venous reflux, obstruction, collateralization, and dilation across different pelvic venous territories. Its non-specific clinical presentation and overlap with gynecological, gastrointestinal, and musculoskeletal disorders may lead to significant diagnostic delay. A 42-year-old woman presented to a general and family medicine consultation with a six-year history of chronic pelvic pain, progressively worsening over the previous six months. She described persistent pressure-like pelvic pain, rated 7/10 in intensity, aggravated by prolonged standing and associated with severe deep dyspareunia, which prevented sexual intercourse, associated with low back pain radiating to the pelvis and both thighs, lower-limb heaviness, and significant sleep disturbance. She denied urinary symptoms or a relationship with the menstrual cycle. During the previous six years, she had undergone repeated medical assessments, with symptoms being attributed to recurrent gynecological infections, probable irritable bowel syndrome, and other non-specific causes. Previous investigations, including colonoscopy and emergency department assessments, had not identified a clear etiology for her symptoms. Physical examination revealed hypogastric tenderness and mild superficial lower-limb varicosities, without vulvar or perineal varices. Pelvic and lumbar computed tomography (CT) demonstrated bilateral dilated periuterine veins measuring up to 13 mm, raising suspicion for a symptomatic pelvic venous disorder. The patient was referred to vascular surgery for further assessment; however, specialist evaluation remained pending at the time of manuscript revision. Pelvic venous disease should be considered in women with persistent pelvic pain, particularly when symptoms worsen with prolonged standing or sexual intercourse and are accompanied by low back pain or lower-limb heaviness. The absence of vulvar varices or previous inconclusive investigations does not exclude a possible pelvic venous etiology. This case illustrates how the non-specific presentation of pelvic venous disease may result in years of fragmented investigation and delayed recognition. Continuity of care in general and family medicine facilitated a longitudinal review of the patient's symptoms and previous investigations, allowing recognition of a pattern suggestive of pelvic venous disease. Greater awareness of pelvic venous disease in primary care may facilitate earlier consideration and appropriate specialist referral in women with otherwise unexplained chronic pelvic pain.

Its non-specific clinical presentation and overlap with gynecological, gastrointestinal, and musculoskeletal disorders may lead to significant diagnostic delay.

title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO.

METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment.

RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted P<0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]).

CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required.

title: Omega-6 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Peripheral Artery Disease: An Individual Participant-Level Analysis of 9 International Prospective Studies.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have previously been associated with several peripheral artery disease (PAD) risk factors. We studied the association between individual omega-6 PUFAs and incident PAD in a multicohort analysis.

METHODS: This study was conducted among participants from 9 cohorts (N=137 704; PAD cases=2014) in the FORCE (Fatty Acids and Outcomes Research Consortium) who were free of clinical PAD at baseline. Omega-6 PUFAs were measured at baseline and with a median follow-up of 14 years. Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were conducted in individual cohorts to evaluate associations of omega-6 PUFAs (continuous cohort-standardized interquintile ranges [difference between the medians of the 10th and 90th omega-6 PUFAs percentiles] and cohort-specific quintiles) with incident clinical PAD adjusting for prespecified covariates. Inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis was used to calculate the combined hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs.

RESULTS: Linoleic acid (LA) was measured in all 9 cohorts, arachidonic acid in 8 (N=33 541; PAD cases=1766), dihomo-γ-LA and γ-LA in 7 (N=29 861; PAD cases=1686), and eicosadienoic acid in 6 (N=27 538; PAD cases=1435). Only LA was associated with a lower risk of incident PAD (quintile 5 versus quintile 1: HR, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.64-0.89]; P=0.0009). Results did not differ in a statistically significant manner by age, sex, diabetes status, or smoking status.

CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that the omega-6 PUFA LA may be protective against PAD, and other omega-6 PUFAs are not associated with PAD incidence. This is further evidence that omega-6 PUFA-disease relationships should be evaluated by individual fatty acids rather than grouped as total omega-6 PUFAs.

We studied the association between individual omega-6 PUFAs and incident PAD in a multicohort analysis. title: Whole-Genome Sequencing and Single-Cell Transcriptomics Identify Human Leukocyte Antigen Loci and a COG5 Variant in Aortic Dissection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic dissection (AD) is a lethal cardiovascular emergency with a complex and underexplored genetic basis.

METHODS: We performed whole-genome sequencing on 151 patients with sporadic Stanford type B AD and 965 healthy controls in a Chinese population as a discovery phase analysis to assess both common and rare variants. Cross-ancestry meta-analyses incorporating 4 external genome-wide association data sets were used to identify population-specific risk loci. To pinpoint functional candidates, we integrated epigenomic profiles and single-cell transcriptomes from human aortic tissues.

RESULTS: Whole-genome sequencing analysis identified 21 candidate common loci and 2 low-frequency variants associated with AD in this discovery cohort. Two candidate common variants in the human leukocyte antigen region (rs9260945 near HLA-A and rs9276409 within HLA-DQA2) showed strong associations and colocalized with regulatory elements in aortic and immune cells, indicating immune-mediated vascular pathology. A low-frequency missense variant in the COG5 gene (rs1203229795, effect allele frequency=0.019) emerged as an independent AD risk factor, likely affecting extracellular matrix glycosylation. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of AD-associated variants in human aortic tissues demonstrated enhanced interactions among fibroblasts, vascular smooth muscle cells, and macrophages, supporting their roles in AD pathogenesis. Integrated gene-based and expression analyses further highlighted TPM4, a marker of vascular smooth muscle cell dedifferentiation, as a putative susceptibility gene in AD.

CONCLUSIONS: This multiomics investigation expands the genetic landscape of sporadic AD in Chinese individuals, revealing immune-related human leukocyte antigen loci and a functionally supported candidate COG5 variant. Our findings offer new insights into AD pathogenesis and identify candidate targets for future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

METHODS: We performed whole-genome sequencing on 151 patients with sporadic Stanford type B AD and 965 healthy controls in a Chinese population as a discovery phase analysis to assess both common and rare variants. Cross-ancestry meta-analyses incorporating 4 external genome-wide association data sets were used to identify population-specific risk loci.

title: Impact of Continuous Baseline and Discharge Blood Pressure on Outcomes After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence linking pre- and post-transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) blood pressure (BP) with cardiovascular outcomes is scarce. This study investigated the associations of pre- and post-TAVI BP and their changes as a continuous variable with cardiovascular outcomes.

METHODS: Patients undergoing TAVI at a tertiary university hospital between 2011 and 2025 with office BP available before and after TAVI were included. The primary outcome was a composite of major adverse cardiac events (MACE) at 1 year. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models incorporating restricted cubic splines for continuous variables were fitted.

RESULTS: Among 1191 patients, BP remained relatively stable from pre-TAVI to 1-year follow-up. Both discharge systolic BP and absolute changes therein from pre- to post-TAVI were significantly associated with MACE at 1 year (P<0.001 for both), whereas baseline systolic BP showed no significant association. BP values <115 mm Hg or >143 mm Hg were associated with a higher risk of MACE 1 year after TAVI. A decrease in systolic BP of -5 to -25 mm Hg was also associated with a lower risk of MACE compared with no change.

CONCLUSIONS: While BP remains generally stable in the year following TAVI, both very low and high systolic BP at discharge were associated with higher 1-year MACE. Furthermore, moderate decreases in systolic BP from baseline to discharge appear to be protective. These findings highlight the potential prognostic value of BP optimization during TAVI follow-up and support the role of BP measurements as a clinically translatable, independently associated with long-term outcomes after TAVI.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Evidence linking pre- and post-transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) blood pressure (BP) with cardiovascular outcomes is scarce. This study investigated the associations of pre- and post-TAVI BP and their changes as a continuous variable with cardiovascular outcomes. METHODS: Patients undergoing TAVI at a tertiary university hospital between 2011 and 2025 with office BP available before and after TAVI were included.

title: Limb Salvage Outcomes Following Endovascular Revascularization for Peripheral Artery Disease in a Southern Indian Population: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background Peripheral artery disease (PAD), particularly chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), is associated with a high risk of limb loss and significant morbidity. Endovascular therapy (ET) has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to surgical revascularization, especially in high-risk patients and those with comorbidities. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of ET in achieving limb salvage in a Southern Indian population. Materials and methods This retrospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary vascular care center and included 142 patients with symptomatic PAD who underwent endovascular intervention between July 2023 and June 2025. Clinical severity and lesion complexity were assessed using the Rutherford classification and the TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus II (TASC II) classification, respectively. The primary endpoint was limb salvage at one year, defined as freedom from major amputation. Secondary endpoints included technical success, restenosis, and procedure-related complications. Results The study population was predominantly male (87.3%) with a mean age of 61.11 ± 12.90 years. Most patients (78.1%) presented with CLTI. Technical success was achieved in 87.3% of procedures. At one-year follow-up, limb salvage was achieved in 95.8% of patients, with major amputation occurring in 4.2% and minor amputation in 9.1%. Restenosis was observed in 14.7% of cases. Procedure-related complications were infrequent and mostly minor, with one all-cause death during follow-up. Conclusions ET is a safe and effective modality for limb salvage in PAD patients, particularly in populations with a high prevalence of diabetes and advanced disease at presentation. High limb salvage rates can be achieved even in cohorts predominantly comprising patients with CLTI, supporting an endovascular-first approach in appropriately selected patients.
englishSummary: Background Peripheral artery disease (PAD), particularly chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), is associated with a high risk of limb loss and significant morbidity. Endovascular therapy (ET) has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to surgical revascularization, especially in high-risk patients and those with comorbidities. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of ET in achieving limb salvage in a Southern Indian population.

title: Outcomes among patients with single-vessel tibial runoff undergoing revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia, and the role of peroneal communicating branch quality.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Data evaluating outcomes among patients with single-vessel tibial runoff are limited. Our aim was to compare outcomes across patients with sole anterior tibial (AT), peroneal, or posterior tibial (PT) runoff following revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and to evaluate whether the quality of peroneal communicating branches (PCBs) affects outcome risk within the peroneal runoff population.

METHODS: All patients undergoing first-time revascularization for CLTI were retrospectively reviewed (2005-2022) and stratified by sole runoff vessel (AT, peroneal, and PT). Primary outcomes were wound healing, major amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and amputation/death, assessed by Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. A subset analysis stratified single-vessel peroneal runoff patients into a three-tiered, PCB grade: Both branches present with at least one robust (PCB grade 1), a single robust branch (PCB grade 2), or no robust branch (PCB grade 3), and compared each with the single-vessel AT/PT reference group.

RESULTS: Overall, 732 patients had single-vessel below-knee runoff: 225 AT, 315 peroneal, and 192 PT. Groups differed significantly in age, sex, and diabetes prevalence. Unadjusted 2-year major amputation rates were significantly higher in the peroneal group [19% vs 9.4% (AT) vs 8.7% (PT); P < .001], as were MALE rates (30% vs 14% vs 26%; P = .01). After adjustment, peroneal runoff was independently associated with higher risk of major amputation [hazard ratio (HR), 1.81; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.04-3.13] and MALE (HR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.03-2.25) compared with AT/PT runoff. These associations persisted in the endovascular cohort (major amputation: HR, 2.09; 95% CI, 1.06-4.13; MALE: HR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.08-2.35) but did not reach significance in the bypass cohort, which was limited by low-event rates. When patients with single-vessel peroneal runoff were stratified by PCB grades, unadjusted 1-year major amputation rates followed a clear anatomically-driven pattern [6.9% (AT/PT) vs 5.4% (PCB grade 1) vs 15% (PCB grade 2) vs 32% (PCB grade 3); P < .001]. After adjustment, when compared with AT/PT runoff, patients without any robust branch (PCB grade 3) had significantly higher risk of major amputation (HR, 3.21; 95% CI, 1.76-4.84) and MALE (HR, 2.41; 95% CI, 1.53-3.79), whereas those with two communicating branches with at least one being robust (PCB grade 1) demonstrated higher rates of complete wound healing (HR, 1.69; 95% CI, 1.09-2.62) and no difference in major amputation or MALE.

CONCLUSIONS: Peroneal runoff is independently associated with worse limb outcomes following revascularization for CLTI, but this risk may be primarily driven by patients with absent or diminutive communicating branches. Patients with robust branching demonstrate outcomes comparable with AT/PT runoff, underscoring the importance of further evaluation and preoperative assessment of PCB quality - using the proposed PCB grading system - in revascularization planning.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Data evaluating outcomes among patients with single-vessel tibial runoff are limited. Our aim was to compare outcomes across patients with sole anterior tibial (AT), peroneal, or posterior tibial (PT) runoff following revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and to evaluate whether the quality of peroneal communicating branches (PCBs) affects outcome risk within the peroneal runoff population. METHODS: All patients undergoing first-time revascularization for CLTI were retrospectively reviewed (2005-2022) and stratified by sole runoff vessel (AT, peroneal, and PT).

title: Optimal Catheter Size for Medium Vessel Occlusion in Aspiration Thrombectomy.
abstract: The efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy for medium vessel occlusion remains controversial, and optimal recanalization strategies are lacking. We investigated factors associated with successful recanalization using aspiration thrombectomy in patients with medium vessel occlusion. We conducted a retrospective study on patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent aspiration thrombectomy for M2 occlusion between July 2021 and November 2025. We examined the factors associated with successful recanalization by focusing on the ratio of the catheter outer diameter to the target vessel inner diameter (Catheter-to-vessel ratio). Overall, 64 patients were included. First-pass successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction ≥ 2c) was achieved in 24 patients. In patients with successful recanalization, the ratio of the catheter outer diameter to the target vessel inner diameter (Catheter-to-vessel ratio) was significantly higher than in those without successful recanalization (p = 0.029). In multivariate analysis, the Catheter-to-vessel ratio was independently associated with successful recanalization after adjustment for catheter position and thrombus size (odds ratio per 0.1 increase, 3.688; 95% confidence interval, 1.478-9.202; p = 0.0007). In the receiver operating characteristic analysis, the threshold for the Catheter-to-vessel ratio distinguishing successful recanalization was 0.70, with a sensitivity of 79% and a specificity of 63%.In aspiration thrombectomy for medium vessel occlusion, a Catheter-to-vessel ratio ≥ 0.70 may be an exploratory indicator associated with first-pass successful reperfusion.
englishSummary: The efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy for medium vessel occlusion remains controversial, and optimal recanalization strategies are lacking. We investigated factors associated with successful recanalization using aspiration thrombectomy in patients with medium vessel occlusion. We conducted a retrospective study on patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent aspiration thrombectomy for M2 occlusion between July 2021 and November 2025.

title: Prospective Evaluation of Standalone Endovascular Embolization for Growing Meningiomas: A Multicenter Study Protocol.
abstract: Endovascular embolization for meningiomas has traditionally been performed as a preoperative adjunct; however, embolization alone can induce tumor necrosis and volume reduction. This study aims to prospectively evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization in patients with growing meningiomas. This multicenter, prospective, single-arm study will include patients diagnosed with meningioma using imaging findings that showed interval growth. The primary end point is tumor growth control at 180 days after treatment, defined as a stable or reduced tumor volume based on quantitative volumetric assessment of the contrast-enhancing portion on magnetic resonance imaging. The secondary end points include the tumor volume change rate, embolized vessels, embolic materials, embolization results and characteristics, procedure-related complications, perioperative complications, functional outcomes (Karnofsky Performance Status and modified Rankin Scale), changes in clinical symptoms, and the need for additional treatment. Exploratory analyses will also assess the association between intratumoral penetration of embolic material and treatment outcomes. Patient recruitment is ongoing, and the results will be reported upon completion of the study. This study represents a prospective attempt to evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization for meningiomas. If safe tumor growth control can be achieved, this study may provide preliminary evidence supporting standalone embolization as a potential less-invasive treatment strategy.

This study aims to prospectively evaluate the efficacy and safety of standalone embolization in patients with growing meningiomas. title: Impact of prior antithrombotic therapy on safety and outcomes of endovascular therapy in large-core acute ischemic stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Evidence on whether prior antithrombotic drug (ATD) use affects outcomes after endovascular therapy (EVT) is limited in patients with large-core acute ischemic stroke.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a subanalysis of the Recovery by Endovascular Salvage for Cerebral Ultra-acute Embolism-Japan Large Ischemic Core Trial, which assessed the efficacy of EVT in patients with large-vessel occlusion and extensive early ischemic changes. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-3 at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) within 48 hours, symptomatic ICH, 90-day mortality, ordinal mRS shift, and ≥8-point improvement in National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score at 48 hours. Logistic regression models were used to assess treatment effects and interactions between ATD and EVT.

RESULTS: A total of 202 patients were included (ATD, n = 70; no ATD, n = 132). There was no significant interaction between use of ATD and the effect of EVT in terms of the primary outcome (pinteraction=0.944) or secondary outcomes (pinteraction=0.218-0.752). In the EVT cohort, prior ATD use was not associated with the primary outcome (adjusted OR 1.16, 95% CI 0.41-3.23). Results were consistent for antiplatelet drugs (adjusted OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.18-2.71) and anticoagulants (adjusted OR 1.52, 95% CI 0.45-5.20).

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory subanalysis, prior ATD use did not significantly modify the observed treatment effect of EVT in patients with large-core acute ischemic stroke. These findings suggest that prior ATD use alone should not preclude consideration of EVT.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a subanalysis of the Recovery by Endovascular Salvage for Cerebral Ultra-acute Embolism-Japan Large Ischemic Core Trial, which assessed the efficacy of EVT in patients with large-vessel occlusion and extensive early ischemic changes. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-3 at 90 days.

title: Achieving an endovascular therapy door-to-device time under 90 minutes in patients with ischemic stroke was associated with 90-day mRS.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The American Heart Association (AHA) has a current goal of performing 50% of endovascular therapy (EVT) procedures with a door-to-device (DTD) time of 90 minutes or less for direct arriving patients. Initiatives to improve DTD times need evidence of patient benefit to justify long-term adoption.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective study of patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy for ischemic stroke. The likelihood of a favorable patient outcome was quantified for patients with a DTD time ≤90 minutes compared to patients with a DTD time >90 minutes.

RESULTS: DTD ≤90 minutes was associated with an increased odds of having a more favorable (0-2) modified Rankin Score at 90-days (AOR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.15-2.00; P = .004) post stroke compared to DTD >90 minutes. We did not find that DTD under or over 90 minutes had a significant association with discharge home (AOR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.00-1.46; P = .051) or patients' length of stay (β, -0.48; 95% CI, -1.30-0.34; P = .20).

CONCLUSIONS: Our study supports that EVT completed with DTD time ≤90 minutes was associated with better functional outcomes for patients.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective study of patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy for ischemic stroke.
