title: Global Disparity Within the Management of Traumatic Abdominal Vascular Injuries: Analysis of a Global Dataset.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular injuries are common to trauma and carry a high risk to limb and life. Integrating specialist vascular care into existing trauma systems is essential; however, global data on this topic remains limited. This study describes global patterns of abdominal vascular trauma, through secondary analysis of the Global Outcomes After Laparotomy for Trauma (GOAL-Trauma) study dataset, examining system- and patient-level differences across resource settings.

METHODS: Patients of any age with blunt or penetrating trauma who underwent an abdominal vascular procedure during trauma laparotomy were included. Patient characteristics, injury patterns, peri-operative factors, and outcomes were recorded. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics and differences across Human Development Index (HDI) tertiles were analyzed with the Kruskal-Wallis or χ2 tests, where appropriate.

RESULTS: A total of 178 patients from 82 hospitals across 33 countries were included, representing one in 10 patients (178 of 1769) of the original dataset. A higher proportion of patients had vascular procedures in the upper HDI tertile (64 of 492, 13.0%), compared to middle (82 of 714, 11.5%) and lower (32 of 563, 5.7%) HDI tertiles. The median time from injury to operation was 5.0 hours (IQR 2.0-9.0). Among patients who were hypotensive on presentation, time from arrival to operation was significantly longer in the lower HDI tertile (p = 0.033). The most common regions of vascular injury were the inferior vena cava (37 patients, 20.8%) and iliac vein (30 patients, 16.9%). Thirty day post-operative mortality was 17.4% (31 of 178 patients), with only around half of the patients (94 of 178, 52.8%) discharged to their usual place of residence.

CONCLUSIONS: As trauma systems become integrated into national healthcare services, prioritizing vascular care is crucial. There remains considerable variation in the provision of vascular services in trauma globally, yet given the time-critical nature of vascular injuries, it is essential to ensure effective, integrated care pathways.

Integrating specialist vascular care into existing trauma systems is essential; however, global data on this topic remains limited. This study describes global patterns of abdominal vascular trauma, through secondary analysis of the Global Outcomes After Laparotomy for Trauma (GOAL-Trauma) study dataset, examining system- and patient-level differences across resource settings.

title: A comparison of aspiration thrombectomy with catheter-directed thrombolysis in the management of Paget-Schroetter syndrome.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute subclavian vein thrombosis secondary to thoracic outlet syndrome (Paget-Schroetter syndrome [PSS]) requires the prompt clearing of thrombus from the subclavian vein through catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) or aspiration thrombectomy (ASP). Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS.

METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP. Venograms were assessed for patency, stenosis, and subclavian post-thrombotic changes (PTC). PTC were graded based on the degree of luminal encroachment and vessel irregularity: mild (<10%), moderate (10%-50%), and severe (50%-99%). Interventions were assessed: (1) within 1 week of the procedure, (2) before subclavian vein decompression, (3) 2 weeks after subclavian vein decompression, and (4) patency on the last venogram. Standardized outcomes were assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 110 patients with PSS were treated over 5 years. Of these patients, 54 met the inclusion criteria: 28 underwent CDT and 26 underwent ASP. At 1 week following the procedure, rethrombosis occurred in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 6 (23.1%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .5). Failure to clear thrombosis occurred in 13.8% of patients who underwent ASP. The composite rate of early thrombosis and procedural failure was higher in the ASP cohort. Before PSS surgery, occlusion was noted in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 8 (30.8%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .05). PTC was mild in 13 (46.4%) patients receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP (P < .05); moderate in 5 (17.9%) receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (32.1%) receiving CDT and 8 (30.8) receiving ASP. At early follow-up after PSS surgery, PTC was mild in 10 (43.5%) patients receiving CDT and 4 (23.5) receiving ASP; moderate in 2 (8.7%) receiving CDT and 1 (5.9%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (39.1%) receiving CDT and 6 (35.3%) receiving ASP. Occlusion was noted in 2 (8.7%) patients receiving CDT and 6 (35%) receiving ASP. Recanalization resulted in final patency in 22 (95%) patients receiving CDT and 15 (88%) receiving ASP.

CONCLUSIONS: Both ASP and CDT may be employed for clearing thrombus in PSS; however, they differ in early efficacy, PTC, and patency. Our results suggest that while often more rapid and convenient, ASP may be inferior to CAT in the management of PSS.

Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS. METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP.

title: Faculty narrative feedback in the vascular surgery entrustable professional activity pilot is disproportionately focused on patient care and medical knowledge competencies.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Performance feedback is critical to guide vascular surgery trainees' skill development across competency domains. Workplace-based assessment of entrustable professional activity (EPA) allows faculty frequent opportunities to provide and document clinical performance feedback. Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) Milestones were previously mapped to each EPA and accompanying behavioral anchors reflect the range of competencies required to execute each clinical activity. It is unclear how faculty use this information to guide and focus the content of their feedback. We sought to identify the core competencies reflected in narrative feedback in a multi-institutional study of EPA assessments.

METHODS: EPA assessments were collected during a 3-month national Vascular Surgery EPA Pilot in 2024. Trainees were rated on their performance of EPAs on a 4-point Likert scale and faculty had the opportunity to provide feedback. Narrative feedback was qualitatively analyzed using focused coding guided by the Vascular Surgery Milestones 2.0 framework. Feedback was coded using the six ACGME core competencies-patient care (PC), medical knowledge (MK), professionalism, interpersonal and communication skills, practice-based learning and improvement, and systems-based practice (SBP)-to characterize the domains emphasized in feedback. Quality assessment scores were assigned to all narrative feedback using the Quality of Assessment of Learning framework. Descriptive analysis was completed using R.

RESULTS: Faculty completed 983 EPA assessments of 78 trainees across 17 institutions (n = 16 integrated residencies, n = 12 fellowships). Narrative feedback was included in 760 (77%) assessments. Feedback most frequently addressed PC (n = 662, 82%), followed by MK (n = 418, 55%), whereas feedback about practice-based learning and improvement (n = 42, 6%), interpersonal and communication skills (n = 42,6%), professionalism (n = 20, 3%), and SBP (n = 26, 3%) were less common. Most assessments were completed for postgraduate year-3 (29%) and postgraduate year-4 trainees (22%). Most assessments occurred during the intraoperative phase of care (88%), with relatively few occurring in preoperative (7%) or postoperative (5%) phases. In addition, feedback-referencing PC was associated with higher odds of high-quality feedback in comparison with feedback about the other competencies (odds ratio, 25.56; 95% confidence interval, 6.13-106.55).

CONCLUSIONS: In this multi-institutional study of vascular surgery EPA assessments, faculty most frequently provided trainees with feedback on their performance of PC and MK competencies. Feedback on performance related to SBP was infrequently provided and, when provided, was of generally low quality. This has important implications for the use of EPAs to inform ACGME Milestones ratings and suggests alternative assessment tools will continue to be needed to capture performance across all competency domains required of a physician.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Performance feedback is critical to guide vascular surgery trainees' skill development across competency domains. Workplace-based assessment of entrustable professional activity (EPA) allows faculty frequent opportunities to provide and document clinical performance feedback. Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) Milestones were previously mapped to each EPA and accompanying behavioral anchors reflect the range of competencies required to execute each clinical activity.

title: Emerging precision techniques in technology-assisted customized endovascular management of thoracoabdominal aneurysms with anomalous arch branching.
abstract: Thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) repair is highly complex, especially in the presence of rare aortic arch branching anomalies that complicate fenestrated graft deployment. Emerging technologies such as robotic-assisted vascular surgery with haptic feedback and advanced imaging aim to improve precision and reduce technical errors in these challenging cases. Patient-specific 3D-printed vascular models further enhance preoperative planning and intraoperative navigation by improving anatomical understanding in complex arch variants. Spinal cord ischemia remains a major complication after TAAA repair, and reduced operative time through minimally invasive and robotic-assisted approaches may potentially lower this risk, although evidence is still limited. While these innovations show promise in improving surgical accuracy and efficiency, robust multicenter studies are needed to validate their effectiveness and define their role in standard clinical practice.

title: The Central Coupler of ClpXP Controls Intersubunit Communication and Couples Intrasubunit Chemical Energy with Force Generation.
abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

title: Machine Learning-Based Risk Prediction Models for Peripheral Artery Disease: A Nationally Representative Analysis of NHANES 1999-2004.
abstract: BackgroundWe evaluated the association between small dense low-density lipoprotein (sdLDL) and peripheral artery disease (PAD) and developed prediction models using NHANES 1999-2004.MethodsThis weighted cross-sectional study included 3,415 participants (3,227 without PAD and 188 with PAD). PAD was defined by ankle-brachial index (ABI) <0.90; participants with ABI ≥1.40 or missing ABI were excluded. Survey-weighted logistic regression assessed the association between sdLDL and PAD. For machine learning, complete-case data (n=2,828) were split into training (70%) and test (30%) sets before feature selection and preprocessing. Correlation screening, LASSO, encoding, standardization, and SMOTE were restricted to the training set. Nine algorithms were evaluated using discrimination and calibration metrics.ResultssdLDL was not independently associated with PAD in the fully adjusted model (OR=1.01, 95% CI 0.94-1.10, P=0.69). LASSO retained eight predictor domains: age, body mass index, C-reactive protein, education, estimated glomerular filtration rate, hypertension, poverty-income ratio, and smoking. In the test set, gradient boosting machine achieved the highest AUC (0.833, 95% CI 0.777-0.889), followed by logistic regression (0.819) and XGBoost (0.811). SHAP analysis highlighted age, eGFR, and smoking-related variables as important contributors.Conclusions: sdLDL was not independently associated with PAD. Several models showed acceptable discrimination, with GBM performing numerically best and logistic regression remaining competitive. External validation in contemporary cohorts is required.

PAD was defined by ankle-brachial index (ABI) <0.90; participants with ABI ≥1.40 or missing ABI were excluded. Survey-weighted logistic regression assessed the association between sdLDL and PAD.

title: From flossing to fracturing-Subintimal lithotripsy for recoil stenosis modification before interwoven stent implantation.
abstract: A 67-year-old man with chronic limb-threatening ischemia and a highly calcified superficial femoral artery chronic total occlusion underwent subintimal recanalization using the subintimal arterial flossing with antegrade-retrograde intervention (SAFARI) approach after failed antegrade crossing. Predilation caused severe recoil from eccentric calcification. Intravascular lithotripsy (300 pulses at 4 atm) was delivered within the subintimal plane, followed by ultra-high-pressure balloon angioplasty and implantation of an interwoven nitinol stent, achieving <30% residual stenosis. At 3 months, duplex ultrasound imaging confirmed stent patency without fracture, and the wound had healed. This case adds to the limited experience with subintimal intravascular lithotripsy as a vessel-preparation strategy for calcified recoil lesions.

title: Impact of intravascular ultrasound guidance on radiation exposure during endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair: Single-center experience.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the effect of using intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) in endovascular aortic aneurysms repair (EVAR) on reduction of radiation exposure.

METHODS: All EVAR procedures performed for symptomatic and asymptomatic infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms at a single U.K. center between January 2024 and December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were divided into two groups based on imaging guidance used: IVUS-guided EVAR and standard EVAR. The primary end points were radiation dose and fluoroscopy time (FT), whereas the secondary outcomes included intraoperative technical success, change in pre- and postoperative serum creatinine level length of hospital stay, and 30-day morbidity and mortality.

RESULTS: During the study period, 51 patients met inclusion criteria at our center, 30 patients (58.8%) had standard EVAR procedure with fluoroscopy-guidance, whereas 21 patients (41.2%) had IVUS-guided EVAR procedure. Median dose area product in standard EVAR cases was 45.24 Gy cm2 compared with 7.27 Gy cm2 in IVUS-guided EVAR cases (P <.001, highly significant), and median FT in standard EVAR cases was 15.4 minutes compared with 4.5 minutes in IVUS-guided EVAR cases (P <.001, highly significant). Intraoperative technical success achieved in 19 patients (90%) in IVUS-guided cases compared with 28 patients (93%) in standard EVAR cases. The mean postoperative creatinine level was 71.4 ± 16.7 μmol/L in patients who underwent IVUS-guided EVAR cases, compared with 86.0 ± 22.0 μmol/L in patients with standard EVAR.

CONCLUSIONS: IVUS provides accurate and safe graft deployment while reducing the total radiation dose and FT. This significantly reduces the radiation risks to patients and staff while maintaining the highest patient care and procedure safety.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To assess the effect of using intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) in endovascular aortic aneurysms repair (EVAR) on reduction of radiation exposure. METHODS: All EVAR procedures performed for symptomatic and asymptomatic infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms at a single U.K. center between January 2024 and December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed.

title: A Multicenter Case Review Program on the impact of ViTAA Regional Aortic Weakness Maps on clinical decision-making in abdominal aortic aneurysm management.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study, titled the ViTAA Case Review Program, aimed at evaluating the influence of the ViTAA Regional Aortic Weakness (RAW) Maps software on clinical decision-making in the management of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA). The purpose was twofold: first, to determine the impact of RAW Maps on projected patient care decisions compared with the standard of care approach, and second, to train investigators in the effective use of ViTAA RAW Maps for AAA assessment. This paper offers a case series focusing on the experience of participating surgeons in using the ViTAA RAW Maps software.

METHODS: Fifteen North American vascular surgeons participated and were provided with fully anonymized static and multiphase gated computed tomography angiography (CTA) scans obtained from a previous retrospective study. Five cases were selected from a single site and for each, participating physicians developed hypothetical treatment plans based on two imaging approaches: static CTA scans and multiphase gated CTA scans processed with the ViTAA RAW Maps software. These treatment plans were then compared to determine the impact of the ViTAA approach on clinical decision-making.

RESULTS: The ViTAA approach supported significantly higher surgical intervention rates compared with the standard of care, with vascular surgeons being 69% (P < .05) and 88% (P < .01) more likely to recommend surgery (either endovascular or open repair) at baseline and follow-up, respectively. The proportion of cases in which the recommendation changed when the ViTAA analysis was provided was 18.9% at baseline (95% confidence interval, 10.0-35.8) and 28.0% at follow-up (95% confidence interval, 19.1-41.0). ViTAA also prompted more endovascular aneurysm repair (72% more at baseline and 57% more at follow-up; P = .065 and P = .057, respectively), as well as increased fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (6.8% vs 2.7% at baseline and 11% vs 7% at follow-up; not statistically significant, P = .25 and P = .38, respectively). Across the 10 questionnaire items, 73% to 100% of participating physicians responded favorably to questions regarding the functionality and utility of the software.

CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that ViTAA technology may provide additional information for AAA risk stratification by incorporating functional image-derived biomechanical and hemodynamic metrics that offer deeper insight into aortic wall vulnerability. The participating physicians found these additional insights clinically meaningful, with the potential to influence management decisions for the reviewed cases. The usability of the software also suggests feasible integration into future workflows.

The purpose was twofold: first, to determine the impact of RAW Maps on projected patient care decisions compared with the standard of care approach, and second, to train investigators in the effective use of ViTAA RAW Maps for AAA assessment. This paper offers a case series focusing on the experience of participating surgeons in using the ViTAA RAW Maps software.

title: Long-Term Safety and Efficacy of Upadacitinib in Patients with Psoriatic Arthritis: 5-Year Results from the Phase 3 SELECT-PsA 1 Study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In the phase 3 SELECT-PsA 1 study, treatment with upadacitinib (UPA), an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor, improved signs and symptoms of psoriatic arthritis (PsA) from weeks 12 through 152. We now report the long-term extension phase, evaluating safety and efficacy of upadacitinib versus adalimumab (ADA) up to week 260 (~ 5 years).

METHODS: Data on treatment-emergent adverse events and all primary and secondary endpoints were collected through week 260 for patients who received a placebo or ≥ 1 dose of UPA at either 15 mg (UPA15) or 30 mg (UPA30) daily, or ADA 40 mg every other week. For non-radiographic binary endpoints, both observed data and non-responder imputation methods were used, whereas for radiographic binary endpoints, the observed data method was used. For continuous endpoints, observed data and mixed-effects model repeated-measures analyses were employed.

RESULTS: A total of 1704 patients received at least one dose of study drug, with 983 (57.7%) completing 260 weeks of treatment. The safety profile of UPA through week 260 was consistent with data from weeks 104 and 152. UPA treatment was associated with higher rates of serious infections, herpes zoster, lymphopenia, creatine kinase elevation, and non-melanoma skin cancer compared with ADA treatment. The exposure-adjusted incidence rates for major adverse cardiovascular events (n/100 PY [95% CI]: UPA15, 0.4 [0.2, 0.8]; UPA30, 0.4 [0.1, 0.9]; ADA, 0.3 [0.1, 0.7]) and venous thromboembolism (UPA15, 0.2 [0.0, 0.5]; UPA30, 0.4 [0.1, 0.9]; ADA, 0.2 [0.0, 0.6]) were low and comparable across treatment groups. Efficacy improvements observed with UPA at weeks 56 and 104 were maintained through week 260 and were comparable to those achieved with ADA.

CONCLUSIONS: The safety profile of UPA over 5 years remained consistent with that observed at weeks 104 and 152, with no new signals identified.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier, NCT03104400.

title: Endovascular magnetic filters for removing excess chemotherapeutic drugs from blood flow using dimensionless scaling laws.
abstract: Intra-arterial chemotherapy (IAC) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by the escape of chemotherapeutic agents into systemic circulation, causing severe side effects such as heart failure. This study aims to develop and optimize endovascular magnetic filtration devices to enhance IAC efficacy, by targeted removal of excess drug-coated ultrasmall superparamagnetic iron oxide (USPIO) particles from circulation. Device performance was evaluated through multi-physics simulations that coupled the transport of drug-coated magnetic particles in blood flow with magnetic interactions and magnetophoretic forces. A dimensional analysis framework was applied to characterize particle capture efficiency ( CE ) across alternative device designs, and numerical predictions were compared with published benchtop experiments. Optimized multi-stage filters achieved up to ~80% predicted capture efficiency, while reducing the risk of intravascular device collapse. These results demonstrate a novel strategy for reducing systemic toxicity in IAC through endovascular magnetic filtration, indicating its potential to improve the safety and effectiveness of HCC treatment.

title: Staged Endovascular Management of May-Thurner Syndrome Caused by a Mycotic Right Common Iliac Artery Aneurysm: A Case Report.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: May-Thurner syndrome (MTS) usually results from compression of the left common iliac vein (LCIV) between the right common iliac artery (RCIA) and vertebral body. Aneurysmal arterial causes are rare, and a mycotic RCIA aneurysm is exceptional. This case report presents staged endovascular exclusion of a rapidly enlarging mycotic RCIA aneurysm followed by recanalisation and stenting of a chronically occluded LCIV.

REPORT: A 57 year old man with disseminated methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection, lumbar spinal fusion hardware infection, and an inferior vena cava (IVC) filter placed for acute left lower limb deep vein thrombosis was found, during attempted filter retrieval, to have an uncannulatable left iliac venous system. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated a saccular RCIA aneurysm enlarging to approximately 4.5 cm over six months, compressing and occluding the LCIV with extensive pelvic collaterals. The aneurysm was excluded with overlapping covered stent grafts after internal iliac artery coil embolisation. One month later, the LCIV was recanalised and reconstructed with venoplasty and a dedicated venous stent, and the IVC filter was retrieved. The arterial endograft and venous stent remained patent throughout follow up; the excluded aneurysm progressively shrank and had completely resolved on imaging at approximately 31 months, with improved leg swelling.

CONCLUSION: A mycotic RCIA aneurysm is a rare cause of MTS. In a patient at high surgical risk with hardware infection, a staged endovascular approach, arterial aneurysm exclusion followed by interval venous reconstruction, achieved durable aneurysm exclusion, restored venous outflow, and permitted IVC filter retrieval, offering a minimally invasive alternative to open repair. The durability of implanting a vascular device within an infected field remains uncertain and mandates prolonged antimicrobial therapy and close surveillance.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: May-Thurner syndrome (MTS) usually results from compression of the left common iliac vein (LCIV) between the right common iliac artery (RCIA) and vertebral body. Aneurysmal arterial causes are rare, and a mycotic RCIA aneurysm is exceptional. This case report presents staged endovascular exclusion of a rapidly enlarging mycotic RCIA aneurysm followed by recanalisation and stenting of a chronically occluded LCIV.

title: Endovascular hemorrhage control as a bridge to definitive open repair of a tracheoinnominate fistula.
abstract: A tracheoinnominate fistula (TIF) is an uncommon but lethal complication of tracheostomy that requires rapid intervention to prevent exsanguination. Here, we report the management of a tracheoinnominate fistula using bronchial blockade and endovascular tools to protect the airway, stop bleeding, and stabilize the patient. Twelve days later, repair was performed through a sternotomy with debridement of the injured innominate and reconstruction of the right carotid and subclavian arteries using a rifampin-soaked Dacron graft from the ascending aorta. The tracheal injury was repaired and soft tissue coverage achieved with a thymic flap. The patient recovered without complications and is in good general condition 2 years after the event.

title: Primary Aortic Wall Myxoma Presenting With Recurrent Systemic Embolization: A Hybrid Surgical Management Strategy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary aortic wall myxoma is exceptionally rare and may mimic mural thrombus or acute aortic dissection.

CASE SUMMARY: A 38-year-old man presented after approximately 12 hours of acute left lower-limb ischemia with concomitant left upper-limb occlusion. Computed tomography angiography showed filling defects in the ascending and descending thoracic aorta. Recurrent embolization after peripheral thromboembolectomy prompted emergency ascending aortic exploration. A friable intramural myxoma was excised with ascending aortic graft replacement; the descending lesion was excluded by staged thoracic endovascular aortic repair while therapeutic anticoagulation was maintained.

DISCUSSION: Histopathology confirmed an aortic wall myxoma. The case illustrates the limitations of imaging and an individualized hybrid strategy for suspected multifocal aortic involvement.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Recurrent embolization after embolectomy should prompt urgent proximal-source control. Hybrid repair may be considered when anatomy and clinical urgency support it.

CASE SUMMARY: A 38-year-old man presented after approximately 12 hours of acute left lower-limb ischemia with concomitant left upper-limb occlusion. Computed tomography angiography showed filling defects in the ascending and descending thoracic aorta.

title: Perioperative management of DOAC in elective orthopedic surgery: a prospective cohort analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Treatment with direct oral anticoagulants is usually interrupted prior to surgery to reduce bleeding risk. Current guidelines recommend standardized interruption protocols, but the actual preoperative plasma levels and their clinical implications in real-world surgical populations are not well characterized. The aim of this study was to assess preoperative DOAC plasma concentrations and postoperative bleeding and thromboembolic outcomes in patients undergoing elective orthopedic surgery.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational study at Danderyd Hospital, Stockholm, Sweden. Adults (≥ 18 years) treated with apixaban, rivaroxaban, or dabigatran for atrial fibrillation or venous thromboembolism and scheduled for high-bleeding-risk orthopedic procedures were included. DOAC interruption followed national guidelines. Plasma DOAC levels were measured preoperatively using LC-MS/MS. Clinical outcomes, including bleeding and thromboembolic events, were recorded up to 30 days postoperatively.

RESULTS: A total of 54 patients receiving ongoing DOAC therapy (mean age, 75.5 years; 54% male) were included, of whom 87% were on apixaban. Plasma DOAC concentrations had a mean of 6.7 ng/mL (range, <1.9 to 23.1 ng/mL), and 38% of patients had levels below the limit of detection (< 2.0 ng/mL). One patient had a concentration >30 ng/mL. Five patients (16%) experienced clinically relevant non-major bleeding; four of these had undetectable DOAC levels. No major bleeding, thromboembolic events, or deaths were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Standardized interruption protocols for DOAC therapy result in low or undetectable plasma levels in most patients undergoing high-risk elective orthopedic surgery. Routine preoperative DOAC level testing appears unnecessary in the general population but may be valuable in subgroups at high risk of bleeding.

Current guidelines recommend standardized interruption protocols, but the actual preoperative plasma levels and their clinical implications in real-world surgical populations are not well characterized. The aim of this study was to assess preoperative DOAC plasma concentrations and postoperative bleeding and thromboembolic outcomes in patients undergoing elective orthopedic surgery.

title: Morphological, clinical, and procedural determinants of embolization outcomes in non-cavernous cerebral dural arteriovenous fistulas: A retrospective study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this retrospective study was to determine whether dAVF (dural arteriovenous fistula) characteristics influences treatment indication, embolization techniques, complications, radiation burden, and outcome.

METHODS AND MATERIALS: Patients treated by embolization for a brain dAVF were included. Excluded were cavernous sinus and surgically treated dAVF. Patients' demographics, clinical and treatment data were retrieved. dAVF clusters were formed: haemorrhagic versus non-haemorrhagic onset and sinus versus non-sinus type and impact on treatment indication, complications, radiation burden, functional and angiographic outcome was analyzed.

RESULTS: In a study involving 119 dAVF in 115 patients, 33 patients (mean age 62 years ± 1.8, 72.7% males) presented with a haemorrhagic onset, while 82 (mean age 58 years ± 1.6, 57.3% females) exhibiting 86 dAVF had no bleeding. The sigmoid sinus was over-represented in the latter (52.3%), whereas a cerebrocortical occipital vein was frequently involved in the former group (27,3%). All but one haemorrhagic dAVF demonstrated a Borden-III classification. At six months, the prevalence of mRS class "0" was significantly higher in the non-haemorrhagic dAVF group (70.7% versus 32.3%) compared to the sinus-type clusters, where no such difference was observed. Six months angiography revealed occlusion in 88.2% of 102 catheterized fistulae, similar for all groups. Onyx volume and injection time was significantly higher in non-haemorrhagic and sinus-type dAVF. In non-haemorrhagic dAVF, fluoroscopy time (66.16 versus 40.48 minutes) and the number of acquisitions (68 versus 50) was significantly higher, but not radiation exposure. Although rare, mortality occurred only in sinus-type non-haemorrhagic dAVF. Facial nerve palsy was the major adverse event in non-haemorrhagic dAVF.

CONCLUSION: Employing comparable techniques, occluding non-haemorrhagic onset dAVF takes longer and requires a larger embolic volume, yet it presents a higher likelihood of achieving an excellent functional outcome. Occlusion rates are high in all dAVF clusters. Managing non-haemorrhagic, sinus-type dAVFs requires careful attention.

METHODS AND MATERIALS: Patients treated by embolization for a brain dAVF were included. Excluded were cavernous sinus and surgically treated dAVF.

title: One-year outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy and catheter-directed thrombolysis in acute pulmonary embolism.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although anticoagulation remains the standard of care for acute pulmonary embolism (PE), mechanical thrombectomy (MT) and catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) have emerged as effective interventional options for rapid clot removal. However, their comparative outcomes remain incompletely defined. Hence, this study compared the outcomes of MT and CDT for acute PE at a tertiary referral center in the United States.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of all patients who underwent MT or CDT for acute PE across a single hospital system between January 2021 and April 2025. Patients were stratified into MT and CDT groups based on the treatment received. Baseline characteristics, procedural data, and clinical outcomes were analyzed. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. The secondary outcomes included length of hospital stay, major adverse events, reintervention, and PE recurrence. Patients were followed up for up to 1 year or until death.

RESULTS: A total of 724 patients were included in this study: 569 (79%) underwent MT and 155 (21%) received CDT. The mean age was 63 ± 16 years, and 49% were female. Most patients (76%) were classified as intermediate-high risk, with a mean right ventricle to left ventricle ratio of 1.5 ± 0.5. Bilateral or saddle embolism was present in 93% of patients. Patients in the MT group were more likely to have a simplified PE severity index of >0 (73% vs 60%; P < .001). Age and the rates of cancer, chronic cardiopulmonary disease, and concurrent deep vein thrombosis were similar between the groups. The median procedure duration was longer for MT (66 minutes, interquartile range, 46-89) than for CDT (58 minutes, interquartile range, 40-77; P = .003). The median postoperative length of stay was 3 days in both groups. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative adverse cardiac events (2.5% vs 0%; P = .048), and CDT was associated with higher intensive care unit admission rates (83% vs 36%; P < .001). However, the 30-day mortality rate was similar between the groups (CDT: 2.6% vs MT: 4.6%; P = .27). Additionally, the 1-year incidence rates of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (MT: 4.5% vs CDT: 3.4%; P = .69), PE recurrence (MT: 4.4% vs CDT: 2.5%; P = .31), and all-cause mortality (MT: 7.8% vs CDT: 5.8%; P = .41) were not statistically significantly different between the MT and CDT groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, MT and CDT for acute PE showed statistically comparable 30-day mortality rates and 1-year recurrence rates of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and PE. MT was associated with a higher incidence of intraoperative cardiac complications, and CDT was associated with more frequent intensive care unit admission.

However, their comparative outcomes remain incompletely defined. Hence, this study compared the outcomes of MT and CDT for acute PE at a tertiary referral center in the United States.

title: Design and baseline characteristics of the CagriSema cardiovascular outcomes trial (REDEFINE 3).
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cagrilintide-semaglutide (CagriSema) is a fixed-dose combination of the amylin receptor agonist cagrilintide and the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist semaglutide administered subcutaneously once weekly. CagriSema has demonstrated significant weight reduction and improved glycemic control in participants with excess adiposity and type 2 diabetes (T2D).

METHODS: REDEFINE 3 is a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving participants with established cardiovascular disease (CVD) and body mass index (BMI) ≥25.0 kg/m2 with/without T2D randomized to CagriSema 2.4 mg/2.4 mg or placebo, plus standard of care. The safety objective is to confirm noninferiority of CagriSema compared with placebo on cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke (MACE-3). The efficacy objective is to confirm the superiority of CagriSema compared with placebo on cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or revascularization (MACE-4).

RESULTS: Between 1/2023 and 12/2024, 7,076 adults at 575 sites in 24 countries were randomized. Mean age at baseline was 66 years. BMI ≥30 kg/m2 was present in 76% of participants (n = 5,370). In participants with T2D (n = 4,348, 61%), the mean duration of T2D was 12 years and mean glycated hemoglobin was 7.7%. Most participants had a prior myocardial infarction (n = 4,369, 62%). Prior stroke (n = 1,311, 19%) and peripheral arterial disease (n = 769, 11%) were less common, and 617 participants (9%) had more than one qualifying CVD criteria.

CONCLUSION: The REDEFINE 3 trial will provide evidence regarding the cardiovascular safety and efficacy of CagriSema, a novel fixed-dose combination therapy that could improve cardiovascular outcomes in a broad population of people with established CVD and excess adiposity.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The REDEFINE 3 trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05669755).

CagriSema has demonstrated significant weight reduction and improved glycemic control in participants with excess adiposity and type 2 diabetes (T2D). METHODS: REDEFINE 3 is a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving participants with established cardiovascular disease (CVD) and body mass index (BMI) ≥25.0 kg/m2 with/without T2D randomized to CagriSema 2.4 mg/2.4 mg or placebo, plus standard of care.

title: A Compact Unified Model for Moderate-to-Severe Carotid Artery Stenosis Using Image Segmentation: A Multicenter Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a new artificial intelligence model, the compact unified model (CU-Model), for moderate-to-severe carotid artery stenosis using digital subtraction angiography (DSA) images compared to clinical reference standards.

METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, 156 patients with confirmed moderate-to-severe carotid artery stenosis were included. A pretrained CU-Model (trained on public non-clinical datasets for optical flow and stereo matching) was applied to raw DSA images without any fine-tuning on clinical data to avoid data leakage. The model served exclusively as a post-acquisition support tool: cardiologists applied it immediately after procedures for automated vessel segmentation and highlighting. Final North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) measurements and interpreta-tions were performed manually under expert supervision by 2 blinded researchers.

RESULTS: The CU-Model identified left internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis in 84 patients and right ICA stenosis in 72. It misclassified only 1 moderate left ICA stenosis case as normal, achieving 99.4% sensitivity (155/156) for any stenosis detection. For stenosis severity grading, strong agreement with DSA was observed (moderate: 57.68 ± 5.94 vs. 57.71 ± 6.19, r = 0.83, P < .001, 95% CI: 0.76-0.88; severe: 86.96 ± 5.97 vs. 87.02 ± 6.18, r = 0.91, P < .001, 95% CI: 0.85-0.95). Of 156 cases, 106 were moderate (50%-69%) and 50 severe (≥70%), using NASCET-adapted thresholds accounting for measurement variability. Hypertension (77%), smoking, and syncope were common, with significant association in symptomatic patients (P < .05).

CONCLUSION: The CU-Model demonstrates strong concordance with DSA as a practical, post-procedure support tool for vessel segmentation. Pending larger validation studies, it shows promise for enhancing clinical workflow efficiency.

METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, 156 patients with confirmed moderate-to-severe carotid artery stenosis were included. A pretrained CU-Model (trained on public non-clinical datasets for optical flow and stereo matching) was applied to raw DSA images without any fine-tuning on clinical data to avoid data leakage.

title: Emergency management of postoperative airway obstruction following carotid endarterectomy: a systematic review.
abstract: Postoperative airway obstruction after carotid endarterectomy presents a significant challenge to anaesthetists. Airway oedema, with or without haematoma, may rapidly develop with life-threatening consequences. This systematic review aims to inform best practice in the management of postoperative airway obstruction following carotid endarterectomy. A literature search was conducted for manuscripts published between 01/01/2000 and 01/07/2025. Articles describing the anaesthetic management of adult patients who developed postoperative airway obstruction following carotid endarterectomy were included. Reference lists of the reviewed articles were also scrutinised for additional relevant sources. Outcome measures were the presentation of airway obstruction, success rate of airway interventions, duration of tracheal intubation and incidence of airway-related morbidity and mortality. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. The literature search yielded 284 articles, of which 32 full papers were reviewed. Six papers were deemed pertinent, in addition to five identified from review of references, for a total of 11 included in this systematic review (five case reports, three case series and three retrospective observational studies) detailing the management of airway compromise post-carotid endarterectomy in 84 cases. Clinical signs correlate poorly with anatomical distortion, and laryngeal oedema is generally more severe than anticipated. Prompt haematoma evacuation improved the success rate of airway management, without associated morbidity or mortality. Surgical exploration under local anaesthesia was efficacious and may avoid the need for airway intervention. Awake tracheal intubation was associated with fewer complications than asleep tracheal intubation and should be considered where time and patient cooperation allow. Emergency front-of-neck access should not be delayed for repeated attempts at tracheal intubation with a high chance of failure. Patients' tracheas should remain intubated for sufficient time after surgical exploration, allowing airway oedema to resolve prior to extubation.
englishSummary: Postoperative airway obstruction after carotid endarterectomy presents a significant challenge to anaesthetists. Airway oedema, with or without haematoma, may rapidly develop with life-threatening consequences. This systematic review aims to inform best practice in the management of postoperative airway obstruction following carotid endarterectomy.

title: Higher fibrosis-4 index is associated with 1-year in-stent restenosis after carotid artery stenting.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-stent restenosis (ISR) is a clinically important complication of carotid artery stenting (CAS); however, practical risk markers remain understudied. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with atherosclerotic risk, and the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index, a non-invasive marker of liver fibrosis, has been linked to carotid atherosclerosis progression. Therefore, this study examined whether the FIB-4 index was associated with ISR after CAS.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 132 patients who underwent CAS between 2010 and 2023. ISR was defined as peak systolic velocity ≥175 cm/s on at least two consecutive duplex examinations. The primary analysis evaluated FIB-4 continuously per 1-SD increase using Cox models. Secondary exploratory analyses used a cohort-derived cutoff determined by the Youden index.

RESULTS: ISR occurred in 16/132 (12%) patients. When analyzed continuously, FIB-4 was not significantly associated with ISR in univariable analysis (HR per 1-SD increase, 1.34; 95% CI, 0.88-2.04; p = 0.172) or in a parsimonious model adjusted for sex and stent design (adjusted HR, 1.40; 95% CI, 0.89-2.21; p = 0.142). The cohort-derived cutoff was 2.08. In secondary exploratory analysis, FIB-4 ≥ 2.08 was associated with higher ISR risk after adjustment for sex and stent design (adjusted HR, 3.93; 95% CI, 1.42-10.9; p = 0.008).

CONCLUSIONS: Although continuous FIB-4 was not significantly associated with ISR, exploratory cutoff-based analyses suggested an association between higher FIB-4 and 1-year ISR after CAS. Further validation is required before clinical use.

Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with atherosclerotic risk, and the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index, a non-invasive marker of liver fibrosis, has been linked to carotid atherosclerosis progression. Therefore, this study examined whether the FIB-4 index was associated with ISR after CAS.

title: Proton pump inhibitor use was not associated with reduced gastrointestinal bleeding risk in ischemic stroke patients treated with dual antiplatelet therapy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the association between proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use and gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients receiving dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT).

METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 3,122 AIS patients with large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) treated with DAPT at Qingdao University Affiliated Hospital (September 2020-December 2023). Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for GIB were calculated using binary logistic regression, controlling for confounders including age, sex, and other baseline characteristics. To address confounding by indication, we additionally performed 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) as a sensitivity analysis, with conditional logistic regression applied to the matched cohort.

RESULTS: 45.0% (n = 1,404) received concomitant PPI. No significant difference in GIB incidence was observed between PPI users and non-PPI users (2.1% vs. 1.3%, p = 0.12). Subgroup analyses revealed that PPI use was significantly associated with increased GIB risk in non-endovascular therapy patients (aOR = 2.08, p = 0.03), particularly those with posterior circulation infarction (aOR = 5.96, p = 0.006). These findings were further supported by propensity score matching analysis (conditional OR = 1.64, 95% CI 0.87-3.09, p = 0.124 for the overall cohort; conditional OR = 12.29, 95% CI 1.59-94.90, p = 0.016 for posterior circulation infarction in the non-endovascular subgroup). No significant association between PPI use and GIB risk was found in endovascular therapy or age-stratified subgroups.

CONCLUSION: PPI use was not associated with reduced overall GIB risk in DAPT-treated AIS patients. Routine PPI prophylaxis may be unnecessary for low-bleeding-risk populations, while the association observed in posterior circulation infarction remains hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective validation.

METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 3,122 AIS patients with large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) treated with DAPT at Qingdao University Affiliated Hospital (September 2020-December 2023). Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for GIB were calculated using binary logistic regression, controlling for confounders including age, sex, and other baseline characteristics.

title: Chocolate Balloon Versus Conventional Balloon for Vessel Preparation Before Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Femoropopliteal Lesions: A Real-World Propensity Score-Matched Study.
abstract: To evaluate the procedural and 1-year clinical outcomes of the Chocolate balloon versus conventional plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) for vessel preparation before drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment of femoropopliteal lesions. This retrospective subgroup analysis of the multicenter PROMISING registry included patients with femoropopliteal lesions treated with DCB. Before propensity score matching (PSM), 817 patients underwent POBA and 379 underwent Chocolate balloon angioplasty. After 1:1 PSM, 254 patients were included in each group. The primary endpoint was bailout stenting. Secondary endpoints included maximum DCB diameter, stent length, postprocedural ankle-brachial index (ABI), 1-year clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR), major amputation, all-cause mortality, amputation-free survival (AFS), and major adverse events (MAE). After PSM, bailout stenting occurred less frequently in the Chocolate balloon group than in the POBA group (20.47% vs 29.92%, p = 0.014). The Chocolate balloon group also showed a trend toward shorter stent length (20.67 ± 9.75 cm vs 23.71 ± 10.62 cm, p = 0.097) and allowed use of larger DCBs (4.96 ± 0.52 mm vs 4.74 ± 0.61 mm, p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression identified Chocolate balloon use as an independent protective factor against bailout stenting, whereas chronic total occlusion and severe calcification were independent predictors of bailout stenting. No significant differences were observed in 1-year clinical outcomes. Compared with POBA, Chocolate balloon vessel preparation reduced bailout stenting and enabled use of larger DCBs, suggesting potential procedural advantages in complex femoropopliteal lesions. However, these procedural benefits did not translate into improved 1-year clinical outcomes.

title: Impact of the infusion line on co-loading and highly diluted norepinephrine administration through a single peripheral venous catheter: An in vitro simulation of the infusion protocol used during cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rapid crystalloid co-loading and prophylactic norepinephrine may share a peripheral intravenous catheter during cesarean delivery. We assessed whether infusion-system architecture alters fluid and drug delivery.

METHODS: Six infusion-system configurations were tested in vitro. Norepinephrine 8 μg/mL was infused at 30 mL/h (4 μg/min) while 1000 mL saline was delivered from a pressure bag initially inflated to 300 mmHg. Outcomes were crystalloid volume delivered during the first 10 min, time within the norepinephrine target range of 3.5-4.5 μg/min, and the proportion of measurements outside ±12.5% of the configuration-specific median.

RESULTS: Crystalloid volume at 10 min ranged from 596 ± 30 to 947 ± 30 mL between configurations (P < 0.001). Time within the norepinephrine target range ranged from 32.8 ± 6.1% to 71.4 ± 9.9% (P = 0.019), and instability ranged from 23.8 ± 6.2% to 54.6 ± 13.0% (P < 0.001). Among the configurations tested, those in which pressurized crystalloid entered downstream of the convergence of actively controlled drug infusions showed the most favorable balance between crystalloid delivery and norepinephrine stability.

DISCUSSION: Infusion-system architecture influenced both rapid crystalloid delivery and distal norepinephrine stability. When pressurized crystalloid and actively controlled drugs share a peripheral intravenous catheter, a distal crystalloid entry may represent a favorable system architecture. Clinical relevance requires further evaluation.

We assessed whether infusion-system architecture alters fluid and drug delivery. METHODS: Six infusion-system configurations were tested in vitro.

title: [Predictive value and threshold effect analysis of the novel systemic immune-inflammatory complex index for functional outcomes at 90 days after reperfusion therapy in acute ischemic stroke].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the correlation between the baseline systemic immune-inflammatory complex index (SIICI) and the 90-day functional prognosis of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) undergoing reperfusion therapy, as well as the threshold effect.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 1 919 AIS patients who received reperfusion therapy and were admitted to The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China from January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2025 were enrolled. Patients were divided into good prognosis group [modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score was 0-2] and a poor prognosis group (mRS score was 3-6) according to the 90-day score after onset. The clinical data and blood routine indicators within 24 hours after onset were collected, and SIICI and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) were calculated. Univariate Logistic regression analysis was performed to screen 90-day functional prognosis-related influencing factors in patients with AIS after reperfusion therapy. Multivariate Logistic regression with multi-gradient adjustment was used to determine whether SIICI was an independent risk factor for poor functional prognosis or not. The restricted cubic spline (RCS) model was applied to analyze the dose-response relationship between SIICI and the risk of poor functional prognosis, and piecewise linear regression model was used for threshold effect analysis. Subjects were randomly divided into a training set and a validation set at a ratio of 7 : 3 for constructing a prognostic prediction model based on SIICI and internal validation. The receiver operator characteristic curve (ROC curve), calibration curve and decision curve analysis (DCA) were plotted to evaluate the discrimination, calibration and clinical net benefit of the model.

RESULTS: All 1 919 AIS patients were enrolled in the final analysis, including 1 176 cases (61.28%) in the good prognosis group and 743 cases (38.72%) in the poor prognosis group. Univariate Logistic regression analysis showed that advanced age, history of atrial fibrillation, bridging therapy, endovascular thrombectomy, elevated baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, prolonged total length of hospital stay, increased white blood cell count, elevated neutrophil count, elevated monocyte count, increased SII and elevated SIICI were risk factors for poor 90-day functional prognosis of AIS patients, and the history of hyperlipidemia and elevated lymphocyte count were protective factors (all P<0.05). Multivariate Logistic regression analysis demonstrated that after adjusting for gender, age, past medical history, Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment (TOAST) classification and baseline NIHSS score, SIICI remained an independent risk factor for poor 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients [odds ratio (OR)=1.008, 95% confidence interval (95%CI) was 1.001-1.014, P=0.022], whereas SII showed no statistical significance after adjustment (OR=1.010, 95%CI was 0.999-1.020, P=0.067), suggesting that SIICI possessed better stability of independent association than the traditional inflammatory index SII. The RCS model verified a significant non-linear relationship between SIICI and the risk of poor 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients (P<0.001). The optimal inflection point value of SIICI determined by piecewise linear regression was 15.03. When SIICI<15.03, each one-unit increase in SIICI was associated with an 11% increased risk of poor functional prognosis (OR=1.112, 95%CI was 1.078-1.147, P<0.001). When SIICI≥15.03, no statistically significant correlation was observed between SIICI and poor functional prognosis (OR=1.005, 95%CI was 0.998-1.012, P=0.136). For the SIICI-based prognosis prediction model, the area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.656 (95%CI was 0.626-0.686) in the training set and 0.639 (95%CI was 0.593-0.686) in the validation set, indicating favorable prognostic discrimination ability. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test yielded P=0.064, suggesting good model calibration. DCA revealed that the model obtained significant clinical net benefit within the high-risk threshold range of 0-0.8.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline SIICI is independently correlated with the 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients after reperfusion therapy and shows a significant threshold effect. It exhibits superior predictive performance compared with the traditional inflammatory index SII. The prognostic prediction model constructed based on SIICI can assist clinicians in stratifying the risk of early functional prognosis in patients with AIS undergoing reperfusion therapy.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 1 919 AIS patients who received reperfusion therapy and were admitted to The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China from January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2025 were enrolled.

title: Vascular Management Strategies and Outcomes of Infectious Arterial Complications Involving the Kidney Transplant Vasculature: A Systematic Review and Evidence-Informed Treatment Framework.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Infectious arterial complications involving the kidney transplant (KT) vasculature are rare but life-threatening and frequently result in KT loss. The lack of evidence-based guidance for vascular management strategies underscores the need for systematic synthesis to inform clinical decision-making.

METHODS: A systematic search was performed from database inception through August 22, 2025, for reports of culture-proven infectious vascular complications-including arterial rupture, detachment, pseudoaneurysm, aneurysm, thrombosis, or stenosis-involving the transplant renal artery, iliac vessels, or arterial anastomosis in KT recipients. Eligible studies reported vascular management strategies. Due to methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively using proportion-based comparisons.

RESULTS: Eighty reports (1972-2025) comprising 139 cases were included. Candida species were most frequent, followed by Pseudomonas, Aspergillus, and Staphylococcus species. Pseudoaneurysm and arterial rupture were the predominant clinical presentation, typically occuring within the first month after transplantation. Outcome patterns differed by transplant nephrectomy status, with vascular management strategies performed without transplant nephrectomy demonstrating higher reported proportions of uneventful follow-up. Autologous interposition grafting demonstrated the most favorable outcome pattern (86.7% uneventful recovery; 6.7% reintervention and mortality), even when transplant nephrectomy is unavoidable. Covered stent placement was the most frequently reported intervention andshowed favorable outcomes in selected KT-preserving cases (75% uneventful recovery). Primary surgical repair had the highest reintervention proportion (59.1%), whereas arterial ligation had the highest mortality (43.8%) and accounted for all reported limb loss.

CONCLUSION: Across five decades of case-based evidence, autologous interposition grafting demonstrated the most favorable outcome pattern and may represent the preferred vascular management strategy when durable arterial reconstruction is feasible, including when transplant nephrectomy is required. Covered stent placement may provide a useful option in selected cases or as a temporizing strategy for hemorrhage control. These findings should guide rather than define management decisions given the heterogeneous evidence base.

HIGHLIGHTS: First systematic synthesis of management strategies for infectious arterial complications involving the kidney transplant vasculature Candida was the most frequently reported pathogen; pseudoaneurysm and arterial rupture were the predominant presentations Vascular management strategies performed without transplant nephrectomy demonstrated higher reported proportions of uneventful follow-up Autologous interposition grafting showed the most favorable reported outcome pattern, even when transplant nephrectomy is unavoidable Ligation and primary repair were associated with higher reported mortality and reintervention, respectively.

The lack of evidence-based guidance for vascular management strategies underscores the need for systematic synthesis to inform clinical decision-making. title: Longitudinal monitoring of adalimumab levels and anti-adalimumab antibodies in Chinese patients with ankylosing spondylitis: a prospective cohort study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to clarify the association between longitudinal adalimumab concentrations, anti-adalimumab antibodies (AAA) levels, and clinical response in Chinese patients with ankylosing spondylitis (AS).

METHODS: A prospective multi-center, observational cohort study of AS patients receiving adalimumab therapy was conducted. Disease activity was assessed with the AS Disease Activity Score (ASDAS), and clinical responders were defined based on ASDAS improvement together with C-reactive protein normalization. Adalimumab concentrations were measured using a validated sandwich immunoassay. Measurement of AAA levels was performed with a laboratory-developed immunoassay system integrating electrochemiluminescence technology with specific immunomagnetic separation, with result reported as signal-to-noise ratio (S/N).

RESULTS: A total of 140 patients receiving adalimumab monotherapy were included. The median follow-up period was 169 days, and 711 plasma samples were available for adalimumab concentrations and AAA levels measurements. Seven patients had pre-existing AAA, and 120 (90.2%) of the remaining 133 patients tested positive for AAA during follow-up. A total of 48 patients were excluded from the exposure-response relationship dataset owing to pre-existing AAA (n=7), lack of active disease (n=26), incomplete follow-up (n=8), and prolonged dosing intervals (n=7). Among the remaining 92 patients, a total of 58 (63%) achieved clinical response. Adalimumab concentrations were higher, and AAA levels were significantly lower, in responders compared with non-responders at multiple time points. Exposure-response relationship models also revealed a steady-state adalimumab concentration target of 5.1 μg/mL and a week-4 concentration target of 3.3 μg/mL, corresponding to an 80% probability of clinical response. Thirty-six of 92 patients (39.1%) exhibited AAA-S/N values exceeding the putative clinically meaningful threshold (AAA-S/N=10). Patients in the high-AAA group (AAA-S/N≥10) had lower drug levels (median: 1.5 μg/mL vs. 6.9 μg/mL, P<0.0001) and poorer response rates (38.8% vs. 78.6%, P = 0.0002), relative to those in the low-AAA group (AAA-S/N<10). Furthermore, patients who were week-4 AAA-positive exhibited a 1.8-fold increased risk of non-response (relative risk, 95% confidence interval, 1.1-2.8).

CONCLUSIONS: Our results demonstrate that longitudinal profiles of adalimumab concentrations and AAA levels show a strong association with clinical responses in this Chinese AS cohort, which may inform therapeutic drug monitoring-guided adalimumab treatment strategies that remain to be further validated.

Disease activity was assessed with the AS Disease Activity Score (ASDAS), and clinical responders were defined based on ASDAS improvement together with C-reactive protein normalization.

title: Topologically complex knotted proteins are processed differentially by ATP-dependent proteases ClpXP and ClpAP.
abstract: Knotted proteins can present a distinct topological and mechanical challenge to the AAA+ cellular degradation machineries, determined by the relative size of the knot and the pore dimensions of these enzymes. In this study, we investigated the degradation mechanism of knotted proteins of different topological complexities by two E. coli. AAA+ proteases ClpXP and ClpAP. While ClpXP efficiently degraded all knotted substrates, regardless of their topology, ClpAP exhibited a striking functional divergence. Despite its robust double-ring ATPase architecture, ClpAP failed to degrade the 41-knotted miRFP and degraded the 31-knotted CAIX and more complex 52-knotted UCHL1 slower than ClpXP. We have demonstrated that this disparity is not dictated merely by absolute knot complexity, but is critically governed by the length of the knot tail, which determines whether a knot can spontaneously unthread or is forced to tighten during the translocation. Furthermore, based on the slower processing of a sterically constrained covalent dimeric substrate Arc-ssrA, we propose that ClpAP's hindered processing of knotted substrates stems from its smaller axial pore. Overall, we propose a unified physical model in which the successful degradation of a knotted protein relies on a delicate interplay among knot compaction, tail-mediated unthreading, and the architectural permissiveness of the unfoldase pore.

In this study, we investigated the degradation mechanism of knotted proteins of different topological complexities by two E. coli.

title: Temporal Net Water Uptake Evolution and Its Association with Functional Outcome in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Subacute lesion growth after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is associated with worse functional outcomes. The ischemic lesion severity can be assessed with net water uptake (NWU), a CT-based marker of edema. Pretreatment NWU has been associated with worse functional outcomes; however, it remains unclear how the temporal changes in NWU influence functional outcomes. In this study, we aimed to determine how associations between NWU and functional outcome vary across imaging times up to 1 week after stroke.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included patients from the Multicenter Randomized Clinical Trial of Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke in the Netherlands (MRCLEAN-NO IV) trial with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion who were treated with endovascular treatment and had baseline, 24-hour, and 1-week follow-up noncontrast CT scans. Functional outcome at 90 days was evaluated using the mRS, analyzed both as functional independence (mRS 0-2) and across the full ordinal distribution (mRS 0-6). In the primary analysis, associations between NWU measured at different imaging time points and functional independence were examined using univariable and multivariable logistic regression models. To evaluate temporal changes in NWU, ΔNWU was calculated at different time intervals (baseline to 24 hours, 24 hours to 1 week, and baseline to 1 week), and its association with outcomes was analyzed using analogous regression models.

RESULTS: Of 539 MRCLEAN-NO IV patients, 115 were included in this study. The median time from stroke onset to randomization was 92 (IQR, 70-140) minutes. The median NWU evolved from 4.3% (interquartile range [IQR], 2.1%-6.8%) at baseline to 9.0% (IQR, 3.0%-13%) at 24 hours and 15% (IQR, 11%-19%) at 1 week. The median patient-level change (ΔNWU) from baseline to 1 week was 10% (IQR, 5.3%-16%). NWU measured at 1 week, but not at baseline or 24 hours, was significantly associated with functional dependence, with an adjusted OR (aOR) of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.47-0.90) per 5-percentage-point increase in NWU. Furthermore, a higher increase in NWU from baseline to 1-week imaging was significantly associated with functional dependence, with an aOR of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.47-0.86) per 5-percentage-point increase in ΔNWU1wk-BL.

CONCLUSIONS: In our population, NWU measured at 1 week is associated with 90-day clinical outcomes, suggesting that lesion evolution continues in the first week after stroke onset and may therefore represent a target for secondary treatments to improve clinical outcomes.

The ischemic lesion severity can be assessed with net water uptake (NWU), a CT-based marker of edema. Pretreatment NWU has been associated with worse functional outcomes; however, it remains unclear how the temporal changes in NWU influence functional outcomes.

title: Deep Learning-Based Noncontrast CT Imaging Markers Enhance Posttransfer DWI Core Volume Prediction.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Deep learning enables the extraction of ischemic lesion size and hypodensity imaging markers from deep learning-based NCCT (DLNCCT) assessment in patients with acute ischemic stroke, but it remains unclear whether those markers can predict posttransfer core volume.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We performed a post hoc analysis of prospectively enrolled patients transferred from a primary stroke center (PSC) to a comprehensive stroke center (CSC) for endovascular treatment (EVT). Using a validated DLNCCT segmentation method, we quantified total lesion volume (per 10 mL), modified net water uptake (mNWU %), and severely hypodense volume (≤26 Hounsfield units [HU] per 10 mL) and compared these markers with core lab rated ASPECTS (per point decrease) and CTP-based evaluation for their association with (adjusted regression coefficient [95% CI]) and predictive performance in addition to baseline variables (R 2 ± SEs) for posttransfer CSC admission DWI core volume.

RESULTS: We included 420 patients (239 [57%] men) with a median age of 72 years (interquartile range: 61-80). We observed 11.2 mL (95% CI, 8.3-14.1] larger posttransfer core volumes per point decrease in ASPECTS, and 10.0 mL (95% CI, 6.8-13.3), and 20.0 mL (95% CI, 12.7-27.2) larger posttransfer core volumes per 10-mL increase in total and severely hypodense DLNCCT volume, respectively. mNWU was not associated with posttransfer core volume (P = .63). In addition to clinical baseline and CTA variables, posttransfer core volume prediction with ASPECTS (R 2: 0.49 ± 0.02) and DLNCCT (R 2: 0.50 ± 0.02) did not differ significantly (P = .58). Compared with using CTP imaging markers (R 2: 0.56 ± 0.02), adding ASPECTS (R 2: 0.63 ± 0.02; P < .01) and DLNCCT (R 2: 0.65 ± 0.01; P < .01) improved performance for posttransfer core volume prediction.

CONCLUSIONS: Total and severely hypodense DLNCCT volumes are independent predictors for posttransfer core volume. These DLNCCT markers improved CTP-based posttransfer core volume prediction.

title: Impact of Balloon-Guided Catheter Position on First-Pass Effect in Mechanical Thrombectomy for Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The first-pass effect (FPE; complete or near-complete reperfusion [extended TICI 2b-3] after a single thrombectomy pass) is a key functional outcome determinant. This study identified factors associated with FPE and quantitatively evaluated how balloon-guided catheter (BGC) positioning relates to FPE achievement during anterior circulation mechanical thrombectomy.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively maintained database of consecutive patients with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy using a BGC between May 2022 and February 2025. The BGC tip to the proximal petrous ICA distance was measured using lateral angiography at the initial BGC position. Factors associated with FPE were evaluated using univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis determined the optimal cutoff value for predicting FPE.

RESULTS: Among 110 patients (median age, 81 years; 54% men), 56% achieved FPE. A shorter BGC tip to proximal petrous ICA distance was independently associated with higher FPE rates (adjusted OR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.98; P < .001). Greater distance correlated with longer procedure time (r = 0.3; P < .001) and more thrombectomy passes (P < .001). Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified 24 mm as the optimal cutoff (area under the curve, 0.7). Distal BGC positioning was associated with fewer distal emboli and shorter recanalization time without serious complications.

CONCLUSIONS: Distal BGC placement within 24 mm of the proximal petrous ICA independently predicted higher FPE achievement and greater procedural efficiency. Quantitative BGC position assessment may provide a practical intraoperative metric to optimize mechanical thrombectomy strategies.

This study identified factors associated with FPE and quantitatively evaluated how balloon-guided catheter (BGC) positioning relates to FPE achievement during anterior circulation mechanical thrombectomy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospectively maintained database of consecutive patients with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy using a BGC between May 2022 and February 2025.

title: SELECT-CT: Symptom Evaluation, Lesion Estimation, and Curated Triage to CT-A Simple Algorithm to Select the Right Patients for Emergent Code Stroke CT.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The intended purpose of multimodal Code Stroke CT (CSCT) is to rapidly identify patients with acute ischemic stroke who are likely to benefit from mechanical thrombectomy. This study aimed to evaluate a new clinical algorithm for reliably identifying thrombectomy candidates while reducing the number of CSCT scans that are currently inundating radiology services.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was performed on consecutive patients who underwent mechanical thrombectomy at a comprehensive stroke center during a 2-year period. The Symptom Evaluation, Lesion Estimation, and Clinical Triage for CT (SELECT-CT) algorithm, ie, an NIHSS score threshold of ≥2 and/or any posterior circulation or disabling symptoms, was applied to identify patients with large and distal medium vessel occlusions who may benefit from thrombectomy. The performance of SELECT-CT and 6 different NIHSS score thresholds (from ≥1 to ≥6) for reducing CSCT scan numbers, while correctly identifying patients treated with thrombectomy, was also assessed.

RESULTS: During the study period 4921 patients had CSCT scans, yielding a 5% thrombectomy rate. Of 240 patients (median age 73; 54.6% male) who underwent thrombectomy, the NIHSS score ≥6 captured only 198 (83%), including 151 of 166 patients (91%) with an anterior circulation large vessel occlusion. Conversely, the threshold of ≥2 alone captured 229 of 240 (95%) thrombectomy patients. Using SELECT-CT, performance improved to correct identification of 232 of 240 (97%) thrombectomy patients, including all who should be treated based on current evidence. Applying NIHSS score thresholds of ≥6 and ≥2 for patient triage to CSCT reduced scan volume by 76% and 47%, respectively. The more cautious and nuanced approach using SELECT-CT achieved a 30% reduction in scan numbers.

CONCLUSIONS: The SELECT-CT algorithm can reduce CSCT scan workload while still identifying patients who should be treated with thrombectomy.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was performed on consecutive patients who underwent mechanical thrombectomy at a comprehensive stroke center during a 2-year period.

title: Impact of direct-to-operating room transfer protocol for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of a direct-to-operating room (DOR) transfer protocol for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) on surgical volume, interhospital transfer patterns, and surgical outcomes at a tertiary referral center.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-institution cohort study used institutional databases and the Vascular Quality Initiative registry to identify all patients undergoing rAAA repair between 2014 and 2024. In January 2020, a multidisciplinary rapid-response transfer protocol was implemented to facilitate DOR transfers. Patients were stratified into pre- and postimplementation cohorts. Differences in case volume, transfer patterns, transfer distance, time to treatment, and surgical outcomes between groups were assessed using univariable analysis, with statistical significance set at P < .05.

RESULTS: A total of 96 patients underwent rAAA repair during the study period, with 28.1% treated before and 71.9% treated after implementation of the transfer protocol. Baseline characteristics were similar between cohorts, except for a higher prevalence of diabetes (40.7% vs 14.5%; P = .005) and former smokers (59.3% vs 34.8%; P = .029) in the preimplementation group. The annual rAAA repair volume increased threefold after implementation, from a mean of 4.5 to 13.8 cases/year. Overall, 86.5% of patients were transferred from outside hospitals, with a significant increase in the proportion of external transfers after implementation (70.4% vs 92.8%; P = .007). Median transfer distance increased from 23.7 to 49.1 miles (P = .017) and time from transfer acceptance to operating room arrival decreased from 173 to 124 minutes (P = .145). Distance-adjusted transfer time decreased significantly from 9.5 to 4.1 min/mile (P = .017). Endovascular repair was performed in 68.8% of patients, with no difference between cohorts. In-hospital stroke (6.2%), myocardial infarction (7.3%), and mortality (22.9%) rates were similar between groups. Median length of stay was 6.6 days. Thirty-day outcomes did not differ between cohorts, with readmission in 13.5%, reintervention in 36.5%, and mortality in 25.0% of patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of a multidisciplinary DOR protocol for rAAA was associated with a sustained increase in surgical volume, higher rates of interhospital transfer, expansion of the regional referral network, and lower distance-adjusted transfer times, with perioperative outcomes remaining within contemporary benchmarks.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-institution cohort study used institutional databases and the Vascular Quality Initiative registry to identify all patients undergoing rAAA repair between 2014 and 2024. In January 2020, a multidisciplinary rapid-response transfer protocol was implemented to facilitate DOR transfers.

title: Drug-Eluting Resorbable Scaffolds for Infrapopliteal Peripheral Artery Disease: A State-of-the-Art Review.
abstract: Drug-eluting resorbable scaffolds (DRS) have been developed to overcome the key limitations of conventional endovascular therapies for below-the-knee (BTK) peripheral artery disease (PAD), including acute recoil, restenosis, and the sequela of long-term permanent metallic implants. DRS provides a temporary mechanical support and localized antiproliferative drug delivery after which the scaffold is gradually resorbed, ultimately restoring native vessel architecture to preserve future revascularization options. Over the past decade, numerous prospective and observational studies have evaluated both polymer- and magnesium alloy-based DRS platforms and have demonstrated favorable patency, wound healing, and limb salvage outcomes in patients with advanced infrapopliteal PAD. Most recently, randomized evidence from the LIFE-BTK trial has demonstrated superior patency and reduced rates of revascularization with DRS-treated lesions as compared with plain balloon angioplasty. In this state-of-the-art review, we summarize the existing evidence evaluating DRS devices for BTK PAD and present an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical outcomes for DRS-based endovascular interventions.
